articles.body: Gael Monfils celebrates 40th birthday with first-round win at US Open | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Gael Monfils celebrates 40th birthday with first-round win at US Open AFP Gael Monfils gestures during first round of 2026 US Open Adam Hunger / CTK / AP France's Gael Monfils turned back the clock Tuesday, making the most of a US Open wild card and an adoring New York crowd to advance to the second round. Playing on his 40th birthday, Monfils opened shakily against Adolfo Daniel Vallejo of Paraguay, but decisively turned the tables after the first set for a 2-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-0 win. Monfils, who will retire after this season, played with his trademark showmanship, offering exaggerated bows after embellishing a putaway shot in the fourth set with a leap in the air. Match stats: Vallejo vs Monfils Flashscore Evidence of approval came when the crowd joined an impromptu performance of "Happy Birthday" after the match. "You guys always make it electric, amazing," Monfils said in an on-court interview. "Let's keep it going for the second one." This is Monfils' 18th appearance at the US Open. His best showing came in 2016 when he reached the semi-finals and lost to Novak Djokovic Monfils, who reached a career-high ranking of sixth in 2016, is down to 311th, having only played a handful of tournaments in 2026. In contrast to Monfils, who is playing in his 70th Grand Slam tournament, Tuesday marked just the third of the 22-year-old Vallejo. US Open 2026 The US Open is the fourth and final Grand Slam of the tennis season, running from August 30th to September 13th. It is a hard-court tournament held at Flushing Meadows in New York City. articles.body: Tiger Woods to change DUI plea | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Tigers Woods to change 'not guilty' plea in upcoming hearing for DUI case AFP Tigers Wood pleads guilty to DUI Andrew Redington / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA Tiger Woods, who pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence after crashing his car in Florida in March, is expected to formally change his plea, court documents showed Tuesday. "change of plea" hearing early Wednesday morning was added to the golf superstar's case docket at a Martin County court, online records showed. Woods ' lawyer did not immediately respond to AFP's request for comment about the nature of the change of plea. The 15-time major winner crashed his SUV into a trailer being pulled by a pickup truck near his Jupiter Island home in March. He was assessed to be impaired by officers at the scene and had opioid painkillers with him. Woods pleaded not guilty to misdemeanor charges of DUI with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test, telling authorities he was looking at his phone and changing radio channels when he crashed. Days later, he said he was "stepping away" to seek treatment and focus on his health. He was cleared by a judge to travel overseas to an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. Woods made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour's Travelers Championship in June. The following month, a judge ruled that prosecutors could review Woods' hospital treatment, as well as the golfer's prescription drug records. In both cases, the information can be reviewed only by prosecutors, designated law enforcement officers, experts, and Woods's defense team. Woods has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate, 2021 California car crash. articles.body: 49ers DC Raheem Morris Gushes Over This Defensive Lineman Jan 4, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons head coach Raheem Morris on the sideline against the New Orleans Saints in the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With Nick Bosa out of practice, the 49ers have been able to take a closer look at their other defensive ends. One player who has been seeing a healthy amount of starting reps is defensive end Sam Okuayinonu. He was a bit of an underrated player for the 49ers last year.Â It seems heâs been taking it up a notch throughout training camp. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was asked about Okuayinonu stepping up with Bosa out, to which he replied with a gushing answer.Â âI think just the pitbull mentality that he has. Heâs a barnyard bully. He can do whatever you want him to do,â Morris said. âHeâs kind of got that role where he can be that spinner we talked about. He can play at the line of scrimmage, plays with great strength, is able to go out there and shed blocks, be able to cause havoc.Â âHis ability to turn and run and get to the ball. I think weâve seen a big-time screen. Thatâs a standard type play for the 49ers and what heâs able to do. So, Iâm really excited about all of those guys and him getting his opportunity to go out there and do some of those things if it presents itself I know heâll be ready.â Okuayinonu receives a pretty big vote of confidence from Morris. Maybe heâs embellishing a bit because Okuayinonu may be in for a good chunk of playing time in Week 1. Bosaâs status to play in Australia is up in the air. In any case, if Okuayinonu has been stepping up and impacting like Morris is making him out to be, then itâll be huge. The 49ers need someone at defensive end to step up. Okuayinonu can do it. He would flash a few times a game last season, despite the defensive front being mediocre. Heâs decent against the run and the pass. Thereâs some explosiveness and good strength when he snaps off the ball. He was a player I advocated for the 49ers to bring back in free agency. Sure enough, they recognized that they have a solid rotational player on their hands. However, Okuayinonu must now face the reality of being one of the lead rushers with Bosa possibly out. articles.title: Gauff feeling 'incredible' after advancing to second round of US Open
articles.source_type: Live scores, results archive, fixtures and match detail
articles.body: Gauff feeling 'incredible' after advancing to second round of US Open | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Gauff feeling 'incredible' after advancing to second round of US Open AFP Coco Gauff during US Open first round Marcin Cholewinski / Zuma Press Coco Gauff opened her 2026 US Open campaign with a solid straight-set win over Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez that showcased her improved serve. The fourth-seeded Gauff , who won the New York Grand Slam in 2023, was broken only once to top the 53rd-ranked Sonmez 6-3, 6-4 in a hard-hitting battle fought mostly from the baseline. "It's incredible to be back on this court," an exuberant Gauff told the on-court interviewer. "I love playing in this atmosphere." Sonmez-Gauff matchup stats Flashscore Gauff, whose service woes last year contributed to a fourth-round exit, came into Flushing Meadows this time feeling much better about the stroke, having won the WTA 1000 event in Cincinnati this month. The American star blazed through the opening set without facing a break point, with Sonmez often unable to return Gauff's serve or offering only a weak reply that could be batted off easily. Gauff said she had worked to make the toss more consistent under the tutelage of biomechanics expert Gavin Macmillan, who previously helped Aryna Sabalenka retool her serve, improvements that helped the Belarusian rise to number one. "It's been a gradual change with the serve," Gauff said. "Slowly it's adapting to maybe the way it should look." Gauff broke early in the second set, but the Turkish player raised the level of her game with heavy ground strokes and sneaky forays to the net to finish points with deft volleys. Sonmez broke back for 2-2 and briefly took the lead. But at 2-3, Gauff fought off multiple break points in a lengthy game that the American eventually nabbed with another big serve. Gauff called the hold for 3-3 as "real important." "I like to challenge my opponent to let them keep up the level the whole match, and if they do, you know I clap my hands, and I walk off court with my head held high," Gauff said. "But I was able to settle down." US Open 2026 The US Open is the fourth and final Grand Slam of the tennis season, running from August 30th to September 13th. Question: You know what's the only thing cooler than getting great QB value with an early round pick? Answer: Getting great QB Value with a late-round pick! Presenting: My favorite late-round QBs (outside the top 12) in the DraftKings best ball streets. Goff's utter lack of a rushing floor will continue to make him cheap in drafts and cause fantasy nerds to claim he has "no upside." Well, Goff has eight top-5 finishes the last two seasons, which literally only trails Lamar Jackson Josh Allen Jalen Hurts and Joe Burrow . That's it. That's the entire list. I'd say the man is pretty capable of putting up big point totals! For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Kyler Murray, Vikings ADP: QB18 (pick 118.6) Kyler Murray hasn't exactly played to the best of his abilities in recent years. His highs in 2020 and 2021 were quite awesome and helped him secure that initial $230.5 million bag from the Cardinals, but unfortunately, things simply haven't been as good in recent years. We can see this quite clearly with adjusted net yards per attempt, which factors in touchdowns, interceptions and sacks into the traditional pass yards-per-attempt equation. So yeah, REALLY not great in 2025 — BUT it's also not like we've been looking at an overly stable situation here both in terms of Kyler's offensive environment as well as his own health. Murray suffered a torn ACL on Dec. 12, 2022 HC Kliff Kingsbury was fired following the 2022 season The Cardinals hired HC Jonathan Gannon and OC Drew Petzing prior to the 2023 season Murray suffered a foot injury in early 2025 that landed him on the sideline for what wound up being the entire season Of course, the latter injury was viewed as a "soft benching" with Jacoby Brissett generally doing a good job of leading this passing offense. This is the toughest obstacle for Kyler truthers to get around: Our most recent sample size of the 2025 season was ROUGH any way you cut it. That said: There's still reason for optimism thanks to three key factors. 1. Some advanced stats still painted Murray in a positive light in 2025. Specifically, EPA per dropback (+0.06, 15th) and PFF passing grade (69.5, tied 22nd). The former mark was better than guys like Joe Burrow Trevor Lawrence and Justin Herbert , while the latter cleared the likes of Lamar Jackson Daniel Jones and Baker Mayfield 2. This remains one of the position's most dangerous rushers. Last season, Murray actually averaged his most rushing yards per game (34.6) since his ACL injury. The film reflects the reality that this is still a dangerous man in the open field . Overall, Murray's average of 8.5 yards per scramble was good for the position's eighth-best mark last season and ranked ahead of guys like Patrick Mahomes and Jaxson Dart 3. Kyler didn't get a ton of help from his friends last season. Specifically, the alleged generational WR Marvin Harrison Jr., who had some rough ( and I mean ROUGH ) moments early in 2025. Overall, this Cardinals offense simply wasn't very QB-friendly. It finished 28th in my " Supporting Cast Rating ," which is the average of every team's rank in PFF rushing, receiving, run-blocking and pass-blocking grades (everything except passing). Good news: Minnesota finished 13th in Supporting Cast Rating last year! You could even argue they're higher when considering the schematic impact that renowned QB whisperer Kevin O'Connell has had on his passing games over the years. The potential for Kyler to improve his passing thanks to this new-and-improved offensive environment and keep on keeping on as a rusher paints the picture of an exciting late-round fantasy QB option in 2026. Check out our Fantasy Football ADP Report for a comprehensive tool with live-updated ADP data for multiple league formats and sites. Malik Willis, Dolphins ADP: QB21 (pick 133.7) Yes, we are dealing with a small sample size with Malik Willis . Originally drafted by the Titans in the third round in 2022, Willis has just six career starts and 155 career pass attempts to his name. Also yes, Willis was absolute nails with his opportunities in Green Bay. Obviously, Matt LaFleur and the offense's plethora of playmakers deserve a lot of credit, but either way: We're looking at a guy who has literally functioned as the NFL's most-efficient passer during the last two seasons. Overall, Willis leads all QBs in yards per attempt, adjusted yards per attempt, yards per completion, completion rate, passer rating and explosive pass play rate since 2024 And yet, it's his performance in two additional stats — EPA per dropback and completion percentage over expected — that are most impressive. That's him all the way up in the top-right-hand corner in the chart below. Not too shabby! Even more impressive was the manner in which he picked up yards in 2025. His 2024 film was definitely a bit gadgety (7.5 average target depth) and featured the Packers HEAVILY lean on their run game, but we saw a legit increase in aDOT in 2025 (9.7 yards!), which reflected the reality that he was hardly being schemed to success. There are downfield DIMES all over the film. And hey, all that is cool before even considering the massive plus that Willis brings to the run game thanks to his explosive rushing ability While he didn't run at the combine, Willis reportedly ran a 4.37-second 40-yard dash at Liberty's Pro Day Willis has averaged the position's fourth-most yards per scramble (8.9) the last two seasons Nobody has averaged more yards per rush (10.6) on read options This latter tool is particularly important when projecting Willis' fantasy impact in Miami. Since 2016, there have been 28 QBs with 100-plus rush attempts in a season, and 26 (93%) finished as a top-12 fantasy QB in fantasy points per game There's also at least some optimism that Bobby Slowik can rekindle some of his 2023 magic; he has spent the better part of the last 15 years working with Kyle Shanahan and Mike McDaniel after all. That said: Willis certainly doesn't check every box we look for. The Dolphins ' cheap/bad WR and TE rooms give them a good case as having the league's worst group of pass-catchers, and Vegas fully expects this offense to be one of the lowest-scoring groups in the league (29th). And yet, the re-draft price is cheap. There should be a weekly borderline QB1 floor here if the history of high-volume dual-threat QBs holds true. Fade these WR/TE busts. Updated on September 2, 2026 12:01AM EST Share By: Jim Coventry @jimcoventryNFL Updated on September 2, 2026 12:01AM EST Fantasy Football Busts Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Draft season rewards discipline, not headlines. Every year a handful of wide receivers and tight ends get bid up past what the tape and the target competition actually support, and this year's group of overpriced names has some big ones. Fantasy Football Busts 2026 None of the six players below are bad players. They are just priced for outcomes that require the tape, the target competition or their own recent history to cooperate, and I do not like those odds at their current cost. Jameson Williams, WR, Lions - ADP: 60.2 Jameson Williams turned in back-to-back solid seasons, going from a 58-catch, 1,001-yard, seven-touchdown campaign in 2024 to 65 catches for 1,117 yards and seven scores in 2025. That kind of steady growth usually earns a bump in draft rooms, and it has this draft season, but context matters more than the box score suggests. Sam LaPorta 's health did a lot of the heavy lifting last season. With LaPorta on the field, Williams' role shrank to a modest 4.3 targets and 10.2 PPR points per game. Once LaPorta went down, that number jumped to 7.9 targets and 18.4 points. Betting on Williams at this price means betting LaPorta gets hurt again. Williams also posted a drop rate among the worst of any starting wide receiver in 2025, and Detroit's offensive line took a hit this offseason when longtime left tackle Taylor Decker retired. If his replacement struggles protecting Jared Goff 's blind side, the deep shots that fuel Williams' ceiling get harder to complete. Bottom line: Fade Williams. Both of his big seasons had an outside factor propping them up, either a defense in freefall or an injury to the player ahead of him, and he's being drafted as if that production was entirely his own doing. I would rather bet on likely regression than pay this price. For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Davante Adams, WR, Rams - ADP: 50.4 Davante Adams found real chemistry with Matthew Stafford in their first year together, scoring 14 touchdowns despite Stafford missing most of training camp. That production kept his price respectable, but the underlying trend points the other way. Adams turns 34 in December and is coming off back-to-back seasons compromised by hamstring injuries. Even before the hamstring injury cost him time last year, his per game numbers had already slipped to 4.3 catches and 56 yards. Scheme is the bigger issue. The Rams went from 46 percent to 50 percent of snaps in 13 personnel after their Week 8 bye, a personnel package that squeezes Adams' snap share. If Stafford's 46-touchdown season regresses even slightly, Adams absorbs the hit directly. Bottom line: Fade Adams. He's a Hall of Fame talent, but betting on a receiver about to turn 34 with recent injury history, in an offense trending toward heavier personnel, does not make sense at his cost. Check out our Fantasy Football ADP Report for a comprehensive tool with live-updated ADP data for multiple league formats and sites. Mike Evans, WR, 49ers - ADP: 67.6 Mike Evans has scored at least 11 touchdowns in each of the last two full seasons, and touchdown production like that tends to keep a receiver's price propped up in fantasy drafts even as everything else about his profile ages. The everything else is the problem. Evans has missed 12 games in his last two seasons and ranks in the bottom-5 percent of the league in yards after catch. Before last year's injuries limited him, he averaged just 11.3 PPR points and 47 yards per game. He has already dealt with two injuries in August. Now he lands on a new team with a new quarterback in Brock Purdy and a new scheme built to create space for receivers rather than lean on the contested catch profile that is all Evans has left. Recent history for receivers his age changing teams and schemes does not favor a smooth transition. Bottom line: Fade Evans. I love him as a player, but Father Time and a scheme mismatch are already working against him. I am not paying a top-30 wide receiver price for one in decline. Brian Thomas, WR, Jaguars - ADP: 83.5 Brian Thomas looked like a foundational piece after an 87-catch, 1,282-yard, 10-touchdown debut. The follow-up season told a different story, with production collapsing to a 48-catch, 707-yard, two-touchdown line as target competition and a changing offense caught up to him. The bigger concern heading into 2026 is role. Jacksonville's staff seems settled on using Thomas primarily as an outside deep threat rather than having him run the full route tree, an approach that caps his weekly target count by design. That profile can produce big plays, but it does not produce the target floor a top wide receiver price requires. Travis Hunter could eat into Thomas' snaps, and the target competition that already ate into Thomas' role last year is not going away. Bottom line: Fade Thomas. A capped role by design plus real target competition is a bad combination at his current price. I would rather find that upside later in the draft. Kyle Pitts, TE, Falcons - ADP: 75.0 Kyle Pitts finally delivered the breakout last season everyone waited years for, catching 88 passes for 928 yards and five touchdowns, the first time he posted more than 53 catches and 667 yards since his rookie season in 2021. That leap shows up in the efficiency marks too, with Pitts ranking in the top 13 percent of tight ends in route efficiency and the top 6 percent in target volume at the position. The path back to that ceiling has real friction this year. Drake London still commands a significant share of the target pie, the quarterback competition between Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa is unresolved, and the passing scheme in Atlanta is not built to funnel high raw volume through any one weapon not named London or Bijan Robinson . Remember, Pitts had a massive chunk of his fantasy production when London was injured. Pitts was slightly above his career norms when London was healthy. None of that makes Pitts a bad player. It makes him a tight end whose price assumes last year's leap simply repeats, when the target competition and quarterback uncertainty argue for a steadier, more capped outcome. Bottom line: Fade Pitts. I would rather bank a cheaper floor at the position than pay for a repeat of last year's ceiling with this much target competition and offensive uncertainty in the way. Let him go a round later. Jake Ferguson, TE, Cowboys - ADP: 111.1 Jake Ferguson posted 82 receptions and eight touchdowns last year, both career highs. But his touchdown production says more about touchdown luck than a repeatable role, as his receiving scores have swung wildly since 2023, with five and zero the two years before last season. Ferguson ranks in the bottom 4 percent of tight ends in explosive play rate, his average depth of target sits at just 4.6 yards, and he did not record a single deep completion all season. His yards per reception have declined every year, from 10.7 to 8.4 to 7.3. The role split matters too. With CeeDee Lamb healthy, Ferguson's per game production drops to 7.0 PPR points, and he faded hard down the stretch, failing to top 20 receiving yards in any of his final four games. He is a clear third read behind Lamb and George Pickens when both are healthy. Bottom line: Fade Ferguson. Eight touchdowns on a bottom-of-the-league efficiency profile will not repeat, and he is a name-value pick riding a career year that his underlying numbers do not support. articles.excerpt: Rookie skipper Craig Albernaz hasn't shown he is up for this, and couldn't get out of his own way in a big spot against the lowly Rockies

articles.body: More Curious Managing Decisions Cost Orioles Dearly In Loss At Colorado Sep 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Baltimore Orioles pitcher Kyle Bradish (38) pitches in the first inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was nothing short of curious that Craig Albernaz would opt to give a 23-year old kid who had barely worked as a reliver in the minors his MLB debut in a 2-2 game in the worst pitching park in MLB, but also totally in character for him. Heâs performed like an overmatched puppet all season â the third handpicked novice baseball exec Mike Elias installed in eight years â and as the moments got bigger for the Orioles on this winning tear to potentially make something of their season, you just knew the skipper would come up small. Giving Luis DeLeon the 7th inning right after Baltimore tied the game was dubious enough. But he also chose not to keep Coby Mayoâs hot bat in the lineup, newly acquired $5M waiver claim Luis Robert Jr. play at all â the lineup came out ridiculously late, in hopes he might one assumes â and we got the return of Heston Kjerstad to the majors for the first time since June 2025 before weâd see Robert make his Orioles debut . Yeah, one is a lefty and the other is a righty â I get the match-ups of it all - but Albernaz didnât handle this like the playoff game it was, his suspect lineup came up short again and the Orioles lost, 4-2, to lowly Colorado at Coors Field. "We had a bunch of guys down because of the workload," Albernaz said, trying to explain why this kid got his debut in that spot. Of course, this being Albernaz, wonderfully out his depth, he couldn't even stick to his own story, again, as before the game he said of De Leon: "We're not going to ambush him and throw him in the fire right away." A victory would have taken them above .500 for the first time since April 14 and secured their second five-game win streak of the season, but Albernaz chose to get experimental instead. They fell to 69-70 and 1.5 games behind the Guardians for the final Wild Card spot. Kyle Bradish, staked to a $100M contract extension, continued to show obvious signs of having not pitched even 40 innings either of the last two years due to Tommy John surgery, and labored to escape five innings, and Elias better get serious about a six-man rotation NOW, Holliday Giveth And Taketh The Orioles barely scratched out two runs Monday in Colorado against a bad starter and horrible staff, needing Colton Cowserâs miracle catch to negate a game-winning homer. They were worse Tuesday against an even worse starter (Gabriel Hughes this time). They scored once Tuesday with Pete Alonso staying in a pickle long enough for a run to score. The other came off Jackson Hollidayâs bat, a solo homer to tie the game (he had three hits against the Rockies, one of his fatherâs former teams, after a great series start in St. Louis, where his dad, Matt, also starred). But Holliday dropped an absolutely routine pop up to start the seventh, with De Leon making his first pitches ever on an MLB mound and only recently converting to the pen in preparation for what he projects to here. Mickey Moniak wheeled all the way to second and two batters later TJ Rumfield hammered a center-cut slider for a two-run lead. The Oâs were lucky it wasnât worse and Bradish was lucky he was facing a bad team (Colorado snapped a 10-game losing streak at home). Bradish couldnât miss bats, again (8 swing and miss), and he couldnât throw enough strikes and he was pitching out of jams starting in the first inning. Albernaz left him out to dry last time out when he was clearly not right after consecutive walks and he needed 95 pitches to survive five innings here. Bradish threw 48 sinkers (more than half his total) and got a total of eight called strikes and whiffs with that pitch. That wonât play, and is troubling. "Battling command a little bit," is what Albernaz mustered, still probably not seeing Bradish's situation for what it is. Bradish isnât getting any ground balls (two in this game) and heâs allowed 47 hits inÂ 34 2/3 innings over his last seven starts, allowing five homers in that span. He has just 27 strikeouts in those starts and he and Brandon Young and Wednesdayâs starter, Trevor Rogers, are all showing serious signs of fatigue. articles.body: New Jersey Devils trade for Luke Evangelista | Flashscore.com All Football Transfer News Premier League US Open Features Champions League Darts Snooker Golf Cycling MLB NFL Most read on Flashscore News Deadline Day LIVE: Balogun decides against Everton move as Sunderland tie up Fofana Swedish tennis ace collapses twice on court during Challenger event in China Flashscore sources: Everton still keen on Grealish after Richarlison agreement Man City confirm joint British record signing of Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea New Jersey Devils acquire Luke Evangelista from Predators for draft picks Eric Himmelheber Nashville Predators' Luke Evangelista George Walker IV / CTK / AP The New Jersey Devils acquired forward Luke Evangelista from the Nashville Predators in exchange for a 2028 conditional first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. Evangelista , 24, has spent all four years of his NHL career with the Preds. The Toronto, Ontario, native is coming off a career season after posting 56 points with 12 goals and a career-high 44 assists, which shattered his previous best of 23. After being selected 42nd overall in the 2020 NHL Draft, Evangelista wouldn't make his debut until the 2022-2023 season, when he put up seven goals and eight assists in 24 games, putting together an average ice time of 16:34, which was almost a full three minutes more than the following two seasons. Despite averaging 13:57 of ice time in his second season, Evangelista put up what is still a career-high 16 goals, along with 23 assists, in 80 games. He would have a down season in 2024-2025 (10g, 22a) after missing four weeks with a lower-body injury, playing in 68 games, before bouncing back this past year. The Devils needed a top-six winger. Now Evangelista has a chance to help both the Devils and himself. The right wing playmaker is currently in the final year of his two-year, $6 million deal and is set to become a restricted free agent after this season. articles.title: Tiger Woods' Son Charlie Helps Benjamin Win American Heritage Invitational
articles.excerpt: Charlie Woods opens his senior season helping The Benjamin School win the American Heritage Golf Invitational as the Buccaneers chase another FHSAA Class 1A title.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Tiger Woods' Son Charlie Helps Benjamin Win American Heritage Invitational Charlie Woods, the son of Tiger Woods, is trying to help The Benjamin School pursue another Florida golf state championship | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect There are still plenty of rounds ahead for Charlie Woods, including those that will eventually take him from high school golf to Florida State. But his final season at Benjamin School has begun in a familiar place: with his team holding a trophy. Woods Helps the Buccaneers Open the Season with a Win Woods helped Benjamin win the American Heritage Golf Invitational in Plantation, Florida, as the Buccaneers opened another season with championship expectations. Woods and teammate Brooks Colton led Benjamin to the team title, an early marker for a program attempting to repeat as FHSAA Class 1A state champion. Woods and Colton tied for first, each shooting a 3-under par 69. The Son of Tiger Woods Has Long Endure the Spotlght For Woods, the tournament also represents the beginning of the last chapter of a high school career that has unfolded under considerably more attention than most. That comes with the last name. The son of 15-time major champion Tiger Woods has spent years playing junior tournaments and appearing alongside his father at the PNC Championship, where every swing can become a highlight and every result can become a headline. His senior season at Benjamin offers something slightly different. This is his team. His school. And one final opportunity to chase a state championship before college golf begins. Florida State Will Be His Next Stop Woods committed to Florida State last year, choosing the Seminoles as the next stop in a golf career that has been watched closely since long before he was old enough to drive himself to the course. Before Tallahassee, however, there is still work remaining with the Buccaneers. Benjamin captured the Class 1A state championship last fall â Woods carding a 4-under 68 in the final round â and he enters his senior year as one of the recognizable faces of a program attempting to do it again. The American Heritage Invitational is only an early-season tournament. It will not define Woods' senior year, and it certainly will not tell us what kind of golfer he will become at Florida State or beyond. But senior seasons are collections of lasts: last first tournament, last regular season, last run toward a state championship with the teammates who helped make high school feel like something more than a waiting room for whatever comes next. For Charlie Woods, the last first has already ended with a tournament win. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.body: Ipswich vs Liverpool Prediction, Lineups & Team News | RotoWire Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Prediction, Predicted Lineups & Team News Ipswich Town vs Liverpool prediction, predicted lineups, team news, injuries, odds and tactical analysis for Friday’s Premier League match at Portman Road. September 1, 2026 Share By: Adam Zdroik @RotoZdroik September 1, 2026 Game Previews Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Prediction, Predicted Lineups & Team News Ipswich Town host Liverpool at Portman Road on Friday night with the visitors still searching for their first Premier League win of the season. Liverpool have taken two points from two matches, but both required late rescue acts: a 99th-minute penalty at Newcastle and an 82nd-minute equalizer against Nottingham Forest. That is why our Ipswich Town vs Liverpool prediction leans toward a draw despite Liverpool entering as heavy favorites. Andoni Iraola's side have struggled to control games for long stretches, while Ipswich have scored in both league matches and already shown they can make bigger sides uncomfortable. Victor Munoz has been Liverpool's new difference-maker, producing the decisive moment in both games, and he is projected to start again Friday. Bradley Barcola is also available after completing his blockbuster move from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday, giving Iraola another option as Liverpool try to turn late recoveries into a complete performance. This preview covers predicted lineups injury news , head-to-head history, the tactical matchup and a score prediction for Friday's Premier League game in Suffolk. When & Where to Watch (USA) Friday, Sept. 4 at 8:00 PM BST / 3:00 PM ET / 12:00 PM PT Venue: Portman Road, Ipswich English TV: USA Network Streaming: Peacock, Fubo, Sling Blue, DirecTV Stream Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Lineups & Injury News Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Predicted Lineups Predicted lineups: Ipswich are projected to name the same XI that started at Old Trafford, though Emersonn is a genuine doubt after limping out of that game. Liverpool are projected in a 4-2-3-1 with Victor Munoz and Cody Gapko again starting on the wings, and Barcola available but not in the XI five days after signing. This widget updates automatically when official lineups drop. Ipswich Town IPS Liverpool LIV Predicted Predicted Ipswich Town Predicted Lineup not yet posted Check back closer to kickoff Liverpool Predicted Lineup not yet posted Check back closer to kickoff Confirmed Predicted Lineups via RotoWire Ipswich Town predicted starting XI (4-2-3-1): Kjell Scherpen Dara O'Shea Issa Diop Jacob Greaves Leif Davis Sasa Lukic Marcelino Nunez Abdul Fatawu Julio Enciso Daizen Maeda Emersonn Liverpool predicted starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson Jeremie Frimpong Jeremy Jacquet Virgil van Dijk Milos Kerkez Ryan Gravenberch Dominik Szoboszlai Victor Munoz Florian Wirtz Cody Gakpo Alexander Isak Check the Premier League injury table and the player news feed before kickoff because there are still some questions. Ipswich Town Team News & Injuries Emersonn is the one to watch. Ipswich's club-record striker scored on his Premier League debut against Sunderland, then jarred his knee in the first half at Old Trafford and came off. Gary O'Neil was hopeful rather than reassuring afterwards: "we're hopeful it's not serious. It was like a landing and a jarring of the knee." He also conceded "it could be anything at this stage." Chuba Akpom , who scored the consolation at Old Trafford, is the alternative. Jaden Philogene is out with an ankle problem into the middle of the month, which matters beyond his absence because he is second on Ipswich's penalty list. Azor Matusiwa and Jack Taylor are both unavailable, and Florentino Luis , the 16 million pound arrival from Burnley, is still a fitness concern. Exequiel Palacios is the newest option. Ipswich signed the Argentina midfielder from Bayer Leverkusen on Aug. 27 on a deal to 2030, and he is a World Cup winner, though the club were awaiting visa clearance when they announced him. Emersonn does not make it, Ipswich lose the only player who has scored a goal from open play for them this season and the shape becomes Akpom or nothing. Liverpool Team News & Injuries The headline is an arrival rather than an absence. Bradley Barcola completed a move from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday for 106 million pounds rising to 123 million, signing a five-year deal and taking the No. 29 shirt, and he was expected to train with the group before Friday. He is not in the projected XI, which makes his involvement the first real selection question Andoni Iraola has had to answer. Munoz is the other one. He replaced Ngumoha on 63 minutes at Newcastle and won the penalty that rescued a point in the 99th, then came on against Nottingham Forest and scored the equalizer in the 82nd. Iraola singled out his work off the ball: "Victor has played really well. Defensively and offensively he did a very good job and was always a threat." The injury list is long but stable. Conor Bradley is out after knee surgery and Giovanni Leoni is still working back from an ACL injury, so Frimpong covers right back. Hugo Ekitike is out until 2027 with a ruptured Achilles and Federico Chiesa has a back problem. Joe Gomez is closest to a return. Curtis Jones has gone, completing a move to Inter Milan. The XI therefore looks settled apart from one place, and the 106 million pound winger is sitting behind it. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Head-to-Head Record These clubs have met 74 times, with Liverpool winning 39 to Ipswich's 14 and 21 drawn. The relevant run is longer than most: Ipswich have not beaten Liverpool since Dec. 10, 2000, a nine-game winless stretch spanning nearly 26 years. Portman Road is worse. Liverpool are unbeaten in their last seven visits and have not lost a league game here since the 1985-86 season. The two meetings in Ipswich's last top-flight campaign both went Liverpool's way, 2-0 here in August 2024 in Ipswich's first top-flight match in 22 years, and 4-1 at Anfield in January 2025. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Tactical Analysis Liverpool are 13th with two points, and the way they got them is the reason this game is live. They trailed at Newcastle and needed a stoppage-time penalty, then trailed twice at home to Forest and equalized in the 82nd minute. The first-half numbers against Forest were alarming for a side at Anfield: 0.25 expected goals to 1.29, and no big chances to three. Iraola has not tried to dress it up. "We were quite passive without the ball," he said afterwards, and pointed out that both Forest goals came from throw-ins that Liverpool "didn't defend properly." His closing line was blunter still: "I hope this serves as a lesson for the future." He also has the strangest possible context for the job, because his Bournemouth side finished sixth last season, three points behind the Liverpool team whose manager he replaced. Liverpool finished fifth, sacked Arne Slot a year after winning the title, and lost Mohamed Salah Ibrahima Konate and Andrew Robertson on free transfers. Ipswich are 12th, a point above them, and their two games have been opposites. They beat Sunderland with seven new signings in the starting XI, then conceded five at Old Trafford after leading through Leif Davis . O'Neil's own diagnosis was about duration rather than quality: "we lost control of the momentum. How we respond for the last half-hour is what we need to get better at." That is the question Friday asks, because a promoted side leading Liverpool at home on a Friday night has to survive the last half-hour to get anything out of it. What Ipswich do have is a spine built from O'Neil's last job. He arrived from Strasbourg in June and Ipswich then signed two players from there, Julio Enciso for around 30 million pounds and Abdoul Ouattara for 17 million. Enciso has been their best player, setting up the move for the winner against Sunderland and looking lively at Old Trafford, and O'Neil has been unusually warm about him: "it's rare to find a player like him. He's desperate to help the team." Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Odds Liverpool are around -180 on the road and Ipswich are out past +400, with the draw near +340. For more markets and the rest of the matchweek, see RotoWire's soccer betting page and the best sportsbook promos Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Key Matchups Alexander Isak Issa Diop and Jacob Greaves Isak scored his first of the season against Forest and is the one Liverpool player whose finishing can settle a game like this without the rest of the performance being any good. Diop and Greaves kept Sunderland to a single goal and then had an afternoon at Old Trafford neither will want back, with Greaves putting through his own net off a Harry Maguire shot. The pairing defends the box reasonably well and struggles when it has to defend space, which is precisely what Isak wants. If Ipswich sit deep and compact he will have a quiet hour. If they push out to chase the game, he decides it. Julio Enciso Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai Enciso is the most likely source of anything Ipswich create, and Liverpool's double pivot is where Iraola says his team went passive. Gravenberch is one of the better ball-carrying midfielders in the league but Liverpool conceded both Forest goals from throw-ins, which is the sort of second-phase sloppiness a No. 10 with Enciso's close control punishes. Ipswich also have Marcelino Nunez and Sasa Lukic behind him rather than in front, so Enciso gets to play facing forward. Whoever wins that zone decides whether this is a Liverpool possession exercise or a genuinely awkward Friday night. Ipswich Town Corners & free kicks: Leif Davis Sasa Lukic Abdul Fatawu Marcelino Nunez Jack Clarke Penalties: Julio Enciso Jack Clarke Jaden Philogene Liverpool Corners & free kicks: Dominik Szoboszlai Cody Gakpo Florian Wirtz Alexis Mac Allister Penalties: Dominik Szoboszlai Alexander Isak Enciso could be Ipswich's main PK taker, though that information has yet to be revealed. Szoboszlai has already converted one for Liverpool this season, in the 99th minute at St James' Park. Ipswich Town vs Liverpool Prediction Liverpool are the better side, but they have not controlled either league match yet and Ipswich have scored in both of theirs. Portman Road on a Friday night is exactly the kind of game that can punish a side still searching for rhythm. If Emersonn misses out, Ipswich lose some punch, but Liverpool have yet to keep a clean sheet and I'm not ready to trust either defense. Score Prediction: Ipswich Town 2-2 Liverpool Upcoming Fixtures Ipswich travel to Crystal Palace on Sept. 12. Liverpool go to Bournemouth on Sept. 20, which is Iraola's first return to the club he left in June. articles.body: Indiana vs North Texas: How to Watch the Season Opener Brady Quinn welcomes fans during the BIg Noon Kickoff before the Indiana versus UCLA football game at Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect College Football is finally back, and the focus can shift from the courtroom to the field. Indiana Hoosiers fans will have their program spotlighted on national TV as FOX's Big Noon Kickoff game on Saturday against North Texas - after all, Indiana the defending national champion. How to Watch Indiana vs North Texas Who: No. 6 Miami (0-0) vs. North Texas (0-0) When: Saturday, Sept. 5, 12 p.m. ET Where: Bloomington, Indiana TV: FOX (Gus Johnson, Joel Klatt, Jenny Taft) Radio: IU Radio Network (Don Fischer and Buck Suhr) Series history: Tied 1-1 Last meeting: The Hoosiers and Mean Green have met twice in their histories. The last meeting came in 2014 when Kevin Wilson was guiding the Hoosiers and Nate Sudfeld threw for over 300 yards in a 49-24 win for Indiana. Last Time Out: Both teams will be playing their first game of the 2026 season. As good as Indiana has been, it hasn't started the first two seasons under Curt Cignetti like it might have wanted to - Indiana beat FIU 31-7 in the 2024 season opener, and 27-14 over Old Dominion last year. Indiana is coming off a 16-0 season that saw the Hoosiers raise the national championship trophy after defeating Miami 27-21. While many of the heroes from 2025 have moved on to the next level, there will be plenty of star power on the field. Indiana returns All-Americans on both sides of the ball, headlined by offensive lineman Carter Smith. While quarterback Josh Hoover is the new guy in town, he has over 9,000 passing yards and 71 touchdowns to his name. Hoover will have plenty of weapons to throw to as Charlie Becker returns and is joined by Nick Marsh and Tyler Morris. The running game has its weapons too, with Turbo Richard coming in from Boston College to join Khobie Martin and Lee Beebe Jr. The Indiana defense may be one of the best units in the country. Isaiah Jones and Rolijah Hardy man the middle of the defense while Tyrique Tucker heads up a strong defensive line unit. Playoff hero Jamari Sharpe returns to lock down opponents' top wide receivers. Indiana is riding a 15-game home winning streak and will see a sellout crowd fill the stands in Memorial Stadium for the fifth-straight home game. articles.title: Premier League transfer window grades: Ranking all 20 clubs on their summer business
articles.source_type: Fantasy Premier League news, predictions, player notes
articles.body: Premier League transfer window grades: Ranking all 20 clubs on their summer business - NBC Sports Skip navigation MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores Login Favorites Sign up to follow your favorites on all your devices. Sign up Odds by Premier League Videos The 2 Robbies Premier League transfer window grades: Ranking all 20 clubs on their summer business Joe Prince-Wright Joe Prince-Wright Published September 2, 2026 02:57 AM Facebook Twitter Email That was one of the wildest summer transfer windows in Premier League history and now that it’s over, let’s dish out some grades on who did the best business in a record-breaking window. MORE Every transfer deal for all 20 Premier League clubs It’s a real mixed bag out there as plenty of teams spent big, but quite a few are left with a weaker squad than at the start of the summer. Below we give a grade to each Premier League team based on their business and how well they’ve done with ins and outs. Arsenal: B+ In reality, they didn’t need to do much business this summer. Bringing in Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa to upgrade their midfield and defense respectively was magnificent, and Christos Tzolis looks like a bit of a bargain. Another forward option would have been nice but overall a very positive window as the reigning champions were able to move on some fringe players — Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus the most notable departures — to free up space for youngsters such as Max Dowman to shine. Jackson to Villa: Top Premier League highlights Watch Nicolas Jackson's best Premier League moments for Chelsea after he completed his move to Aston Villa. Aston Villa: C- Villa have just done one of the greatest dismantle-and-rebuild jobs in transfer window history. Unai Emery and the decision makers at Villa must be exhausted will have their fingers crossed that their decisions prove to be the right ones. Ollie Watkins, Emiliano Martinez, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Morgan Rogers all left as Villa brought in massive transfer fees for most. Villa have made their squad much younger, but that’s always a huge risk. New signings Ibrahim Mbaye, Nicolas Jackson, Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Zion Suzuki are all very good players, while Leon Goretzka will add quality and experience, but Villa’s transfer window probably went too far with the outgoings. Time will tell if this all works out but you can never underestimate Emery’s ability to improve players. Bournemouth: C- Bit of a strange window for Bournemouth who have the Europa League to deal with this season and haven’t really strengthened their squad. The main thing was keeping young talents Alex Scott, Junior Kroupi and Rayan, which was a big positive. Other than that, new manager Marco Rose may feel his squad is a little thin. Brentford: C+ What a sensible bunch the Bees are. Mamadou Sangare looks like a proper star in midfield as their recruitment model has done it again. Other than that, Brentford trimmed their squad but upgraded impressively in the wide areas with Malick Diouf and Jaidon Anthony fitting in perfectly to their style of play. No nonsense. Just savvy business. Brighton: B- Quite an overhaul, once again, for the Seagulls and you get the sense they may have sold a couple of experienced players too many this summer. Danny Welbeck, Joel Veltman, Jan Paul van Hecke and Carlos Baleba all leaving in the same window is a lot, but we should always trust their scouting network as it already seems to unearth a couple of gems with Luka Vuskovic (big money and big things expected) and Malick Yalcouye (on loan the last few years, but now ready to impress) being very good prospects. Chelsea: B+ Losing Enzo Fernandez right at the end of the window was a blow and Xabi Alonso will be frustrated Chelsea couldn’t bring Lamine Camara in. That said, Alonso got Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix in early, and Emiliano Martinez in late, and Chelsea’s squad looks very strong. Chelsea still have players who can ease the pressure on Moises Caicedo if he struggles with injuries. They look set for an outside title challenge with no European action to distract them. Lowe Down: Can Chelsea challenge Arsenal? Rebecca Lowe answers Robbie Earle's and Tim Howard's most pressing questions from Matchweek 2, including her thoughts on Chelsea's ability to challenge Arsenal for the title, what success looks like for Spurs, and more. Coventry City: D Just okay would be the summary if they hadn’t lost to Hull City at the weekend, but things are feeling a bit negative about Frank Lampard’s side right now. They brought in plenty of new players but nobody that really surprises you as a statement buy. Taiwo Awoniyi and Sidiki Cherif will get a few goals up top, but Coventry look set for a season of struggle. Crystal Palace: D- Really underwhelming window for new manager Pierre Sage, especially with the Europa League set to push their squad to the limits. Losing Daniel Muñoz was a blow, while keeping Adam Wharton was a big plus. The situation up top is intriguing with Jean-Philippe Mateta still around but seemingly far from happy. Overall, a poor window. Everton: C+ Folarin Balogun’s not happening late on is a huge blow as Beto left and now Everton are a player light up top. That is pretty much unheard of. Jack Grealish coming back on loan was a massive addition too, while Hayden Hackney is a solid player and Ainsley-Maitland Niles adds depth. But losing Iliman Ndiaye can’t be understated. Simply put, he was Everton’s best player for two seasons. Overall, David Moyes will feel like his squad isn’t stronger than it was at the start of the summer. That is never the aim and the Balogun debacle will leave a sour taste for a long time. Ndiaye to Man City: Top Premier League highlights Watch Iliman Ndiaye's best Premier League moments for Everton as he completes his move to Manchester City. Fulham: D- Alvaro Arbeloa has added some attacking talents he knows well from his time in Real Madrid’s youth setup in Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, while midfielder Shea Charles has excellent potential. A late flurry of deals strengthened them slightly. But it feels like Fulham have gone backwards this summer while a lot of other teams around them strengthened. Worrying times for the Cottagers. Hull City: B+ Overall, great business for a team which didn’t expect to be in the Premier League this season and already has six points on the board from two games. Nobel Mendy and Konstantinos Tzolakis look like great signings at center back and in goal respectively, while Mohamed-Ali Cho and Ilyas Ansah add some real quality and depth in attack. Hull had to bring in plenty of new players, and they did. Ipswich Town: B+ Basically, see above! Another promoted team which has done plenty of business this summer and they’ve done it really well (hoping to replicate “the Sunderland model” of last season). Gary O’Neil was appointed later in the summer, so it was a tough start to the window for the Tractor Boys but they’ve done really well. Julio Enciso, Abdul Fatawu, Daizen Maeda and Emersonn are a very good attacking quartet, and the addition of Argentina international Exequiel Palacios in midfield will be brilliant. Leeds: B Very solid summer as Daniel Farke trimmed his squad a little and added real quality in the form of Harry Wilson, James Trafford, Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic. There is a really good core group at Leeds, so they didn’t need to do much business. But what they did, they did well. The only question mark: will they ultimately need more cover for Dominic Calvert-Lewin up top? Liverpool: B- Bit of a strange summer overall. It took months to sign Bradley Barcola for huge money, but they got it done and that is a huge deal and he’s a top player. New manager Andoni Iraola might be concerned about a lack of options in midfield and defense, though. Still, Barcola and Victor Munoz add even more firepower to their attack and Jeremy Jacquet looks a real talent at center back and Ronald Araujo adds defensive cover. Liverpool's defense looked 'vulnerable' v. Forest Rebecca Lowe, Robbie Earle, and Tim Howard react to Liverpool's four-goal draw with Nottingham Forest in Matchweek 2, their second 2-2 draw to start the season. Manchester City: B+ In a summer where they lost incredible experience in Rodri, Bernardo Silva, Nathan Ake and John Stones, City went big to back new manager Enzo Maresca and they have a brand new midfield. Spending over $430 million on Elliot Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez (right at the deadline) is a massive statement, while Iliman Ndiaye and Allan add more creativity out wide. Overall, plenty of ins and outs as a new era begins and City’s squad is very strong while also bringing in a lot of money from selling fringe players. City showing no signs of slowing down this season The Generation xG crew detail Manchester City's setup under Enzo Maresca and praise the team for not showing any signs of regression without Pep Guardiola. Manchester United: C+ Midfield additions were key as Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos all arrived. Does that make them that much stronger? Perhaps, but it feels like some new defensive options were needed as well. Michael Carrick’s squad also has to contend with being back in the Champions League, which will push them to their limits. United feel a little light in numbers. Man United's quality shines in rout of Ipswich Rebecca Lowe, Robbie Earle, and Tim Howard share their thoughts on Manchester United's performance in a 5-2 victory over Ipswich Town in Matchweek 2. Newcastle United: B What a huge summer of change for Newcastle, but the early signs under new manager Matthias Jaissle look good. Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali moving on hurt, but Newcastle got huge money for them. They have added real talent in several areas and their squad arguably looks a lot stronger with Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez ready-made stars, and Matias Fernandez-Pardo a slightly longer-term play at $70 million. It’s still early days, but they recovered well in the window after a tough start. Jaissle 'perfect' for Newcastle with Wissa, Elanga Robbie Earle and Robbie Mustoe name Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle as the underappreciated performer of the week, highlighting how he has gotten the most out of his attacking pair of Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga. Nottingham Forest: C Just a very boring transfer window for Forest, which is very unusual for them! In all seriousness, they had a big squad and new manager Oliver Glasner has trimmed it well while adding quality in Daniel Munoz, Ousmane Diomande, Xaver Schlager and Liam Delap. Losing Elliot Anderson was obviously a blow, but they spent the money well and look solid. Sunderland: C+ Feels like they could have signed a few more players to help them cope with the grind of the Europa League, but a late flurry of deals boosted their grade. Kevin Danso is a really solid addition at center back. And both Malick Fofana and Dodi Lukebakio are huge talents out wide and will add extra cutting edge and creativity if those deals get over the line. Tottenham Hotspur: B A monster window for Spurs, but things will take some time to settle down under Roberto De Zerbi. Overall, they are stronger than at the start of the summer. Sandro Tonali, Jan Paul van Hecke, Savio, Omar Marmoush, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi are all good signings on paper. It did feel like they panicked a little with some of their moves towards the end when they weren’t able to move as many players on as they would have liked, plus the fees they accepted for Cristian Romero and Djed Spence felt low. Anyway, a

articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Terry Francona Deserves Plenty of Credit for Key Decision in Redsâ Win Aug 30, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Cincinnati Reds manager Terry Francona (77) makes a pitching change against the Chicago Cubs during the sixth inning at Wrigley Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Reds picked up a big win over the San Diego Padres on Tuesday night, and manager Terry Francona deserves plenty of credit for one decision that paid off at a huge moment. With Jose Trevino due up with the bases loaded and Tyler Stephenson available off the bench, Francona elected to stick with Trevino rather than turn to his starting catcher as a pinch-hitter. The decision worked. Trevino laced a line drive up the middle to give the Reds a 3-2 lead before Juan Brito followed with an RBI single. After the game, Francona explained his decision to stick with Trevino in that situation. "I just know he can get to velocity," Francona said of Trevino . "That guy for them was throwing 98, 99. I also know he could hit into a double play, but we had Steve-o behind him if he didn't drive him in, but he had a really good at-bat and so did Brito." The numbers show exactly why. The Numbers Back Francona Up Aug 30, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Cincinnati Reds manager Terry Francona (77) makes a pitching change against the Chicago Cubs during the sixth inning at Wrigley Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trevino entered the night hitting .269 against pitches 95 mph or faster this season with an impressive .615 slugging percentage. For comparison, big-league hitters are batting .240 with a .376 slugging percentage against 95-plus mph pitches. That means Trevino isn't simply good against velocity compared to his Reds teammates. He has been significantly better than the league as a whole. Stephenson, who was on deck and going to pinch-hit if Trevino got out, has also handled velocity well, batting .299 with a .494 slugging percentage against pitches of at least 95 mph. But Francona trusted Trevino, and it paid off. Itâs notable because the Reds have struggled as a team against velocity. Matt McLain (.132 AVG/.276 SLG), TJ Friedl (.115/.197), Eugenio SuÃ¡rez (.170/.264), Ke'Bryan Hayes (.195/.317) and Spencer Steer (.172/.264) are among the Reds hitters who have struggled against pitches of at least 95 mph this season Francona had a specific reason for sticking with Trevino in such a huge spot, and it was one the average fan would have never known. The numbers backed up his thinking, and ultimately, so did the result. It was a small decision that ended up making a big difference in the Redsâ win. Follow me on X at @RedsDaily4 for more. articles.body: West Virginiaâs Depth Chart Leaves Plenty to be Decided West Virginia University tight end Ryan Ward | Christopher Hall â West Virginia on SI West Virginia University head coach Rich Rodriguez released the depth chart on Tuesday evening, although the two-deep is not finalized. âThere's some âORsâ on there,â stated Rodriguez. Players can push the competition into the season, or it could be the case no one separated themselves among the position group. Rodriguez is hopeful the competition has continued. âI think, mostly it's in a good way. If you have an âorâ because you're not sure either one of them are ready to do that, that makes it a little bit not so good,â he said. âBut I think most of our ORâs, and probably all of them, are because we feel good about multiple guys at those positions.â Among the starters, there are two âORsâ on offense, three on defense and three among the specialists. The starting quarterback has been highly anticipated and Pete Nakos of On3 reported on Friday that Oklahoma transfer Mike Hawkins Jr. will be the starter for the Mountaineers. Nonetheless, the depth chart for the season opener against Coastal Carolina has an OR between returning starter Scotty Fox Jr. and Hawkins. The tight end room dealt with injuries during fall camp, and it appears junior Ryan Ward and freshman Kade Bush will share the duties in week one. Defensively, the competition continues on the outside with edge rushers, Coastal Carolina transfer, Zeke Durham-Campbell and JUCO transfer Darius Wiley, and at WILL, between Cam Torbor and Ashton Woods, while free safeties JUCO transfer Andrew Powdrell and freshman Matt Sieg will overlook the secondary. Kickoff duties may linger into week two if there are not enough opportunities, but entering in year two, Nate Flowers is battling Western Kentucky transfer Jack Cassidy, while Troy transfer receiver DJ Epps and freshman safety Matt Seig The biggest surprise is along the offensive line. Returning starting center and Rimington Award Watch nominee Landon Livingston currently sits behind Wes King. âMy challenge to the guys in spring ball and then five weeks ago or four weeks ago when camp started was, âdon't be concerned where you're at in the depth chart. Just show that you're good enough to win with, that we can play you and not be nervous that it diminishes our chances to have successâ. So, I think they've done that,â Rodriguez said. âI didn't see guys worried about who's first or second out there.âYou hope. West Virginia welcomed over 80 new Mountaineers to the program in the offseason, which provides a little more anxiety than maybe a typical season opener. âA little more anxious because we have so many new guys that even though a lot of them have played some college football, they haven't played in this system.â Rodriguez said. âSo, that's probably adding to the anxiety a little bit, but I'm anxious for those guys.â âThey've worked hard,â he added. âWe got a hard week coming up and get ready and we'll see what we have.â WVU Depth Chart OFFENSE QB: Mike Hawkins OR Scotty Fox Jr., Jyron Hughley OR Max Brown RB: Cam Cook, Amari Latimer, Chris Talley, Martavious Boswell WR (X): Jaden Bray, TaRon Francis, Landon Drumm WR (SL): DJ Epps, Cyrus Traugh, Armoni Bomar-Weaver WR (Z): John Neider, Cyrus Traugh, Keon Hutchins TE: Josh Sapp OR Ryan Ward, Kade Bush OR Cam Ball LT: Kevin Brown, Malik Agbo, Deshawn Woods LG: Nick Krahe, Lamarcus Dillard Wes King, Josh Aisosa RG: Bubba Grayson, Cam Griffin RT: Carsten Casady, Aidan Woods DEFENSE EDGE: Zeke Durham-Campbell OR Darius Wiley, Emerson Joy DT: Corey McIntyre Jr., KJ Henson OR Yendor Mack NT: Nate Gabriel, Will LeBlanc, Taylor Brown BAN: Harper Holloman, David Afogho, Tobi Haastrup OR Jeremiah Johnson WILL: Cam Torbor OR Ashton Woods MIKE: Ben Cutter, Tyler Stolsky OR Isaiah Patterson N/S: Geimere Latimer, Miles Khatri CB: Chams Diagne, Keyshawn Robinson CB: Nick Taylor, Jaire Rawlison FS: Andrew Powdrell OR Matt Sieg BS: Kamari Wilson, Da'Mare Williams OR Kameron Reddic SPECIAL TEAMS Jack Cassidy OR Nate Flower KO: Nate Flower, Jack Cassidy Bryan Hansen, Mack Flynn Bryan Hansen, Mack Flynn LS: Macguire Moss, Kaden Seller KR: DJ Epps OR Matt Sieg PR: DJ Epps OR Matt Sieg Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.body: USC Coach Lincoln Riley Address Coliseum Attendance Controversy Southern California Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley celebrates with fans after the game against the UCLA Bruins at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Coach Lincoln Riley spent the first day of September getting his USC Trojans prepared for a short week. USC received three days to gameplan against an upset-minded Fresno State Bulldogs team once the 2026 schedule came out. Now the Bulldogs are on the mind of Riley and the Trojans three days after rolling past San Jose State. Aug 29, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley during the game against the San Jose State Spartans at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Turns out USC's theme song is on the mind of the Bulldogs, though. Fresno State blared the famed fight song through the speakers during its own practice session. All to prepare for the Trojans. Meanwhile, here's everything Riley said following USC's first game week preparation for the primetime showdown set for Sept. 4. Lincoln Riley Gets Honest About Attendance Criticism "I mean, this is USC. People are going to pay attention to this program. They're going to have an opinion. It's part of being a blue blood school." "I don't buy into the false narrative. I think that comes from a lot of people who don't follow our program. And most of those have never stepped foot inside the coliseum." "During my years here, attendance has gone up every single year. As has our play inside the Coliseum including running the table last year in front of a lot of epic atmospheres. I expect that to happen this year." Gary Patterson Still Not Content About USC Defensive Performance USC Trojans defensive coordinator Gary Patterson | USC Trojans on SI "I mean, for three quarters it was really, really good. Definitely some things to impove on [though]." "But played really good down there for awhile. I thought the guys flew around, we communicated and we pretty much eliminated the run game and made some plays on the ball." "It's a different style game compared to what we're going to play in this league [the Big Ten]. I thought we came out and started faster defensively." Lincoln Riley on Playing Younger Defenders Aug 29, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) drops back for a pass second quarter against the San JosÃ© State Spartans at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "I think at the end of the game, we committed ourselves that there were a few guys that if we got the game in hand, we were going to play [them] and we stuck to that. Which I'm glad we did because it was good for those guys to get reps." "We had a couple of guys who handled it well. But we had a couple of guys who didn't handle it well as we could have. We had more bust in the fourth quarter than we had in the entire game combined. And we had some opportunities to make some competitive plays, [including] picking off a couple of balls that we didn't make." "And also, give them credit [the Spartans]. They made some wacky plays and made some good plays on the scramble. They made a couple of incredible plays on the ball." Lincoln Riley on Relationship with Matt Entz Dec 27, 2025; Tucson, AZ, USA; Fresno State Bulldogs head coach Matt Entz against the Miami (OH) RedHawks during the Snoop Dogg Arizona Bowl at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "We have a good relationship. Him and his wife Brenda are great people. That was great to have him with us for that year. It was also great to have another head coach in the room." "He did a great job here. Sad to see him go but happy for him to get the opportunity at Fresno. Seems like it's a good fit for him. He's a really good football coach and took over a proud program that has a lot of great history and tradition in the way they play. So yeah, a lot of respect for him." "That's one of those schools that, other than the week we're playing them, we all root for around here. You know, I hope they win every other game except this one." Lincoln Riley on Play of USC Safeties Nov 15, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans cornerback Alex Graham (27) safety Christian Pierce (24) cornerback Decarlos Nicholson (17) and safety Kennedy Urlacher (28) celebrate after Iowa Hawkeyes turn the ball over on fourth down during the second half at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "Starters played pretty well. I mean, I though A.G. [Alex Graham], Prophet [Brown] and Christian Pierce all did a nice job and handled the calls. And I thought we tackled well and did a pretty nice job in coverage." "We had a couple of things we need to clean up on. But that group was pretty sharp." "Then everybody else had good plays, but their bad plays showed up more. And that's obviously what you've got to live at. I mean, Maddie [cornerback Madden Riordan ], K.U. [Kennedy Urlacher], some of the different guys we played there at the end all had some really good plays. But they had a couple of plays that hurt us too. So need a couple of those guys to play sharper." Riley on Physicality of USC to Start Season Aug 29, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans running back Waymond Jordan (2) carries the ball against the San Jose State Spartans in the first half at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "I would say I like the physicality. I thought we reset the line of scrimmage a lot." "If you looked at the tape and saw the line of scrimmage, it was moving. I thought there were a few times in the perimeter and box that we weren't as clean as we needed to be." "The backs ran hard, but we did miss a couple of cuts we felt like that we left out there. I think the biggest thing is we had some chances for some explosive runs. We were pretty steady in the run game but would love to pop a couple [of explosives] in there. We'll need to do a better job of that." Riley on Luke Wafle's Debut Aug 29, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley reacts against the San Jose State Spartans in the first half at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "My expectations are really high for him. He's proof that he can be a really outstanding player at a young age. At least throughout fall camp, that's what we've seen." "The thing I love about Luke is that he's an every down style player. A lof of freshmen come out and either they're pretty decent against the run but maybe have a lot of development to do in the pass rush, or vice versa." "Luke is advanced at both, both physically and in knowledge. And he's just going to get better and better." "But the thing I liked the most about him was he didn't hesitate. He went in there and played aggressive, was around the football and around the quarterback. And he was really close to making a bunch of others. And again, I think that's just scratching the surface of how good this guy can be for years to come." On Jayden Maiava's Poise in Front of Riley Aug 29, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) throws the ball against the San Jose State Spartans at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "He was pretty sharp. He had one read that he really wants back." "But other than, he took care of the ball. They obviously came in with the game plan to try to make him not make throws all the time and make him more patient. Earlier times in his career, he wouldn't have liked that so much." "But he did a good job staying patient and steady, especially playing like 37 freshman. I don't think that's ever happened here. I started thinking back in all my years I never started one. But Jayden trusting those guys was what he did best." and , and for the latest news. Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... articles.title: How The NC State Newcomers Performed Against Virginia
articles.excerpt: NC State welcomed new additions to the team this season. We’ll take a look back to see which newcomers stood out on Saturday.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: How The NC State Newcomers Performed Against Virginia Aug 29, 2026; Charlottesville, Virginia, USA; North Carolina State Wolfpack linebacker LaCorian Hodge (35) and linebacker Harvey Dyson III (5) sack Virginia Cavaliers quarterback Beau Pribula (7) during the second quarter of the game against the Virginia Cavaliers at Scott Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the Wolfpack struggled as a unit against Virginia, a few players made their NC State debuts last Saturday.Â Weâll check in on a few newcomers who contributed in Week 0 and whose names youâll be seeing more of this season. Â Special Teams: Jackson Waller, PÂ We begin with Special Teams since this unit was the busiest on Saturday, including Jackson Waller (P), who punted 7 times for an average of 46.7 yards.Â He booted three that were over 50 yards while dropping another 3 inside Virginiaâs 20-yard line.Â Waller was a highly decorated punter coming out of high school. He transferred into NC State this season from Arkansas State. Waller has a nice boot. As a starter for the Red Wolves, 19 of his 59 kicks were inside the 20-yard line last season. Waller has an opportunity to quickly develop into a fan favorite if the State offense continues to flounder. Special Teams: Victor Snow, PR Snow completed 2 returns against Virginia for 32 yards. His longest run was for 29 yards.Â Snowâs an experienced punt returner from his time at Buffalo. In his junior season, he led the MAC with an average of 14.5 yards per return.Â Special Teams: King Mack, KR King Mackâs opening 32-yard return was one of the more exciting aspects of this game for NC State. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of the only exciting parts of this game.Â Mack only made 2 returns in the game. His 54 all-purpose yards led the team.Â While at Penn State, he averaged 28 yards per return last season.Â Itâs early, but Mack showed flashes of explosiveness when he had the ball. Donât be surprised if he returns one or two kicks to the end zone this season. Â Offense: Victor Snow, WR Itâs not flashy, but Victor Snow caught 1 pass for 5 yards against Virginia. Once Snow and Bailey get on the same page this season, it will spell trouble for most secondaries.Â Snow spent three seasons with Buffalo, where he was the teamâs second-leading receiver last season (815 yards).Â Snowâs greatest attribute is that heâs an endzone magnet. He led the entire Buffalo offense with 10 touchdowns in 2025.Â Offense: Davion Dozier, WR Dozier caught 2 passes against Virginia for 14 yards. His longest reception was for 14 yards.Â Dozier played with Appalachian State last season and was one of the teamâs leading receivers. Â He hauled in 30 passes for 448 yards and five touchdowns for the Mountaineers.Â Defense: King Mack, SÂ Mackâs 7 tackles tied for 2nd most on the team. Heâs got a high motor, and itâll be fun to see how he continues developing while on this defense.Â Defense: Harvey Dyson III, LB He tallied 5 tackles, 1 solo, a half-sack, and 1 tackle for loss. State fans hope that Dyson III brings his game-wrecking ability to NC State. He led the American Conference with 8 sacks in 2025. He also ranked in the top three in the conference for forced fumbles (2) and tackles for loss (12).Â Aug 29, 2026; Charlottesville, Virginia, USA; North Carolina State Wolfpack linebacker Harvey Dyson III (5) during the second quarter during the game against the Virginia Cavaliers at Scott Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Defense: Popo Aguirre, LB Aguirre logged a career-high in tackles on Saturday (18). In his postgame comments, Aguirre said heâs ready to get back to the lab and get better as a team. âDefinitely not the outcome we wanted,â Aguirre said. âBut I believe in Coach Doeren, believe in Coach Eliot, and what we got going on.âÂ Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations...
