He impressed at youth level, earning Arsenal’s 2021/22 Scholar of the Year award, and enjoyed four loan spells away from the Emirates Stadium, firstly in League One with Lincoln City that season. The 2022/23 campaign saw him make a combined 41 Championship outings across stints with Rotherham United and Coventry City, helping the Sky Blues reach the play-off final. Norton-Cuffy made another 40 second-tier appearances for Millwall in 2023/24 before leaving Arsenal permanently for Genoa in August 2024. articles.excerpt: In this blog, we take a look at the Ideal FPL GW3 Wildcard team, Drafts, and the Players to Target in your Gameweek 3 Wildcard team. The post FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts – Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target appeared first on ALLABOUTFPL: Your one stop place for all FPL tips, FPL captain picks, FPL news, FPL players, previews, reviews,differential picks, analysis and weekly updates. .

articles.body: FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts - Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target Skip To Content Trending Now FPL GW3 Midfielders FPL GW3 Free Hit cons of gw3 wildcard pros of gw3 wildcard fpl gameweek 3 wildcard FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts – Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target FPL GW3 Ultimate Guide and Tips FPL Wildcard FPL Wildcard Drafts Game week Preview Wildcard September 1, 2026 September 1, 2026 allaboutfpl FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts – Pros, Cons, Tips and Players to Target GW3 has emerged as a popular Gameweek to wildcard amongst FPL managers due to a variety of reasons. Bruno or No Bruno? Palmer now or Palmer Later? Lots of questions to answer. In this blog, we look at the Pros and cons of the FPL GW3 Wildcard, the Ideal FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts, and the Players to target in your Gameweek 3 Wildcard team. Link to all our FPL GW3 blogs including scout picks, players to target, buy, hold, sell analysis, differentials, captaincy metrics, best forwards, and more. Completely free to access as well! FPL GW3 Wildcard Guide Pros & Cons of Wildcarding in FPL GW3: Pros of GW3 Wildcard: Projections from Fantasy Football Hub Get Haaland in ahead of COV(H) and long term if you started with No Haaland in GW1. Attack Teams with Good Fixture runs and have cheap assets like Newcastle(Wissa, Elanga, Hall, Dedic) and Brighton(De Cuyper, Verbruggen, Gross) Catch good price changes(Eg. Konsa) who might be a starter now or even later at just 4.4 million. Cons of GW3 Wildcard: Chelsea and Arsenal play each other and it will be a really difficult match to call with respect to Goals and Clean sheets. You will want to have Double Arsenal defense and Double Chelsea attack long term but it will be a trickier call to take in GW3 on who to bench/start. You will be up against managers who are likely to have Haaland as Triple Captain vs COV(H). You can’t use more than one chip in a single Gameweek. Wildcard might be needed later for other fixture swings- Like GW6 or around GW15 as highlighted in our Chip Strategy article. Bruno or No-Bruno, Palmer or No Palmer will be a tough decision to make. Bruno has had an absolutely massive 23 points in GW2 vs Ipswich, courtesy of 3 goals and 1 Assist. But there is an argument that can be made to not captain Bruno Fernandes in the next 5-6 weeks and switch between Palmer and Haaland. No Bruno- Captaincy Ticker: GW3- Haaland vs COV(H) GW4- Palmer vs HUL(H) GW5- Haaland vs SUN(H) GW6- Palmer vs BOU(H) GW7- Haaland vs IPS(H) GW8- Haaland vs AVL(A)/Palmer vs TOT(H) The other alternative is to wait out a week and Wildcard in GW4 after Chelsea and Arsenal have played each other. Here are some of the Pros of a GW3 Wildcard vs Pros of a GW4 Wildcard. GW3 Wildcard vs GW4 Wildcard: GW3 Wildcard GW4 Wildcard Helps you target Manchester City assets ahead of COV(H). Works better in case of no Haaland in GW1 Helps you skip the Chelsea vs Arsenal fixture in GW3 and target them full-fledged in GW4 on Wildcard. Triple up on both Chelsea (Attack) and Arsenal (Likely defense) without them facing each other. Can catch lots of Price Changes(City assets, Arsenal defenders) One more week of information regarding assets that are tricky with minutes in the long term, like Konsa, De Cuyper, Dedic, etc. Good entry points for teams like Man City, Brentford Better Entry points for Teams like Chelsea, Newcastle, Brighton, and Better Exit points for Man United, Liverpool This is how a GW4 Wildcard Draft would look like. FPL GW4 Wildcard Draft: Players to Target on FPL GW3 Wildcard: Goalkeepers: Raya, Verbruggen, Hornicek Defenders: Calafiori, Konsa, Gabriel, De Cuyper, Hall, Thiaw, Dedic, Ajer, Egan, Thomas, Muharemovic, Canvot, Andersen, Castagne, Tarkowski Midfielders: Bruno Fernandes, Palmer, Rogers, Cherki, Mbeumo, Foden, Szoboszlai, Wirtz, Elanga, Gross, Dewsbury Hall, Sangare, Slater Forwards: Haaland, Pedro, Wissa, Calvert-Lewin Fantasy Football Hub(FFHUB) Fantasy Football Hub is a high-quality FPL website offering a wide range of FPL content, tools, data, planners, and more. Memberships are available for the 2026/27 season at a 50% discount along with a win-your-mini-league or get-your-money-back guarantee T&C Applicable (Click on the image above to claim the offer) FPL GW3 Wildcard Drafts FPL GW3 Wildcard Draft 1 with Bruno Fernandes This is a Template GW3 Wildcard Draft covering all the bases- Haaland, Pedro, Bruno, Palmer, Szoboszlai, Wissa, and Double Arsenal defense. Goal Keeper and Defenders: Verbruggen is the Budget GK with a good run of fixtures. Calafiori picks himself with 2 assists and 2 clean sheets and is the next nailed defender in the Arsenal lineup after Gabriel. He is also 2.5 million cheaper than Gabriel, which makes him an easy lock. Konsa is the second Arsenal defender. At just 4.4 million, you have to take up that risk to get an Arsenal defender. He should be first choice in the long term and can play both CB and RB. With Mosquera injured(Watch out for PC updates), He could be in for a start as soon as GW3. Ajer and Hall are two of the total 4 defenders who have hit DEFCON in both games. Ajer is always good for DEFCON when he plays at CB, and Hall also carries an excellent attacking threat(with a good run of fixtures from GW4). Brentford and Newcastle defenders also rotate really well, as seen below. Dedic is also looking really good with 🅰️🅰️🅰️ in 3 games. And just for £4.5. Livramento is back in training, though, but according to Newcastle fans, Livra doesn’t walk in directly, and Dedic is likely to keep starting games at least in the short-medium run. Midfielders: Palmer is an easy lock in most of the GW3 Wildcard Drafts(unless on GW4 Free Hit). Chelsea Bruno Fernandes is coming on the back of 23 points haul courtesy of 3 goals and an assist in GW2 vs Ipswich. He is in red-hot form and has multiple routes to points. Pascal Gross and Szoboszlai are midfielders who have multiple routes to points- penalties, Set Pieces, and DEFCON. On top of it, they also have a good fixture run. Slater is the 4.5 Midfielder enabler in this draft who is a starter for Hull and is also on set pieces. Forwards: Haaland and Joao Pedro pick themselves in every Wildcard Draft. Wissa also should be a lock according to me, as Newcastle have a good run of fixtures playing HUL(H), COV(A) in GW5 and GW6. Calvert-Lewin is also another option to consider if you want a set-and-forget option. Isak is a good shout with good fixtures in GW3 and GW4, but it is a difficult price point to swap later on, and he hasn’t shown much to warrant a gamble. FPL GW3 Wildcard Draft 2 with No Bruno Fernandes This is a Draft with No Bruno Fernandes with Mbeumo coming in as the Manchester United cover . The money is used to upgrade and get Cherki as well ahead of COV(H). Cherki got 2 brilliant goals vs Palace in GW2 and is the man in form. De Cuyper(4.6) also comes into this draft with Brighton suffering more injuries and De Cuyper continuing to play as LW. He has already got a goal and an assist in the first 2 games. In this draft, Cherki to Foden is also an option, and that will allow you to upgrade Hall/Muharemovic to Calafiori, completing the elite Arsenal defense triple-up. Sangare and Muharemovic are 2 other DEFCON beasts and are easy long-term options irrespective of fixtures. Sangare has hit DEFCON in both games so far, while Muharemovic has hit DEFCON in one game and averaged more than 10 DEFCON/game in Serie A last season. This is not a very ideal scenario as they play each other in GW3 but could work out well long-term. Anderson comes in as the cheaper alternative to Cherki, and the funds are used in a defence upgrade with O’Reilly coming in as another Premium Defender ahead of COV(H). He has been playing midfield for City so far and could easily get a 15-16 pointer in any of the games. articles.title: Hull City complete Iroegbunam signing
articles.excerpt: Hull City are delighted to announce the signing of defensive midfielder Tim Iroegbunam from Everton for an undisclosed fee. The 23-year-old has penned a five-year deal with the Tigers until the summer of 2031. Birmingham-born Iroegbunam has made 60 appearances in the Premier League – 48 for Everton and 12 for Aston Villa, where he began his senior career after joining from West Bromwich Albion’s academy. Handed his debut in a 2-0 win at Brighton & Hove Albion in February 2022, he spent the 2022/23 season on loan at Queens Park Rangers, scoring twice in 32 Championship matches. The midfielder helped Villa secure a fourth-place finish and reach the Conference League semi-finals in 2023/24, playing five games in Europe, before leaving that summer for Everton in a £9m deal. He made 21 outings in his maiden year with the Toffees and featured in 29 of their 38 Premier League fixtures last term, including 17 starts. The former England youth international was part of the Young Lions team that won the European Under-19 Championship in 2022, making 13 appearances across the Under-19 and Under-20 age groups. articles.title: Ndiaye Leaves Everton
articles.excerpt: Everton can confirm Iliman Ndiaye has signed for Manchester City on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee. The Senegalese winger joins Enzo Maresca’s side after two years with the Toffees, featuring 74 times across all competitions and scoring 17 goals. Signed from Marseille in July 2024, Ndiaye made history by becoming the last-ever goalscorer for an Everton Men’s player at Goodison Park when he struck twice in the Blues’ 2-0 victory over Southampton in May 2025. He again entered his name into the Club’s illustrious history at the start of last season, netting the first goal for Everton at Hill Dickinson Stadium during the Toffees’ 2-0 win against Brighton & Hove Albion. Ndiaye – a Senegal international who featured at this summer’s FIFA World Cup – played 32 times for Everton in the Premier League during 2025/26, recording six goals and three assists. The Club thanks Iliman for his contributions to Everton across the past two years and wishes him success for the future.

This brings us to today's goal: Six bigger-picture takeaways from preseason that may or may not ultimately matter, but hey, there's no football this week, and I found them interesting, so maybe you will too! Thanks to TruMedia and PFF for all referenced statistics. As always: It's a great day to be great. Use code "IAN35" for 35 percent off a RotoWire subscription. Preseason Trend No. 1: The Mike McDaniel Impact is REAL in Los Angeles Mike McDaniel's ability to largely get the most out of Tua Tagovailoa and the Dolphins over the years has made him a bit of a rock star in the play-caller streets. One of his key schematic principles was the use of pre-snap shift/motion as well as play-action: He easily ranked first in both of these metrics during the 2022-2025 seasons . The other teams near the top of the leaderboard ( Lions Rams 49ers Packers Chiefs ) reflect the reality that offenses consistently clicking these "easy buttons" are among the most well-schemed groups in the league. Well, at least based on our three preseason data points, it sure looks like McDaniel's Los Angeles hasn't fallen far from the tree. This is true for pre-snap shift/motion 2025 Chargers: 64.3 percent motion - 18th 2026 preseason: 83.8 percent - 1st … as well as play-action rate 2025 Chargers: 25.1 percent - 17th 2026 preseason: 36.6 percent - 2nd Hell, we also saw McDaniel REALLY lean into outside size (56.1%, 1st) relative to what the Chargers did last season (17.6%, 29th), and Los Angeles also emerged as a leader in multi-TE formations (37.1%, 4th) just one year removed from ranking 31st in percentage of plays with two or more tight ends on the field. Now, none of this is guaranteed to produce a juggernaut offense — especially if the offensive line (again) struggles to overcome injuries — but hey, it's certainly a good start! I'm holding firm on my bold prediction that the Chargers finish as the league's No. 1 scoring offense this season, and have accordingly loaded up on their fantasy-relevant talents of most shapes and sizes throughout draft season. For up-to-the-minute updates on injuries, news and everything going on around the NFL, head to RotoWire's NFL Fantasy Football News Today or follow @RotoWireNFL on X. Preseason Trend No. 2: The Raiders are MOVING People on the Line of Scrimmage This one is admittedly a bit more performance-based, but an improvement from the Raiders' big uglies up front does profile as relevant considering just how dire things were last season. I'm also more inclined to put some extra attention on these numbers considering each of the team's starting five offensive linemen played 30-plus snaps this August. Anyway: We saw a pretty big improvement here in the pass blocking department. Raiders pressure rate allowed: 2025: 37.8 percent - 30th 2026 preseason: 28.6 percent - T-9th And ESPECIALLY in run blocking. Raiders RB rush yards before contact per carry: 2025: 0.61 - 31st 2026 preseason: 1.66 - 3rd Overall, Klint Kubiak's squad joined the Seahawks, Cowboys and Chiefs as the only teams to rank top-10 in both of these categories this preseason. The Raiders' devotion to running plenty of multi-TE sets (43.4%, 3rd most) could help explain why. Here's to hoping Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is healthy enough to take advantage of this come Week 1! Check out our Fantasy Football ADP Report for a comprehensive tool with live-updated ADP data for multiple league formats and sites. Preseason Trend No. 3: This Commanders Offense Didn't Look Great! Particularly on the line of scrimmage: Washington ranked 21st in both pressure rate and RB yards before contact per rush in the preseason. The former was even more concerning considering the Commanders allowed the third-fastest time-to-pressure of any offense. Reminder: LT Laremy Tunsil (triceps, IR) is expected to miss a significant portion of the season. RotoWire offensive line rankings have this group ranked just 27th coming into the season. We only saw Jayden Daniels take two dropbacks in preseason … and they resulted in two pressures and a sack. There were two additional data points that I didn't love from this group: Washington had an NFL-low 30.3 percent pass play rate on first downs this preseason. Last in the league by a whopping 7.5 percentage points. Not great! The Commanders only had a 20.6 percent play-action rate (24th). That's a pretty big decrease (-9.2%) from last season when they ranked sixth. This is all even more concerning when we've had beat reporters be VERY open about the offense's lackluster performance during training camp. Here's to hoping Jayden Daniels is ready to put his Superman cape on — he's going to need to shoulder plenty of the load here for this offense to re-reach 2024 heights if the preseason is any indication of what we should expect from this offensive line and scheme. Use RotoWire's interactive Mock Draft Simulator to prepare for every scenario in your 2026 fantasy football drafts. Preseason Trend No. 4: Death, Taxes, Brian Daboll not using Pre-Snap Shift/Motion Maybe the Titans were truly just keeping things vanilla in preseason. Beat reporters said they saw more pre-snap movement in training camp. Then again, it's not like this August's scheme looks too different from what Daboll has always done over the years. While he has generally increased his pre-snap window dressing come September, this has still been a pretty stale offense relative to the rest of the league. Brian Daboll pre-snap shift/motion: 2026 preseason: 18.8 percent - 32nd 2025 Giants: 46.4 percent - 32nd 2022-2025 regular season Giants: 49.3 percent - 29th 2022-2025 preseason Giants: 29.7 percent - 29th The team's inability to get No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate a single reception, or Cam Ward a completion thrown 10-plus yards downfield, also doesn't add a ton of confidence to the idea that this group is ready to hit the ground running. Here's hoping Daboll and company are ready to open things up come Week 1! Get ready for your draft by visiting our Custom Fantasy Football Rankings for a list of the top players for the season ahead, customized for your league. Preseason Trend No. 5: Finally Some Play-Action in Cincy? The Bengals' offense has obviously been nothing short of awesome with a healthy Joe Burrow over the years, but there has been a rather startling lack of play-action usage. Consider: The Bengals rank 31st in play-action rate (19.5%) since drafting Burrow first overall in 2020, and they were last in 2025 (17.2%). But then something funny happened this preseason: coach Zac Taylor had the boys embracing some play action for once! Overall, the Bengals' 34.9 percent play-action rate was good for fourth highest in the preseason … though we did see them also post a top-5 mark last August (28.7%, 5th). Still, I'm at least somewhat optimistic here based on the fact that Burrow specifically utilized *three* under-center, play-action dropbacks during his seven dropbacks (43%). Quite the increase from what we saw throughout last season (24 total, 8.3% of dropbacks)! We'll check back in on this trend in October and see if Taylor and company actually stick with it this time around. Preseason Trend No. 6: Matt Nagy and the Giants did Some Good Things! Specifically, Nagy leaned into the very pre-snap shift/motion that Daboll never did. Giants pre-snap shift/motion: 2026 preseason : 54.9 percent - 10th 2022-2025 regular seasons : 49.3 percent - 29th 2022-2025 preseasons : 29.7 percent - 29th Additionally, the offensive line played pretty great on its way to allowing a minuscule 21.2 percent pressure rate — good for the second lowest of preseason! That's quite an improvement over what we saw during the 2022-2025 regular seasons (40.1%, 32nd) and preseasons (34.7%, 29th) alike. Similar to the Raiders: There's at least some extra reason for optimism with this sticking considering all key members (other than stud LT Andrew Thomas ) got a decent bit of run this preseason. articles.body: Who Should I Draft: Travis Etienne vs Cam Skattebo | RotoWire Who Should I Draft: Travis Etienne vs. Cam Skattebo (2026 Fantasy Football) Should you draft Travis Etienne or Cam Skattebo? Projections are tight but I really like the upside of Skattebo and here's why. Updated on September 1, 2026 4:23PM EST Share By: Tyler Huntington @tylerhuntington Updated on September 1, 2026 4:23PM EST Who Should I Draft? Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. Two backs, projected within three points of each other, going within a couple picks of each other in the fourth round of most fantasy football drafts. This is as even as the widget gets - Etienne at 203 half-PPR points, Skattebo at 206 - so the tiebreakers are the whole story, and they point somewhere the projection total doesn't. All half-PPR below. The scoring section matters a little here, because one of these guys catches meaningfully more passes. Travis Etienne Fantasy Outlook vs ADP: RB19 Etienne is the steady vet in this pair, and the projection reflects a real workhorse role: 203 half-PPR points on 226 carries for 1070 yards and seven scores. He even holds a razor-thin edge in total projection and floor, so if your instinct is 'give me the established guy with the known workload,' Etienne rewards it. Alvin Kamara is already expected to miss time in 2026 so the newest New Orleans Saint is locked and loaded for a full time role. The issue is what happens above the median. His 249 point ceiling is nearly 40 points below Skattebo's, because his profile is volume-forward and grounded - lots of carries, modest passing-game work (34 catches), not a lot of week-winning spike. He's a solid RB2 whose best weeks look like everyone else's good weeks. In a vacuum that's a perfectly good pick. Very close floor projection, but it isn't an edge - it's noise, and it's the only row Etienne clearly wins, aside from ADP. Very close floor projection, but it isn't an edge - it's noise, and it's the only row Etienne clearly wins, aside from ADP. Bottom Line: A dead-even projection with a workhorse's carry count, but the lower ceiling and less receiving juice. The safe half of a coin flip. Cam Skattebo Fantasy Outlook vs ADP: RB18 Skattebo is coming off a brutal leg injury, and normally I'm the one waving people off the guys that are riddled with injury histories - but the numbers here earn it. Same projection as Etienne to within a rounding error, and a ceiling of 288 that towers nearly 40 points above him. That gap is built on passing-game work and big plays. Pass-catching backs carry the highest ceilings in fantasy because the receptions stack on top of the rushing floor, and in a modern offense that usage is exactly what turns a fine RB2 into a league-winner. The tool hands Skattebo the coin-flip edge on that ceiling, and he's going a hair earlier than Etienne to boot. He's a risk, and the week-to-week can wobble. But the receiving role is the tell, and it's pointing up. Bottom Line: The same projection with a 40-point-higher ceiling and more pass-game work. The tie-breaking upside is real. Travis Etienne vs Cam Skattebo: The Verdict The tool below has these two in a dead heat on projection - scroll to the ceiling and receiving rows to see what breaks the tie. The tool calls it a coin flip and gives Skattebo the nod on ceiling, and I'm coming down the same way: Skattebo is my pick. When two backs project dead even, I take the one with the pass-catching role, because those catches are both the safer floor and the higher ceiling - it's the profile that wins you a week and rarely craters. Etienne is the pick if you'd rather have the vet's known workload and you're allergic to variance, and I understand the impulse at an even projection. But 'even projection, way higher ceiling, more receptions, going a touch earlier' is four boxes, and Skattebo checks the ones that decide close calls. What flips me: a training-camp signal that Skattebo's receiving role is smaller than projected. Strip the pass-game edge and this reverts to the vet. As long as those targets are real, take the ceiling. Best Ceiling: Cam Skattebo - 295.8, nearly 60 points clear Best Floor: Travis Etienne - by a hair, part of a near-tie Receiving Edge: Cam Skattebo Most Proven Workload: Travis Etienne My Pick: Cam Skattebo Travis Etienne or Cam Skattebo PPR Scoring Skattebo's receiving edge means full PPR widens his lead and makes this pick more comfortable. Standard scoring strips the reception points and pulls the two nearly even on their almost-identical rushing lines - close enough that Etienne's proven role becomes a fair tiebreak. So: Skattebo in half and full PPR. In a standard league, it's a genuine coin flip and I wouldn't argue with the vet. Fantasy Football Tools Everything you need to dominate your draft, in one place. articles.body: 'I know this is the perfect fit' - Ndiaye completes £65m move to Man City Skip to content Football News Premier League News ‘I know this is the perfect fit’ – Ndiaye completes £65m move to Man City City have swelled their attacking ranks on deadline day. Nicholas McGee Last Update: 36 minutes ago 2 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Manchester City have completed the signing of Senegal winger Iliman Ndiaye from Everton Ndiaye has made the move to the Etihad Stadium on a five-year deal after City agreed a £65million with the Merseyside club. The 26-year-old was at one point set to join Tottenham, with Spurs striker Richarlison going the other way. But City swooped in after that transfer fell through, with Ndiaye delighted to have the chance to prove himself for Enzo Maresca’s side after excelling in his time with Everton. “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this,” he told City’s official website “City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up. “To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands. “It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good. “I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit. “City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.” Ndiaye scored 17 goals and provided four assists for Everton after joining from Marseille in 2024. He could make his debut when City host Coventry City this weekend, having won each of their opening two games. Topics Everton F.C. Manchester City F.C. Stay updated on key player injuries and how they impact fantasy football lineups each week. September 1, 2026 Share By: Jeff Stotts @InStreetClothes September 1, 2026 Injury Analysis Mock Draft Simulator Prep for your 2026 Fantasy Football draft with free, unlimited drafts, and real-time grades. NFL teams have trimmed down their rosters to 53 players, with injuries and health influencing countless decisions around the league. For the first in-season NFL injury report, understanding transactional terms used in the process can be beneficial on draft day especially for opportunistic fantasy managers able to draft a player at a discounted rate. The first thing to understand for is the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With training camp over the Active/PUP list is no longer available to teams. Instead, franchises must now utilize the Reserve/PUP list for these designated players. Players placed on the Reserve/PUP do not count toward the team's 53-man roster and cannot appear in the team's first four regular season contests. This season, players can participate in a 21-day practice period while still stashed on the Reserve/PUP list after the team has played in two regular season games. This allows medical teams to better evaluate players in anticipation of their return following the team's fourth game played. If the player is not activated to the 53-man roster during this window, they must sit out the remainder of the year. Notable players starting the year on the Reserve/PUP include Green Bay's Micah Parsons and Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet . Receiver Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list late last week and is hoping to be ready for Week 1 after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. For the first in-season NFL injury report, understanding transactional terms used in the process can be beneficial on draft day especially for opportunistic fantasy managers able to draft a player at a discounted rate. The first thing to understand for is the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list. With training camp over the Active/PUP list is no longer available to teams. Instead, franchises must now utilize the Reserve/PUP list for these designated players. Players placed on the Reserve/PUP do not count toward the team's 53-man roster and cannot appear in the team's first four regular season contests. This season, players can participate in a 21-day practice period while still stashed on the Reserve/PUP list after the team has played in two regular season games. This allows medical teams to better evaluate players in anticipation of their return following the team's fourth game played. If the player is not activated to the 53-man roster during this window, they must sit out the remainder of the year. Notable players starting the year on the Reserve/PUP include Green Bay's Micah Parsons and Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet . Receiver Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list late last week and is hoping to be ready for Week 1 after undergoing offseason ankle surgery. If a player is ineligible for the PUP list but becomes injured, teams must now consider using the injured reserve (IR). Like the PUP list, any player placed on the IR must miss a minimum of four weeks. A player can only return from an IR designation twice a season, and each team is granted a total of eight IR-to-return designations for the year. The number grows to 10 if they make the playoffs. Like the PUP list, these players can utilize a three-week window to ramp up their activity level. At the conclusion of the 21 days, the player must be activated, placed on season-ending IR, or be released or traded. Several big names were allotted IR designations entering the regular season including James Conner Tank Dell Jordyn Tyson and Christian Kirk IR and PUP list designations may be frustrating, but it does provide a degree of clarity regarding a player's status. Once a player is placed on either list, those willing to invest in him know they will have to proceed without the individual for at least four weeks. The use of the IR can also be used as a good indicator of the health of another player on the team's roster. For example, Conner's designation in Arizona suggests the team feels good about Jeremiyah Love 's availability for Week 1. The rookie running back is working his way back from a high-ankle sprain suffered August 13 but is "progressing really well" according to head coach Mike LaFleur. Turf Burns Emeka Egbuka : The second-year wide receiver has been sidelined since August 12 when he suffered a toe sprain in practice. Toe sprains, particularly those involving the big toe, can be extremely limiting, especially for wideouts. The big toe is crucial in driving the foot off the ground when running or jumping while also withstanding the high amount of stress that comes with weight bearing. Egbuka's Week 1 availability remains in doubt, and I'm moving him down my draft board just a bit. Puka Nacua : The Rams wideout has been limited by soreness in a specific muscle in his core. Nacua's injury involves the psoas muscle. The psoas sits just under the ribs at the lower spine. Its fibers run down through the pelvis, anchoring to the upper femur. It merges with another muscle, the iliacus, to form the iliopsoas, one of the primary hip flexors. Based on this location, a psoas injury can result in pain in the lower back, groin or hip, and be very limiting. Fortunately, Nacua was able to return to practice Sunday, and it looks like he will avoid any missed time. Look for the Rams to handle him conservatively in the days leading up to Week 1. Luther Burden : In Chicago, Burden is recovering from a groin injury sustained in the early days of training camp. The timeline suggests Burden's injury was a more moderate strain. He has resumed limited practice, and the team is optimistic he will be in uniform for Week 1. Chris Olave : Given Olave's checkered NFL injury history, his fans had to hate seeing him leave practice early last week. The team relayed he simply had the wind knocked out of him and it opted to be cautious with his care. He was back at practice the next day and remains the top target in New Orleans. Wan'Dale Robinson : The Titans receiver appears to have avoided a concussion after taking a hard hit in a joint practice with the Bears . The medical staff will monitor his status for any late developing signs or symptoms, but for now he appears okay. Zach Charbonnet : We know Charbonnet will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season as he recovers from the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear sustained in postseason. The timing of his injury made a Week 1 return unlikely, and an exact target date remains uncertain. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to start for Seattle with George Holani also set for carries. If Price runs well, the Seahawks could opt for an even more cautious approach with Charbonnet's care to ensure his long-term health. As a result, Charbonnet's fantasy value seems tied to the success of Price. Patrick Mahomes : The former MVP avoided the IR and is on track to start Week 1. As discussed last week, quarterbacks are one of the positions best poised to return to a high level of play following an ACL tear, and I'm bullish on Mahomes entering the year. He may not put up the same numbers he did when he first burst onto the scene, but he remains a reliable fantasy quarterback with a high ceiling. An early season bye in Week 5 should also help him better navigate his comeback. Draft Pass The Draft Pass unlocks this article and every draft tool we build. articles.title: Patterson Signs For Torino
articles.excerpt: Nathan Patterson has left Everton, signing for Serie A club Torino on a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee. The 24-year-old full-back joined the Blues from Rangers in January 2022, playing 68 times for the Club across all competitions. Patterson made his Toffees debut in an FA Cup fifth-round victory over Boreham Wood in March 2022, and the following year, played 19 Premier League matches in his first full season on Merseyside. A highlight of that campaign arrived when the young Scot started in Everton’s emphatic 5-1 victory at Brighton & Hove Albion in May 2023, when Patterson excellently tamed tricky winger Kaoru Mitoma. On the international stage, the defender helped Scotland qualify for this summer’s 2026 FIFA World Cup finals, where he earned caps against Haiti, Morocco and Brazil. Everyone at Everton thanks Nathan for his commitment to the Club across the past four-and-a-half years and wishes him all the best for the next step in his career.

articles.title: Ryan Poles Defines Bears' Trade of Gervon Dexter as Ideal Timing
articles.excerpt: The Bears GM has learned how to get rid of drafted players who may not fit, and getting back something in return made trading their defensive tackle possible.
articles.source_type: Gameweek squads, team news round-ups, deadline reminders
articles.body: Ryan Poles Defines Bears' Trade of Gervon Dexter as Ideal Timing Shedeur Sanders pulls away ffrom Gervon Dexter but falls for a sack last year at Soldier Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The confluence of several factors made it possible for GM Ryan Poles to trade defensive tackle Gervon Dexter for a fifth-round pick and cornerback Clark Phillips III. The major one was obviously defensive tackles Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving making huge statements, but it's obvious the Bears had no intention of paying a big contract in the future for Dexter, who has only flashed his talent at times throughout three seasons. "That deal was more about timing than anything," Poles said Tuesday during his annual post-preseason state-of-the-team address. "Timing and fit. "You know we had some young guys really pushing that came in this year with Jordan and Loving. They did a really good job, and we felt like it was a good fit as we moved forward." Final thoughts on the Gervon Dexter trade. The Gervon Dexter trade was about Dexter the rookies just made it easier. Dexter wanted an extension. Chicago didnât want to pay him, solid pass rusher. Not great vs the run. His 44.0 PFF run D grade ranked 107th/134 IDL. For aâ¦ pic.twitter.com/2Pe0Eny0I5 â Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) September 1, 2026 The timing in this case was the Bears owed Dexter a huge deal by next year and at this point felt they could afford to lose a player chosen in Round 2 because they're looking at using lower-priced, promising players this year. The money in the future will be needed for something important, like an extension for quarterback Caleb Williams. Also, the trade now could bring back a little more than a trade at the deadline, and maybe a lot less then if Dexter had been injured. Confident in current group None of that would matter if the Bears GM and coach Ben Johnson thought they lacked the defensive tackles to shut down the run or rush from the interior. They are convinced about both van den Berg and Loving, but also the veteran group including Grady Jarrett, Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street. Also, they have added back veteran defensive tackle James Lynch to the roster, for now, at least. Ryan Poles said the Gervon Dexter trade was largely due to Jordan van den Berg and Jayden Loving looking great in camp. pic.twitter.com/owVDoIztDw â Caleb Williams Fan Club (@CalebFC18) September 1, 2026 "I have a ton of confidence in those guys," Poles said. "They did a good job this preseason. I still think itâs a unit thatâs going to have to work together, whether itâs our blitz packages or the twists and games that we play. Those guys bring it, they have really good motors and they have the skillset to get into the backfield and get some pressure on the quarterback, and the defense is going to have to play as one unit. Thatâs important." As for the trade itself, Poles admitted he has gained the ability dump off parts who may not fit or who failed. In this case, that's Dexter. Still, it doesn't say much for the GM when they've been dumping off draft picks after a year or two. "I think I've been pretty quick to, if there's something that doesn't work out, I think we are pretty good about being honest about that and moving on," Poles said. "I don't think we are an organization, or I'm a GM, that's going to hold on just because it was a draft pick or a trade that you made and now I have to make it work and we are just going to keep that player here when it's not working. That will hurt the team. "I think I mentioned before that the locker room always knows. So we hold true to that. We want to put the best group together regardless of how they are acquired." In Ryan Polesâ first 4 years (2020-2024) heâs had 16 picks from 2nd-5th round Thereâs 7 on the roster at this moment Kyler Gordon Braxton Jones Roschon Johnson Tyrique Stevenson Noah Sewell Austin Boooker Tory Taylor Name one thatâs even an average starter or healthy #Bears â Jake (@Jake_B30) August 30, 2026 It's obvious Phillips was a throw-in on the deal from the way Poles talked about the cornerback addition. He couldn't classify him as a fit for a specific spot. "Most of his tape in Atlanta was outside (as opposed to slot)," Poles said. "In college, he was inside. I liked what that tape looked like, too. Heâs capable of both, but since heâs been in the league, heâs been outside. So weâll see where we start him off and go from there..â Phillips could get a look at slot The obvious need right now is at slot cornerback. The Bears are going with rookie Malik Muhammad, another player who has been outside for the most part. Poles even mentioned they have given safety Xavier Woods a look there and also Cam Lewis and Wrookie safety Dillon Thieneman for a few downs. "I really love this guy as a player. I don't know how anybody can look at this and see any sort of downside" - @adamrank on Clark Phillips #thesickpodcast pic.twitter.com/VS4NdA9rEf â The Sick Podcast with Adam Rank (@sickpodadamrank) September 1, 2026 What he's certain of is they don't have starter Kyler Gordon for now, as he works through his injury. Through the trade, the defensive line has shaped up. Health is returning, although Poles can't yet say defensive end Austin Booker will be available for Week 1 or when defensive tackle/end Shemar Turner will be back from knee surgery. Turner is in the later stages of his rehab, though, Poles added. The defensive line has been labeled a weakness throughout the offseason and losing a veteran player with talent can't be construed as a victory for this season. What the Bears have to hope now is they have benefited in the long run by giving two younger players a chance for playing time earlier in a rotation than they might have had, as they mix with one of the NFC's less impressive veteran tackle groups. While the Bears have been working on cutting down the roster to 53 players, I watched some film on cornerback Clark Phillips III. Here are some clips from his Week 18 performance against the Panthers in the 2024 season. 1 vs 1 against Xavier Legette. pic.twitter.com/TVhR9VXtRe â Nicholas Moreano (@NicholasMoreano) August 30, 2026 Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Loading recommendations... He covered the Bears as a beat writer for Suburban Chicago Newspapers, the Daily Southtown, Copley News Service and has been a contributor for the Daily Herald, the Associated Press, Bear Report, CBS Sports.com and The Sporting News. articles.body: Arsenal: Deal to sign next Kvaratskhelia secured by man who unearthed PSG star Arsenal have signed the next Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Arsenal have agreed a deal to sign Georgian playmaker Andria Bartishvili – the next Khvicha Kvaratshkelia – with the man who unearthed the now-Paris Saint-Germain star key to the transfer. The Gunners have made a habit of signing youngsters who they think can become stars this summer. So far, they’ve landed Igor Tyjon from Blackburn, Vincent Joseph from Liverpool, Axel Donczew from Cardiff, Elijah Upson from Tottenham, and Mylo Bernard from Crystal Palace. They will also see Ecuadorian twins Edwin and Holger Quintero and Irish midfielder Victor Ozhianvuna join when they turn 18. And their latest signing will also do the same, joining from Kolkheti 1913. The Athletic Arsenal correspondent James McNicholas reports the Gunners have secured the services of 17-year-old Georgian playmaker Bartishvili. The young Georgian is already being labelled the next Kvaratskhelia, after the PSG superstar, and there is a strong link between the compatriots. Per McNicholas, the pursuit at Arsenal has been led by the assistant to sporting director Andrea Berta, Mauricio Micheli. The now-Arsenal man was the scout at Napoli who is credited with helping to identify Kvaratskhelia when he joined the Italian club from Dinamo Batumi in 2022. The winger went on to win Serie A with Napoli twice before making a big move to PSG, where he’s now a two-time European champion. Arsenal will hope that Bartishvili can have a similar impact for them to what his compatriot has had for the clubs he’s played for since leaving Georgia himself. Andria Bartishvili confirms Arsenal news Barthishvili himself has confirmed the news of his transfer on social media. Posting on his Instagram story, he said: “A very big thank you to everyone for the congratulations.” The 17-year-old is on loan with Iberia 1999 until December. There, he has two goals and three assists in 24 appearances. He will join Arsenal in 2027, when he has turned 18. It’s likely that he’ll play in the academy side to start with, or be sent on loan to another senior side, before being introduced into the Arsenal senior side at some juncture beyond that. articles.title: Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1?
articles.excerpt: Alex Hunter analyzes the Vikings' backfield of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones heading into Week 1 of the NFL season. The post Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings’ No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: Is Jordan Mason or Aaron Jones the Vikings' No. 1 RB heading into Week 1? Once again, it’s a debate on who will be the lead back for the Vikings this season between Mason and Jones. Jones sits atop the depth chart, but will the 31-year-old actually be the RB1 over the 27-year-old Mason heading into the regular season? First off, let’s look at how these backs were used and performed last season. Last Season Jones has always been one of the most efficient rushers in the league during his career, but he slowed down in his ninth season in 2025, averaging a career-worst 4.2 YPC. Mason was more effective at 4.8 YPC, but this was also a career-low for the 27-year-old. Despite Mason being more productive on the ground, Jones held an edge in rushing usage. In the 11 games these two backs played together, Jones out carried Mason 105-85. However, Mason was trusted more in the red zone, outcarrying Jones 15-10 in that area. As a result, Mason rushed for six touchdowns while Jones only found the paydirt twice with his legs. In the passing game, Jones was the unquestioned primary receiving back over Mason. Jones saw 33 targets on 175 routes, whereas Mason only saw eight targets on 65 routes. Overall, Jones outsnapped Mason 331-207. As you can see, when both these backs were healthy last season, Jones was the lead back in every department, outside of red zone rushing, but will this continue this season? Week 1 Outlook After being the lead back last season, Jones drew the start in the lone preseason game that he and Mason both were active for this summer. That being said, these two backs usage was nearly identical. Jones saw three carries and one target on five snaps while Mason saw three carries on four snaps. Albeit a preseason game, this may be an indicator that Jones and Mason are going to split the rushing workload pretty evenly this season, which makes sense, after Mason was the more productive rusher a year ago. If Mason will see more carries, it’s hard to imagine he doesn’t retain his role as the primary rusher in the red zone, giving him more touchdown equity over Jones. Although, Jones should continue to be the main pass catching back for this offense, given the major difference in their receiving usage last season and simply because Jones has always been a reliable pass catcher throughout his career, compared to Mason, who has never done much in this department. This should once again be a two-man backfield with positive game scripts favoring Mason and negative game scripts favoring Jones. For next Sunday’s regular season opener vs. the Packers, the Vikings are a 1.5-point home favorite on DraftKings Sportsbook . This is an optimal setup for Mason to produce. Minnesota will likely want to rely on their run game if they get ahead and while it likely won’t be by much, Mason should finish this game with more touches, even if Jones technically gets the start. Make no mistake, though, this backfield will be tough to predict on a weekly basis when both Mason and Jones are healthy, and even if Mason begins 2026 with a better performance in Week 1, that doesn’t mean he is the Vikings’ RB1 for the season. articles.title: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons
articles.excerpt: Keagan Smith takes a look at the Atlanta Falcons' win total for the 2026 NFL regular season and breaks down the best bet for the over/under. The post 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons appeared first on DraftKings Network .
articles.source_type: Captain picks ranked with reasoning, gameweek rankings, DFS targets
articles.body: 2026 NFL Win Total Prediction, Pick: Atlanta Falcons Mediocrity has been a consistent theme for the Atlanta Falcons in recent years. For the first time in a while, though, the team knocked the hiring of a head coach out of the park and could be positioned to turn things around. There are plenty of standout pieces on offense, but the quarterback and the defense do remain more uncertain when evaluating team success. Now, the question is whether Kevin Stefanski will live up to his status as a two-time Coach of the Year winner. Here’s a look at the Falcons’ win total over/under for the 2026-27 NFL season with a top betting pick. Atlanta Falcons 2026 win total, best bet When the Falcons hired Kevin Stefanski as the franchise’s new head coach, there was plenty to be excited about. The two-time Coach of the Year kept the Cleveland Browns relevant for several years even despite operating with his hands tied at times, and he’s well-regarded as one of the NFL’s better names in terms of the coaching hierarchy. Giving him Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts had, and still has, many fans salivating. It’s tough to not get excited, but then you consider the rest of the context surrounding this team. The quarterback play is a massive unknown. Incumbent starter Michael Penix Jr. didn’t live up to expectations in the pros before tearing his ACL again, so how he fares coming off the injury is anyone’s guess. The team signed former Miami Dolphin Tua Tagovailoa to compete for the starting job, but his limitations are known and his preseason performance was one for the ages – not in a good way, either. When some fans are clamoring for an UDFA like Jack Strand, it says a lot about the situation under center. Then there’s the defense. Atlanta has been relatively pedestrian in that regard over the last few years, ranking 15th in yards per game (326.6) and 19th in points per game allowed (23.6) last season. While the Falcons’ pass rush was excellent with a franchise-record 57 sacks in 2025, two key EDGE talents are facing shortened campaigns – Jalon Walker tore an ACL and will miss the full season while James Pearce Jr. will serve an eight-game suspension to begin 2026. The club signed help in the front seven, adding Za’Darius Smith, Christian Harris and Samson Ebukam at linebacker while trading for defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Jr.; losing a combined 16 sacks between Walker and Pearce is tough, though. On the back end, A.J. Terrell and Jessie Bates reprise their roles as the top to players in the secondary. Drafting Avieon Terrell, the brother of A.J., also brings a high-upside pick into the mix. There’s room for this unit to improve this year, especially with Stefanski in the mix and Jeff Ulbrich retained at defensive coordinator. They’ll just have to prove it while overcoming the loss of Walker and weathering the storm of Pearce’s suspension. RELATED 2026 Fantasy Football Rankings: Top 160 players for PPR drafts and redraft leagues DraftKings Sportsbook lists the Falcons’ over/under total at 7.5 wins, with the under favored at -140 odds and the over at +120. Atlanta does see the benefit of playing in a weak NFC South, so that’s a bit of a boost in terms of the win total. No team in this division was above .500 last season, with all three of the Carolina Panthers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Falcons finishing 8-9. The New Orleans Saints also went 6-11 last year. There’s not a strong case for improvement from Carolina, but it’s fairly easy to see a world where both Tampa Bay and New Orleans wind up with a winning record. Due to that weak division, the Falcons do have the fourth-easiest schedule in 2026 based on opponents’ 2025 winning percentage (0.465). That certainly sets the team up to play competitive football, but the question is twofold – can they trust either of these quarterbacks, and can the defense stay afloat without two of its top talents on the edge. Those tasks may be easier said than done. Assuming the Saints and Bucs get back to winning games in the NFC South, the Falcons should stay under this win total of 7.5 in 2026. articles.title: Beto Departs Everton
articles.excerpt: Everton can confirm Beto has left the Club to join Serie A side Fiorentina on a permanent transfer for an undisclosed fee. The 28-year-old striker – who signed for Everton in August 2023 – played 113 times across all competitions for the Toffees, netting 25 goals and proving a popular figure with Evertonians. After signing from Udinese three years ago, Beto scored on his Blues debut against Doncaster Rovers in the Carabao Cup. His first of 20 Premier League goals arrived in December 2023, striking against Newcastle United in a memorable 3-0 victory at Goodison Park. In February 2025, Beto – a Guinea Bissau international – opened the scoring in Goodison’s last-ever Men’s Merseyside derby – a dramatic 2-2 draw on an iconic night under the lights at the Grand Old Lady. Everyone connected with Everton thanks Beto for his dedication, commitment and service throughout his time at the Club and wishes him all the best for the next chapter of his career in Italy.

articles.body: Milwaukee Brewers vs. Chicago Cubs prediction, pick for Tuesday 9/1/26 The Cubs (78-60) took care of business in dominant fashion on Monday. Chicago racked up 17 runs and a whopping nine homers during a blowout win over the Brewers (85-53). Milwaukee, responsible for the best record in baseball, will be eager to turn the page on Tuesday. Can the visitors even up this series tonight at Wrigley Field? The Cubs are favorites (-123) over the Brewers; the over/under is set at ten runs . Below, I’ve laid out my preview, prediction, and best bet for Tuesday’s showdown between Milwaukee and Chicago on DraftKings Sportsbook Brewers vs. Cubs pick, best bet today Cubs ML (-123) : Chicago, fresh off of Monday’s rout, looks the part of a World Series contender. It’s difficult to envision baseball’s highest-scoring offense slowing down tonight at home against a middling arm such as Gasser. Brewers vs. Cubs prediction, preview Robert Gasser will get the nod this evening for the visitors. Over 82.1 innings of work (15 starts), the right-hander has notched a 4.59 ERA, 1.30 WHIP and 78 strikeouts (8.5 K/9). Despite middling numbers, the 27-year-old isn’t a complete pushover on the mound. He’s allowed three earned runs or less in six of his last seven appearances. Still, it’s difficult to get too excited when it comes to Gasser’s chances tonight. He ranks inside the 40th percentile or worse in xERA (4.22), xBA (.253), chase rate (29.4%) and ground ball rate (32.8%). That last statistic could prove consequential on Tuesday. Gasser’s inability to keep the ball on the ground doesn’t bode well heading into today’s matchup. The Cubs are one of baseball’s most power-happy clubs, leading the majors in home runs (196). In fact, the North Siders smacked 62 dingers during August. That’s a National League record for one club over the course of a single month. Chicago hitters have posted a 29.0% fly ball rate, third-highest in baseball. Gasser’s knack for giving up the long ball (1.4 HR/9) makes navigating tonight’s opponent a difficult task. MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong and third baseman Alex Bregman are both swinging hot bats. RELATED Best Home Run Props for Tuesday 9/1/26 As for the other side, Matthew Boyd will take the hill tonight. The former All-Star has battled injuries for much of 2025. However, when healthy, he remains an above-average arm. The southpaw has notched a 3.99 ERA, 1.22 WHIP and 76 strikeouts (7.1 K/9) during 97.0 innings of work. That’s not to say the veteran has been perfect; he’s surrendered at least four runs in three of his last five appearances. However, he remains above-average when it comes to limiting free passes (2.8 BB/9). Whether or not he’s at his best, Boyd should provide Chicago with some length. The lefty has tossed six innings or more in nine of his previous ten outings. Milwaukee’s lineup, while unorthodox, gets the job done. Despite a lack of home run power, this group is at its best when stringing together base hits. The Brewers are third in runs scored (686), third in batting average (.255) and second in on-base percentage (.338). However, tonight’s contest could present some difficulty for the NL Central leaders. The Brew Crew have put up a .700 OPS against left-handed pitching, 13th-worst in the big leagues. Best Bet: Cubs ML (-123) Gasser doesn’t inspire much confidence. His propensity for fly balls should have this homer-happy Cubs lineup licking its chops on Tuesday. Boyd is far from an ace, but this isn’t the most intimidating matchup. The Brewers haven’t been the most dangerous group at the plate against lefties. Equipped with the superior starter and deeper lineup, Chicago makes plenty of sense this evening at home. articles.title: FPL Gameweek 2 Review – Analysis of Every Fixture
articles.excerpt: FPL Gameweek 2 Review – Every Fixture Analysed Greetings all, and welcome to a full, detailed, and indeed hopefully helpful review of FPL Gameweek 2. It was certainly a high scoring week. I (Joe) know that because everyone around me seemed to be scoring 100+ pts, while I meandered along with my pedestrian 88pts. Bruno […] The post FPL Gameweek 2 Review – Analysis of Every Fixture appeared first on Full90 FPL .
articles.source_type: Gameweek previews, transfer tips, captaincy corner, fixture focus
articles.body: FPL Gameweek 2 Review - Analysis of Every Fixture Skip to content FPL Gameweek 2 Review - Every Fixture Analysed Greetings all, and welcome to a full, detailed, and indeed hopefully helpful review of FPL Gameweek 2. It was certainly a high scoring week. I (Joe) know that because everyone around me seemed to be scoring 100+ pts, while I meandered along with my pedestrian 88pts. Bruno and Haaland – i.e. 2/3 of the most highly owned players (JP being the other), and the two captaincy options – obviously made for the bulk of that. We also got returns from a ton of other widely-owned fellas though – Raya, Calafiori, Gabriel, Mbeumo, Rogers, Palmer, JP himself, DCL, and so on and so forth. If only all of the players that loads of us own would score every week, this game would be easy. Anyway, enough faffing about. Let’s get on with the Gameweek 2 review! FPL Gameweek 2 Review In an incredible stroke of creative genius, I’ve decided to go through all the weekend’s games in order. Crazy, I know, but it just might work. Here are the main FPL takeaways for every Gameweek 2 fixture. Crystal Palace 1 – 4 Man City I wouldn’t read too much into this game for Palace City got off to a slow start this season, between GW1 and the community shield, but they’re obviously one of the best attacks in the league, so getting battered by them doesn’t really mean anything. It’s not exactly great to still have not scored a goal for themselves (this one being an OG) after 2 games. But Everton away, then City, aren’t the easiest opening fixtures. We’ll learn a lot more about them in the next few games – Fulham, Ipswich, Leeds, Forest – against sides far more on their level. I will also note that their schedule gets very busy, very quickly now. They’ve got a League Cup game after next weekend, and Europa League games consistently thereafter, so they’re basically playing twice a week for ages now. I would be… concerned about how they balance that with the Prem, since their squad isn’t great, and they could well be a great team to target once the Europa League does start up . Losing these two games doesn’t immediately make that so, however. As noted, City’s attack was always going to click sooner rather than later, and here it clicked in style. I thought no- Haaland was ridiculous before the season, and him grabbing two goals here – ahead of an incredible fixture next week – hardly changed my mind. Given that he has Man U’s crap defence, Sunderland home, then Liverpool’s crap defence coming up too, I’d get him in immediately, if you went without to start the year. Cherki is unsurprisingly one of the most transferred-in players right now, and I’ve got no problem with it. Benching him for the first game was bizarre, but that’s not happening again any time soon. If you’ve got a City spot free, he’d be my number one target on their team, and one of my top targets overall. I won’t be moving Semenyo to him myself… but I wish I’d just picked him to start with, right now. I’d also stick by the City defence . They haven’t cleaned yet, but they have held both opponents to less than 1xG… and obviously you have to start them all against Coventry anyway. I wouldn’t panic on Anderson either. He hit 14 DC’s this week, and has a solid 0.34 xGI/game so far, so attacking returns should come to back up those DefCon points. (And, again, you shouldn’t be selling any City players before Coventry at home… obviously). Liverpool 2 – 2 Notts Forest I can’t say Liverpool’s actual production looks any different under Iraola. They started last season all over the place, relying on pretty late goals (in that case, to get wins), and they’re doing the same thing again. The defence still looks crap. 4 goals conceded in their first 2 games, and they gave up a whopping 2.88 xG to Forest (including a pen, obviously). Unfortunately, they also play Ipswich next week. I doubt they’ll clean in that game either, based on how rubbish they are at the back and Ipswich scoring 2 goals in both their games so far, but you probably have to just hold onto Virgil anyway and pray. They looked better going forward in this game than against Newcastle (not that they could’ve looked much worse). Isak even remembered how to put the ball in the net! Admittedly it was absolutely put on a plate for him, but hey, we don’t care about how easy the chances are in FPL, as long as our forwards score. I’m holding him for Ipswich and Fulham, then will strongly reassess when their fixtures turn drastically. Wirtz looked better too, and I’d also hold him. He had one goal disallowed, hit the bar with another shot, and got the assist for Munoz’s goal. Speaking of – I like the look of Munoz quite a bit. I didn’t actually think he looked that amazing when he came on against Newcastle, but he still got the ‘assist’ (won a pen), and took his goal very well here. He looks very good value at 6.5, particularly as he’s presumably nailed there with Barcola to play on the left. I’d be hesitant about bringing him in though – since again you only get 2 good fixtures – unless you’re planning a wildcard around GW5 or 6. Finally, Szobszlai is driving me crazy as a non-owner. First he gets bailed out of a GW1 blank by a last minute pen. Then he gets shifted to RB this game after Frimpong went off (which helped his DC’s last season) and promptly hit on DefCons. Sigh. Obviously you’re holding him if you’ve got him. And if I’d known the Frimpong experiment was going to last less than 2 games, I’d have got him too. I just wanted to have a little moan. (I’ll be saying this a lot, but…) it’s too early to judge Forest yet. Glasner is a good manager, and I’d assume they’ll finish around midtable, and be a solid team. They did well here… but they also just lost two games in a row to Leeds (including in the League Cup), not scoring a goal either time, so let’s wait and see. MGW is obviously great, and I’m somewhat wishing I’d taken him over Semenyo for 0.5 less. He gets Spurs at home next, Villa away (meh), but then Coventry home and Palace. If you are desperate to rid yourself of an Mbeumo type, for example (not that I would be), he’d probably be my 2nd choice after Cherki. I’d also have Neco Williams on the early wildcard watchlist. No clean sheets yet obviously, but he did have an assist here and hit on DC’s, and is only 5.0 (the same price as stupid Van Hecke, for example, who this idiot picked instead). Coventry 0 – 1 Hull One for the bench boosters out there… and that’s about it. Coventry are the worst team in the league right now, and we should target them mercilessly. Hull haven’t been as bad as we all expected so far… but let’s not get carried away. It’s been two games, and I’d still also have them pencilled in as one of the best matchups around until we’ve seen them prove us wrong a few more times. Bournemouth 1 – 1 Everton Bournemouth have been the unluckiest team so far this season, losing 4pts already in extra time. It’s too early yet to decide whether losing Iraola has actually affected them or not. They’ve been fine in both games, and had plenty of shots here (15, for a 2.26 xG). I’d still roughly have them pegged as a good-not-great team, and a tricky matchup when they’re at home, until further notice. It’s too early to actually consider Scott , but he’d be somewhere on my budget midfielder watchlist going forward. He hit a very good 386 DC’s last season, and got 5 attacking returns on a 6.74 xGI. One to keep an eye on, especially if you’re looking to wildcard around GW 7 or so, when their fixtures get better and we’ll have several more weeks of data on him. All hail James Tarkowski , our FPL Defensive Lord and Saviour. You just have to love him. He cleaned in his first game, and missed his DC’s by 1. He hit on DC’s this game, and got an injury time goal, and got 2 bonus points, good for a whopping 12pts total. He is currently the 14th-highest owned defender, miles behind the likes of VVD who costs 0.5 more. I am baffled. Aside from that, I’d only note the return of Garner for Everton. He only got 61mins here, as he continues to work back from injury, but still managed to rack up 10 DC’s in that time. He’ll almost certainly be in my wildcard team, whenever that happens. Spurs 0 – 2 Newcastle I’d love to pile on Spurs , but they weren’t exactly awful here. They actually looked pretty good going forward, and got 16 shots off, with 5 on target. Newcastle got 2 shots on target… and scored with both. I thought they’d be fine defensively before the season, after their heavy spending there. Obviously, as of now, I was wrong. I still think they’ll gel and be fine before too long, but for now they’re definitely one of the better teams in the league to target, as they were for much of last season. More on them next week in general, once their latest avalanche of transfer dealings have been settled, and we begin to have some vague idea of who’s actually going to start for them – particularly up top. Newcastle are basically the anti-Spurs. They also made tons of signings, most people thought they’d struggle this season, and they’ve actually been fine. I thought they played very well against Liverpool, and were incredibly unlucky not to win. Now they’ve come and nicked a 2-0 away to Spurs – nice! They’ve also got a few intriguing FPL options already. Hall is currently only 5.0 (though will definitely rise), which is cheap in today’s FPL. He’s hit on DC’s in both games so far, has had 0.34 and 0.35 xGI, and even got 3 bonus points at the weekend. Obviously the latter isn’t going to happen often, but if he’s going to get DefCons and threaten attacking returns, at that price, he’ll be a great pick. They’ve also got good defensive fixtures basically all the way through to Arsenal in Gameweek 11. I like him a lot… and it’s very tempting to bin stupid Van Hecke for him right now. I don’t know what the hell’s gotten into Elanga , but I like it. He was awful last season, and has been brilliant in both games so far. They’re basically just constantly pinging balls over the top for him, which – given that he’s rapid – is working out very well. Two goals already, super cheap at only 6.1, and their upcoming fixtures are good for attackers too. He’d probably be my top pick among budget mids right now. Wissa also appears to have been resuccitated. He was excellent against Liverpool (1 xG, 1 assist, and his all-round play was very good), and took his goal brilliantly here. He’s also super cheap, at 6.1, and obviously has those same very good fixtures. I’d just about take him over DCL right now if you had neither, given those fixtures, but wouldn’t actually make that move obviously. Chelsea 4 – 3 Brighton There’s not much I can say here that you don’t already know. Chelsea’s attack is brilliant and their defence is rubbish. 7-5 aggregate score, across their first two games – ridiculous. All three of the big hitters – Palmer, JP, and Rogers – look great. I still wouldn’t bring them in for Arsenal away (though I’m sure many, many people will), but would gladly load up on as many of them as you can straight after that… particularly as ‘straight after that’ in this case means Hull at home. The defence will (probably) get better, especially when Caicedo is fit again. For now it’s obviously a complete stay-away though, regardless of fixtures. I’d continue to back Brighton as being very good this season. Obviously they dismantled Villa, and they got 14 shots off here, 5 on target, and had a ridiculous 75% of the ball. I still don’t particularly fancy any of their players in FPL (though congrats to the Gross owners for getting completely bailed out at the end!). But I do think they have to rank as one of the harder matchups to go against right now, especially for your defenders (and let’s not forget they were excellent defensively last season too). Chelsea are shipping out an underwhelming duo, but why are Spurs so eager to take them? (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Even after relegation scares in back-to-back seasons, the most pessimistic of Spurs supporters probably wouldn't have predicted being rock bottom after two games, with a -5 goal difference. Or perhaps they would have, from recent trauma build-up. Still, Tottenham Hotspur ’s summer incomings have been impressive, and arrived with an expectation of achieving European football this season. But the North London club, at best, could be considered slightly overzealous in regard to its expenditure this summer, and their haste in helping to solve Chelsea ’s wage bill issue is worrying, to say the least. Tottenham Hotspur secure services of Chelsea duo, but why? Spurs are in the process of signing Tosin Adarabioyo (Image credit: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) Ahead of Tuesday’s transfer deadline at 11pm BST, Spurs look set to secure the services of Chelsea duo Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo. Their London rivals are willing to shift the pair in an effort to solve their wage bill issues, and Spurs seem all too eager to aid them in this regard. Xabi Alonso has a fine squad to work with this season, and he's successfully shifted deadwood (Image credit: Getty Images) Mudryk will sign on a season-long loan, while Adarabioyo is expected to move on a permanent transfer for around £7 million — combined, they recorded zero goals and zero assists in 23 Premier League appearances last season. Chelsea, in contrast to the North London club, are fourth in the Premier League table, having taken two wins from two against Brighton and Fulham — blockbuster 3-2 and 4-3 victories. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Last season, they finished in 10th, accumulating just nine additional points to Spurs’ tally of 41, which saw them capable of being relegated all the way until the Premier League’s final gameweek. If you stare hard enough, you’ll find that there was likely an expectation for the two clubs to perform as peers this season, yet Tottenham Hotspur have, rather alarmingly, found themselves vacuuming the crumbs up off the floor in Chelsea’s kitchen. And that should worry fans of the North London club — after an initially serious summer in which Spurs secured the services of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio, Jan Paul van Hecke, Omar Marmoush, and further Premier League-proven talent, this is a concerning sign. Omar Marmoush has also arrived on loan, but that is entirely different (Image credit: Alamy) It’s one thing to take players from Manchester City ; Enzo Maresca’s men will likely challenge for the Premier League title this season, and the Savio-Marmoush duo bring multiple top-level seasons of experience under Pep Guardiola’s wing to London. But a pair of 'B squad' players from Chelsea with little observable Premier League impact? What benefits could this duo bring that outweigh the positive impact it will have on the Blues’ wage bill, and their rivals’ ability to compete? How good can Mudryk and Tosin possibly be, for paying £7m and the pair’s wages, to prevent Chelsea from getting the last laugh here? During a summer in which Spurs appeared determined to turn a page, their performances on the pitch have scarcely improved, and their transfer business will conclude on a sour note. And while fans of the North London club will surely stay focused on seeing the likes of Fernandes, Tonali, Savio and Marmoush come good, they should keep a closer eye on the duo that Chelsea appear overwhelmingly likely to have fleeced them for. It clearly bothered him When head coach Todd Monken subsequently named Watson QB1 to start the season, fans found more ways to show their displeasure While Watson didn’t play in the Browns’ preseason finale last Thursday, he was on the sideline and spent most of his time with a towel over his head — perhaps trying to be as incognito as possible. But does it bother Monken that Cleveland fans clearly have not wholly embraced his choice for starting quarterback? “Absolutely not,” Monken said in his Tuesday press conference, via transcript from the team. “Would I prefer that we would all be on the same page? Yeah, but that has nothing to do with my decision, and it can never have anything to do with my decision. “My decision has got to be about what’s best for the Browns in Week 1 and all the way through the season, and as long as I’m the head coach here.” To that end, Monken said he has confidence Watson will be able to push the ball down the field to create explosive plays. “You’re not going to be elite on offense and score points if you can’t create explosives,” Monken said. “It’s so hard to drive the football the length of the field without an explosive. You can look at the studies in terms of percentage of scoring a touchdown or getting a field goal with one explosive in a drive. Obviously, that comes after you’ve gotten the first first down. Every coordinator is going to say we’re chasing explosives, and everyone runs with, ‘Oh [you’re] chasing explosives.’ Well, no shit. Everyone’s chasing explosives and trying to not to turn it over. And that’s what you’re trying to do. What’s the defense trying to do? Turn you over and not allow explosives. That’s really the big chess match is that. The ways that you win. “So, obviously having explosive players helps that. Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. The 76ers announced Wednesday that they have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas to contracts. we have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas. ✍️ pic.twitter.com/1vIxBv5QBe — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) September 1, 2026 Those are Exhibit 10 contracts, which are training camp contracts where a player can get a bonus (up to $85,000) if they sign to play with Philadelphia’s G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats. All three of Fall, Nelson and Thomas have two-way eligibility left, and the 76ers do have one open two-way contract spot they could give out if someone stands out in training camp. Fall, the 7'6" fan-favorite center, spent two seasons in Boston and one in Cleveland, but has been out of the NBA since 2022, playing overseas. He also played in the NBA All-Star Friday Night Celebrity Game last February in Los Angeles. Nelson is the son of former NBA player and current 76ers Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Jameer Nelson. He was in the Spurs’ training camp two years ago and then with their G League team, then in the Kings’ training camp last season and played for their G League affiliate, the Stockton Kings. Last season with Stockton, he averaged 19.9 points and 3.7 assists per game. Thomas, a 6'7" wing, was in training camp last season with Philadelphia and averaged 12.5 points and five rebounds a game for the Blue Coats when he played with them. Unlike the NFL or other sports, there are very rarely training camp battles for a roster spot in the NBA, and in this case, Philadelphia’s roster is set. It has 14 players under contract for next season and plans to enter the season at that number, deciding whether to add a 15th player down the line. Liverpool target electric Bundesliga winger Jamie Leweling Liverpool are looking to raid Stuttgart. According to Sky Germany , both Liverpool and Everton are after Stuttgart forward Jamie Leweling, with the former deeming him a potential Salah replacement. The 25-year-old is contracted to the Bundesliga side until 2029, meaning he will not come for cheap, or easily, however, his contributions during the 2025-26 season could make the late plunge worth it. articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi and Tottenham Hotspur receive major transfer deadline day boost
articles.excerpt: Tottenham Hotspur have been handed a lift on transfer deadline day as Swedish international Dejan Kulusevski returned to full team training, 477 days after suffering a complex knee injury. The 26-year-old forward has not featured in a competitive fixture since May 2025, when a challenge during a Premier League defeat to Crystal Palace left him with patella cartilage damage in his right knee. While initial diagnoses suggested a minor knock, subsequent scans revealed significant cartilage damage requiring surgery. Dejan Kulusevski returns to Spurs training after 477 days (Image credit: Getty Images) His rehabilitation was heavily disrupted by setbacks and because cartilage lacks a direct blood supply, the joint failed to heal naturally under increased workloads, forcing Kulusevski to undergo a second surgical procedure to clean out the affected area. In total, the Swede's 15-month ordeal has forced him to sit out well over 60 matches for club and country.
