While initial diagnoses suggested a minor knock, subsequent scans revealed significant cartilage damage requiring surgery. Dejan Kulusevski returns to Spurs training after 477 days (Image credit: Getty Images) His rehabilitation was heavily disrupted by setbacks and because cartilage lacks a direct blood supply, the joint failed to heal naturally under increased workloads, forcing Kulusevski to undergo a second surgical procedure to clean out the affected area. In total, the Swede's 15-month ordeal has forced him to sit out well over 60 matches for club and country. Dejan Kulusevski (Image credit: Getty Images) From the sidelines, Kulusevski has watched a turbulent chapter in Spurs ’ recent history unfold. Former manager Ange Postecoglou departed, Thomas Frank arrived and left, then so did Igor Tudor. New head coach Roberto De Zerbi has since taken the reins, but Kulusevski has been out of action for so long, he has missed Tottenham's 2025 Europa League title, as well as the entirety of last season's domestic struggles, including a 17th-place Premier League finish. He was also forced to miss Sweden’s 2026 World Cup campaign. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. For De Zerbi, who has faced a frustrating start to the 2026/27 campaign following consecutive losses to Brentford and Newcastle , Kulusevski’s return provides a boost to Tottenham’s attacking options. The versatile attacker’s ability to operate as a direct right-winger or more of a central playmaker offers De Zerbi the options his side has lacked for quite some time. Given that Kulusevski has spent 477 days away from first-team action, realistic expectations must be maintained. Re-integrating into high-intensity Premier League football following two surgical procedures and a prolonged period of inactivity will require significant patience from Spurs supporters, and it will inevitably take time before he recovers full match sharpness and rhythm. Plenty has changed at Spurs since Kulusevski last featured, including the personnel (Image credit: Getty Images) Nevertheless, stepping back onto the training pitch alongside his teammates is a significant milestone. "After 477 days I came back to full team training," Kulusevski wrote on social media. "Everything is impossible until is [sic] not. Want to see a miracle. Be one. See u soon." Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Brian Gutekunst: Packers haven’t seen the Josh Jacobs video Mike Florio Mike Florio Published September 1, 2026 02:58 PM Facebook Twitter Email The misdemeanor battery case against Packers running back Josh Jacobs includes surveillance video from a camera in his garage. The police report strongly suggests that the video includes images of the alleged assault. On Tuesday, Packers G.M. Brian Gutekunst was asked at a press conference whether the team has seen it. We have not seen the video ,” Gutekunst said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. “Again, those are legal things going on right now, so we’ll let those play out. That’s really not for us, but in the appropriate times, if those things become available, we’ll figure that stuff out when that time comes.” Gutekunst also was asked whether the team needs to see the video before making a decision about Jacobs’s future with the team. “Again, we’re going to lean on the legal process and let that happen, but we’ll take things as they come,” Gutekunst said. The situation brings back memories of the weeks preceding the release of the notorious Ray Rice elevator video. The league, as of August 2014, had not seen the video. We argued that it would be easy for the league to get it. It was part of his case file, and Rice ultimately controlled his case file. If the league told Rice he couldn’t play until his lawyer made the video available for review, the league would have quickly gotten it. It sparked a somewhat spirited debate by phone with a league official. The conversation ended with this prediction: “If you don’t get that video, TMZ eventually will.” (By early September, TMZ had gotten it — and then all hell broke loose.) In this case, it would be even easier for the league or the team to inspect the video. It came from Jacobs’s house. He owns the footage. Why wouldn’t the Packers want to see it? Coach Matt LaFleur recently said regarding Jacobs, "[W]hat he tells me, I believe him and I trust him. I’m going to do that until proven otherwise.” One way to be proven otherwise, or to have LaFleur’s current belief confirmed, would be to tell him to produce the video. articles.title: Arroyo: We need the fans dreaming with us
articles.excerpt: Head coach Natalia Arroyo highlighted the importance of the Villa fans heading into the 2026/27 campaign after the squad rounded off their pre-season schedule with a 0-0 draw against West Ham United on Sunday. It was a strong performance at our new secondary home Keys Park, with the team collecting a confidence boosting clean sheet for their efforts. Midfielder Lucia Kendall almost provided perfect ending for the watching home fans with a stunning long range strike but was denied the winner by a superb save in stoppage time. Speaking to VillaTV post-match Arroyo said: “ It was a positive test to play in front of our fans and to finish the pre-season with that feeling, with that connection and this energy. “ We were missing them. We need them dreaming with us.” Arroyo continued, “When we get to these moments where we are drawing and in these last actions, I love that they push, that they shoot with us, that they put the leg in with us and block any shot. General Manager Ryan Poles was asked today if Gordon will play for the Bears. Poles answered, “I don’t know.” “I would hope so,” Poles continued. “I still have hope there. He’s going to have to continue to work hard and come back to play football again.” Poles emphasized the need for Gordon, who was out all summer with a calf injury, to push through the discomfort of rehabilitation. “Any time you have an injury and you’re coming back from something, there’s discomfort that you have to push through. And that’s what it comes down to. So we haven’t been able to get over that hump and we’re not progressing as fast as we would like. That’s really all I have to say about that,” Poles said. The Bears signed Gordon to a three-year, $40 million contract extension last year, and Gordon played in just three games last season as he struggled with groin, hamstring and calf injuries. articles.title: ROSELLA AYANE IS A BLUE
articles.excerpt: Ipswich Town Women is excited to announce the permanent signing of Rosella Ayane from Leicester City. The experienced forward, who has spent most of her career in the Barclays Women’s Super League, arrives at Town on an initial one-year deal. Rosella came through the Academy at Chelsea and made her senior debut for the club at the start of the 2013/14 campaign during a win over Doncaster Rovers Belles. Loan moves to Millwall, Bristol City and Everton soon followed before a permanent switch to Apollon Limassol in Cyprus, where she scored 19 goals in 19 games. Rosella returned to England to re-sign for the Robins for a season before joining Spurs at the start of the 2019/20 campaign. Across six years in North London scored 12 goals in 109 appearances and also helped the side to a Women’s FA Cup final against Manchester United in 2024. Rosella also brings international experience into the group, having played 35 times and found the net 11 times for Morocco. Via Sam Farmer of the L.A. Times , Kroenke has bought the Los Angeles Angels of Major League Baseball. Diggins hasn’t played since she scored 19 points in a 98-90 loss at Las Vegas on July 3. Chicago (15-25) was eliminated from playoff contention on Aug. 23. It has four games left when the WNBA returns from its break for the FIBA World Cup. “We’re in full support of Skylar and want to make sure we are steadfastly prioritizing her health,” general manager Jeff Pagliocca said Tuesday in a statement. “Skylar made a strong effort to get back to the court this season. She’s been in constant communication with us through the entire process.” Diggins, who turned 36 on Aug. 2, signed with Chicago on the first day of free agency in April. She averaged 14.2 points and 4.9 assists during a rocky season with the Sky. Following a June 7 loss at Toronto, Diggins called for more leadership and maturity from players and coaches. When coach Tyler Marsh made plans to use the seven-time All-Star as a reserve, Diggins posted on Instagram about her frustration with the decision. The injury sidelined Diggins before she could play in a reserve role with Chicago. She started each of her 19 games this season. Stroud during season Josh Alper Josh Alper Published September 1, 2026 02:17 PM Facebook Twitter Email The Texans are taking a page from the Steelers’ book on contract negotiations The Steelers have long refused to engage in contract negotiations with players during the regular season and Texans General Manager Nick Caserio said that Houston will take the same approach with quarterback C.J. Stroud this year. Caserio said in July and again on Tuesday that the team has had talks with the 2023 first-round pick about a new deal, but that those talks will be put on hold when the Texans face the Bills in Week 1. “If we don’t get it figured out before the season starts, then it’ll be something we address in the offseason ,” Caserio said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. The Texans have already picked up their option on Stroud’s contract for 2027, so the quarterback will remain under contract regardless of how things play out on the field this year. A strong season would make it harder for the Texans to continue playing the waiting game, but anything resembling Stroud’s postseason performance from last season would lead to a lot of questions about the future of the quarterback position in Houston. If Salas appears behind the plate, he will be the youngest catcher in the big leagues since Ivan Rodriguez, who was 19 when he debuted with the Texas Rangers on June 20, 1991. Salas, who signed with the Padres in 2023 for a record $5.6 million bonus as a top international prospect, has progressed quickly through their minor league system despite a back injury that caused him to miss most of the 2025 season. The Padres’ top prospect batted .286 with seven home runs, and 37 RBIs in 72 games this year at Double-A. After being promoted to Triple-A on July 29, Salas hit .326 with three homers and 24 RBIs. articles.title: Arsenal youngster given transfer lifeline as Fulham miss out: report
articles.excerpt: The proposed move would see Nwaneri join Bundesliga club Borussia Dortmund on loan, without an option to purchase, according to reports. Arsenal , who will strive to retain the Premier League title for the first time in the North London club’s history this season, are willing to part ways with their 19-year-old prospect. Borussia Dortmund ’s interest in Nwaneri pre-dates the signing of Giannis Konstantelias; however, the Gunners youngster is expected to receive greater playing minutes after the Greek attacker sustained a recent injury. Konstantelias suffers ligament injury, Nwaneri travels for medical to Dortmund The 19-year-old will be hoping this move is more fruitful than his loan period with Marseille (Image credit: Getty Images) According to transfers expert David Ornstein , the 19-year-old is travelling today to Dortmund to undergo his medical exam. Konstantelias is braced for a lengthy sideline spell after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury in his debut Bundesliga appearance versus Hamburger SV — in which he also hit his first goal. Arsenal's Ethan Nwaneri is heading out on loan (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google The proposed move would see Nwaneri join Bundesliga club Borussia Dortmund on loan, without an option to purchase, according to reports. Arsenal , who will strive to retain the Premier League title for the first time in the North London club’s history this season, are willing to part ways with their 19-year-old prospect. Borussia Dortmund ’s interest in Nwaneri pre-dates the signing of Giannis Konstantelias; however, the Gunners youngster is expected to receive greater playing minutes after the Greek attacker sustained a recent injury. Konstantelias suffers ligament injury, Nwaneri travels for medical to Dortmund The 19-year-old will be hoping this move is more fruitful than his loan period with Marseille (Image credit: Getty Images) According to transfers expert David Ornstein , the 19-year-old is travelling today to Dortmund to undergo his medical exam. Konstantelias is braced for a lengthy sideline spell after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury in his debut Bundesliga appearance versus Hamburger SV — in which he also hit his first goal. Dortmund found themselves needing an additional attacking player (Image credit: Kristian Skeie - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) Dortmund prevailed 2-0 on the day, with Konstantelias scoring his side’s second: a glorious right-footed effort from just inside the box. Following the Greek’s injury, Dortmund reached out to Arsenal and made it clear that Nwaneri’s arrival had become a priority, before an arrangement was ironed out. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Prior to this heightened interest, the youngster was reportedly considering a loan move to Fulham , prioritising a stay in the Premier League. This will no longer happen. The 19-year-old did not appear in the squad for the Gunners’ 3-0 pre-season victory against Manchester City in the Community Shield, missing out alongside Gabriel Martinelli. The Brazilian has since departed for Saudi Arabia, and Nwaneri is now Bundesliga-bound, with Arteta’s side hoping that the 19-year-old is able to develop further with Dortmund. Martinelli also failed to make the Community Shield squad, and has since made the move to Saudi Arabia (Image credit: Marc Atkins/Getty Images) The youngster spent the second half of the 2025/26 season on loan with Marseille in Ligue 1 , scoring twice, and assisting once, in nine French top-flight appearances. Nwaneri also scored against Dortmund for Arsenal in pre-season, during a 3-2 loss in the Emirates Cup — and converted his penalty in the post-match shootout. Since making his Premier League debut for the North London club in 2022, aged just 15, Nwaneri has failed to break into a side that has competed for the English top-flight title in four successive seasons. He has made 51 appearances for Arsenal, scoring 10 and assisting two, with Mikel Arteta confessing in August that he would like the 19-year-old to stay, but that he needs to receive further opportunities. The club reportedly weighed up the benefits of selling their youngster outright, however, a loan period has been agreed. Should Nwaneri seize the chances he will receive at Dortmund, a sale or place in the first team are both possible for him upon his return to London. articles.title: Under-17s off to winning start in Premier League Cup
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-17s got off to a winning start in the U17 Premier League Cup, thanks to a 3-2 victory over Southampton. Goals from Leyland Waite, Denzel Decardi-Nelson and Fikayo Solanke secured the three points for the Cherries. It ensures the Cherries get off to the strongest possible start in a group that also contains Chelsea and West Ham United. After the game, under-18s assistant coach, Elliot Head, spoke to afcb.co.uk: "The first half was a tight game with chances for both teams. "We regained the ball high up the pitch a few teams that lead to some good chances which we weren't quite able to capitalise from." The Cherries went into the interval level at 0-0, after tight first-half. Scoring in the 50th and 55th minute, the Cherries were then forced back into their own half, as Southampton brought the score level. The winner came in the 88th minute and secured all three points for the Cherries. Head continued: "The lads showed fantastic attitude throughout the game and had to dig deep after coming off the back of four games in ten days." The next under-17 cup game is away at Chelsea on 15th September.

General Manager John Lynch has now provided a clearer timeline for that to happen. In an interview with KNBR on Tuesday, Lynch said Bosa would like to practice on Wednesday. “Nick worked to the side yesterday, and I think that’s the plan today,” Lynch said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. “ Wednesday, he wants to get out on the field . articles.title: Doku, Cherki, and Now Ndiaye? Man City’s Penchant for Dribblers Is No Coincidence
articles.excerpt: Manchester City are loading up on players known for their dribbling ability, with Iliman Ndiaye seemingly their next new face. The post Doku, Cherki, and Now Ndiaye? Man City’s Penchant for Dribblers Is No Coincidence appeared first on Opta Analyst .
articles.source_type: xG methodology, expected points tables, head-to-head records, supercomputer projections
articles.body: Doku, Cherki, and Now Ndiaye? Man City’s Penchant for Dribblers Is No Coincidence | Opta Analyst Manchester City are loading up on players known for their dribbling ability, with Iliman Ndiaye seemingly their next new face. For a while, a fairly popular theory suggested Manchester City was a place that suffocated individual creativity in favour of focus on positional football and “the system”. It was a theory (myth?) that led to some believing Pep Guardiola simply didn’t value dribblers. Of course, the reality was almost certainly never quite as black and white as that, but there was a notable moment a few years ago. When City signed Jérémy Doku in 2023, the Belgian was not thought of as the type of winger Guardiola would typically go for, in that his primary strength was beating his man and tallying a high volume of dribbles. He didn’t score lots, his end product was called into question, and there were questions about how he’d fit into a team built around passing ability and possession retention. But he steadily developed into one of the Premier League’s best and most effective one-v-one wingers, and 2025-26 suggested his level was only continuing to rise. Whereas there’s a perception some players had certain individualistic qualities limited by Guardiola, with Jack Grealish the most common example, Doku feels very similar – just more mature – to the player they signed from Rennes. Last year, City then added Rayan Cherki , arguably even more of a maverick than Doku, and the Frenchman enjoyed a brilliant first season in the Premier League. Antoine Semenyo was another frequent dribbler who joined City in January from Bournemouth, and now they appear to be adding Iliman Ndiaye to form a formidable foursome of dribble-first attackers – and that’s ignoring the fact Phil Foden is pretty handy on the ball, and new signing Allan is highly regarded for his ball carrying. Guardiola may have gone, replaced by Enzo Maresca, but the club’s thinking has apparently been unchanged. Assuming Ndiaye’s reported £65 million move from Everton is completed, City will have the Premier League’s top three players from 2025-26 for dribble attempts: Doku (162), Semenyo (144) and Ndiaye (136). Similarly, they’ll have four of last season’s top eight for most dribbles completed: Doku (84), Ndiaye (65), Semenyo (59) and Cherki (51). And it’s worth saying that Elliot Anderson , another of City’s summer recruits, was only just behind Cherki on 50 (though admittedly from almost twice as many minutes). This seems far too deliberate for it to be a coincidence. Guardiola did say in the past that he felt the “future of football” would steer away from his possession dominance ideology and instead be defined by more transitional styles – and there’s certainly an argument these players can help City make that transition, or at least be more unpredictable. Dribblers bring chaos, and City are a team who’ll frequently be tasked with breaking through compact defences and low blocks; in fact, they spent 23.4% of their build-up time last season against a low block, the third-greatest proportion in the Premier League. Sure, maybe you can find a way through with an extra five or 10 passes; or perhaps someone like Ndiaye can slice the opposition open in a fraction of the time with a mere swivel of the hips. It seems highly unlikely City will completely abandon Guardiola’s possession-oriented principles, but some of their signings in recent years suggest an attempt to diversify their threat, and Ndiaye would be a continuation of that. In fairness to Guardiola, the story goes that when he first joined City, his initial instruction to the club’s recruitment team was to “find me players who can dribble”. And actually, several of his title-winning teams were full of players willing to attempt taking on their marker. In 2021-22 (782), 2020-21 (845), 2018-19 (801) and 2017-18 (797), City ranked in the top six for dribble attempts in the Premier League while also winning the title – otherwise, though, there’s been little correlation between the two elements. City obviously aren’t alone in valuing ball carriers or dribblers, but you’d do well to find a squad with a greater concentration of such talent in the Premier League if they can add Ndiaye to their ranks. articles.body: Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal Skip to content News Football Transfer News, Rumours & Gossip Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal Gabriel Jesus has joined Barcelona. Mitch Fretton Last Update: 1 hour ago 3 min read Add us as a preferred source on Google Barcelona have completed the signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal on a permanent deal for a reported fee of £8.6m. The 29-year-old had fallen down the pecking order at Arsenal in recent seasons amid a series of injury problems, while Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres had become the club’s preferred options at centre-forward. Napoli had also shown an interest in Jesus, but the former Manchester City striker has opted to continue his career in Spain. Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022 and scored 32 goals while providing 22 assists in 123 appearances for the Gunners. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta confirmed before his side’s win over Aston Villa that Jesus was no longer training with the first-team squad. Jesus becomes Barcelona’s third signing from a Premier League club this summer, following the arrivals of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle and Rodri from Manchester City. GJ is blaugrana. 🤙 pic.twitter.com/brzvMFKTJb — FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 1, 2026 Table of Contents When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? When does the summer transfer window 2026 close? The window opened on Monday June 15 and will shut on Tuesday September 1. After that, every Premier League club can register a squad of up to 25 players, 17 of whom are allowed to be non-Home Grown Players. A Home Grown Player has been registered with any club affiliated to the English or Welsh Football Association for three entire seasons or 36 months across their career before his 21st birthday, or the end of the season during which they turn 21. Under-21 players do not count towards the 25-man limit. What time does the Premier League transfer window shut on transfer deadline day? The deadline is 23:00 BST in the Premier League, but clubs can have an extra two hours to file the remaining documentation if they submit a deal sheet confirming that an agreement has been reached. The deal sheet must arrive fully completed before the transfer window closes. For international transfers, clubs also have to comply with the FIFA Transfer Matching System deadline of midnight. When does the summer transfer window close around Europe? There are slight variations between the major European leagues. Here’s when they shut. League Date BST close Premier League Sept 1 23:00 18:00 15:00 LaLiga Sept 1 22:59 17:59 14:59 Serie A Sept 1 19:00 14:00 11:00 Bundesliga Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 Ligue 1 Aug 31 19:00 14:00 11:00 When does the 2026/27 winter transfer window open? The Premier League winter transfer window opens on Friday January 1, 2027 and closes on Monday February 1, 2027 at 23:00 BST. Can Premier League clubs sign players outside of the window? Clubs can only add players outside of transfer windows who are free agents and if they have room in their 25-man squad. Premier League teams can still announce deals with other clubs, but those players will not be registered to play until the window re-opens. This means there is usually little to no movement when the window closes, with four months to wait until the window re-opens. Players can be released by Premier League clubs at any time, but the usual rule is that they cannot sign for another side outside of the market. Sign up France’s Tronchon sprints to Vuelta stage win and Mas retains lead gifted by Pogacar’s crash Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 01:04 PM Facebook Twitter Email Highlights: 2026 Vuelta a España, Stage 10 September 1, 2026 02:30 PM Relive the top moments from Stage 10 of the 2026 La Vuelta a España, where riders took on a 184.7km journey through the hills from Alcaraz to Elche de la Sierra. ELCHE DE LA SIERRA, Spain — French rider Bastien Tronchon got a career best result winning Stage 10 of the Spanish Vuelta, and Enric Mas retained the leader’s red jersey he was gifted by Tadej Pogacar’s race-ending crash. The 24-year-old Tronchon sprinted clear over the final 20 yards of a hilly 115-mile stage between Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra. Magnus Cort was second and Thibau Nys placed third. Wout van Aert was fourth. Tronchon put his right hand to his helmet in surprise crossing the line and sobbed tearfully when his Groupama-FDJ United teammates congratulated him. Mas retained his overall lead of 1 minute, 18 seconds ahead of Primoz Roglic, the 36-year-old Slovenian who is chasing a record fifth Vuelta title. Felix Gall stayed 1:39 back in third. The Vuelta was upended over the weekend when Pogacar, the leader and overwhelming favorite to win the three-week race, crashed out and fractured his left collarbone. Stage 10 crested three third-category climbs and let a seven-man breakaway, only one of them within an hour of Mas’s overall time, build a lead of more than two and a half minutes. The peloton reeled in the last of the breakaway inside the final 3.5 miles and caught further attempts by riders to steal away for the win. Stage 11 is a flat stage suiting the sprinters over 96 miles from Cartagena to Lorca. The Vuelta finishes in Granada on Sept. 13. Previously, they fell to the Cityzens in 2022/23 after leading for the campaign’s bulk, again in 2023/24, then to a Mohamed Salah-led Liverpool in 2024/25. The Gunners , who secured the English top-flight crown with 85 points in May, have never retained the Premier League title, however, their quest to do so now appears slightly easier, and less expensive, following an accidental discovery versus Aston Villa Do Arsenal really need a left winger? Eze put in a solid shift at Villa Park (Image credit: Getty Images) Mikel Arteta’s men emerged victorious on Monday evening, taking home three points following a 1-0 victory at Villa Park. That was evidenced by both players being absent from the Community Shield final squad, in which the North London club ran riot from an offensive perspective, scoring three in under 50 minutes. On the bench that day were Eze, Saka, Viktor Gyokeres and Declan Rice, with Kai Havertz, Noni Madueke, Bruno Guimaraes and Tzolis handed starts versus Enzo Maresca’s side. And with Eze’s appearance against Villa, it appears that any fears regarding reinforcement on the left flank have been alleviated, with the Englishman well-adjusted to challenge for the role. Arsenal's depth is staggering, however, late outgoings threatened their left flank (Image credit: Getty Images) The statistics painted a clear picture: 80% pass accuracy, three duels won, seven carries for a total distance of almost 100 metres, one of which being progressive, and six kilometres covered. And, more importantly, three points for the Gunners after a dominant second half — limiting the chasing Villans to 0.24 Expected Goals (xG) while Arteta’s side racked up 0.7, and bagged the deciding goal. Much has been made of Arsenal’s strength in the position, yet Eze’s appearance now certainly warrants consideration as an alternate to Tzolis. The Gunners reportedly tried their luck with Malick Fofana at Lyon , but were rebuffed after low-balling for the player. That appears to have allowed Sunderland to sign the winger for a price the French club deem more acceptable, in one of the strongest deals of the summer transfer window Positioned second in the Premier League table, and yet to concede a goal, the future appears bright for Arteta’s side. And fans would be forgiven for interpreting Eze’s cameo as a firm statement — Arsenal can retain their top-flight title, and they already hold all the necessary keys to do so. articles.body: Whitworth makes permanent switch to Wigan Athletic Skip navigation Whitworth makes permanent switch to Wigan Athletic Announcement 12 hours ago Crystal Palace goalkeeper Joe Whitworth has completed a permanent transfer to Wigan Athletic. Whitworth joined Palace in November 2016 at the age of 13 and progressed through the Academy. He became the club’s youngest-ever Premier League ‘keeper, making his debut away at Brighton & Hove Albion in March 2023 before starting against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium. Having captained Darren Powell’s side to Premier League International Cup glory against PSV Eindhoven, he was named Under-21s Player of the Season in 2023/24. The ‘keeper spent the past two seasons on loan with Exeter City and won their Player of the Season award in his first campaign. He now joins Gary Caldwell’s Wigan following their strong finish to last season in League One. Everyone at Crystal Palace would like to thank Joe for his efforts and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career. Sign up AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks AFC East Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets AFC North Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers AFC South Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans AFC West Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers NFC East Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders NFC North Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings NFC South Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFC West Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks Rumor Mill Peacock PFT Shop Tony Romo pleads no contest to OWI charge in Wisconsin, vows to return to CBS Mike Florio Mike Florio Published September 1, 2026 12:44 PM Facebook Twitter Email Less than a week after an unnamed spokesperson issued a statement on behalf of former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo, Romo has addressed his July arrest for operating while intoxicated directly. On Tuesday, Romo posted a statement on Instagram. In the message, he discloses that he has pleaded no contest. He also explains that pain medication from multiple back surgeries created an “over-reliance” on alcohol. Romo also vows to return to CBS, “in time.” It’s unknown wheter CBS is on board with that part of the plan; the network placed him on leave eight days after the incident, and it has promoted J.J. Watt into Romo’s spot on the top NFL broadcast team. Here’s the full text of Romo’s statement: “Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life. I played for more than 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting. “Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better. “This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me. “This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWl in Wisconsin. I own this completely. “Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol. “As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. This is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward. “That path requires honesty. “None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them. “The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public. “I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know. “As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.” We wish Romo the best as he addresses the issues that led to the OWI charge. And we applaud him for speaking on the issue directly, and not through an unnamed P.R. firm. Owning the situation is perhaps the biggest step toward resolving it. Whether Romo’s candor resolves the situation with CBS to his satisfaction hinges entirely on CBS. Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Sign up NBC Olympics Olympics on Peacock LA 2028 Team USA Benjamin Karl, after epic shirtless gold medal celebration, reverses retirement decision Nick Zaccardi Nick Zaccardi Published September 1, 2026 12:43 PM Facebook Twitter Email Austrian Benjamin Karl, who won Olympic snowboarding gold at age 40, then became a global sensation for his shirtless celebration, is reversing his decision to retire after the 2026 Olympic season. Karl, who races parallel giant slalom, plans to compete in the 2026-27 season, highlighted by a home World Championships in Montafon in March. “It has been a long and difficult journey from competing in regional races all the way to the very top of the sport,” Karl said, according to a social media post . “I have been snowboarding for 30 years, and over time, many things started to feel almost like a given. But my recent experiences have shown me that nothing should ever be taken for granted. “I have learned to appreciate again just how much support I have received over all these years — support that is anything but a given. Now I am really looking forward to continuing my career.” At the Milan Cortina Games, Karl broke the record for oldest individual Winter Olympic gold medalist. Later in the Games, 41-year-old American Elana Meyers Taylor broke Karl’s record with monobob gold. Karl considered a switch to cycling after the Games. “However, a number of things happened over the summer that I simply could not have foreseen,” Karl said in the post. “At the same time, I increasingly came to realize that, quite simply, I am a snowboarder who loves riding his bike.” Karl previously won Olympic medals in 2010 (silver), 2014 (bronze in parallel slalom) and 2022 (gold). He is a five-time world champion between parallel slalom (no longer on the Olympic program) and parellel giant slalom, the most recent title in 2021. 40 YEARS OLD. BACK-TO-BACK GOLD. articles.body: In open letter to NBA GMs, Victor Oladipo says his body is finally right, wants another chance - NBC Sports Skip navigation MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores Login Favorites Sign up to follow your favorites on all your devices. Sign up Odds by Schedule Scores Player News ATLANTIC Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets New York Knicks Philadelphia 76ers Toronto Raptors CENTRAL Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Detroit Pistons Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks SOUTHEAST Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Miami Heat Orlando Magic Washington Wizards NORTHWEST Denver Nuggets Minnesota Timberwolves Oklahoma City Thunder Portland Trail Blazers Utah Jazz PACIFIC Golden State Warriors Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Phoenix Suns Sacramento Kings SOUTHWEST Dallas Mavericks Houston Rockets Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans San Antonio Spurs ATLANTIC Boston Celtics Brooklyn Nets New York Knicks Philadelphia 76ers Toronto Raptors CENTRAL Chicago Bulls Cleveland Cavaliers Detroit Pistons Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks SOUTHEAST Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Miami Heat Orlando Magic Washington Wizards NORTHWEST Denver Nuggets Minnesota Timberwolves Oklahoma City Thunder Portland Trail Blazers Utah Jazz PACIFIC Golden State Warriors Los Angeles Clippers Los Angeles Lakers Phoenix Suns Sacramento Kings SOUTHWEST Dallas Mavericks Houston Rockets Memphis Grizzlies New Orleans Pelicans San Antonio Spurs Fantasy Betting Standings Player Stats Team Stats Player Stats Team Stats Videos In open letter to NBA GMs, Victor Oladipo says his body is finally right, wants another chance Kurt Helin Kurt Helin Published September 1, 2026 12:22 PM Facebook Twitter Email Victor Oladipo is a man robbed of his peak seasons by injuries. In 2017-18, he averaged 23.1 points and 4.3 assists per game for the Pacers, won Most Improved Player and was an All-Star, an All-NBA and an All-Defensive Team player. Then the next season he ruptured his quadriceps tendon, and he was never physically right again. Oladipo, now 34, hasn’t played in the NBA in three seasons. In an open letter to general managers at The Players Tribune , Oladipo said it took a long time for him to stop chasing what was lost and just be patient and get his body right. He said he is finally in that place, can still contribute to a winning basketball team, and wants that chance. “Me, in this moment of my life, at 34 years old. The version of her dad that got kicked all the way down the mountain, then spent years trying to climb back up, only to get kicked back down, again and again … but never once quit trying to climb. The version of her dad that, let’s be real, is probably getting counted out by a lot of people, and is probably getting laughed at by a few of them … but has managed to keep his faith, and keep his purpose. The version of her dad that’s finally found the perspective, and the humility, to write a letter like this one. “To say to any GM who’s willing to listen: I believe my body is finally right. I believe I still have GREAT (and more importantly, WINNING) basketball in front of me. I believe I can be a valuable contributor to an NBA locker room. And what I’m asking for right now is an opportunity to prove it.... “So that’s where I’m at with everything. I don’t know how my journey here is going to end....... Maybe a team out there will give me a chance. Maybe no team will. That’s really up to you all. But if you’re in an NBA front office, and you took the time to read this: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.” Oladipo has been linked to Sacramento as a potential backup to rookie Darius Acuff Jr., but nothing official has come of that. Oladipo played in the G League for the Wisconsin Herd part of last season and averaged 13.5 points per game in the regular season, shooting 32.5% from 3-point range. He has also played some in China in recent years. Oladipo faces the reality many older players do: Most teams would rather give a bench point guard spot (or any position) to a young player they can develop and hold on to for years than to one on the back end of a career. Still, there is a real role for mature, quality veterans in the locker room who can still contribute something on the court. Whether Oladipo is that guy and gets a chance remains to be seen, but he’s made his pitch. Mentions Victor Oladipo Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

Now they’re three key members of the Rams’ defense. McDuffie was traded to the Rams in March, Garrett was traded to the Rams a couple months later, and Donald just came out of retirement. McDuffie told Andrew Siciliano of NFL Media that he wouldn’t believed it was possible for Rams General Manager Les Snead and head coach Sean McVay to bring all three of them onto the same team. I probably would’ve said you’re lying , for real,” McDuffie said. “There’s no way you can get me. There’s no way you can get Myles. There’s no way you can get A.D. But, hey, hat off to Les. Hat off to Sean. Those guys are masterminds and they did it.” The 25-year-old McDuffie has already been a first-team All-Pro once and won Super Bowl rings twice in his first four NFL seasons -- and he’s the least accomplished of the trio: Garrett has been named the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year two of the last three years, while Donald is one of only three players in NFL history to win Defensive Player of the Year three times. Most teams don’t add even one player with those kinds of credentials to their defense in an offseason. The Rams added three. McDuffie is still having a hard time believing it’s real. articles.body: Scottie Scheffler loves what it takes to be great. He can do without fame that comes with greatness - NBC Sports Skip navigation MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores MLB NFL NBA NHL Premier League NASCAR College Football Men’s College Basketball Player News NFL Player News NBA Player News MLB Player News Scores NFL Scores NBA Scores MLB Scores Login Favorites Sign up to follow your favorites on all your devices. Sign up Men’s Leaderboards Women’s Leaderboards Men’s Leaderboards Women’s Leaderboards PGA Tour LPGA DP World Tour Korn Ferry Tour PGA Tour Champions PGA Tour LPGA DP World Tour Korn Ferry Tour PGA Tour Champions The Open PGA Tour LPGA News Watch Live Schedule Scottie Scheffler loves what it takes to be great. He can do without fame that comes with greatness Associated Press Associated Press Published September 1, 2026 12:19 PM Facebook Twitter Email Scheffler: FedExCup a 'nice way to finish' year August 30, 2026 08:29 PM Scottie Scheffler recalls his Round 4 comeback at the Tour Championship to win his second career FedExCup, calling his performance in the playoffs "a nice way to finish off the season." ATLANTA — Scottie Scheffler’s final act of the season was to sign his winning scorecard. After a few minutes to exhale, his wife and two sons having come into the room, he placed his cap over the fixed camera the PGA Tour now installs in previously private scoring areas. Content is king. It wasn’t quite the level of Brian Harman smirking and shooting the bird at the camera in Minnesota, which made Scheffler chuckle and pump his fist. Both were playful moments, and yet East Lake shed a little light on Scheffler’s incredible staying power. Scheffler loves what it takes to be the best player in golf, even the tedious work. He just doesn’t care for all the noise and notoriety that accompany greatness. “I have a tendency to keep my head down and kind of stay in my own lane when I’m out there playing,” he said during the trophy presentation at the Tour Championship. “It’s really fun when you’re able to win and celebrate with the fans in moments like these, and have my family here.” Still, his priority is to crush more than to engage. So he added somewhat apologetically, “I feel bad sometimes. I really do keep my head down and try to focus as much as I can. But I really do hear all the cheers, and I’m very thankful for all of them.” The RBC Heritage at Hilton Head is reputed to be among the most chill tournaments on the schedule, the perfect place to decompress right after the Masters. During the pro-am that week, Scheffler said he felt a calmer vibe at Augusta National despite the enormous pressure, mainly because of the space inside the ropes and spectators (patrons) who cheer, not scream. When he reached the ninth tee, fans at Hilton Head were screaming his name as he waited for the fairway to clear to tee off. Scheffler turned and smiled. It’s part of the deal, and he knows that by now. But this extraordinary run of dominance allows for speculation how long he can keep it up as the attention gets brighter. Winning is hard. The trappings that come with it can be exhausting. The way Scheffler showed up seemingly every week — he finished first, second or third in half of the 20 tournaments he played — and then capped off the season by winning two of the three postseason tournaments was satisfying. It also makes him a shoo-in to be voted PGA Tour player of the year for a fifth straight time. That would tie Tiger Woods for winning the most in a row. Best comparison with Tiger is separation Comparisons with Woods, just like athletes in any sport across generations, are for pool halls and podcasts. Scheffler brushed off the inevitable moment of passing Woods at No. 1 on the PGA Tour career earnings list, a spot Woods held for nearly 26 years. “I wouldn’t really consider that a Tiger record being broken,” Scheffler said. “I think it just shows one of the many effects he had on the game of a golf in a positive way.” Woods never played for a prize fund of $10 million in his peak years from 1997 through 2009. Scheffler played for an average purse of $19.25 million this year. When it comes to money records, it just isn’t a fair fight. The real benchmark — 82 tour wins — is still a long way off. Scheffler has gone three straight years with three wins or more. Woods went 10 out of 11 years winning at least four times. Scheffler, however, has separated himself in a similar manner as Woods. His points average in the world ranking is more than double that of Rory McIlroy at No. 2. This is his 171st week in a row at No. 1 in the world. Woods holds the record with 281 consecutive weeks at No. 1. A milestone that for years looks untouchable is now at least thinkable. Practice makes close to perfect for Scheffler There is not much drama with Scheffler, and he likes it that way. His obsession is such that he once said he had to force himself to find something other than golf to think about. Having two young boys have helped. “Part of what’s great about golf and part of what’s very frustrating about golf is it’s kind of an endless puzzle you’re always trying to solve,” Scheffler said. “I feel like in order to become good at this game, you have to really enjoy the harder parts of it, the stuff that’s a little bit more mundane.” For Scheffler, that would be the first 10 minutes on the stationary bike. Cardio work is not his favorite. Neither is a cold plunge at 5:30 a.m. “Do I want to go in there and freeze? No, but I do it,” he said in January. Practice, however, doesn’t get old. Neither does competing. His caddie, Ted Scott, once told of a round they played at Cypress Point early in 2025. Scheffler was returning from slicing open his right hand when he tried to use a wine glass to cut ravioli. He showed Scott no mercy that day, prompting the caddie to say, “Scottie don’t play games when he’s playing games.” It’s all about getting the most out of every day, from the cold plunge to the bike to the range to the first tee. Scheffler is relentless and it’s a matter of how long he can keep up this pace. “I don’t feel like I take days off. I’m highly competitive, and I’m very proud of being able to have the consistent results I’ve had over the years,” he said. “I feel like it’s a gift to play out here on the PGA Tour, and I don’t want to take it for granted. ... I don’t want to look back at the end of my career and feel like I could have done more in order to play well.” Add favorite players, teams, and leagues with an NBCUniversal Profile Continue

articles.title: Palace sign Honest Ahanor on loan
articles.excerpt: Crystal Palace are delighted to announce the loan signing of talented young defender Honest Ahanor.
articles.source_type: Sage press conferences, named XIs, injury updates
articles.body: Palace sign Honest Ahanor on loan Skip navigation Palace sign Honest Ahanor on loan Announcement 1 day ago Crystal Palace are delighted to announce the loan signing of talented young defender Honest Ahanor. A senior Italy international at just 18-years-old, Ahanor joins Palace on loan from Atalanta until the end of the 2026/27 season. The left-footed defender came through Genoa’s youth system and made his senior debut in Serie A as a 16-year-old, starting against Juventus in September 2024. Having featured six times for Genoa, Ahanor last summer transferred to Atalanta, where he has since played 35 times in all competitions – including nine times in the UEFA Champions League. The teenager impressed to such an extent that, in June, Ahanor won his first two senior international caps for Italy, keeping clean sheets in wins against both Luxembourg and Greece. Ahanor said upon joining: “I'm very happy to be here and to be a part of this great family. "To be at one of the best clubs for young players in the Premier League is something which makes me grateful and excited." Chairman Steve Parish said: “Honest is an exciting young talent whose arrival offers further competition for places ahead of another European campaign at Selhurst Park. "We are pleased to have him with us in South London.” Related News Announcement Club First-team Signings Honest Ahanor Related News More News

articles.title: First Interview: Ahanor sets out target for Palace
articles.excerpt: Honest Ahanor is targeting more continental glory for Crystal Palace this season, in his first interview after joining on loan from Atalanta.
articles.source_type: Sage press conferences, named XIs, injury updates
articles.body: First Interview: Ahanor sets out target for Palace Skip navigation First Interview: Ahanor sets out target for Palace Video 1 day ago Honest Ahanor is targeting more continental glory for Crystal Palace this season, in his first interview after joining on loan from Atalanta. Speaking to Palace TV, the talented 18-year-old defender believes the Eagles can build upon their recent successes in the FA Cup and UEFA Conference League with Europa League glory this season – and wants to play a key part in helping them do so. Ahanor said upon signing: “I'm really excited to be here. The Premier League is one of the most important leagues in the world. “To be at one of the best clubs for young players in this league is something which makes me grateful and happy. “To come here on loan, and try to be the best player I can in this league, is something which makes me grateful. “I think that for the team, the important thing is to be top – to do our best. Last year, Crystal Palace won the Conference League. This year, we're going to play in the Europa League. "We're going to try to get to the final and try, maybe, to win the cup – why not?!” Quote Icons I hope that we can... do a lot of things together Honest Ahanor Ahanor has some impressive credentials to his name despite his tender years, having spent much of his career thus far playing up the age groups – culminating in him playing 35 times for Atalanta last season, including nine times in the UEFA Champions League. The teenager said of his own game: “I think that from a young age, I'm very calm. I'm very hungry about football. I like to play. I like to let all the people feel my passion. “I hope to play in the next few weeks at the stadium, to feel the passion of the fans and to be with them. “I think that for all players, the passion of the fans is really important. To feel the club, to feel the shirt, to feel all the city… it's something that can improve you, improve the team to keep working, to try to improve. “I hope soon to play in the stadium, to feel the passion of the fans. I hope that we can be a family and try to do a lot of things together.” You can watch Ahanor’s first full Palace TV interview above! September 1 257 comments 1 September 2026 257 comments As Manchester City prepare to host Coventry City in Gameweek 3, many Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers are set to deploy the Triple Captain chip on Erling Haaland (£15.5m). Indeed, the leading chip in our Gameweek 3 poll is the Triple Captain . Around 30% of responders say they’re playing that chip this week. Here, we take a look at some of the pros and cons of using the Triple Captain chip on Haaland in Gameweek 3. Cherki, Mbeumo, Newcastle players: Buy, keep or sell in Gameweek 3? Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. PROS ALREADY OFF THE MARK Haaland is up and running. He scored twice in the 4-1 away victory at Crystal Palace in Gameweek 2. First, he found the net with a looping header, before a powerhouse finish late on. Prior to that, he blanked at home to Bournemouth, but on another day, he scores plenty. With no signs of rustiness after the World Cup, Haaland has recorded nine shots in the box in the first two Gameweeks, the most of any player in FPL. Above: Erling Haaland’s shot map in 2026/27 HOME COMFORTS Haaland is usually a reliable option on home turf. Under Pep Guardiola last season, he amassed 120 points, with 15 goals and four assists in 17 matches at the Etihad Stadium. In that period, he supplied six double-digit hauls and averaged 7.4 points per match. Paired with elite underlying numbers, the Norwegian penalty-taker probably has the best Triple Captain credentials of any player. NEWLY-PROMOTED OPPOSITION Moreover, it’s newly-promoted Coventry at home in Gameweek 3. Frank Lampard’s men have lost both of their first two matches, having conceded four times to Arsenal and Hull City. They’ve failed to find the net, too. In truth, Coventry’s start to the 2026/27 season hasn’t been terrible, but they have lacked physicality and goal threat, a concern ahead of Saturday’s trip to City. It also sounds like playmaker Rayan Cherki (£7.7m) will be going all-out to assist Haaland in this match. “When I saw Enzo [Maresca] was going to change me, I didn’t like that and I need to show them that I want to play and want to score and give assists for Erling. Today I didn’t give a lot of balls for him [Haaland]. The next time I want to give Erling a lot of balls.” – Rayan Cherki in Gameweek 2 The chance that Haaland may get a Double Gameweek in the first half of the season is extremely unlikely, so using the Triple Captain chip at home to newly-promoted opposition looks like a solid play. TAKE ON THE WILDCARDERS This is a simple one. Plenty of engaged Fantasy managers are on a Wildcard this week, mostly those who opted not to start with Haaland. They can’t Triple Captain him because they are already playing a chip, so this could be an opportunity to take them on. GOOD XMINS Haaland has completed the full 90 minutes in both matches so far this season. That might not be the case later in the season, especially when you factor in Europe. For example, City host Ipswich in Gameweek 7. But on either side of that encounter, they have Champions League fixtures against Paris Saint-Germain and AEK Athens, followed by an early Saturday kick-off away at Aston Villa. His minutes are probably going to be more uncertain, then. articles.title: City complete Enzo Fernández signing from Chelsea
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: City complete Enzo Fernández signing from Chelsea Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Manchester City have completed the signing of Enzo Fernández from Chelsea on a five-year contract. The Argentina international’s deal means he will remain at the Etihad Stadium until the summer of 2031. At just 25, Fernández is armed with a wealth of top-level experience, having won four major trophies during his time playing on homeland with both Defensa y Justicia and River Plate, before helping Benfica on their way to Primeira Liga success and becoming a key member of the Chelsea team that won the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup in 2025. Indeed, during his time in west London he developed a reputation as one of the most technically gifted central midfielders in the Premier League. And at international level, he won the 2022 World Cup and 2024 Copa America with Argentina, before appearing in another World Cup final this summer as La Albiceleste lost to Spain in the final. Fernández says he could not be happier to have joined City at this stage of his career. On joining Manchester City, Fernández said: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times. “Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are. “I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success. “If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player. “I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here. “I want to thank Hugo, Enzo, Khaldoon and everyone at City who has made this deal possible. I want to take the faith shown in me and repay it as soon as possible.” Director of Football Hugo Viana added: “At Manchester City, we are always looking to bring in world-class players and Enzo fits the bill. “He is a complete midfielder: technically gifted, hardworking, tenacious and a goalscorer. “He is adept at playing different styles of football. He is comfortable playing a possession-based game, and he can play on the counter effectively, too. “To have played in two World Cup finals and won major trophies in multiple countries at just 25 says everything you need to know about his mentality, professionalism and technical quality. “We are delighted to bring him here and feel very strongly he will improve our team.” Everyone at City would like to send a warm welcome to Enzo and wish him well during his time here. We all look forward to seeing him play in sky blue very soon. The complete midfielder Born in Villa Bonich, San Martin, part of the Buenos Aires metropolis, Enzo Fernández was gripped by football from an early age. His family is largely made up of River Plate obsessives - in fact, he’s named after the famous River attacking midfielder Enzo Francescoli. Fernández had a ball at his feet as soon as he could and football was the only life he has ever envisaged for himself. He joined River aged just six and gradually worked his way through the youth ranks at his boyhood club, before moving to Defensa y Justicia on a two-year loan switch when he was 18. At Defensa y Justicia he played under manager Hernan Crespo, the former Parma, Inter and AC Milan striker - an icon of Argentinian football. Fernández gradually established himself as a regular and won the 2020 Copa Sudamericana and the 2021 Recopa Sudamericana. It was a transformative loan move for Fernández, who returned to River a better, more complete player and helped them win the league title in 2021. A star was truly born. European clubs were soon swarming, and it was Benfica who captured his signature, joining the Portuguese giants in the summer of 2022. Handed the No.13 shirt synonymous with club legend Eusebio, he transitioned to European football effortlessly. But it was the 2022 World Cup that saw Fernández catapulted to global fame. Argentina won their third trophy, and Fernández was exceptional. He was just 21, yet the fullness of his game became a huge talking point across football. It seemed he could do everything: a fighter, a goalscorer and a player who controls matches. As a result of his performances and just six months after moving to Portugal and with Benfica on course for title success, he made his move to the Premier League with Chelsea, where he went on to win the Europa Conference League, the FIFA Club World Cup and established himself as one of the division’s finest talents. He also won the Copa America with Argentina in 2024 and appeared in another World Cup final this summer as La Albiceleste lost to Spain in the final. He currently has 49 caps and has scored eight goals. It’s a glittering CV for a man his age. And now comes a move to Manchester City. So, what are City getting? In short, a winner and a world-class talent. Fernández is arguably the perfect modern midfielder – a player comfortable in possession, with outstanding technique, wonderful vision, a great range of passing and the ability to score goals. He gets involved in games and never shies away, a leader who thrives on big occasions and in pressure situations. His knack of arriving in the box late and getting on the end of balls is perhaps his most striking asset. He scored 15 goals and contributed seven assists for Chelsea last season in 54 games across all competitions. A matchwinner of the highest calibre. One thing is for certain: City will be a more complete proposition with Fernández in the side. Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is off to the perfect start in 2026/27 (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Few pundits or supporters could see anything other than Arsenal retaining the Premier League trophy this season before opening day. Mikel Arteta has strengthened his squad in all areas of the pitch, whilst the managerial changes at their major rivals over the last eight months have left them not yet in a position to challenge. The Spaniard’s side weren’t the most attractive title winners last term, as tension crept into their approach as they chased their first championship in 22 years, but they have started this campaign with renewed confidence. Arteta at Villa Park on Monday night (Image credit: Getty Images) Last season, Bukayo Saka , Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard all had their lowest goal contributions in the last three years, so ensuring those attackers stay injury-free will naturally make some improvement. However, there are also clear indications that they are evolving stylistically, with new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis adding more creativity. Back-to-back titles? You wouldn't bet against them (Image credit: Getty Images) The sample size for this season is still relatively small, but the midfield seems to be progressing the ball forward more quickly, as they show signs of greater variation in their attacks. Arsenal have only added centre-back Ezri Konsa this summer, though their full-backs are another area where they can increase their output in the final third. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Arteta likes to purchase full-backs who are comfortable in central areas, with Riccardo Calafiori, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie all having spent considerable time at centre-back throughout their careers. This enables them to not only offer cover in the centre of defence, but also make runs inside their wingers, invert into central positions in possession and provide physicality from set-pieces. Calafiori is perhaps the most interesting example, as he was one of the best centre-backs in Serie A during the 2023/24 campaign. Riccardo Calafiori (Image credit: Getty Images) Under the management of Thiago Motta at Bologna , he illustrated his ability to carry the ball forward and make line-breaking passes, whilst simultaneously intercepting opposition attacks and winning duels against robust strikers. After moving to the Emirates, he switched back to the role which he had predominantly played in his formative years at Roma At Villa Park on Bank Holiday Monday, Unai Emery had clearly devised a plan to nullify his influence, with John McGinn playing on the right-hand side directly against him. John McGinn (Image credit: Getty Images) The Scotsman was happy to track him more centrally, whilst Boubacar Kamara and Matty Cash also took on the responsibility of monitoring the Italian as he glided into their area of the pitch. However, just before the hour mark, substitute Eberechi Eze played a pass inside and Calafiori displayed his athleticism to wrap his foot around and scoop the ball into the path of Saka, who bundled it past Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. After a discussion with Arteta, Calafiori and Arsenal almost repeated the move when Eze played him in once more, only for the offside flag to be raised just after the left-back had cleverly dragged the ball past a trailing Alysson. In the 97 minute, he was the furthest Arsenal player up the pitch as his team went in search of scoring a second. The Italian has been directly involved in a goal in his last three games, including his early finish in the Community Shield against Manchester City. "It was very different," said Arteta after the match when reminded his team had lost on their last visit to the ground. "That shows our maturity, and it shows we have players who can change the momentum and understand what is needed in the game." Calafiori is one of those players, and it would be a huge surprise if he didn’t record a seasonal best for goal contributions in Arsenal’s pursuit of back-to-back titles. articles.title: Grealish returns to Everton for second loan spell

articles.body: Grealish returns to Everton for second loan spell Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Jack Grealish has joined Everton on a season-long loan deal. Having spent the 2025/26 season on loan with the Toffees, Grealish will now return to the Hill Dickinson Stadium outfit for a second successive campaign. He makes the latest move up the M62 having made 159 appearances for City, scoring 17 goals since joining in the summer of 2021. After making the move to City from Aston Villa, the England winger subsequently went on to play a key role during what proved the most successful period in the Club’s history. In that time, the 30-year-old helped City win seven major trophies, a haul that included three Premier League titles, the FA Cup, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup. Grealish’s maiden season at the Club in 2021/22 saw him play his part as City claimed what was a fourth Premier League title under Pep Guardiola with the Birmingham-born wide man featuring 39 times overall. However, his Etihad career truly took flight the following term with Grealish going on to prove a key component of the side that secured the historic Treble of Premier League, FA Cup and a maiden UEFA Champions League success. Grealish started both the 2023 FA Cup final where City beat Manchester United 2-1 and 2023 UEFA Champions League final which saw the Blues memorably beat Inter 1-0 to claim a first European Cup and with it the Treble. More notable success was to follow for the attacking winger in 2023/24. Grealish was part of the City teams that lifted both the 2023 UEFA Super Cup and 2023 FIFA Club World Cup, in the process becoming the first English side to secure the Big Five of league, FA Cup, Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World in the same calendar year. And another memorable season was capped with Grealish helping City create yet more history by becoming the first English men’s side to win four Premier League titles in a row. A further 32 appearances followed in what proved a frustrating 2024/25 season for City before Grealish then spent the 2056/26 campaign on loan at fellow Premier League side Everton where he made 22 appearances in total before a foot injury cut short his campaign. Everyone at Manchester City would like to wish Jack the very best of luck during his time at Everton. articles.title: Ndiaye signs for City
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: Ndiaye signs for City Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Manchester City are delighted to announce the signing of Iliman Ndiaye on a five-year deal. The 26-year-old Senegal international arrives at the Etihad Stadium armed with significant Premier League experience after two years at Everton. Before that, he represented Marseille and shone in the Championship with Sheffield United during their 2022/23 promotion campaign. He has also represented his country on 44 occasions, including at the 2022 and 2026 World Cups. An attacking threat who can play on the wing or through the middle, Ndiaye is two-footed and a source of creativity and goals. Indeed, his dribbling ability has seen him garner a reputation as one of the most entertaining players in England’s top-flight. And now he’ll take his place as part of Enzo Maresca’s reshaped City squad as we look to have a successful 2026/27 season. “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. “City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up. “To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands. “It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good. “I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit. “City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.” Director of Football Hugo Viana added: “Iliman is a very talented footballer. “He’s had to work incredibly hard to reach this level and in my first conversation with him it was immediately obvious how grounded he is and the determination he has to be the best player he can be. “I’ve no doubt City fans will get a thrill seeing him in action for us. “We know this Club develops players. We make a commitment to every single player we sign that we will make them better footballers. “I am really excited to see the level Iliman can reach in the years ahead because I know for sure working with Enzo and his staff is going ensure he becomes a top-class Premier League player.” Special talent, boundless belief Iliman Ndiaye catches the eye on the football pitch. Few can match his skill and close control whether in tight spaces or one-v-one against elite Premier League defenders. And while that showmanship is a key facet of what makes him an attractive prospect, it doesn’t tell the whole story. Ndiaye’s route to the very top of the tree in European football has been unusual to say the least. Born in France, he represented his hometown of Rouen at first before moving to Marseille in the south of the country and then on to Dakar in Senegal. He then moved to London as a teenager and had trials with several of England’s biggest clubs but to no avail. Instead, he joined non-League side Boreham Wood and made something of a name for himself on the Rising Ballers YouTube channel. Son of a dancer and choreographer, it’s easy to see where his agility and flair came from. Stepovers, flicks, seal dribbles galore. But under all that was a steely determination to carve out a professional career. Eventually he was spotted by Sheffield United scouts and he had his big break. In 2022/23, he was the Blades’ Player of the Year as they sealed promotion to the top-flight before he got his move back to Marseille, who he had followed since being there as a boy. However, he was back in England 12 months later with Everton. In his two years with the Toffees, he’s regularly had fans, pundits and opponents drooling of his command of the football while City fans may recall a special strike at the Etihad Stadium on Boxing Day 2024. But now he’ll bring both that brilliance and dedication to City as he makes his latest step up.
