Andoni Iraola (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google At the start of the summer, most Liverpool supporters and observers would have identified three key areas of the team that needed addressing in the transfer market. The obvious was a winger to effectively replace Mohamed Salah. In signing Bradley Barcola, Liverpool have done that but on the opposite wing. Barcola , though, you could argue, is actually the replacement for Luis Diaz, who departed the year before. Liverpool's glaring right-back issue Trent Alexander-Arnold holds the Premier League trophy amid Liverpool's title celebrations at Anfield in May 2025 (Image credit: Getty Images) The next two positions that most supporters would have wanted to see addressed also revolved around the lack of replacing other previously departed legends. Fabinho left Liverpool three years ago now, but still his role in midfield as a defence-first player hasn’t been replaced. Have Liverpool replaced Fabinho yet? Many fans don't think so (Image credit: Getty Images) While Trent Alexander-Arnold left a year ago and no matter how hard he tries, Jeremie Frimpong simply isn’t a replacement, or even an actual right back. Liverpool, though, have gone through the summer seemingly without any desire to add either a midfielder or a right-back, despite the clear need in each instance. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Arguably it’s at right-back which is the biggest issue, although both full-back positions are areas of major concern and this was highlighted in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest - Andoni Iraola's first home game in charge. Frimpong and Milos Kerkez were hooked in the 72nd minute, with Liverpool 2-1 down at the time. Now, there are potentially several other reasons (not least youngster Trey Nyoni's impressive cameo in midfield) why Iraola’s team enjoyed their best 20 minutes of the game from that point on, but certainly a contributing factor was the full-backs being replaced. Szoboszlai can learn like Milner - and become a better midfielder Dominik Szobsozlai, as he was regularly last season, moved to right-back, immediately giving Liverpool a player who can actually put in a cross and also be defensively stronger than the player he was replacing. The Hungarian might not necessarily like playing there, but Iraola could do far worse than have the same conversation Jurgen Klopp had with James Milner in 2016 in explaining how he wanted the midfielder to be his left-back for the season ahead. A year later, Milner explained what he learned in the new position: “But at times you have to curb that and adapt to the match situation and maybe sometimes hold back a bit if the time of the game suits that. I think sensing danger early is the biggest thing to learn. When you play in midfield you’re obviously always switched on to defending.” Dominik Szoboszlai was occasionally used at right-back by Arne Slot last season (Image credit: Getty Images) Those words about “sensing danger early” are incredibly timely, with Iraola’s pre-Nottingham Forest press conference featuring a very similar message when discussing his midfield’s need to find a balance after being caught out twice by Newcastle in the opening fixture. “There are players that are very good, they’re smelling, ‘OK, there is real danger, I can’t take the risk of going (forward),” explained Iraola. “Now I think I have to stay’. “Recognising those situations is the job we have to do now.” A season at right-back, then, would actually help Szoboszlai learn that side of his game and make him a better midfielder in future. That should be the message Iraola gives him in order to get the Reds’ No. 8 to buy into the role. Would Szoboszlai particularly enjoy it? Probably not, but it’s about what’s best for the team, as Milner succinctly explained: “It’s about whatever’s best for the team and ultimately I just want to be out there playing games, contributing and helping this football club.” And if Szoboszlai has designs on becoming Liverpool captain after Virgil van Dijk departs, then a selfless season at right back would show he puts the team first and give him a new understanding of the team and overall patterns of play. Liverpool solve two issues with Szoboszlai role change Dominik Szoboszlai (Image credit: Getty Images) For Liverpool, they’d be getting a far more reliable outlet on the right, who can produce crosses like the one Szoboszlai did for Alexander Isak against Forest, which the £125 million man couldn’t get on the end of. No Liverpool player had more touches, created more chances or made more accurate crosses than Szoboszlai against Forest. He made three stat-recorded accurate crosses, while Frimpong and Kerkez made none between them. The duo attempted six, with none of them finding their target. It was a similar story against Newcastle the week before. Of course, stats on crossing is pretty flawed, a player can produce a wonderful cross but if the forward doesn’t get on the end of it, it’s recorded as a failed cross. The eye test tells us that Szoboszlai’s crossing was significantly better than Frimpong’s versus Forest. Of that there is no doubt. He can also move inside more to create numbers-up situations in midfield, again more akin to Alexander-Arnold did. Liverpool’s focus on signing attacking wingers for Iraola this summer has neglected the right-back and midfield positions, but moving Szobsozlai fixes both, at least temporarily. If Iraola is serious about getting the best out of his squad, and Szoboszlai is serious about being a team player, it’s a change that would significantly benefit Liverpool this season. TOPICS Matt Ladson Matt Ladson is the co-founder and editor of This Is Anfield, the independent Liverpool news and comment website, and covers all areas of the Reds for FourFourTwo – including transfer analysis, interviews, title wins and European trophies. As well as writing about Liverpool for FourFourTwo he also contributes to other titles including Yahoo and Bleacher Report. He is a lifelong fan of the Reds. articles.body: McCarthy says men's U21s will have learned a lot from Arsenal draw CLUB TICKETS SHOP Main Club Sponsor TICKETS SHOP McCarthy says men's U21s will have learned a lot from Arsenal draw The Gunners scored a late equaliser in Monday's Premier League 2 game. 2026-09-01T09:30+01:00 Jason McCarthy believes his players will have learned a lot after letting a slip lead against Arsenal. ð·Simon Roe. Albion menâs U21s coach Jason McCarthy was disappointed that his side could not hold out for a first victory of the season in Premier League 2 after Arsenal scored a late goal to secure a 2-2 at the American Express Elite Performance Centre on Monday. But he believes that the match will provide a good learning experience for his young players. Albion came from 1-0 down to lead 2-1 after 62 minutes thanks to goals from Younes Ibrahim and half-time substitute Bailey Palmer. But Arsenalâs own sub, Evan Mooney, tied the scores in the 88th minute. âI thought we played really well,â McCarthy said. âThe data tells me, and my eye tells me, that we were the better team against a very strong Arsenal side. So I think we can be really pleased about that. âWe probably allowed one too many transitions in the game, and that's a strength of theirs. That meant that after 75 minutes we started to fatigue, and they came into the game. Bailey Palmer came off the bench to equalise against Arsenal. ð·Paul Hazlewood âWe ended up with a very young back five, but that was a really good experience for them, and a great test and a good marker for us to see where we're at. Arsenal will be up there at the end of the season, but hopefully we will too.â The team reacted well to going behind and kept the momentum going after half time. âI thought we had really good solutions for their press in the game,â he added. âWe were very good at finding the spare man, and then changing the tempo.â A feature of Albionâs best spell was how regularly they were able to release left-back Sean Keogh down the wing in the same way that the first team have deployed Maxim De Cuyper in recent weeks. âIt's the wonderful thing about our club,â Jason said. âThere's alignment running from the first team right the way through to the younger age groups in the academy. So you're right, you can see, hopefully, through our first team into our group, some similar principles and even similar profiles of players that allow us to have alignment.â Share this post Previous Article Next Article Ticketing Chema Andres joins Albion from VfB Stuttgart 6 mins ago Amario Cozier-Duberry signs new contract and joins Middlesbrough on loan 36 mins ago Burton Albion sign Mark O'Mahony on loan 2 hours ago Latest Matias Orozco joins Castellon on season-long loan 3 hours ago Igor Julio completes permanent transfer to Burnley 3 hours ago Eiran Cashin joins Derby County on loan 4 hours ago Charlie Tasker joins Rochdale on loan 5 hours ago Freddie Simmonds signs new contract and joins AFC Wimbledon on loan 6 hours ago Date for Liverpool away game changed 6 hours ago Together Making History MAIN CLUB PARTNERS MAIN CLUB PARTNERS FOLLOW US FOLLOW US Club Men's Women's Club Men's Women's Club Men's Women's ____________________________________________________________ The official site of the Brighton & Hove Albion Football Club Company Details Policies and Reports Accessibility Modern Slavery Contact Us Careers

Vivianne Miedema of Manchester City (Image credit: Kate Green - WSL/WSL Football via Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Vivianne Miedema helped Manchester City break Chelsea’s six-year Women’s Super League winning streak last season as they claimed victory under new manager Andree Jeglertz. Manchester City claimed their first WSL title since 2016 last term, before going on to complete a domestic double by beating Brighton to lift the FA Cup. Miedema, who joined from Arsenal in 2024, says the achievement represented the culmination of a period of change at the club and something she wanted to help the City achieve when she moved from WSL rivals Arsenal. Latest Videos From FourFourTwo Watch full video here: 'People didn't expect City to do as well as we did' Miedema joined Man City two years ago after seven years with Arsenal (Image credit: Getty Images) Miedema claimed her second WSL title, having previously won with Arenal in 2019. She joined City in summer 2024 and after an injury-affected first season, last season scored 10 goals and made five assists to help City win their first league title in a decade. “Every single league title is special for different reasons,” Miedema said. Vivianne Miedema goes through on goal (Image credit: Getty Images) “For me, after having left Arsenal after seven years and moving to City, I wanted to come here and help the club win things because they hadn't done that in a while. “And my first year was tough personally with injuries, but also as a team with all the injuries we had and we didn’t get the result that we wanted to get. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “So coming back last season and doing what we did definitely felt like a full circle moment. It was really special to be part of it and to be able to celebrate the league and FA Cup win as well.” After six years of dominance, it was going to take a lot to knock Chelsea off their pedestal. But new manager Jeglertz, aided by a lack of Champions League football due to a fourth-placed finish in the 2024/25 season, helped City do just that. “Coming in last summer, there were a lot of changes, new people coming in and a new coach coming in. But I think we showed so much progress over the year. Miedema in her Arsenal days (Image credit: Getty Images) “We always believed that we could do really well, but a lot of people didn't expect us to do as well as we did. Throughout the season, we adjusted and grew and that led us to win the league and the FA Cup too. “For this year, regardless of if we are the champions or if we were chasing it, it doesn’t change our goals. Some of the girls haven’t been in this position before and it will be different. “And looking at all the signings that other clubs are making, I think the league is going to be extremely exciting to see how it's going to pan out.” Miedema (R) swaps shirts with Bournemouth's Kenni (L) (Image credit: Charlie Crowhurst - The FA/The FA via Getty Images) 'Isn't that why we love football?' This year, the league has expanded by two teams to a field of 14 teams. A number of high profile players have also joined the WSL this season, something Miedema says speaks volumes of where the league is at. “It’s amazing to see that so many big players want to come play in England and that the league has increased by two teams as well,” she added. “It’s only going to get more exciting and more difficult to actually win it. To be in the league now and try to be successful again is going to be extremely difficult. But isnt’t that why we love football? “That’s the reason every good player wants to come to England, because you want to measure yourself against the best.” After a season away from Champions League football, City will be back competing against Europe’s best. “I’m really excited to be back but it's going to be tough because you're going to be travelling a lot, you're going to be playing a lot of games. “I think some of the girls will have to get used to it. But it's a competition you want to be playing and you want to measure yourself with the best in Europe. “I can't wait to see how we do in the Champions League because it’s a completely different challenge to playing in the WSL.” TOPICS Ayisha Gulati Women's Football Writer Ayisha Gulati is the women's football writer at FourFourTwo . Fresh from a summer covering the Lionesses’ triumphant Euro 2025 campaign in Switzerland, she brings a passion for all things WSL, UWCL, and international women’s football. She has interviewed names including Alessia Russo and Aitana Bonmati and enjoys telling stories that capture the excitement on and off the pitch. articles.title: Ndiaye: I want to get fans off their seat and help City win games
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: Ndiaye: I want to get fans off their seat and help City win games Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd New signing Iliman Ndiaye says he’s keen to entertain City fans while winning games of football. The 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a five-year deal at the Etihad Stadium and follows the likes of Elliot Anderson, Gerónimo Rulli, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan in bolstering Enzo Maresca’s young, hungry squad. A prodigiously talented attacking midfielder who can play on either wing, Ndiaye has garnered a reputation as one of the most enjoyable players to watch in the Premier League over the last two terms at Everton. Asked in his first City Studios interview to describe the way he plays, Ndiaye lit up. “A really skilful player who likes to dribble,” he began. “I like to get fans off their seat but most importantly, to help the team win. And by using my best attributes, I feel like I can do that here.” Our new man took an unusual route to the top of the game. Growing up in northern France, he initially moved to Marseille in the south of the country before heading on to Dakar in Senegal. He then came to the UK, where he started playing for Boreham Wood and with the Rising Ballers before starting his path in the professional game at 19. With all that in mind, Ndiaye credits his dad – a dancer and choreographer - with building a lot of the foundations for the way he dribbles and moves on the pitch. “With my dad, I’ve been practicing it since I was young. Obviously until now, it’s natural. Whatever I do, it comes from everything I was doing when I was younger,” he said. “I was really keen on that dribbling side, watching the best dribblers in the world on tapes and then just practicing it on the pitch with my dad. “Pele. Maradona. Zidane. Messi. All these dribbling players. Obviously Neymar, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo the Brazilian. All the best ones. “If you want to be the best you have to look at what the best people do and that’s where my dribbling is coming from. “My dad has been really important. From my first training. From my first team in France. “He’s always been by my side, with my mum, with my sisters, they’ve always been there and had that belief in me that one day I could make it. “Obviously they believed what I believed too in me wanting to be one of the best players in the world, reaching the top level, so they’ve been really important for me and they’ve helped me get to where I am today.” Ndiaye enjoyed a strong relationship with Everton fans and believes it’s vital that the players and fans work together if a side is to be successful. “It’s really important,” he stated. “They help you on the pitch, you help each other, they give you a boost and fire. “As much as you already have that fire to win for the team, you want to win for the fans. You want to see them happy and be able to connect with them.” Share More like this Topics News Men's Team Iliman Ndiaye New signing Further reading Most read Update: Vivianne Miedema City seal signing of winger Allan Elias Manchester City and PUMA unveil the 2026/27 Third Kit Pre-Match Collection Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! articles.title: Ndiaye: My heart was set on joining City
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: Ndiaye: My heart was set on joining City Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd New signing Iliman Ndiaye has expressed his joy at sealing a summer transfer deadline day move to the Etihad, declaring: ‘There was nothing else I wanted other than to join Manchester City.’ The Senegalese international has become City’s latest 2026 summer recruit, further bolstering Enzo Maresca’s exciting new-look squad after sealing a move from Everton where he has shone bright for the past few seasons. The 26-year-old attacking midfielder/winger has signed a five-year contract, one that will keep him at City through to the summer of 2031. After putting pen to paper on the deal, Ndiaye revealed how immensely proud he was to have joined City. And he revealed that after speaking with both manager Enzo Maresca and Director of Football Hugo Viana, his heart had been set on coming to the Etihad and how he was convinced he and City made for the perfect fit. “It’s easy to make the decision about whether you want to be at Manchester City or not,” Ndiaye said. “You can see the recent history; you want to be part of that project. “They talked to me about where we could go, what we could achieve with me in the team, and I was interested from the beginning. “There was nothing else that I wanted other than joining Manchester City. “Obviously, you want to be part of this new project. I’ve seen recently what they’ve been doing, and I feel like I will fit right in it. “I’m super excited to start. “It’s an unbelievable moment. I’ve worked so hard to get to this point and I’m super excited and really grateful for this opportunity.” Now that he has clinched the move up the M62, Ndiaye said his hopes and ambitions were simple and clearcut. Namely to play his part in helping the Club go on to achieve even more silverware looking both to this season and beyond. “Wherever you are, you want to win games and trophies,” Ndiaye pointed out. “You have your solo targets as well but most importantly; it’s the team target. “When you think about the team, if you work hard, it will come naturally. “If you have the mindset to do it for the team and the fans, then the targets will come by itself.” Share More like this Topics News Men's Team Iliman Ndiaye Manchester City New signing Further reading Most read Update: Vivianne Miedema City seal signing of winger Allan Elias Manchester City and PUMA unveil the 2026/27 Third Kit Pre-Match Collection Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! articles.title: 10 things you might not know about Iliman Ndiaye
articles.source_type: Club-published FPL Scout Report each gameweek, team news, kick-off info
articles.body: 10 things you might not know about Iliman Ndiaye Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd Iliman Ndiaye is a City player! The versatile forward has joined City after two years at Everton. Here’s a few things to help you get to know our new man a little better… Birthplace Ndiaye hails from Rouen in the north west of France. The city was one of the most powerful in Europe during medieval times and was where Joan of Arc was tried and executed. It remains an architectural hotspot for tourists, despite being damaged during World War II. Ndiaye spent the first 11 years of his life there before moving to the south of France with Marseille and then to Senegal as a teenager. Unusual route Our new man has taken the path less trodden to the very top table of European football. After returning to Europe following two years as a teenager in Dakar, he wound up in the youth side at non-league north London outfit Boreham Wood. That’s where he got his first contract before catching the eye of Sheffield United scouts and then eventually moving on to Marseille and Everton. Bouncing back Beyond that very specific path into football, Ndiaye has had to have a thick skin throughout his life. In an interview with Everton last year, he told of all the clubs who passed up the opportunity to sign him as a youngster. “I went to trial with Southampton, Reading, Tottenham, Chelsea, Crystal Palace. I used to be very small and they said they had similar players. People told my dad to his face that I will never be a football player.” Moves like Ndiaye Iliman is the son of a dancer and choreographer and, in an interview with Sky Sports, our new man put a lot of his silky skills and eccentric movements with the ball at his feet down to his dad’s influence. “He told me everything I know,” he said. “With his dancing and choreography, he added it into the way I do things like stepovers. He used to tell me when you do stepovers, your body can still go like this and that.” Big family Ndiaye is one of nine siblings. He shared a house with seven sisters and one brother growing up but he says that shaped a lot of who he has become. “Family is important to me,” he said in an interview with Everton. “They’ve always been behind me through everything. The hard times and the good times and now I’ve got my own family. I love it.” Rising Ballers Ndiaye also spent time with Rising Ballers, the famous YouTube team, during his development. During one particular video with them seven years ago, footage of his famous skills and mind-blowing control of the ball can be seen on a cage in London. In that video, he credits his time in Senegal and the uneven surfaces there with teaching him how to adapt to unfamiliar and difficult conditions. Choices Born in France to a Senegalese father and French mother, Ndiaye could have represented either nation. However, he chose Senegal and has gone on to play for them 44 times since his debut in 2022. In that time, they’ve finished third at AFCON 2024 and he’s been to both the 2022 and 2026 World Cups. Breakthrough year As City were winning an historic Treble in 2022/23, Ndiaye was enjoying a season that very much put him on the map. He was named in the Championship Team of the Year and as Sheffield United’s Player of the Year as the Blades earned promotion to the top-flight. There was plenty of excitement at Bramall Lane about how he’d fare in the Premier League but he wouldn’t get the chance to show what he could do, leaving for Marseille that summer. Record v City City fans may remember one stunning goal that Ndiaye struck at the Etihad Stadium. With City 1-0 up on Boxing Day in 2024, Ndiaye controlled a cross with his right foot, allowed it to bounce and immediately took a snapshot with the same peg. It flew into the top corner before anyone could react and was a perfect example of the unorthodox but wildly entertaining way in which he plays the game. That’s his only goal in five games against us – four coming for Everton and one for Sheffield United. Squad number history Ndiaye has worn lots of different squad numbers during his career. He’s had 10 since arriving at Everton in the summer of 2024 but before that, he wore 29 at Marseille and Sheffield United as well as 25 with Boreham Wood. For Senegal, he dons the number 13. articles.body: Events Explainer: Be part of Sunday's season opener against Birmingham! Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd The wait is over... City are back in WSL action at the Joie Stadium this Sunday! Join us from 14:30 (UK) as the WSL and WSL 2 champions lock horns on a memorable opening weekend of the campaign. City ended the 2025/26 campaign with a 100% home record and the best attacking record in the division, but Birmingham will be keen to cause an upset on their return to the top flight after a four-year hiatus. get your City v Birmingham tickets It promises to be a thrilling afternoon of action and entertainment both on and off the pitch. With limited tickets remaining, make sure you secure your seat and be part of the moment, with a rundown of how the day will look below... 13:00 – Gates open Arrive early to make the most of everything happening around the stadium before kick-off. Head under the Jumbo Screen as soon as the gates open, where our Playmakers will be looking for supporters to take part in some exciting pre-match activations on the pitch. You could even find yourself at the heart of the matchday entertainment! We have two Fan Zones this weekend, each offering something different... Behind the West Stand – Kids Fanzone Perfect for younger fans, with face painting, inflatables, Dream Team activities and plenty of football fun. Behind the South Stand – NEW - Additional Fanzone A dedicated space for those fans looking for something a little different. Enjoy our food market with plenty of snacks refreshments available, including sweet treats and coffee options. There are also activities for everyone to enjoy, including a photobooth and the chance to see both of the WSL and FA Cup trophies up close! 13:45 – Team News Revealed Be in your seat as City’s first starting XI of the season is revealed live inside the stadium, followed by a pre-match chat with Head Coach Andrée Jeglertz. You’ll also be among the first to discover our brand-new matchday look for the 2026/27 season... a fresh look to represent an exciting new chapter in our history! 13:50 – Warm-ups begin The players take to the pitch to begin their preparations, accompanied by music from our resident DJ Laura Dean. For this game, we are also giving fans the chance to help soundtrack matchdays by suggesting the songs you’d love to hear at the Joie Stadium by submitting songs here: Create your playlist for City v Birmingham 🎵 Some of our players’ favourite tracks will also be included throughout the pre-match build-up, so stay tuned to hear an exciting mix of tracks across the afternoon! 14:00 – City Quiz returns Don’t miss our pre-match quiz either, where one lucky supporter could win a signed Manchester City shirt! Each quiz focuses on one of our players... can you answer the most questions correctly and in the shortest amount of time to come out on top? 14:15 – The countdown begins As kick-off approaches, make sure you’re in your seat for an exclusive pre-match ceremony. Enjoy a reminder of the City team, our exciting new blue button and a special ceremony to welcome the reigning WSL champions, before the players take to the field. It’s a moment you’ll want to experience from the stands, so make sure you’re ready for the action in plenty of time! 14:30 – Kick-off Watch the WSL champions in action as we look to get our defence of the title off to a flying start! Half-time – Revolut Wheel of Wishes returns The popular Revolut Wheel of Wishes is back! One lucky fan will have the opportunity to spin the wheel at half-time and win some incredible prizes. To be in with a chance of taking part, make sure you have a Revolut account and submit your RevTag before Thursday. Coming with little ones? Don’t miss our Joie Buggy Park Our free Joie Buggy Park is available once again, allowing supporters to safely leave their prams during the match before collecting them after full-time. The dedicated area is available below the West Stand at the Joie Stadium. Food and drink There will be a wide range of food and drink options available throughout the Joie Stadium, with additional vendors around the concourse to help you fuel your matchday. Following the successful trial last season, supporters can once again enjoy alcohol inside the seating bowl, making it the perfect way to spend a Sunday afternoon. Please note that supporters seated in Blocks W1, W2 and W3 are located within the Alcohol-Free Zone and alcohol cannot be taken into these areas. Sun 06 Sep Barclays WSL Man City 14:30 BST Birmingham Plan your visit With strong demand expected for our opening fixture, don’t leave it too late to secure your ticket and make sure you’ve planned your trip in advance. articles.body: Etihad Player of the Month: August nominees revealed! Manchester City Official App Manchester City FC Ltd It’s the first Etihad Player of the Month vote of the 2026/27 season! August ushered in a new era as Enzo Maresca took charge of his first matches since replacing Pep Guardiola as City boss. The Italian has overseen Premier League victories over Bournemouth and Crystal Palace since the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal. Here are our three nominees this month… Rayan Cherki With star turns in both of our league wins, Cherki has had a fine start to his second campaign in England. He came on in the second half of the opening weekend clash with Bournemouth with City behind in the game. Two assists later, including a bamboozling run and pass for Joško Gvardiol’s late winner, and the game was flipped. He started a few days later at Crystal Palace and ran the show from the off, with two stunning goals playing a big role in our 4-1 win. Marc Guéhi Guéhi’s role in the Bournemouth game was perhaps Maresca’s biggest tactical tweak so far. A centre-back by trade, he appeared in midfield alongside new man Elliot Anderson and looked at home throughout, even cropping up with the equaliser. He was back in his trusty defensive role at Selhurst Park. It might have been his former stomping ground, but Guéhi was pivotal to City’s victory over his previous employers. Joško Gvardiol Despite starting from left-back, Gvardiol remains a real headache for opposition defences. Marauding forward to provide an extra man in attack, the Croatian looks so at home in the final third. He demonstrated that with his composed finish late on to beat Bournemouth as well as picking up an assist against Crystal Palace, all while doing his due diligence out of possession. The poll is open until 17:00 (UK) on Friday, when we’ll reveal your winner. Cast your vote below! Have your say on who should win PGA Tour's Player of the Year award Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Have your say! Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy and Matt Fitzpatrick among names who could claim honour Tuesday 1 September 2026 11:32, UK Image: Who will be crowned the 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year? Rory McIlroy insists it’s 'all to play for' in the race to be crowned PGA Tour Player of the Year, but who is still in contention for the coveted Jack Nicklaus Award? Ahead of the BMW Championship, McIlroy said there was 'no chance' he should be considered, despite defending his title at The Masters and placing tied-for-fourth at the Tour Championship. Scottie Scheffler has won the award - determined by a vote by PGA Tour members - each of the last four seasons and is in the running to win his fifth consecutive title, after the world No 1 secured a three-stroke victory at the Tour Championship on August 30 , to claim his second FedExCup title How Scheffler clinched thrilling FedExCup victory Scheffler overtakes Woods in PGA Tour career money list Latest PGA Tour news, reports and highlights Get Sky Sports stream golf with no contract Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After defending his Masters title and finishing tied-fourth at the Tour Championship, Rory McIlroy finds himself in the mix to be crowned the Player of the Year Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young are all multiple winners on the PGA Tour in 2026 and are also in contention to win the coveted award. The Brazilian moves to the Spotify Camp Nou in a deal worth £8.6m (€10m), where he has penned a deal until June 2029. The Jesus deal may not end Barcelona's pursuit of Julian Alvarez. Sky Sports News has been told they are completely separate. Jesus, who joined Arsenal from Manchester City in a £45m deal four years ago, had also been subject of interest from Napoli. He scored 32 goals in 123 appearances for Arsenal, but managed just three Premier League starts last season. The 29-year-old missed most of last year after picking up a knee injury in a January 2025 FA Cup tie against Manchester United. Jesus has made 64 international appearances for Brazil but has not featured for the Selecao since November 2023. Also See: Transfer Centre LIVE on your phone! Papers - latest headlines Premier League ins and outs Download the Sky Sports App Jesus delights at 'dream' move Speaking at his Barcelona unveiling, Jesus expressed his delight at the move having been training separately from his team-mates at Arsenal due to the uncertainty surrounding his future. "I have strong faith in God and I knew that if I did things well, anything could happen," he said. "I have always been a guy who respects everyone so I thought things would turn out well. I was working very hard at Arsenal, separately from the other players of course. "I kept giving my best because I knew a good thing would happen, and now it's happened. A week ago, I received the message that it could happen. When I started to think it was a real possibility, it made me very excited and made me want to be here a lot." Jesus confirmed he spoke to countryman Raphinha and former Manchester City team-mates Joao Cancelo, Rodri and Eric Garcia when finalising the move. "They only had good things to say about Barcelona, the dressing room, the players, the staff, the coaching," he added. "I have the opportunity now to be here at Barca now. I had the opportunity 10 years ago, but life took me in a different direction. But now, I can be here. It's a dream for me." Arsenal confirm Vieira sale Arsenal also confirmed the sale of Fabio Vieira Hamburg on Deadline Day. The deal for the midfielder is worth £7.7m. The Gunners signed Vieira from Porto for up to £34m in June 2022. articles.title: Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku
articles.source_type: Team news, season previews, transfer and injury reporting
articles.body: Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku As Newcastle United complete the £51m signing of Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille, Adam Bate speaks to the player's former coach to find out what makes the Belgian forward so good: "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. He is very explosive, very fast" Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 1 September 2026 23:05, UK Image: Belgium international Matias Fernandez-Pardo is making the move to the Premier League with Newcastle United There is one special quality that will have convinced Newcastle United that Matias Fernandez-Pardo can thrive in the Premier League. "He is very explosive, very fast," his former coach Arnar Vidarsson tells Sky Sports . "He has this unbelievable power." Indeed, Vidarsson, who worked with Fernandez-Pardo at Gent prior to his move to Lille, sees similarities with another Belgian winger who has become a Premier League star. "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. They have a similar profile," he says. "It is that power, that speed, that ability to go past people without needing space." That Doku trademark of slowing the defender down and then suddenly speeding up? He has it too. "Matias can go past people in one or two metres because of this explosiveness." Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports analyses Newcastle's new signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo Got Sky? Watch Premier League LIVE on your phone No Sky? Get Sky Sports stream with no contract on NOW The reason why Newcastle have been persuaded to pay £51m to bring the 21-year-old Belgium international to the Premier League is that Fernandez-Pardo has shown that he can bring goals too. He has evolved into more of a forward than a winger. Image: Matias Fernandez-Pardo's heat map and shot map for Lille in European competition "In my opinion, his best position is central," says Vidarsson. "That is how he scored most of his goals and how Lille scouted him in his last season with Gent." It happened fast. He made his full league debut in March 2024 and played his last game for the club that August. A run of eight goals in 11 games did that. "The coach started to use him as a striker. Before that, he had always been on the wing. He made a good decision because Matias started to score a lot. After that spell playing centrally, there was big interest in him." Vidarsson's relationship with Fernandez-Pardo pre-dates that first-team breakthrough. The Icelandic coach, now working in coach development for FIFA, was responsible for talent management at Gent as well as working with the development squad there. Also See: Download the Sky Sports app Transfer Centre LIVE! Get Sky Sports Stream Sky Sports with NOW He remembers a quiet boy, one well supported by his family. "His relationship with his father was strong. His father was all in, basically his assistant, driving him everywhere and taking good care of him. Matias did not talk too much." He came alive on the pitch. The young Fernandez-Pardo was a wide player for Gent's second team. It was a learning process. "His decision-making on the wing was not always the best," Vidarsson recalls. "That is something that Doku, for example, also had when he was at Anderlecht." Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matias Fernandez-Pardo arrives in Newcastle ahead of his move from Lille He caveats it by saying this was a few years ago. "Players develop. But he was going past people and not knowing when to cross, when to cut inside, when to go outside, when to find space in behind. And sometimes he did not have the mentality to run for the team." Vidarsson puts that down to the fact that he had probably outgrown the level and was itching for the first-team opportunity that he soon seized. "That is typical of a young player who was being asked to go from the first team to play for the second team." The breakthrough came in early 2024 when Gent sold three attacking players for significant sums of money. Malick Fofana and Gift Orban both moved to Lyon. Hugo Cuypers was sold to Chicago Fire. "That freed up the space for Matias to play," he explains. The rest is history and Fernandez-Pardo earned his own switch that summer. "I think it was a great move for him to go to Lille," says Vidarsson. After a promising first season adjusting to the level, he played a key role in qualifying Lille for the Champions League. Given that achievement, there is some surprise within football that Fernandez-Pardo has been so keen to leave. Certainly, there is a feeling that playing a season of Champions League football with the French club would have aided his development. Vidarsson himself preaches caution in expecting too much on Tyneside, at least in the short term. "I would say they are taking, not a risk, but let's say giving him an opportunity," he says, rather diplomatically. This is another step up for him, after all. "He has the potential but I really do believe that he will need one season to adapt before he can shine and become a top player in the Premier League. Because everything in the Premier League is faster, more intense. Everything there happens at a faster tempo." There is a belief that Matthias Jaissle's vertical style of play could suit Fernandez-Pardo - if he is used in the channel rather than just stuck out on the wing. "It will probably always be better for Matias to play in a system as one of two strikers," argues Vidarsson. "Because of his speed, he needs space. On the wing, you can direct him in one direction and then he becomes a little easier to mark." That might change, of course. In part, because he can "grow into a bigger club, into a bigger environment" at Newcastle. Transfer Centre LIVE! Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want! The World Cup felt like a missed opportunity as Fernandez-Pardo was restricted to just three appearances off the bench for Belgium. Tired of waiting, he has pushed for the club move that he craved and the chance now to play in the Premier League. There is much to learn and much to prove. But Newcastle supporters have reason to be excited. Not because Fernandez-Pardo is the finished article, but because he isn't. And because he possesses that one quality that means he always has the capacity to excite. "What he has, of course, is that special thing that a lot of clubs are looking for in modern football, that speed, that ability to go past people and do something in small spaces. He has those attributes and they are really difficult to create. You are just born with it." Play Super 6 to win £1m! Play Super 6 for a chance to win £1m! Enter for free. Adingra SUN 4.9m 28/08 Chadi Riad CRY 4.4m 28/08 Cherki MCI 7.6m Scout Picks - Bus Team FPL Gameweek 3 early Scout Picks: Piling up on Man City August 31 421 comments 31 August 2026 421 comments We’ve put together our Scout Picks ‘bus team’ for Gameweek 3 of Fantasy Premier League (FPL). The upcoming Scout Squad nominations , as well as the pre-match press conferences, will help shape our finalised picks. However, this early draft, at the very least, offers an insight into the players and teams who will be under consideration. There are, as ever, certain restrictions for our squad: An £83.0m overall budget for our starting XI An overall squad limit of £100.0m No more than three players per team A reminder, too, that the Scout Picks are for the upcoming Gameweek in isolation. GAMEWEEK 3 FIXTURES Using our free-to-all ticker, here is the Gameweek 3 difficulty ranking – although unbeaten Hull City may have something to say about this… THE LIKELY LADS Although he has a trickier fixture away at Everton, Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) has to be here after Sunday’s epic haul . It sent a reminder to FPL managers about why he should never be easily overlooked, nor confidently sold. The fact that Everton have conceded a league-second-worst 10 big chances in the first two Gameweeks is also in Bruno’s favour. Not that there’ll be any captaincy debate this week, as Erling Haaland (£15.5m) surely dominates the armband discussion, at home to Coventry City. In fact, the main questions are whether it’s time to activate Triple Captain, and which Manchester City colleagues should complete a triple-up. Antoine Semenyo (£8.5m) very likely starts, as he always does, but Phil Foden (£7.0m) and Rayan Cherki (£7.6m) are cheaper – and the latter is setting FPL pulses racing. As this is a one-week lineup, we’ll go with Cherki – but be careful about permanently buying the Frenchman. He didn’t start in Gameweek 1, and spoke on Friday night about nearly being substituted at half-time . It’s a sign of Cherki’s quality that he’s already on two goals and two assists, but the possible purchase of Cody Gakpo (£7.0m) could ultimately mean he and Foden will be fighting for the same ‘number 10’ role. Sticking with Enzo Maresca’s lot, there’ll be some defensive coverage too. Ideally, an ‘out of position’ Nico O’Reilly (£6.5m), but Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m) saves a bit of money and, in fairness, has delivered an attacking return in both outings. IN CONTENTION Gameweek 1’s top scorer, Maxim De Cuyper (£4.6m), remained on the wing against Chelsea. Not that he was involved in Brighton and Hove Albion’s three goals, but next up is Leeds United and Coventry. On these days, it’ll be hard to resist such out-of-position appeal. Sticking with the Seagulls, Pascal Gross (£5.5m) helped them scrape a respectable result, having found themselves 3-0 down after 32 minutes . He assisted an own goal before heading in a stoppage-time consolation to reach 13 points. But it’s his only shot so far, and Leeds are tough to break down. The Whites have allowed only two big chances. Meanwhile, Dominik Szoboszlai (£7.0m) is ticking along nicely for owners. Scoring from the spot and securing a defensive contribution (DefCon) reward nicely showcases his ‘all-roundedness’. Liverpool attackers need considering, as Ipswich Town have just conceded five at Old Trafford. Could the as-yet-unpriced Bradley Barcola tempt anyone on his debut? We like several Brentford assets for their hosting of Sunderland. Kristoffer Ajer (£4.5m) is one of four defenders to have achieved DefCon success in both Gameweeks, while Mamadou Sangare (£5.6m) has done the same in midfield Kevin Schade (£6.0m) already boasts eight shots inside the box, and Igor Thiago (£8.0m) is the biggest expected goals (xG, -1.81) underachiever. But perhaps picking more than two of these is excessive. In 2025/26, Thiago replaced Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) as the Bees’ main striker. The latter had an awful debut campaign at Newcastle United, but seems reinvigorated under Matthias Jaissle . He already has a goal, an assist and a price rise to his name. Just be aware that the Magpies haven’t won any of their last eight league meetings with Bournemouth. Above: Recent matches between Newcastle and Bournemouth, from FotMob On Saturday, penalty-taking Morgan Gibbs-White (£7.9m) hauled at Anfield , continuing the late-season form that brought seven goals in his final seven starts. The opportunity to go against an under-construction Tottenham Hotspur is tempting. After three successive clean sheets, it’s probably still worth contemplating one Arsenal representative at the back – David Raya (£6.0m), Riccardo Calafiori (£5.6m) or the cheap-as-chips Ezri Konsa (£4.4m) – even though Chelsea have netted seven times. The Gunners still ride high in the clean sheet odds, too… With the Blues conceding five goals in two Gameweeks, might Bukayo Saka (£9.5m) make a late charge for the Picks, as well? THE LONGER SHOTS Chelsea’s goalscoring form is why it’s hard to truly say no to Joao Pedro (£7.6m), despite meeting a defensive wall. He’s bagged a goal and an assist in both matches, and the Brazilian is hard to bench with such a high ownership. Other interesting strikers include departing Blues man Nicolas Jackson (£6.5m), away to Hull City, and Gonzalo Garcia (£6.0m) at home to an increasingly poor Crystal Palace. With Fernandes and intense Man City representation, Liverpool duo Alexander Isak (£9.0m) and Virgil van Dijk (£6.5m) might be too costly. Not that the Reds are defending well anyway… they conceded twice in both outings. Finally, the alternative goalkeeper picks to Raya are Caoimhin Kelleher (£5.0m) and Zion Suzuki (£5.0m). Villa were much better defensively on Monday night, so they may have turned a corner. articles.title: Newcastle U21 0-4 Fulham U21
articles.excerpt: Fulham Under-21s made it back-to-back wins in PL2 with a 4-0 victory at Newcastle United. Our Young Whites have had no problems finding the back of the net in the first few games of the season, but we struck the perfect balance here, with a clean sheet to boot. Dan Casey and Jayden Quashie were both alive in the box in the first half, reacting quickest to loose balls to put us ahead. Quashie doubled his tally immediately after the interval, before Trialist Jose Sani scored for a third straight game with seven minutes to play. Michael Allen saved a penalty late on to cap off a complete away day display. Newcastle proved tricky opponents at Whitley Park last season, winning 3-0 in this fixture back in February, and we had an early scare as the dangerous Trevan Sanusi rattled the crossbar with a thunderous effort. But we quickly responded as Casey handed us the lead after 11 minutes. Macaulay Zepa cut inside onto his left foot and saw a shot cannon back off the post, but Casey was well placed to score the follow up. Villa’s iconic home had a slightly different look and feel to it 108 days on from the last match to be contested in B6 – against Liverpool midway through May – with North Stand renovations well underway. A part of the side’s training camp in Scotland in July, Catesby was on the bench for the Blues’ 4-0 victory over Dundee. He now links up with John Doolan’s Stanley for the maiden loan move of his career.

This title drought stretched back to the days of Arsene Wenger's Invincibles, and for former Gunners midfielder Ray Parlour - a member of that 2004 title-winning squad - the club's wait for the title only made this latest success all the sweeter. And while Parlour admits he did not fathom the idea that the club would have had to wait that long when he celebrated that last success, he believes last season's title was a fitting reward for that at the club. "It was a big relief, because if you’d said to me 22 years ago, back in 2004, that they weren’t going to win it again for such a long time, I’d have said you were mad." Ray Parlour was part of the 2003/04 Premier League-winning side (Image credit: Getty Images) Arsenal had made a habit of near-misses in recent years, registering three consecutive second-place finishes before getting over the hump last season, adding to a prior 11 top-four finishes since that 2003/04 triumph. And while Parlour is quick to praise the playing squad for the victory, he believes the credit should be shared around the club. "The owners and the people who run things behind the scenes deserve plaudits as well, because we all see how things work in football in this day and age," he continues. Arteta snapped a run of three straight second-place finishes last year (Image credit: Getty Images) Parlour is also keenly aware that patience has become increasingly rare in the modern game, with Arsenal bucking this trend and allowing Arteta to continue to build his squad despite repeated near-misses. "Most of the time, when things go wrong, or when a manager fails to win something, they don’t stay in their job. "But Arsenal really stuck by Mikel Arteta and they backed him all the way." articles.title: Boro beaten as Cherries make it two from two in Premier League 2
articles.excerpt: Goals from Harold William, Jonny Day and Dane Ndimukum meant AFC Bournemouth made it two wins out of two to start life in Premier League Two, with a 3-1 success against Middlesbrough. William’s header and Day’s neat finish put the Cherries in the box seat after just 13 minutes at Wyatt Homes Stadium, despite the latter being forced off through injury shortly after. Middlesbrough pulled a goal back through Cruz Ibeh after 52 minutes, with the Cherries left with 10 players after Eugene Nyarko was sent off just before the hour mark. But some resolute defending and two top-drawer saves from goalkeeper Mack Allan kept Alan Connell’s side in front before a slick move made it 3-1 in the 90th minute. Substitute Ndimukum applied an assured finish after meeting Remy Rees-Dottin’s neat flick on the edge of the box. Victory meant the Cherries have taken a maximum six points from their two Premier League 2 fixtures, after stepping up to Category One level this summer. They beat Chelsea in their league curtain-raiser earlier this month. AFC Bournemouth make the trip to Leicester City in the Premier League Cup on Friday (7pm kick-off). articles.title: SAFC U21 defeat at Brentford
articles.excerpt: Brentford U21 5-1 Sunderland U21 Sunderland Under-21 suffered defeat at Brentford in Premier League 2 on Monday afternoon. Kaye Furo scored a hat-trick for the hosts, with Fábio Carvalho and Riley Owen also on target. Furo opened the scoring inside 30 seconds after breaking forward on the counter-attack and finishing well. The Black Cats dominated possession for large spells of the first half, seeing more than 75% of the ball and registering four shots on target, but were unable to find an equaliser before the break. Carvalho doubled Brentford’s advantage nine minutes into the second half, calmly slotting home after Furo won possession and picked out the midfielder inside the box. Sunderland responded three minutes later through Charlie Dinsdale, who squeezed a fierce effort past the goalkeeper from an acute angle. However, Furo restored Brentford’s two-goal lead in the 67th minute, meeting Gustavo Nunes’ corner near the edge of the six-yard box and heading home. The striker completed his hat-trick five minutes from time, bringing down a high ball before advancing and finding the bottom corner. articles.body: Skip navigation Five reasons to watch Palace U21s v PSG on Wednesday (19:00 BST) Academy 31 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s begin their Premier League International Cup campaign against none other than Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday, 2nd September (19:00 BST) – and there are plenty of reasons to be at Sutton United’s Borough Sports Ground or watching live on Palace TV+! Here are five of them… Buy PSG tickets here! 1. PSG are coming to Sutton Come on, it’s PSG! The French giants are the reigning European and French champions, having won the UEFA Champions League for a second successive season and secured a fifth consecutive Ligue 1 title. Their academy was also named France’s best for 2025/26 by the French Football Federation, showcasing the remarkable talent coming through their ranks. So, while you might not get to see the likes of Ousmane Dembélé or Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, there is every chance you’ll be watching some of the next generation of Parisian stars. And you can do it all for just £1 - 2. It’s £1 to watch future stars It’s not every day you get the chance to watch a European heavyweight in South London, but you can do exactly that on Wednesday – and it’ll cost as little as £1. Season Ticket+, Gold and Junior Gold Members can also enjoy free entry to selected Academy home games, including the International Cup. So whether you’re a regular Academy supporter or have never been to a U21s game before, there’s never been a better time to give it a go. Buy PSG tickets here! Can’t make it to Sutton? You can watch the game LIVE on Palace TV+. 3. A squad full of history-makers The Young Eagles’ squad is packed with players who have enjoyed a memorable 12 months – and plenty more who are ready to make their mark. Last season’s U18 Player of the Season Chuks Okoli could feature alongside Jasper Judd, Charlie Walker-Smith, Euan Danaher and Makai Bernard-Ferguson, who were all part of the side that lifted the club’s first-ever U18 Premier League Cup. There could also be a chance to see Joel Drakes-Thomas, who became Palace’s youngest-ever Premier League player when he featured against Leeds United last season. He was one of four Young Eagles – alongside captain George King, Dean Benamar and Benji Casey – to make their senior debuts in the UEFA Conference League against KuPS. King enjoyed an especially memorable campaign, being named U21 Player of the Season, while Casey was crowned Scholar of the Year after scoring 19 goals in 18 appearances. New signing Amaari Sealey could also make his International Cup debut. The attacking midfielder joined Palace from AFC Wimbledon this summer after registering 47 goal contributions during an extraordinary 25/26 campaign in which the Dons’ U18s completed an unprecedented national quadruple. And that’s before you even consider the talent PSG will bring to Sutton. 4. Palace have history in this competition The Premier League International Cup has already produced some memorable nights for the Young Eagles – and Palace will be hoping there are more to come. The first taste of a final came in 22/23, when Palace reached the showpiece at Selhurst Park, only to suffer a 3-1 defeat to Jong PSV. A year later, they had their chance for revenge. Franco Umeh’s deflected second-half strike secured a 1-0 victory over the Dutch side, sending Palace to the trophy for the first time. After an early group-stage exit in 24/25, the Young Eagles bounced back last season, topping their group with wins over Juventus, FC Nordsjælland and Borussia Mönchengladbach. Their run eventually came to an end in the quarter-finals, where they narrowly lost to Real Sociedad. Now, PSG, PSV Eindhoven, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto await in Group C – and another European adventure is ready to begin. 5. You’ve got to be there There’s something different about watching Academy football live – and Wednesday’s clash with PSG is your first chance to watch the Young Eagles on Palace TV+ or at Sutton this season. Palace’s first two Premier League 2 fixtures have both been away from home, with the trip to Arsenal unavailable to watch live due to the Premier League broadcast blackout and the Aston Villa clash taking place on the same night as the first team’s opener against Manchester City. Now, the Young Eagles are finally coming home. It’s a chance to see Palace’s next generation up close, experience the atmosphere around the Young Eagles and watch players at the beginning of their journey towards senior football – with one of Europe’s biggest clubs providing the opposition. With four European opponents heading to Sutton this season, the Premier League International Cup offers a unique chance to see some of the continent’s biggest clubs without leaving South London. Tickets are available for as little as £1 , while you can enjoy all the action live on Palace TV+! articles.title: Everton’s Cup Clash With Wolves Rescheduled
articles.excerpt: Everton’s Carabao Cup third-round tie with Wolverhampton Wanderers at Hill Dickinson Stadium has been rescheduled for Wednesday 16 September (7.45pm kick-off). The Club had initially proposed for the fixture – previously confirmed for Wednesday 9 September – to take place on Wednesday 16 September, but Carabao Cup broadcast selections resulted in the match being scheduled a week earlier. Following Liverpool’s recent UEFA Champions League draw against Atletico Madrid at Anfield on September 9, Everton v Wolves will now take place on Wednesday 16 September. The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports +. The Toffees beat Championship side Preston North End 4-0 to advance to round three of the competition courtesy of Thierno Barry's hat-trick and Brennan Johnson's first goal for the Club. Wolves advanced the previous evening with a 2-0 win away at League One side Sheffield Wednesday, their goals coming from Saheed Olagunju and a Sil Swinkels own goal. Muñoz began his professional career in his native Colombia with Águilas Doradas, making his senior debut in 2017, before joining Atlético Nacional in 2019. A move to Europe followed in 2020 when he joined Belgian side Genk. During his time at the club, Muñoz established himself as one of the division's most effective attacking full-backs, making 122 appearances and scoring 16 goals. articles.body: Daniel Muñoz leaves Crystal Palace Skip navigation Daniel Muñoz leaves Crystal Palace Announcement 31 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace F.C. can confirm that Daniel Muñoz has completed a permanent transfer to Nottingham Forest. The Colombia international joined Palace in January 2024 and won a firm place in the hearts of supporters with 11 goals and 16 assists in 109 matches, winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and UEFA Conference League with the club. Muñoz’s impact during his time with us will go down in history, having provided the assist for Ebere Eze’s FA Cup-winning goal against Manchester City and won the Man of the Match award on that historic day. He also went on to win both the fans’ Player, and Players’ Player, of the Season awards in the 2024/25 campaign. During that season, he netted vital goals against Millwall and Brighton & Hove Albion – the latter completing Palace’s first-ever top-flight league double over our rivals. Muñoz impact continued last season as he scored the club’s first-ever goal in major continental competition against Dynamo Kyiv and went on to feature 12 times in our trophy-winning debut European campaign. Chairman Steve Parish said: “Danny has given us many magical moments down the years and rightly earned his place in the club’s history books. “Everybody at Selhurst Park thanks him for his service and wishes him well.” Related News Announcement Club First-team Related News More News

articles.title: HENRY WINTER: Everton is a footballing institution and community asset... the fact the owners nearly sold Harrison Armstrong shows a lack of understanding and arrogance
articles.excerpt: Rule one for owners: never kill hope, never ruin fans’ chance to dream. That’s what Harrison Armstrong represents to Everton fans: hope, a chance to dream. The 19-year-old midfielder is a local lad, hailing from West Derby, one of their own and fulfilling their own dreams by pulling on the famous royal blue shirt of the club they love. Rule two for owners: don’t sell cherished home-grown talent. Evertonians gathered at the Vitality on Saturday made their anger about the proposed sale of Armstrong to Nottingham Forest for £35m very clear to their unthinking owners, The Friedkin Group (TFG). “Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand,” they sang. “If you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands”. Everton’s manager, David Moyes , was clearly against the sale. TFG saw and heard the backlash, woke up to the folly of the plan, and called off the sale of a player widely considered Everton’s best home-grown talent since Wayne Rooney . Armstrong’s definitely worth keeping and fighting for. Everton fans made their feelings about the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest clear (Image credit: Getty Images

Everton fans made their feelings about the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest clear (Image credit: Getty Images) “The potential sale of Harrison Armstrong goes against everything our fanbase stands for, a young talented Scouser who is the future of our club,” the Everton fans’ group The 1878s, said in a statement. It threatened to stop organising the flags and tifo displays that contribute so much to match-day atmosphere. TFG was toying with the very fabric of Everton life. Also: what’s best for the player’s own development? Moyes looks after young players well, handling the precocious Rooney as best as possible when the bullish teenager launched himself so memorably on the scene in 2002. Moyes tries to shield such prospects in almost a paternal, certainly a pastoral, way. Moyes knows they will leave the footballing family home at some point so tries to prepare them while getting the best out of them. David Moyes was against the proposed sale of Harrison Armstrong (Image credit: Getty Images) Moyes showed vital support for a teenaged Ross Barkley when the teenager suffered a double break of his leg in 2010, even ensuring a new contract for a kid in a hospital bed worried about his future. Moyes will feed Armstrong in and out of the team, not putting too much physical or mental strain on the 19-year-old. Armstrong looks like he can handle the pressure. That is partly down to the learning acquired when sent by Moyes on loan to Preston North End last season. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. A broader dynamic is at work here, one that affects all supporters. Financial sustainability regulations are not fit for purpose when it comes to the development of young talent. From FFP to PSR to SCR, a rethink is required on content as well as lettering. The “pure profit” element to sales of academy starlets is so tempting to the more short-sighted owners. It was one of the reasons why a frustrated Eddie Howe was forced to sacrifice Elliot Anderson in a hurried sale to Forest. It’s why TFG considered offloading Armstrong. The player becomes an accounting item not a sporting asset. Everton needed a late James Tarkowski goal to rescue a point against Bournemouth (Image credit: Getty Images) TFG needs to balance the books at a club which has recorded alarming figures in some recent years, and been punished for it, but there are other more acceptable ways, others who could be sold. From a Premier League perspective, it would make sense if clubs were more incentivised to retain “one of our own”. One way would be to allow the first few years – perhaps 50 first-team games - of an academy graduate’s salary to be offset against SCR calculations. There would then be a financial incentive to keep home-grown talents. Evertonians rightly take great pride that a local player has featured in every league campaign since the Football League commenced in 1888. It actually predates that. The likes of Liverpool-born goalkeeper, Charles Joliffe, played for Everton from 1885 until he was eventually replaced by Robert Smalley, a recruit from Preston. Moyes handled Wayne Rooney well when he broke through as a teenager (Image credit: Getty Images) Armstrong is more than a player to Evertonians. He’s a symbol of the area, almost an antidote to the big-monied modern game. Connection with the community matters hugely, especially in an era where the Premier League is so heavily populated by overseas players. Everton’s owners must have known there would be outrage. If TFG wasn’t aware, then it needs better advisors – or better channels of communication with fans. This is one of the most concerning elements of the whole story: TFG’s lack of understanding in the first place. It’s almost arrogance. Everton Football Club are more than a business; they are a footballing institution, a community asset, a developer of local talent and a beacon of hope. The Armstrong story highlighted that. Owners take note. TOPICS Henry Winter Writer Henry Winter is one of football's most popular and respected writers. Previously the Chief Football Writer for The Times and a Football Correspondent for The Daily Telegraph, his work now primarily features on his Substack. Adingra SUN 4.9m 28/08 Chadi Riad CRY 4.4m 28/08 Cherki MCI 7.6m Moving Target Is Marmoush back on the FPL radar after Spurs move? August 31 88 comments 31 August 2026 88 comments Two days after Savio (£6.5m) did the same, forward Omar Marmoush (£7.0m) joined Tottenham Hotspur from Manchester City. The 27-year-old Egyptian’s initial loan has an obligation to become permanent for up to £60 million next summer. Can Savinho be a good FPL buy at Spurs? So, have big-spending Spurs invested wisely, or overspent again? We’ll attempt to help out Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers below. Score More Points. Win More Mini Leagues. Join FFScout. CAREER SO FAR Marmoush started his career at Cairo-based Wadi Degla and soon moved to the Bundesliga with Wolfsburg, stepping up to their first team in 2020. However, having been loaned out to St Pauli and Stuttgart, his only notable campaign for Die Wölfe came in 2022/23. Even that season was more about cameos than starts. So he decided to join Frankfurt on a free transfer. They gave him the platform to shine against the likes of Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund + RB Leipzig, as well as in continental competitions. STARTS (SUB) GOALS ASSISTS FPL POINTS 2025/26 Manchester City Premier League 8 (13) 2024/25 Manchester City Premier League 14 (2) 2024/25 Eintracht Frankfurt Bundesliga 17 (0) 2023/24 Eintracht Frankfurt Bundesliga 27 (2) 2022/23 Wolfsburg Bundesliga 15 (18) A particularly electric start to 2024/25 caught the attention of several clubs and, in January, he chose Man City, who hadn’t yet replaced Julián Álvarez. The £59 million man scored an early hat-trick versus Newcastle United and, soon after, brought in 12 FPL points against Brighton and Hove Albion. Yet there was a mixed end to the season. Missing a penalty in their FA Cup final defeat, followed three days later by a stunning 30-yard ‘Goal of the Season’ strike at home to Bournemouth. A lot of those early months had Marmoush based on the left-hand side, but a quiet 2025/26 saw him basically be Erling Haaland ‘s (£15.5m) backup. WHERE MARMOUSH FITS IN AT SPURS Showcasing his versatility, FPL keeps switching Marmoush between being a midfielder and a forward. This time, he’s the latter, and that could be how Roberto De Zerbi classifies him. “I think he can play as a central striker. Number 10… different number 10 than Gallagher or Maddison, more of an attacker, but he is a player of big qualities.” Roberto De Zerbi when asked if he sees Omar Marmoush as more of a striker or ’10’ Indeed, in his Gameweek 2 debut against Newcastle United, the Egyptian was stationed up top. Above: Omar Marmoush led the line for Spurs in Gameweek 2, although there was plenty of him drifting deep and left Marmoush’s hot streak at Frankfurt was mostly up front, albeit in a partnership with Hugo Ekitike (£7.5m). Good at receiving passes over the top of opposing defenders, both he and De Zerbi mention his pace in interviews with the club website “Omar is exactly the kind of player we want at this club – ambitious, hungry and determined to make a difference. He brings pace, intelligence and a real threat in front of goal, and I believe he can take our attacking play to another level.” – Roberto De Zerbi Dominic Solanke (£6.0m) presents his only real competition up top, and it feels likelier that Marmoush will be battling for the striker’s role as Richarlison (£6.0m) is on his way out. Compare that to the attacking midfield trident behind the striker, with Savio, Mohammed Kudus (£6.5m), James Maddison (£6.4m), Dejan Kulusevski (£6.5m), Mathys Tel (£5.9m), Xavi Simons (£6.0m) and the potentially incoming Iliman Ndiaye (£6.0m) all options when fit, and Marmoush surely doesn’t add to that melange. LOTS OF SHOTS AT CITY – BUT NOT MANY GILT-EDGED CHANCES Marmoush was a Fantasy midfielder last season and, among his positional peers, he had the best rate of shots per 90 minutes (3.49). Of course, he spent much of his time up front, but even compared to the forwards, Erling Haaland (£15.5m) was the only meaningful name who could better that figure. Above: FPL midfielders sorted by shots per 90 minutes in 2025/26 (min. 500 minutes) It was more volume than quality of chances, though. His average xG per shot was 0.09. For context, Yoane Wissa ‘s (£6.1m) figure was up at 0.27. Above: Omar Marmoush’s xG shotmap in 2025/26, with the bigger circles representing better chances. Green = goal. Blue = blocked/on target. Red = off target. He is, at least, capable of scoring from distance/low-percentage efforts. There were three direct free-kicks in 10 days for Frankfurt. He scored three goals from outside the box in his first half-season at City in 2024/25. And, crucially, he’s overachieved on the xG front in each of the last three seasons. The pinnacle of that came in his final half-campaign at Frankfurt : Above image from Fotmob ANY CHANCE OF PENALTIES OR SET PIECES? Spurs didn’t benefit from a single Premier League penalty last season. They did, however, get four of them in the Champions League: Date Competition Player Outcome On pitch 18/03/2026 Champions League Xavi Simons Scored 09/12/2025 Champions League Xavi Simons Scored 09/12/2025 Champions League Mohamed Kudus Scored Richarlison, Simons 04/11/2025 Champions League Richarlison Missed Simons, of course, is currently injured, while Richarlison is on his way out. Solanke, meanwhile, was off the field when all four of the above spot-kicks were awarded. He’d taken and scored three in April/May of 2024/25, so on paper he should be first in line – but will the striker even start in this new-look Spurs side? Spot-kick duties could be up for grabs, then. Marmoush has a decent record from 12 yards (nine scored, two missed), although his last attempt was a miss in the 2025 FA Cup final. Ndiaye, with his unblemished record of five penalties scored, could also be in the mix if he joins, along with Kudus. As for direct free-kicks, Marmoush is a fan of those. He took three for City in his limited pitch-time in 2025/26. Pedro Porro (£5.5m), Kudus, Maddison and, when fit, Simons provide the competition. Tel might be off them now Corners seem much less likely. He was only a sporadic taker of those at City, and on Saturday, he didn’t deliver any of Spurs’ nine corners. ANY FPL POTENTIAL? The FPL community is just waiting for Spurs’ attack – still goalless after two Gameweeks – to become convincing again. Adding Marmoush and Savio to the mix certainly helps, as will the returns to fitness of Maddison and Kudus, and the potential arrival of Ndiaye. It might just need a little patience! We should have more of a clue by Gameweek 7, when Spurs handily embark on a promising fixture run. Four home matches in seven versus Coventry City, Crystal Palace, Ipswich Town and Fulham, for a player whose 10 Premier League goals have all come at home. The problem with Marmoush is his price. The likes of Ndiaye and Savio could quite easily match or better Marmoush for FPL points, and at a cheaper price, too. Then there are the other FPL forwards. Wissa is £0.9m cheaper and has an excellent fixture run now. Joao Pedro (£7.6m) is only £0.6m more expensive and his own great stretch of matches from Gameweek 4. Marmoush has much to do to wriggle his way into the FPL conversation, then, even if his xMins have been given a serious shot in the arm by this move. 88 Comments Login to Post a Comment Saka Potatoes 01 1 day, 15 hours ago What do you think about this FH squad? articles.title: Tarkowski Reveals Message To Everton Squad Before Late Equaliser
articles.excerpt: James Tarkowski has reflected on the “incredible” moment of striking his 91 st -minute stoppage time leveller against Bournemouth on Saturday – and says he always felt Everton were “going to get a chance”. His late goal at the Vitality Stadium sealed a 1-1 draw for the Toffees, cancelling out Alex Scott’s first-half strike. “It’s always nice not to lose a game when you’ve been 1-0 down for quite a while,” he told evertontv . “We stuck at it. “I thought we defended brilliantly in the second half. We stayed strong, put bodies on the line. Jordan made a few big saves in big moments. “I always felt we were going to get a chance. I was trying to get that message to the lads on a lot of corners they were having, just to say: ‘We’ll punish them. Stick at it, keep defending and we’ll punish them.’ “Thankfully, we did.” Thanking the travelling Toffees for their superb support, he added: “It’s incredible. To score a goal like that in front of those fans is an amazing feeling. “I’d like to watch that footage back now and see those celebrations!”
