articles.body: Okoli, Sealey and Somade ready for PSG test Skip navigation Okoli, Sealey and Somade ready for PSG test Match previews 31 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s are set for a taste of European football on Wednesday night (KO: 19:00 BST) when Paris Saint-Germain visit Sutton United’s Borough Sports Ground in the Premier League International Cup. Ahead of the Young Eagles’ Group C opener, Chuks Okoli, Amaari Sealey and Sean Somade looked ahead to the challenge – from facing one of Europe’s biggest clubs to the different demands of taking on overseas opposition. With Season Ticket+, Gold and Junior Gold Memberships, you’ll be able to enjoy free entry to selected Under-18 and U21 home games! Buy PSG tickets here It is a particularly exciting occasion for Okoli, who has been with Palace since the age of seven and was named the club’s 2025/26 Under-18 Player of the Season. For the versatile midfielder, the pedigree of the visitors is clear. “Obviously a big European team, a lot of pedigree,” he said. “Quite a lot of talent as well, and I know that obviously they've won quite a lot of things, Champions League, a lot of Ligue 1 titles, so I'm expecting a lot of quality from them.” PSG arrive in South London as the reigning European champions and French champions, having won the UEFA Champions League for a second successive season and secured a fifth consecutive Ligue 1 title. Their academy was also named France’s best for 25/26 by the French Football Federation. Sealey, meanwhile, knows the size of the challenge awaiting him on what could be his competitive debut for Palace. The attacking midfielder joined the Young Eagles from AFC Wimbledon over the summer after an outstanding 25/26 campaign, registering 47 goal contributions as the Dons’ U18s completed an unprecedented national quadruple. “Yeah, I'm sure everyone knows that, you know, they're French giants, they're huge in their country and worldwide,” he said. “Obviously their success in European competitions, so obviously it's the perfect test for us.” Somade, a powerful centre-back capable of also playing at right-back, has been at Palace since joining at Under-14 level and is relishing the opportunity to face unfamiliar opposition. “Obviously they have a lot of background, a famous team, known for being good,” he said. “It's going to be a good game.” Quote Icons I'm extremely excited Chuks Okoli The International Cup provides something different from the U21s’ usual domestic schedule. Palace primarily compete in Premier League 2, which features the development sides of all 31 Category One academies, while they will also compete in the EFL Trophy this season The International Cup, meanwhile, brings together 16 Premier League 2 sides and 16 invited European clubs. The teams are split into four groups of eight, with each English side facing their four overseas opponents once. Palace are in Group C alongside PSG, PSV Eindhoven, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto, with all four fixtures taking place at Sutton. For Okoli, that change of scenery also brings different tactical and physical demands. “I think obviously playing against international foreign teams, they come up with different tactics, different play styles, different type of quality,” he said. “So I'm expecting it to probably be faster, more technical, probably even a bit stronger, more physical, so yeah, extremely excited.” Sealey expects the quality across the competition to make for a stern test, but believes Palace can thrive. “Yeah, I feel like there'll be higher quality because I feel like all the teams will try and play good football, including us,” he said. “I feel like most teams will be of such a good nature that it's going to be a hard competition to be in, but I feel like we can do well.” For Somade, simply facing a team from outside England will provide a new experience. “Obviously them being a foreign team, we're not used to playing teams outside of the country,” he said. “I feel like it'll be a different type of challenge and it'll be good.” Quote Icons It's everyone's dream to play in front of fans Amaari Sealey With the first European challenge of the season almost here, all three players were keen to stress the importance of having Palace supporters behind them. Okoli believes that backing could be particularly valuable for a group containing several players experiencing the competition for the first time. “I think it'll be very important for us, especially for us first years of going into a new competition,” he said. “Some of us haven't played yet, so having those people behind us, those people to support us and cheer us on should be good.” Sealey echoed that call, describing playing in front of supporters in a competition such as this as a dream for young players. “Yeah, hugely important for us because, you know, it's everyone's dream to play in front of fans in such big competitions,” he said. “I feel like it's the next step for us, so yeah, come and watch.” And Somade has a simple message for anyone considering making the trip to Sutton or even tuning in on Palace TV+. “I think it'll be good for them to come watch. We'll give our all and as long as they're there, I think we'll try our hardest.” Tickets for the game are available from just £1 - If you can’t make it to the game against PSG on Wednesday, you can watch all the action LIVE on Palace TV+ - Match ticket prices: Adults (21-64): £5 Young Adults (17-21): £1 Seniors (65+): £1 Juniors (2-16): £1 Academy Founder Members: Free Adult Gold, Junior Gold & Season Ticket+ Holders: Free Tickets are available here and will be issued as PDF print-at-home tickets at the point of sale. August 31 0 comments 31 August 2026 0 comments Manchester City last week continued their midfield rebuild by signing highly rated teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi (£5.5m) from Lille. The 18-year-old Morocco international drew plenty of global interest after a promising display at the World Cup, and it was Enzo Maresca’s side who won the race for his signature on a deal reportedly worth up to £86m. It’s all change in the City midfield, then. Fellow big-money signing Elliot Anderson (£6.4m) has arrived but long-serving stars Rodri and Bernardo Silva are gone, as are Nico Gonzalez (£5.5m) and Tijjani Reijnders. So, what are Bouaddi’s prospects from a Fantasy Premier League (FPL) perspective? BRIEF HISTORY Bouaddi joined Lille’s Academy in 2021, signing his first senior contract with the club two years later and earning a first-team debut just days after his 16th birthday. Bouaddi then became one of Ligue 1’s youngest debutants in history during the 2023/24 campaign, going on to make 96 total senior appearances for Lille across all competitions. That included nine appearances in the 2024/25 Champions League, seven of them as a starter, including a home win over Real Madrid on his 17th birthday. BOUADDI’S LEAGUE APPEARANCES FOR LILLE Season Team Starts (sub apps) Mins Goals Assists 2025/2026 Lille 28 (2) 2331 2024/2025 Lille 11 (13) 1149 2023/2024 Lille 1 (8) 128 After representing France at youth level, Bouaddi elected to play for Morocco’s senior international team and subsequently started five of the country’s six World Cup matches this summer. WHERE DOES BOUADDI FIT IN – AND WILL HE START? Above: City’s starting line-ups in the first two Gameweeks, via BBC Sport As a deep-lying midfielder – one who has already drawn comparisons to the great and often unheralded Sergio Busquets – that appears remarkably comfortable in possession despite his young age, Bouaddi’s likeliest route to the first team is to slot into the base of City’s midfield alongside Anderson. We’ve seen defenders Marc Guehi (£6.0m) and Neco O’Reilly (£6.5m) in those roles in Gameweeks 1 and 2. Either way, the transfer fee suggests this is a player that City and Maresca intend on rebuilding their midfield around in partnership with Anderson, so we would expect him to become a regular starter at some point in the future, especially given the loss of Rodri, Reijnders, Bernardo and Gonzalez. Still, the continued presence of an experienced figure like Mateo Kovacic (£5.5m) – as well as a few versatile defenders – does give Maresca options if he elects to ease Bouaddi into Premier League action. The teenage Moroccan was on the bench in Gameweek 2, replacing Anderson late on. O’REILLY CONCERN? One thing to watch out for is the impact on O’Reilly. If Bouaddi eventually comes in alongside Anderson, where does that leave the £6.5m FPL defender? His two starts in 2026/27 have both come in midfield, the first as a ’10’, the second slightly further back. The form of Rayan Cherki (£7.6m) makes the first unlikely to happen much again. O’Reilly back to left-back, then? Possibly, but Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m) has started there in Gameweeks 1 and 2. The Croatian is reportedly viewed as a ‘pillar’ by Maresca. O’Reilly does offer something that Bouaddi and Anderson don’t, in a box-crashing attacking sense. A pairing of the latter two does seem somewhat conservative, and may only be preserved for the ‘bigger’ games. Only ‘mild peril’ for O’Reilly for now, then – but a move for Enzo Fernandez (£6.9m) would really upset the applecart! NOT MUCH GOAL THREAT – BUT WHAT ABOUT DEFCON POTENTIAL? Whenever he does make a starting XI spot his own, Bouaddi’s career to date suggests his main appeal from an FPL perspective comes from his potential for defensive contribution (DefCon) points. The teenage prospect’s total expected goal involvement (xGI) was a miserable 3.33 in 2025/26, so we’ll move swiftly on from attacking threat. Here are his ‘DefCon per 90’ figures from his last two full seasons: Season DefCons per 90 2025/2026 10.55 2024/2025 10.66 Pretty consistent, then, but still some way short of the leading FPL midfielders in 2025/26: Above: FPL midfielders sorted by DefCons per 90 minutes in 2025/26 OVERALL FPL POTENTIAL – AND ANDERSON IMPACT? Bouaddi is an FPL no-go at present. Not only are there game-time concerns, but a repeat of his so-so DefCon rate at Lille wouldn’t compensate for the lack of attacking threat. Mamadou Sangare (£5.6m), for instance, is streets above Bouaddi in those respects right now. So, the Moroccan’s arrival is more about the impact on O’Reilly – who we’ve already discussed above – and Anderson. Anderson is a known and valued commodity when it comes to DefCon points, so it will be interesting to see the effect Bouaddi’s integration may have on the former Nottingham Forest star. Could the newcomer take on the brunt of the defensive work, freeing up Anderson to offer more from an attacking standpoint? That certainly seems more likely than the vice versa option, given Bouaddi is yet to score a senior international goal and also registered just a single assist for Lille last term. Granted, leaving the teenager to fend for himself as a sole No 6 – at least early doors – may be considered too much of a baptism of fire in the Premier League. Bouaddi was in a two-man pairing for Lille, regularly in a 4-2-3-1, so it is maybe likelier that we see him continue in a similar set-up alongside Anderson, with the defensive workload shared between the two. It’s worth monitoring the midfield DefCon numbers – in addition to Bouaddi’s minutes, of course – over the coming weeks’ promising fixtures , then, to assess the impact of City’s possession-based style on the DefCon potential of both Anderson and Bouaddi. 0 Comments Login to Post a Comment No comments have been submitted for this post yet. David Luiz's second Chelsea spell ended in 2019 (Image credit: Alamy) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google During two trophy-laden spells at Chelsea, David Luiz turned out for the club almost 250 times, helping the Blues win the Champions League, Premier League, FA Cup and Europa League. But shortly after signing a new contract in 2019 and just weeks after he started in Chelsea’s 4-1 Europa League final win over Arsenal , the Brazilian defender signed for the Gunners in an £8million deal. The reason for making this bold move across the capital with the ink on his new deal still wet was a simple one - the hiring of his former teammate Frank Lampard as Chelsea boss. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List Luiz on why Lampard’s Chelsea wasn’t for him Luiz has recently turned 30 when Lampard, fresh from a stint on charge of Derby County, was handed the Stamford Bridge top job, but age was not a factor for Luiz, who is still playing as a 39-year-old for Cypriot side Pafos. “I was already over 30 and had renewed my contract with Chelsea,” Luiz tells FourFourTwo . “No-one had ever broken the club policy of renewing for two years after the age of 30, and I renewed for two years. Luiz swapped Chelsea for Arsenal after Frank Lampard's arrival (Image credit: PA) “Then after two months, I went to Arsenal. It was down to the decision to bring Frank Lampard in as manager. In pre-season, I already could see the way he was going to play wasn’t going to leave me happy. “At that age, I thought “I want to enjoy the game in the way I play it”, so it was better to leave.” The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. For Luiz, this was a decision made as a matter of principle. “There are two kinds of workers in life,” he continues. “Those who work to protect themselves and the job, and those who want to do something different. In any company, 90 per cent protect the job, but I want to be part of the 10 per cent. “It would have been easy to have stayed quietly at Chelsea, but I’m not like that. So I sat down with Frank Lampard and said ‘I want to leave – the way you’re going to play won’t be good for me, and the way I’d play in your system won’t be good for you either’.” Luiz did not see himself fitting into Lampard's system A year after playing his final match for Chelsea against Arsenal in the Europa League final, there was another twist of fate for Luiz. “Life is so funny – later that season, the FA Cup final was between Arsenal and Chelsea. I leave, telling the manager I don’t think his philosophy would suit me, that maybe it wouldn’t work to win anything, then at the end of the season the final is against him. “So if I won, in theory I was right. If I lost, I wasn’t. Thank God, we managed to win, and I was very respectful in the way I behaved, not celebrating, and respecting the history I built at Chelsea.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.title: Under-18s looking to "bounce back" after defeat to Ipswich
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth under-18s Lead Coach, James Lowy, says his side will "bounce back" after a 6-2 defeat away at Ipswich Town. Goals from a trialist and Harley Simpson saw the Cherries go into half-time level at 2-2, before Ipswich secured the three points in the second-half. James Lowy spoke to afcb.co.uk: "It was a game of two halves. I thought we competed really well in the first-half and put ourselves in a good position. "We created a number of opportunities through pressing and regaining the ball high, but we didn't capitalise on those opportunities. "For us to compete at this level, they are chances that we would need to take. "In the second-half, we struggled to compete in our duels. In and around the final third we lacked some quality and could have done better with some chances too. "Ipswich defended well, and the difference was in both boxes today. "It's been a really tough period for us physically, with games coming thick and fast. "We have a young squad and some injures, so it is important for us now to rest and recover and put ourselves in the best position going into West Ham on Saturday." Lowy's players are back in action this Saturday (5th September).

Geoff Hurst fires home his third goal in the 1966 World Cup final (Image credit: Alamy) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Sir Geoff Hurst will forever be at the centre of English football’s greatest-ever achievement. The former West Ham striker’s iconic hat-trick saw the Three Lions conquer the world at Wembley 60 summers ago, but just months earlier, his place at the 1966 World Cup was far from assured. It would take patience, preparation and an unfortunate injury to Jimmy Greaves for Hurst to get his opportunity under Sir Alf Ramsey. Geoff Hurst on waiting for his England chance Hurst didn't make his England debut until February 1966 (Image credit: Getty Images) As Hurst looks back on his rise into the England starting XI that summer, he admits that he was eager to keep his expectations in check in the run-up to the tournament, “Well, you don't get too far ahead of yourself,” Hurst tells FourFourTwo . “You might find it surprising but, although we were successful at West Ham, it was never really on my radar." Jimmy Greaves was England's No.9 going into the tournament (Image credit: Getty Images) Hurst’s approach of letting his club football at Upton Park do the talking would pay off, though, as the call did come just in time. “It was quite a surprise when I received a letter from the FA in December ‘65 saying I was picked for the game in February against West Germany at Wembley . You come and play and do your best, and hopefully the manager sees enough in you. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “Thankfully, he did. It wasn’t just me, either. Martin Peters , my team-mate at West Ham and room-mate on England duty, played his first game in May that year. He went on to score the other goal in the final, of course. We were cutting it fine!” While Hurst was named in Ramsey’s 22-man squad for the World Cup, he didn’t actually start a game until the quarter-final win over Argentina, after first-choice striker Jimmy Greaves injured himself in the final group game. But was that a source of frustration for Hurst? “Not for one second,” he insists. “I was honestly just so ecstatic to be in the squad for a home World Cup. Alf Ramsey with the Jules Rimet trophy after England's 1966 World Cup victory (Image credit: Alamy) “I often joke that Alf Ramsay picked two average players ahead of me, in Jimmy Greaves and Roger Hunt, before finally getting it right. But, of course, those two were phenomenal strikers and I was thrilled to support the team however I could. “That was a good attitude because, when your chance comes in life, you have to be ready to take it and I did. “Saying that, I was honestly so sad for the great Jimmy Greaves, who damaged his leg against France. He deserved to play on.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.body: Chelsea 4-3 Brighton Stats: Cole Palmer Decides Seven-Goal Thriller as Xabi Alonso's Men Stay Perfect | Opta Analyst Chelsea beat Brighton in a seven-goal Premier League epic on Sunday, with Cole Palmer and João Pedro both on target again. Relive all the moments from the game with our Chelsea vs Brighton stats page. Cole Palmer scored what proved to be the winner as Chelsea remained perfect in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso, beating Brighton 4-3 in a thriller at Stamford Bridge. It looked like being a routine outing for the Blues when Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and João Pedro struck to put them 3-0 up inside 32 minutes. But former Brighton striker João Pedro also scored at the wrong end following a sumptuous volley from Malick Yalcouyé , as Brighton threatened a stunning comeback. Palmer gave Chelsea breathing room once more when he found the bottom-left corner in trademark fashion, though, and Pascal Gross’ header came too late for Brighton as the hosts climbed to third in the early-season table, with two wins from two matches. Chelsea had only needed 31 seconds to make the breakthrough in their season-opening win over Fulham, and though they had to wait a little longer on Sunday, another fast start left Brighton shellshocked. Lavia was on hand to tap home in the fourth minute after Mats Wieffer nodded João Pedro’s header off the line, and only 10 minutes later, Neto met Morgan Rogers’ left-sided cross with a first-time finish off the outside of his right boot. Joao Pedro – who was jeered by the away fans throughout – missed a glorious chance to make it 3-0 when he stroked wide with time and space inside the area, but he celebrated in front of his former supporters when he took in Jorrel Hato’s pass and finished soon after. Emiliano Martínez’ first test in the Chelsea net was to catch Yalcouye’s effort on the stretch, but his hopes of a clean sheet were dashed when the former Swansea City loanee hammered a volley in off the post, on the rebound from Charalampos Kostoulas’ saved lob. Huge chances came and went at both ends early in the second half. Diego Gomez headed wide after being left unmarked from Olivier Boscagli’s free-kick, while Palmer could not keep his shot down when Rogers dug out a cross to find him in front of an unguarded net. Brighton had renewed hope when Gross beat the offside trap following a recycled set-piece and crossed low, with a flick off João Pedro catching out Martinez, and the former Aston Villa goalkeeper then had to be alert to push Boscagli’s drive to safety. But Palmer eased Chelsea’s nerves with a marauding run and finish in the 74 minute, and there was barely time for the game to restart following Gross’ late header. João Pedro the Centre of Attention as Alonso’s Men Entertain Again Playing their first home Premier League game under Alonso, Chelsea could hardly have asked for a better start. Lavia’s goal made them just the second team to begin a Premier League campaign by scoring in the opening four minutes of both of their first two matches, after Bolton Wanderers in 2002-03. That strike also came four years to the day since Lavia’s only previous goal in the competition – which came against the Blues for Southampton. But Brighton refused to go away without a fight, even after going 3-0 down. João Pedro was heavily involved at both ends, registering a goal, an assist and an own goal. He is only the sixth player to do so in a single Premier League game and the first since Son Heung-min against Manchester City in December 2023, while he is the first to ever do so for Chelsea. But it was Palmer’s cultured finish that proved decisive, and he has now netted six times against Brighton in the Premier League – more than he has against any other club. And if they continue in this vein, both Chelsea and Brighton could lay claim to being the Premier League’s chief entertainers. Alonso is only the fourth manager to see his team score seven or more goals in his first two Premier League games, after Bobby Robson (eight in September 1999), Michael Laudrup (eight in August 2012), and Marcelo Bielsa (seven in September 2020). Fabian Hurzeler’s Seagulls, are only the second side since 1950 to score four goals in their first game of an English top-flight season, and then concede four in their second, after Blackpool in 2010-11 (won 4-0 versus Wigan, lost 0-6 to Arsenal). Our Opta match centre delivers you all the Chelsea vs Brighton stats from their Premier League meeting at Stamford Bridge on Sunday 30 August 2026. The match centre below includes team and player stats, expected goals data, passing networks, an Opta chalkboard and more. It gives you everything you need to do your own match analysis. Underneath the match centre you can find the official Opta stats on the game as well. Chelsea vs Brighton: Post-Match Opta Facts Chelsea have won both of their first two games of a top-flight season while scoring 3+ goals each time for the fourth time, after 1936-37, 2010-11, and 2018-19. Chelsea’s Xabi Alonso is only the fourth manager to see his side score 7+ goals in his first two Premier League games, after Bobby Robson (8 in Sep 1999), Michael Laudrup (8 in Aug 2012), and Marcelo Bielsa (7 in Sep 2020). Brighton have lost three consecutive away games in the Premier League for the first time since May 2021 under Graham Potter. Chelsea are only the second side ever to score in the opening four minutes of both of their first two Premier League games of a season, after Bolton Wanderers in 2002-03. Chelsea have gone 18 games without a clean sheet in the Premier League, their longest run without a shutout in league competition since a run of 31 matches between November 1960 and August 1961. Brighton’s possession of 74.4% was the highest on record (from 2003-04) by any side in a Premier League game against Chelsea. Indeed, Chelsea completed 146 passes in this match, their lowest home or away in a Premier League game since 2003-04. Enjoy this? Georgi Kinkladze joined Manchester City in 1995 (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google When Georgi Kinkladze arrived at Manchester City in the summer of 1995, the Georgian playmaker was one of Europe’s most promising young attacking talents. It didn’t take long for the former Dinamo Tbilisi midfielder to become a cult hero at Maine Road, with the signing coming just as the still-young Premier League was beginning to establish itself as a viable destination for some of the continent’s best players. This was proved evident in the fact that City were able to see off AC Milan , one of that era’s greatest sides, to Kinkladze’s signature. Kinkladze on snubbing AC Milan for City City saw of AC Milan to land Kinkladze (Image credit: Getty Images) “There was interest from Italy, but [City chairman] Francis Lee was very determined,” Kinzladze tells FourFourTwo as he looks back at his 1995 move to England. “He flew to see me and convinced me that City was a place where I could be the main man. I didn't know much about Manchester, but I liked the idea of a challenge in England.” Kinkladze quickly became a City fans' favourite (Image credit: Getty Images) It quickly became clear to the young Kinkladze that English football was very different to anything he had previously experienced. “When I arrived, the football was very different. It was much faster and more direct. The weather and the food were hard to get used to, but the fans made it easy. From the first day at Maine Road, they treated me like one of their own. That connection was instant.” The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Alan Ball was the City manager at the time, having spent the previous season in charge at Southampton, famously building his team around Matt Le Tissier , instructing his side to ‘Just the ball to Le Tissier.’ So was that similar with Kinkladze at City? “Alan Ball was very important in my development as a player,” he continues. “He loved technical players and wanted the team to play with flair, even if we were struggling in the table. “The 90s were a different time and sometimes I was targeted by foul play. If you tried to dribble, someone would try to kick you. Vinnie Jones and the Wimbledon Crazy Gang were famous for it. Former England international Alan Ball was in charge of City at the time (Image credit: Alamy) “But I had played in the streets of Tbilisi so I knew how to jump over a tackle. I always thought that if they couldn't catch me, they couldn't hit me.” Those early Premier League days saw a number of big-name foreign players join the league, with Kinkaldze admitting that it was an exciting time to be involved. “It was the start of something new,” he adds. “Seeing Gianfranco Zola , Dennis Bergkamp and Juninho arrive in the Premier League was exciting and it felt like the league was opening up to creative players. “The long ball reputation of English football was changing.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. articles.body: Palace in Europe: Get to know our league phase opponents Skip navigation Palace in Europe: Get to know our league phase opponents First-team 30 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace's eight opponents for the league phase of the UEFA Europa League have now been confirmed – here's the first of two guides, looking at four of the teams we'll be facing. Lyon Country: France Year founded: 1950 Nickname: Les Gones Best European performance: Champions League semi-finals (2009/10 and 2019/20) Pierre Sage faces a reunion with his former team after Palace were awarded a trip to Lyon in the league phase draw. The French side have serious European pedigree from their golden spell in the 2000s, where they won seven straight top-flight titles. During the latter part of this decade, Lyon regularly survived the winter in the Champions League and reached the last 16 of the old format – only beaten by Bayern Munich in the semi-finals in 2010. Despite selling star player Rayan Cherki to Manchester City in the summer of 2025, Lyon enjoyed a decent season in Ligue Un last term, finishing in fourth place to ensure European qualification. They competed in the Europa League last season and started strongly by topping the league table in the first round. However, their journey would end in the last 16 last season where they were eliminated by Celta Vigo. Real Sociedad Country: Spain Year founded: 1909 Nickname: La Real Best European performance: Champions League**** semi-finalists 1982/83 Based in San Sebastian in the Basque region of Spain, Sociedad are UEFA Cup / Europa League regulars, although they are yet to lift a European trophy. They enjoyed a memorable Copa del Rey triumph in 2025/26 to qualify for European football, defeating Atlético Madrid on penalties after a 2-2 draw in the final. Managed by American Pellegrino Matarazzo, la Real finished in 10th place last season in La Liga. Their standout player is Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of Euro 2024, who is also their captain. Current Chelsea manager and former Liverpool and Real Madrid star Xabi Alonso came through the ranks at Sociedad – arguably their most famous academy graduate. TSG Hoffenheim Country: Germany Year founded: 1899 Nickname: Die Kraichgauer Best European performance: Europa League A club that has enjoyed one of German football's most remarkable rises in the 21st century. Hoffenheim only won promotion to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2008, but have played in Europe regularly over the last decade. Their first taste of the Champions League was a play-off defeat to Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in 2017, but they reached the group stage proper for the first time in 2018/19, facing the likes of Lyon and Manchester City. Christian Ilzer took over as manager in 2024 and led them to a fifth place finish in his first full season in charge last term. The most familiar name in their ranks is club legend and Croatia international Andrej Kramarić, who has an impressive 119 caps for his country. Kramarić was actually part of Leicester City's Premier League title winning squad in 2015/16, but left the following summer and been with the German club ever since. Beşiktaş Country: Turkey Year founded: 1903 Nickname: Kara Kartallar Best European performance: European Cup semi-finalists One of Turkey's big three, Beşiktaş may be fourth seeds for the 2026/27 Europa League, but are normally competitive in European competition regardless of their seeding. They did miss out on European football a year ago after a defeat in the Conference League play-offs to Lausanne-Sport, a defeat which saw former Manchester United head coach Ole Gunnar Solskjær leave the club. His replacement Sergen Yalçın did a good job of steadying the ship. Under his management, Beşiktaş finished 4th in the Turkish Super League, winning precisely half of their 34 league games. Yalçın was replaced in the summer by former Fiorentina coach Vincenzo Italiano. His first competitive European tie saw the Turkish side see off Midtjylland in the second qualifying round. Further wins over Hradec Králové and Kauno Žalgiris ensured they booked a place in the league phase of the Europa League. Their marquee signing this summer is a familiar name from the Premier League – Leandro Trossard arriving from Arsenal for £15m. Another familiar name is former Leicester midfielder Wilfred Ndidi. Beşiktaş have won the Turkish championship 16 times, most recently in 2020/21. Related News Club First-team Related News More News

articles.title: Coventry City sign Stephen Mfuni on loan from Manchester City
articles.excerpt: Coventry City are delighted to announce the signing of Stephen Mfuni on a season-long loan from Manchester City. The 18-year-old, who can play at left-back and centre-back, made his senior debut for the Citizens last season in the 10-1 victory over Exeter City in the Emirates FA Cup. Mfuni gained further experience on loan at Championship side Watford, where he made eight appearances during the second half of last season. He’s also featured against EFL sides in the Vertu Trophy for City’s Under 21s and has also been named as a substitute for Premier League and UEFA Champions League matches. The defender has progressed through the ranks at the Etihad Stadium and capped off his youth career by scoring in the FA Youth Cup final, which saw City lift the trophy after a 4-0 triumph over Leeds United in 2024. The talented defender has also been recognised at international level and has represented England from Under 16s through to Under 19s and started all three matches at the 2025 UEFA European Under-19 Championship. articles.title: Mukiele starts for Sunderland against Fulham
articles.excerpt: Régis Le Bris has made one change to his Sunderland AFC side for today’s first home game of the Premier League season against Fulham, kick-off 2pm BST. Nordi Mukiele comes into the heart of the Black Cats’ defence in place of Luke O’Nien, partnering Dan Ballard, with Thomas Meunier and Reinildo completing the back four. Granit Xhaka captains the side from midfield, with Noah Sadiki and Enzo Le Fée alongside him, while Brian Brobbey leads the line. New signing Jules Akoha is among the substitutes. Sunderland: Roefs, Hume, Meunier, Ballard, Mukiele, Reinildo, Xhaka (C), Sadiki, Le Fée, Angulo, Brobbey. Substitutes: Ellborg (GK), O’Nien, Alderete, Talbi, Diarra, Rigg, Mundle, Ahoka, Isidor.

articles.title: TYLER BINDON JOINS CHARLTON ON LOAN
articles.excerpt: Nottingham Forest can confirm Tyler Bindon has joined Charlton Athletic on a season-long loan deal. After appearing for New Zealand at the FIFA World Cup, the 21-year-old defender was part of Oliver Glasner’s squad throughout pre-season. In moving to Nathan Jones’ side, who have won all three of their opening league games, Bindon returns to the Championship after featuring 26 times on loan at Sheffield United in the 2025/26 season. Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Tyler the very best for the season ahead.

articles.excerpt: Fixtures Coventry City Vs. Hull City - Sat, Aug 29 2026, 15:00 Head coach Sergej Jakirović was delighted with his Hull City side once again as they made it two Premier League wins from their opening two games with a 1-0 success away at Coventry City. Liam Millar came up with the all-important match-winning moment late on at the CBS Arena, but the victory was again built upon solid foundations as the Tigers secured a second successive clean sheet on their top flight return. “I’m really happy and pleased. It was an excellent victory,” said Jakirović. “We knew we would have to be strong from the beginning and this was understandable because Coventry were playing their first Premier League home game for 25 years. We were solid, compact and aggressive. articles.body: Skip navigation All you need to know about the International Cup Academy 30 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s face Paris Saint-Germain, PSV Eindhoven, RSC Anderlecht and FC Porto in this season’s Premier League International Cup – here’s everything you need to know about the Young Eagles’ opponents and the competition. The Premier League International Cup Fancy a taste of European football without leaving England? The Premier League International Cup is back! The competition pits the top 16 sides from last season’s Premier League 2 against 16 invited clubs from across Europe. The 32 teams are split into four groups of eight, with four English sides and four European sides in each group. Palace will play each of their four European opponents once, with all group-stage fixtures taking place in England. The Young Eagles will not face the other three English teams in their group. The top two sides from each group progress to the quarter-finals, with the knockout stages decided over one leg. Extra-time and penalties will be used if required. This is Palace’s sixth appearance in the competition, having lifted the trophy in 23/24 after finishing runners-up in their first campaign in 22/23. The Young Eagles have been drawn in Group D this season, with PSG, PSV Eindhoven, Anderlecht and Porto standing between Darren Powell’s side and another run at the trophy. PSG The French giants were named France’s best academy for 25/26 by the French Football Federation, continuing a remarkable record of developing players for the highest level. Ten PSG academy graduates have featured for the club’s first team, while 12 have played in the UEFA Champions League and more than 20 have received call-ups to France’s youth teams. The club’s academy has also produced more than 30 players aged under 23 who are now under professional contract with clubs in the top two divisions of Europe’s top 10 leagues. PSG’s Espoirs have already faced English opposition this season, beating Manchester City 1-0 in pre-season. They finished fourth in their group last season, despite making an excellent start. A 2-0 win over Newcastle United and 3-1 victory against Chelsea put PSG in a strong position, but draws against Brighton & Hove Albion and defeat to Nottingham Forest ultimately ended their hopes of progressing. They’ll be hoping to go further this time around! One to watch: Fabio Domingos. The Luxembourg-born winger joined PSG from Metz in 2025 and has represented Luxembourg at youth level and Cape Verde at senior level. Domingos featured for PSG’s U19s last season as they won the Championnat National U19 title for a third successive year, and has since continued his development with the Espoirs. Match Details Palace U21s v PSG U21s Wednesday, 2nd September KO: 19:00 BST The Borough Sports Ground Premier League International Cup Watch LIVE on Palace TV+! RSC Anderlecht RSC Anderlecht’s academy has produced a host of household names, including Jérémy Doku, Romelu Lukaku and Vincent Kompany, as well as Belgian legends Paul Van Himst and Jef Mermans. Their reserve side, RSCA Futures, compete in the Challenger Pro League – Belgium’s second tier – alongside professional and other reserve sides. Anderlecht made their Premier League International Cup debut in 24/25, becoming the first Belgian club to enter the competition in nine years. Palace came out on top when the sides met in the group stages that season, with Zach Marsh, Mofe Jemide and Jemiah Umolu all on target in a 3-1 victory for the Young Eagles. One to watch: Nunzio Engwanda. The 18-year-old centre-back has already made first-team appearances in the Belgian Pro League and has become a regular for RSCA Futures. Match Details Palace U21s v RSC Anderlecht U21s Wednesday, 14th October KO: 19:00 BST The Borough Sports Ground Premier League International Cup Stream details to be confirmed PSV Eindhoven Next up is a familiar face: PSV Eindhoven. One of Dutch football’s giants, PSV have enjoyed remarkable success in recent seasons, winning three successive Eredivisie titles. They have been crowned Dutch champions 27 times and have a long-standing reputation for producing top-level talent, making Jong PSV another intriguing test for the Young Eagles. Palace and Jong PSV have plenty of history in this competition. The Dutch side edged a dramatic 22/23 final after 120 minutes before winning on penalties, but the Young Eagles got their revenge the following season. In front of more than 2,000 supporters at Selhurst Park, Franco Umeh’s deflected second-half strike secured a 1-0 victory and handed Palace their first Premier League International Cup title Jong PSV have already begun this season’s competition too, drawing 1-1 with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. One to watch: Keziah Ogene. The 18-year-old attacker recently joined PSV from Eintracht Frankfurt and caught the eye against Sunderland, producing an acrobatic finish in the 1-1 draw. Match Details Palace U21s v PSV Eindhoven U21s Tuesday, 19th January KO: 19:00 BST The Borough Sports Ground Premier League International Cup Stream details to be confirmed FC Porto FC Porto are one of Portugal’s biggest clubs and have won more than 30 league titles, alongside a glittering collection of domestic and European honours. Their B team - who could conclude Palace's 26/27 International Cup group-stage - compete in Liga Portugal 2 and have a unique place in Portuguese football history, having become the first reserve side to win the second tier. Porto B are also no strangers to this competition. They are the record winners of the International Cup, lifting the trophy in 16/17 and 17/18. With another European heavyweight waiting in the final group fixture, Palace will face a serious test from start to finish. One to watch: Tiago Andrade. The winger joined Porto as an Under-15 player and has progressed through the club’s academy to the B team. Andrade has already been involved around Porto’s first team and has made an impact at the start of the new campaign. The date for Palace’s meeting with Porto will be released in due course. Ticketing and broadcast details for the confirmed fixtures, meanwhile, will be announced separately. Easter Island (A) When watching the cup draw, any team is keen to avoid a potential banana skin, so Santiago Wanderers probably weren't too thrilled when they pulled out a trip to the remote Juan Fernandez Islands in the 2024 Copa Chile. The fixture meant a journey to Robinson Crusoe Island, 400 miles off the Chilean coast and named after the famed Daniel Defoe novel, which tells the story of a shipwrecked English merchant stranded on a remote island for 28 years. There weren't enough commercial routes available for Santiago Wanderers to reach the island, so they had to call upon a Chilean navy supply ship, the Aquiles, to face unknown opposition. Juan Fernandez's team had been hastily assembled from recreational teams on the island, but were hampered by players missing training for lobster harvesting. They still made their professional opponents sweat though, only narrowly losing 2-1. Easter Island's Estadio de Hanga Roa before its 2014 redevelopment (Image credit: Joe Mewis) It was the second time a team from the country's remote islands had entered the Copa Chile. In 2009, a team from Rapa Nui, more commonly known as Easter Island, hosted Colo-Colo , who are widely regarded as the nation's most successful club. Colo-Colo returned home 4-0 winners, but the most memorable moment was Rapa Nui's pre-match Polynesian war dance, on a field flanked by two of the island's famous Moai statues. Too bad to take part When a club is kicked out of their league, you generally presume they've cheated to win, but for Sueca United it was the reverse – thrown out of the lower levels of Valencia's league system for being so bad they were accused of not trying. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. The club were the brainchild of eccentric actor Pau Codina and offered a chance to those who may not have got a game elsewhere. As admirable as that was, it left Sueca outmatched week after week. Over 11 seasons, they lost more than 300 games in a row, letting in more than 4,000 goals. The average scoreline throughout the club's history was 24-0. Come September 2023, the Valencian Football Federation had lost patience and expelled Sueca United after just two games, including a 40-0molly-whopping. Enough! A derby on a ferry?! Football players stand at a football pitch on the lower deck of a ferry on its way from Hiiumaa to mainland, Estonia, on March 30, 2013 (Image credit: AFP via Getty Images) The Estonian islands of Saaremaa and Hiiumaa have always had a fierce but good-natured rivalry. When they decided to play a football match in 2013, neither side was willing to surrender their home advantage, so they came up with a novel approach to a neutral venue – the game was played aboard the M/S Muhumaa passenger ferry connecting the islands. A grass lawn was laid down on the boat's deck, but there was only room for five-a-side, which probably reduced the risk of any challenges going, erm, overboard if things heated up. Hiiumaa won 4-1 – a surprise, as Saaremaa is home to FC Kuressaare, who play in the Estonian top flight. Unusually, they train in Tallinn but host home games on their island, meaning home matches often require longer journeys than away trips. Have boots, will travel Sudanese side Al Hilal recently achieved an unprecedented feat – winning the league in three different countries, in the space of just two seasons. Displaced from their homeland by a brutal civil war, they and Sudanese rivals Al Merrikh joined Mauritania's Super D1 League for 2024-25. The two countries aren't exactly neighbours, situated around 3,000 miles apart, but Al Hilal duly finished top of the table, albeit only recognised as “honorary champions”, with locals FC Nouadhibou technically the title winners. The two Sudanese clubs then briefly returned to their own country, with Al Hilal winning the Elite League – a short-form event to determine which clubs would represent the nation in continental competitions. Both then joined the Rwanda Premier League for 2025-26, where Al Hilal comfortably completed an unlikely treble. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List Oxygen required There was endless talk about the effects of playing at altitude before England's World Cup win in Mexico City this year, but that was trivial compared to a visit to Peruvian side Union Minas. From the 1980s to the early 2000s, the Cerro de Pasco side reached the summit of Peruvian football with their squad of jobbing veterans and nearly men, aided by substantial home advantage. The Estadio Daniel Alcides Carrion is the highest stadium in the world at around 14,000 feet above sea level – that's about 2,126 Dan Burns, and less than 4,000 feet lower than the base camps on Mount Everest. Opposition teams were so overwhelmed by the altitude that they would frequently be incapacitated, with oxygen masks a common sight in the visiting dressing room at half-time. Union briefly led the top tier standings in the 1998 season, but the decline of the mining industry hit the area hard and they slid down the leagues before halting operations in 2011, only returning last year. Six titles and a funeral Some clubs evoke strong feelings of animosity from their rivals without it being entirely obvious why. For others, it's more apparent. Take Maltese club Valletta FC, for example. The Lilywhites are one of Malta’s most successful clubs – they’ve won 25 league titles and in 2000-01, they laughed in the face of Gerard Houllier’s Liverpool cup treble by winning an almost unheard of domestic sextuple, at once securing the Premier League, Rothmans Trophy, Super Five Cup, Lowenbrau Cup, Super Cup and the Centenary Cup. But it's the way Valletta celebrate their success that antagonises opponents – whenever they win the league, fans hold a mock funeral street parade for their beaten rivals, carrying coffins with the insignia of their rivals through the streets. It was no great surprise then that when Valletta suffered the first relegation of their history in 2023-24, a healthy dose of schadenfreude was expressed by other clubs. Free trip to Tahiti Beautiful Bora Bora (Image credit: Getty Images) Since 1961, the Coupe de France has allowed entrants from French territories around the world, creating some of the most epic away days in world football. The French Football Federation covers the costs, but amateur teams still have to brave getting time off from their day jobs for what could be a lengthy jaunt. In 2024-25, fourth-tier Normandy side US Avranches landed an away match with AS Dragon from Papeete in Tahiti – flying nearly 10,000 miles from rainy northern France to a tropical paradise island in the Pacific Ocean, only to lose on penalties after a 2-2 draw. The wrong club While players will always try to pretend that a transfer is motivated by a previous love for their new club, in reality there are often unspoken reasons behind switching teams. One of the strangest was the case of Congolese winger Thievy Bifouma's move to Iranian side Esteghlal Khuzestan in 2024. The former West Bromwich Albion loanee explained he put pen to paper because he wanted to face Cristiano Ronaldo in the Asian Champions League. “I reviewed the calendar and realised they had a game against Al Nassr – I said to myself this was where I wanted to go,” he told Iranian media. The slight issue was that Al Nassr had a date with Esteghlal FC, based in Tehran, not Esteghlal Khuzestan, a completely different team situated hundreds of miles to the south. “I had no idea there were two teams named Esteghlal,” Bifouma admitted. “When I arrived, my countryman Gael Kakuta called me and asked where I was.” Kakuta played for Esteghlal FC – the pair quickly realised that they wouldn't be team-mates after all. "We got out of jail today, lads" A Young male detention centre for under-20-year-olds known as "Fundaçao Casa" or Febem, established by the Sao Paulo city government to help young offenders back to society (Image credit: Getty Images) There are a fair few prison-based football teams around the world, but Welsh side HMP Prescoed are a rarity – their players aren't made up of guards or support staff, they're inmates at the Category D, or open, prison. The team competes in the Gwent Central League, where a cursory glance at the league table suggests they appear to have an excellent home record, but abysmal away form. The reality is that HMP Prescoed aren't allowed to travel to away matches, for obvious reasons – they play them on their own field but must forfeit every game 5-0 and take a three-point deduction. As a result, the best-case scenario for the season is to finish on zero points. Last season they ended on minus five, having bagged five wins and a draw from their 14 fixtures. Amercian nightmare When the small Caribbean island of Antigua was given a chance to enter a club in the United Soccer League, the third tier of US football, it seemed like a great opportunity. By the time of their ill-fated third campaign in 2013 though, Antigua Barracuda's dream had turned into a nightmare. The league was supposed to be ‘international', but three teams from Puerto Rico were removed during the 2011 season, and by 2013 Barracuda were forced into relocation to the US mainland just to participate at all. The cash-strapped team lived in a cramped hotel in Tampa, Florida, making journeys of up to 10 hours in a tiny minibus to fulfil fixtures. At one point they even had to train in their hotel's car park, as they didn't have access to a pitch. They lost 26 games out of 26. Okinawa's number two team Third-tier Japanese side FC Ryukyu come from the island of Okinawa, famed for its beaches, coral reefs and a well-known Second World War battle. Okinawa was once the Ryukyu Kingdom, a separate entity from Japan, and retains its own unique culture. It's also geographically detached from the rest of Jap

articles.body: U21s preview: Palace host PSG in International Cup opener Skip navigation U21s preview: Palace host PSG in International Cup opener Match previews 30 Aug 2026 Crystal Palace Under-21s begin their 2026/27 Premier League International Cup campaign against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday (2nd September, KO: 19:00 BST) – and there’s plenty to look forward to at Borough Sports Ground. It’s not just the first team flying the flag in Europe this season, with Season Ticket+, Gold and Junior Gold Members able to enjoy free entry to selected Under-18 and Under-21 home games. Buy PSG tickets Story so far... Darren Powell’s U21s have made an unbeaten start to the 2026/27 campaign, drawing 1-1 with Arsenal before securing their first victory with a 2-0 triumph at Aston Villa on Friday night. First-team star Zavier Gozo opened his account for the season at Arsenal, finishing a swift counter-attack to put Palace ahead, before the hosts levelled in the second half. The Young Eagles pushed for a winner late on but had to settle for a point. Palace started Bank Holiday weekend by producing a disciplined display at Villa. Harry Lee was outstanding as the hosts applied sustained pressure after the interval, making a string of excellent saves before Benji Casey broke the deadlock against the run of play. Adler Nascimento then put the result beyond doubt with a superb late finish. Those opening two fixtures came in a new-look Premier League 2, which now features all 31 Category One academies in a single division, with each side playing 20 matches before the top 16 progress to a single-elimination play-off. Now Palace turn their attention to the International Cup, a competition that has already delivered a memorable chapter in the Academy’s history. After finishing runners-up to Jong PSV in 22/23, the Young Eagles went one better the following season, defeating the Dutch side to lift the trophy. Palace’s title defence ended at the group stage in 24/25, while last season they progressed to the quarter-finals, where Real Sociedad got the better of them. There will be hopes that Powell’s side can go even further this time around, beginning with Wednesday night’s intriguing test against PSG! Our opposition – PSG They don’t come much bigger in European football than PSG. The French giants were named France’s best academy for 25/26 by the French Football Federation, showcasing the remarkable conveyor belt of talent coming through their ranks. Ten academy graduates have featured for PSG’s first team, while 12 have played in the UEFA Champions League and more than 20 have represented France at youth level. The club’s reach extends well beyond Paris, too, with more than 30 players aged under 23 developed by PSG now under professional contract with clubs in the top two divisions across Europe’s top 10 leagues. The Espoirs have already had a taste of English opposition this season, beating Manchester City 1-0 in a pre-season friendly, and will be hoping for another positive result on English soil on Wednesday. Last season, PSG finished fourth in their International Cup group. They began with a 2-0 win over Newcastle United before beating Chelsea 3-1, with Housni scoring twice. A 2-2 draw with Brighton & Hove Albion left them needing victory at Nottingham Forest on the final matchday to progress, but a 2-0 defeat brought their campaign to an end - they’ll be aiming to go one better this time around. Premier League International Cup explained Fancy some European football? You’re in the right place. Launched in 14/15, the Premier League International Cup gives Premier League academies the chance to go head-to-head with some of the best young sides from across Europe. The 26/27 competition features the top 16 Premier League 2 sides from last season alongside 16 invited European clubs. The 32 teams are split into four groups of eight, with four PL2 sides and four overseas teams in each. Every club plays four group-stage matches, all hosted in England, with the top two in each group advancing to the quarter-finals. Likely line-up Expected PSG line-up: Vignaud, Zague, Mfutila, Olax (c), Bastaraud, Diyinu Nzinga, Ghalleb, N’Guessan, Nsoki, Bezeme, Domingos. Team news PSG’s International Cup squad is their U21 side, known as the Espoirs. It features players progressing through the club’s academy towards senior football. Several members of the group have already gained experience at Under-19 level as they continue their development in Paris. Last time out… Palace put PSG to the sword in their last meeting, running out 7-3 winners in the International Cup group stages at Dulwich Hamlet’s Champion Hill in September 2022. Paddy McCarthy was in charge of the Young Eagles, with John-Kymani Gordon leading the charge with a hat-trick. Victor Akinwale, David Omilabu, Maliq Cadogan and Fionn Mooney were also on target as Palace extended their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions. It also sent the Young Eagles top of their International Cup group. Can history repeat itself on Wednesday? Key player – Fabio Domingos Fabio Domingos is one to watch for the visitors, with the Luxembourg-born winger joining PSG from Metz in 2025 after representing Luxembourg at youth level and Cape Verde’s senior side. Domingos was part of PSG’s U19 side last season, helping them win the Championnat National U19 title for a third successive year. He has featured for both the U19s and U21s this season, continuing his progression through the Parisian academy. The manager – Jean-François Vulliez Jean-François Vulliez leads PSG’s Under-21s and the Frenchman brings extensive experience in youth development, having spent more than a decade at Lyon, including six years as the club’s academy director. He later moved into senior football, working as an assistant coach at Lyon before taking up the same role at Danish side AC Horsens. Vulliez joined PSG last summer. How to follow The match will be streamed LIVE on Palace TV+ on Wednesday, with coverage beginning at 18:45 BST ahead of the 19:00 BST kick-off. Supporters can also follow live commentary on our Academy X page , with a full match report and reaction published shortly after full-time in our Academy news section Highlights and extended reaction will be available on Palace TV+ Match details Crystal Palace U21s v Paris Saint-Germain U21s Wednesday, 2nd September 19:00 BST Premier League International Cup Borough Sports Ground Match ticket prices Adults (21-64): £5 Young Adults (17-21): £1 Seniors (65+): £1 Juniors (2-16): £1 Academy Founder Members: Free Adult Gold, Junior Gold & Season Ticket+ Holders: Free Tickets are available here and will be issued as PDF print-at-home tickets at the point of sale. articles.body: Tottenham Hotspur 0 Newcastle United 2 | NUFC Match Report. Tottenham Hotspur 0 Newcastle United 2 Published 3 days ago Team Men Second-half strikes from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa sealed a 2-0 win for Newcastle United in Saturday's Premier League clash against Tottenham Hotspur. Luke Vinton Written by After a goalless first half at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Elanga's swivelled finish fired the visitors in front shortly after the hour mark. Wissa's improvised finish, his first competitive goal since January, doubled United's advantage as Matthias Jaissle recorded his first Premier League win in charge of the Magpies. The German head coach made six changes from Wednesday's 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, with Nico González making his Magpies bow following his transfer from Manchester City. Targeting a third successive away win against Spurs, Newcastle went close to taking the lead inside the opening 60 seconds. Elanga, who netted his first Premier League goal for Newcastle in last weekend's 2-2 draw against Liverpool, latched onto Amar Dedić's clever header following Nico González's long-range pass but the Swedish winger's cross-cum shot was turned out by Archie Gray at the back post. Lukáš Horníček produced a strong stop to prevent Mathys Tel from breaking the deadlock as the French forward cut inside from the left flank before his curling effort was pushed away by the Czech shot-stopper. Lewis Hall produced a heroic last-ditch block to prevent Pedro Porro from firing Spurs ahead minutes later, turning the Spanish full-back's close-range effort over the crossbar. The Spurs full-back went close in front of goal as the Magpies defence were unable to clear from a short corner before his volley from the edge of the box flew wide of the target. Wissa went close to netting his first Premier League goal since December as the DR Congo international attempted to fire a shot at goal inside the six-yard area after Elanga nodded the ball into the African striker's path but his effort was blocked by Micky van de Ven. Horníček carried out two terrific saves before the half-time whistle, beating away Andy Robertson's low drive from an acute angle. From the resulting corner, the Czech 'keeper was alert to pushing away Jan Paul van Hecke's close-range header. Lewis Hall went close to breaking the deadlock shortly after the restart as the left-back cut inside on the edge of the box before his curling right-footed effort flew over the crossbar. In the 62nd minute, Elanga broke the deadlock for United. After Nico's impressive long-range pass flew into Dedić's path, the Bosnian full-back nodded the ball into Elanga's path before the Swedish frontman produced a neat turn before firing the ball into the net via the left-hand post. Horníček prevented Porro from drawing Spurs level as the Spaniard's fierce drive from the edge of the box was tipped over the crossbar by the 24-year-old 'keeper. In the 72nd minute, Newcastle extended their advantage as Wissa netted his first goal of the 2026/27 campaign. After Hall's inviting corner from the right flank was nodded towards substitute Nick Woltemade, Wissa was on hand to turn the ball home from close-range. Horníček ensured a first clean sheet of his Magpies career in the closing stages, holding Omar Marmoush's volley after Mateus Fernandes' cross found the unmarked Egyptian inside the penalty area. There was a brief Premier League debut for Bazoumana Touré as the Ivorian winger, who scored on his competitive Magpies bow during Wednesday's win against West Brom, was introduced in stoppage-time. Newcastle United: Lukáš Horníček, Lewis Hall, Sven Botman, Nico González (Sean Steur 71), Yoane Wissa (Jacob Ramsey 82), Harvey Barnes (Bazoumana Touré 90), Malick Thiaw (c), Anthony Elanga (Jacob Murphy 82), Joe Willock (Nick Woltemade 71), Amar Dedić, Lewis Miley. West Ham finished 18th in the Premier League last season (Image credit: Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google West Ham have got their Championship campaign underway as the Hammers look to bounce back from last season’s dire relegation campaign. Nuno Espirito Santos’ side finished the season in 18th place to end a 14-year stay in the top flight, a period which saw them regularly oscillate between European pushes and survival battles. Throughout this time, West Ham have been heavy spenders in the transfer market, but according to one former Hammers star, their recruitment has lacked the foresight and planning to build a balanced squad. Tony Gale on West Ham’s transfer policies Matheus Fernandes was a £40million signing from Southampton in 2025 (Image credit: Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Ex-West Ham favourite Tony Gale believes that the constant turnover of directors of football and other key transfer figures has meant cohesiveness has been lacking, leading to the club falling behind one of their rivals from across London. “Fulham’s buying strategy has been far and away the better of the two,” Gale tells FourFourTwo . “It's designed to build a more balanced squad, with a good sell-on value for players.” Sebastien Haller cost the club £45million in 2019 (Image credit: PA) This has seen the Cottagers establish themselves as a mid-table Premier League side following their 2022 promotion from the Championship , with finishes of 10th, 13th, 11th and 11th over the past four seasons. An effective transfer model, where the ability to develop players so that their sell-on value increases alongside their effectiveness on the pitch is vital in the current financial climate, but for Gale, this is not something West Ham have been able to replicate. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “West Ham seem to have been more reactive than proactive in the transfer market, taking action when a weakness is exposed,” he bemoans. Central to his problem has been the revolving door of decision-makers behind the scenes. “Then there’s been the constant changing of directors of football and the people recruiting,” he adds, before raising the basic issues that this problem brings on. Nuno Espirito Santo will be looking to take the Hammers straight back up (Image credit: Getty Images) “Who’s been doing the buying? An agent comes on the phone and sells you his player. Well, every agent is going to do that.” Gale’s ultimate conclusion here is one of another former Hammers favourite. “What was it Harry Redknapp said? ‘They’ll have your trousers down’.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown. articles.title: Scott: We had chances to go and win the game
articles.excerpt: Midfielder Alex Scott felt AFC Bournemouth “deserved to win the game” after they were pegged back late on in a 1-1 draw against Everton. The Cherries midfielder struck in the opening half at Vitality Stadium, capping off a slick counter-attack after brilliant work from Evanilson. But the Toffees found a leveller in second-half stoppage time through James Tarkowski, meaning Marco Rose’s side were left to settle for a point in their opening home game of the season. Speaking post-match, Scott said: “I think we deserved to win the game. A mistake at the end and it’s cost us three points, which in this league, between three points and one, that’s the margin. “We had chances to go and win the game and we didn’t take them. Now it’s time to focus on Newcastle next week. “I think we were the better team on the day and probably deserved the points but they got stuck in there and got the goal at the end.” Reflecting on his goal. articles.title: West Brom U18 0-4 Fulham U18
articles.excerpt: Fulham Under-18s continued their unbeaten start to the season with a 4-0 victory at West Brom. Andrew Joslin’s side were in control in the first period, but only had Khai Vally’s converted penalty to show for it. But the goals arrived in a slick second half display. Kayden Sessegnon got off the mark for the U18s after prodding home a Will Sutton-Bangura cross, before Bashil Lubega and Sessegnon both rounded West Brom goalkeeper William Rutter to seal a convincing away day victory. The game could have been very different though had Zack Brief not made an important stop within the first 60 seconds. A mix up at the back allowed Frazer Billings to nip in, but Brief was out well to gobble the ball up at the feet of the attacker. But it was mostly all Fulham attacks after that early scare. We had the opportunity to take the lead after just seven minutes when Dylan De-Gale was tripped after wriggling into the box following a neat one-two with Sutton-Bangura. Vally sent Rutter the wrong way to score his third penalty of the season. articles.title: POTM MCATEE DISCUSSES POINT AGAINST LIVERPOOL
articles.excerpt: McAtee discusses Forest’s point against Liverpool Reds took the lead twice at Anfield Midfielder scooped POTM award from the game James McAtee says the Nottingham Forest players didn’t know how to feel after picking up a point against Liverpool. The Reds led twice at Anfield, but two equalisers meant it was a point for the Reds on an afternoon when it could easily have been all three. McAtee was named Player of the Match after an outstanding individual display, but the playmaker was full of praise for his teammates for sticking together and taking a point from the game. “We don’t really know how to feel. To come here and get a point is amazing, but the game was in our hands twice. “There’s a bit of disappointment because we could have got the points, but we’re also happy with the performance. We came here, we stuck together and we put a good point on the board. “It was a credit to the players for taking the lead again after they equalised. But when you come here anything can happen, so we can’t be too disappointed. “We stuck to the game plan, we tried to get in scoring positions, which we did. Alisson made an unbelievable save from Igor which would have seen us 2-0 up at the break.

articles.body: Confirmed line-up: Debut for González at Spurs | NUFC Latest. Confirmed line-up: Debut for González at Spurs Published 3 days ago Team Men New signing Nico González has been handed his Newcastle United debut ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash away at Tottenham Hotspur (kick-off 5:30pm BST). The Spanish midfielder, who arrived on Tyneside from Manchester City earlier this week, is one of six changes from Wednesday's 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup. Goalkeeper Lukáš Horníček, who made his Premier League debut in last week's 2-2 draw against Liverpool, replaces Ewen Jaouen in-between the sticks. Head coach Matthias Jaissle has named an unchanged backline for a third consecutive game, with Malick Thiaw and Sven Botman situated at the heart of United's defence, while Amar Dedić and Lewis Hall are set to play on the respective flanks. González, who made his Premier League bow against Newcastle in February 2025, will line up alongside Lewis Miley in the middle of the park. Harvey Barnes, who netted a second half brace against West Brom, as well as Joe Willock and Anthony Elanga are named in the starting 11 as they aim to provide attacking support for Yoane Wissa, who has three goal involvements in his last three league outings against Spurs. Jaissle has a number of options to deploy from the substitutes' bench if required, including Jacob Ramsey who netted the winning goal in last season's 2-1 victory at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Nick Woltemade, who scored in United's 2-0 win against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup last season, is also named on the bench as well as Bazoumana Touré, Jacob Muphy, Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba. Fabian Schär and Leo Shahar, the latter targeting his Premier League debut, are defensive reinforcements. articles.title: Granit Xhaka's Fulham programme notes
articles.excerpt: Good afternoon everyone, and welcome back to the Stadium of Light for our first home game of the season against Fulham. Before I signed here last summer, I knew exactly why I was coming to Sunderland. The first thing I thought was that if this team believed and worked with the right mentality, we could achieve many things together. Last season, we created memories that will stay with us forever, and you stood with us every step of the way. We achieved something special, and now we have the opportunity to build on that with Premier League and European football ahead of us. We know what you expect from us. Ultimately, I want to win, but we know that doesn’t just start at the weekend – it starts on the training ground earlier that week. It’s a process and a project, and we can’t turn it off and on. We know how hard we need to work. We are in four competitions this season, so we have to take it game-by-game. We are not thinking about anything other than the next game. This is what we did last season, and we will do exactly the same this season. Last weekend was not the result we wanted, but it’s important that we learn from it and continue to work. articles.title: FOREST CLAIM POINT AGAINST LIVERPOOL
articles.excerpt: Nottingham Forest picked up a first point of the 2026/27 Premier League campaign as the Reds drew 2-2 against Liverpool at Anfield. Ndoye opened the scoring with his, and Forest’s, first goal of the campaign, sweeping the ball beyond Alisson at the Kop End. The home side equalised through Alexander Isak’s tap-in on the hour mark. Forest’s lead was restored soon after when Neco Williams was brought down by Alisson, allowing Morgan Gibbs-White to step up and convert from 12 yards. Víctor Muñoz levelled for the second time for Liverpool in the final 10 minutes of the game. Both sides enjoyed chances throughout the entertaining contest, but the result ensures the Reds are off the mark for the season and extends their unbeaten run at Anfield to three successive matches. First half After an even start on Merseyside, Forest fashioned the first sight of goal when Ola Aina’s deep cross was headed into Igor Jesus’ path by Ndoye, only for Liverpool defender Jérémy Jacquet to stretch a boot out and block the effort. Garner replaces summer signing Hayden Hackney, who is among the substitutes having missed the midweek Carabao Cup win at Preston North End with an ankle knock. The rest of Everton's team remains the same as the one which saw off the Eagles at Hill Dickinson Stadium – Harrison Armstrong and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall joining Garner in central midfield, with Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George the wingers, and in-form Thierno Barry up front. The Toffees' backline is again formed of full-backs Merlin Röhl and Vitalii Mykolenko, central defenders James Tarkowski and Jarrad Branthwaite, and goalkeeper Jordan Pickford. Meanwhile, Tim Iroegbunam is on the bench after recovering from an injury sustained in pre-season. articles.title: “Beating Fulham was one of the best nights of my career. I took my shirt off and threw myself onto the turf as if it were a swimming pool” Diego Forlan on his 2010 Europa League success
articles.excerpt: During his two-decade career as a professional footballer, Diego Forlan has played in eight countries across three continents and turned out in a World Cup semi-final on his way to winning more than 100 international caps. This journey has thrown up plenty of career highlights, but for the former Manchester United man, the 2010 Europa League final remains a particular standout. The forward was a key part of Atletico Madrid’s 2-1 extra-time success over Fulham in Hamburg that night, scoring both goals for his side, including a 116th-minute winner to end the Cottagers' fairytale run to their first European final. Forlan on firing Atletico to Europa League glory Forlan joined Atletico Madrid in 2007 (Image credit: Alamy) “That night in Hamburg was one of the best of my career,” Forlan tells FourFourTwo . “A dream final. Not so much because it was a brilliant match, but because of the script.” Fulham’s remarkable run to the final in just their second-ever European campaign had seen them first navigate a group containing Roma , CSKA Moscow and Basel, before Shakhtar Donetsk, Juventus , Wolfsburg and Hamburg were accounted for in the knockouts. This journey has thrown up plenty of career highlights, but for the former Manchester United man, the 2010 Europa League final remains a particular standout. The forward was a key part of Atletico Madrid’s 2-1 extra-time success over Fulham in Hamburg that night, scoring both goals for his side, including a 116th-minute winner to end the Cottagers' fairytale run to their first European final. Forlan on firing Atletico to Europa League glory Forlan joined Atletico Madrid in 2007 (Image credit: Alamy) “That night in Hamburg was one of the best of my career,” Forlan tells FourFourTwo . “A dream final. Not so much because it was a brilliant match, but because of the script.” Fulham’s remarkable run to the final in just their second-ever European campaign had seen them first navigate a group containing Roma , CSKA Moscow and Basel, before Shakhtar Donetsk, Juventus , Wolfsburg and Hamburg were accounted for in the knockouts. Roy Hodgson had led Fulham to the Europa League final (Image credit: PA) “Fulham arrived as the underdog, but they made life very difficult for us,” Forlan continues. I scored after half an hour, Simon Davies equalised, and the final went to extra time.” With the clock continuing to run down, penalties loomed, only for Forlan to deliver when it mattered most, as he took full advantage of a chance that fell his way deep in the second half of extra time. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. “When everything seemed to be heading for a penalty shootout, Sergio Aguero battled for a ball out wide and spotted me in the heart of the box,” he continues. “I managed to get the tip of my boot to it to give Atletico the title.” Forlan’s reaction to the goal was as instinctive as his finish. “I took my shirt off and threw myself onto the turf as if it were a swimming pool,” he recalls. Forlan scored 96 goals in five seasons with Atletico (Image credit: Getty Images) For Forlan, the significance of the goal stretched further than just adding another title to Atletico’s roll of honour. “That goal tasted like glory, because it also marked a turning point for a club that started to feel important again,” he believes. “Spain’s capital, a city used to seeing Real Madrid celebrating titles, was painted red and white, and thousands of fans gathered at Plaza de Neptuno in a huge display of pride.” TOPICS Joe Mewis For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.
