articles.title: Under-18s Defeated By Manchester United
articles.excerpt: Everton Under-18s were beaten 3-0 by Manchester United at Finch Farm on Saturday morning. James McEvoy had the ball in the net early on for the visitors but it was ruled out for offside, before United got one that did count midway through the first half, as the dangerous Edson DeJonge-Seiros crossed from the left and Jariyah Shah slammed into the back of the net. Everton grew into the contest and Harry Brookes saw an effort blocked, while Dafi Pemberton spun cleverly on the edge of the penalty area before pulling his shot wide of the target. The Blues' Rodney Aduda then saw his header well saved after being picked out by Harvey Billington. United had chances, too. Juame Camacho wasn’t far away with a snapshot and Nathaniel Junior-Brown failed to hit the target after catching the hosts' in possession. Early in the second period, Blues' goalkeeper Ted Wilcox safely gathered an attempt from DeJonge-Seiros and, at the other end, a John Dodds close-range volley was athletically turned away by United shot-stopper Charlie Hardy. The second United goal came on 56 minutes – James McEvoy heading home from a dangerous corner. Genuine opportunities were at a premium after that. Freddie Murdock

Matthias Jaissle was confirmed as Eddie Howe's replacement at Newcastle United this summer (Image credit: Newcastle United v Getty Images) Facebook Pinterest Email Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Less than two years ago, FourFourTwo sat inside the bowels of Al Ahli's inner city training ground in Jeddah, and whispers abounded. “If he loses this game, the manager might well be sacked,” one Saudi Pro League expert told us that evening, as we waited for Matthias Jaissle to arrive for his latest pre-match press conference. Al Ahli had won only three of their first eight games of the new league season, and sat eighth in the table before the Jeddah derby with title-challenging Al Ittihad – a fixture that would attract a raucous crowd of 52,546. Given that Jaissle's club were one of the Saudi Pro League's big four – all owned by the country's Public Investment Fund (PIF) – their results were below expectation. Back then, the main focus of our visit to Al Ahli had been the recent signing of Ivan Toney , rather than Jaissle, who was largely unknown to British audiences in October 2024. Our question was whether he could help his new frontman make England's next World Cup squad – Jaissle knew Thomas Tuchel, having played for him in the youth teams at VfB Stuttgart. “Let's see if Thomas calls me and asks how Ivan is doing,” the smartly dressed Jaissle told FFT . “Ivan has the potential, definitely – he must deliver here to be seen in the UK, and we're doing our best to bring him into the best shape.” Prior to this summer's World Cup, Tuchel did indeed call Jaissle to discuss Toney, revealing the “fantastic feedback” he received was enough to persuade him to pick the 30-year-old in his squad. By then, though, Jaissle could easily have been long gone as Al Ahli boss. He did lose that Jeddah derby against Al Ittihad, a tetchy game interrupted by a sandstorm that blew dust from the nearby desert into the stadium. He avoided the sack, but was reportedly on his way out two months later after a loss at Al Kholood, with Max Allegri said to be his long-term replacement. Pick the ultimate 4-4-2 line-up from players in FourFourTwo's definitive Top 100 List That was until ultras protested at the training ground, putting up a banner declaring “Enough failure, leave!” The message was aimed at the club's hierarchy, rather than the manager. Jaissle stayed, and became an Al Ahli legend within months. The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week. Jaissle was a central defender during a playing career that saw him help Hoffenheim to the Bundesliga for the first time in 2008, when he'd just turned 20. He'd been expected to be alongside Mesut Ozil, Mats Hummels and Manuel Neuer as part of the Germany under-21 squad that thrashed England in the final of the Euros in 2009, but damaged his ACL shortly before the tournament and would never be the same player again. Further injuries forced him to retire in 2014, aged 25, before he got a job as a youth coach at RB Leipzig – his former Hoffenheim manager Ralf Rangnick had since become a key man in Red Bull's football project. Jaissle adopted a similarly high-pressing style, and has taken it with him ever since. After a stint as assistant at Danish club Brondby, he joined Red Bull Salzburg, led their feeder side FC Liefering to a joint-highest finish, then was handed the reins at the main club, replacing Jesse Marsch in 2021. Matthias Jaissle poses after leading FC Red Bull Salzburg to the Austrian championship in 2023 (Image credit: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty I) Working with young players such as Benjamin Sesko , Karim Adeyemi, Noah Okafor and Brenden Aaronson, he took Salzburg to a double in his first season, plus the Champions League's knockout stage for the only time in their history. They lost 7-1 at Bayern Munich in the last 16, while Jaissle was still only 33. A season later, they went 30 matches unbeaten on the way to yet another domestic triumph. It was Salzburg's 10th straight title, but they haven't won the league since Jaissle left that summer. The German joined Al Ahli just a month after they'd been one of four clubs to be taken over by the Saudi PIF – together with Al Ittihad, Al Hilal and Cristiano Ronaldo' s Al Nassr. Jaissle's new club had been Saudi Pro League champions in 2016 but relegated since, only returning to the top flight in the same summer as his arrival. They quickly signed Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino, Edouard Mendy, Franck Kessie and ex-Newcastle winger Allan Saint-Maximin, finishing an encouraging third in Jaissle's first season – enough to qualify for the Asian Champions League. Ivan Tony scored 72 goals in two seasons under Jaissle (Image credit: Getty Images) Then came Toney's arrival, and that tricky start to 2024-25 when Jaissle so nearly lost his job. He knew the pressure he was under when we visited, but didn't let it show – remaining professional throughout, even taking time to greet visiting European media afterwards. It was hard not to warm to him. “Things take time – the club has a long-term vision,” Jaissle told us, subtly calling for patience as he attempted to turn around results, while nodding to his ability to improve young players. “I hope we can do better by implementing the philosophy from the top down to the academy, because at some point we'll need the young talents. In my eyes, that is the right approach. “A lot of signings were made before I arrived, so it's important as a coach that you're flexible enough to adapt to a new country, culture and player profiles. In the long run, it's important everyone is aligned, that you improve your squad and players in the way you want to play.” Jaissle replaced Eddie Howe at Newcastle United this summer (Image credit: Getty Images) Jaissle was afforded time to do that. Their progress to the knockout stage of the Asian Champions League had been a factor in him avoiding the sack – Al Ahli had a stronger second half of the league campaign, improving to fifth, then surprisingly became kings of Asia for the first time ever. The Champions League's final three rounds all take place in Jeddah, giving Al Ahli a home advantage that helped, but they still had to defeat reigning Saudi champions Al Hilal in the semis, before a final victory over Japanese side Kawasaki Frontale – conquerors of Ronaldo's Al Nassr. Last term, while finishing third in a three-way domestic race, they went all Brian Clough's Nottingham Forest and became continental champions again. Toney was key, scoring 72 goals in two seasons under Jaissle. When PIF-owned Newcastle were looking for a manager to replace Eddie Howe this summer, it shouldn't have been a surprise that they opted for the German. Howe will be a tough act to follow, having delivered the Magpies a first major honour in 56 years. Why have a manager who's won one historic trophy, though, when you can have a gaffer who's won two? He's interviewed Pele, Zlatan and Santa Claus (it's a long story), as well as covering the World Cup, AFCON and the Clasico. He previously spent 10 years as a newspaper journalist, and completed the 92 in 2017. articles.title: Matthias Jaissle's team news update: González an 'option' for Spurs trip
articles.source_type: Manager team-news updates with named injuries and return timelines
articles.body: Matthias Jaissle's team news update: González an 'optio... | NUFC Latest. Matthias Jaissle's team news update: González an 'option' for Spurs trip Published 5 days ago Team Men Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle says new signing Nico González is an 'option' as he weighs up whether to hand the Spanish midfielder a debut at Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday (kick-off 5.30pm). United travel to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this weekend for their first away game of the new Premier League season, having been denied a win over Liverpool on the opening day by Dominik Szoboszlai's last-gasp penalty in the dying seconds of the 2-2 draw. The German boss also spoke about his ahead of the trip to the capital, where Newcastle won 2-1 last term. Jaissle spoke to the media on Thursday evening ahead of the clash with Roberto De Zerbi's men, who could hand a home debut to former Magpie Sandro Tonali. Here are some of the main talking points from his pre-match briefing: On former Manchester City man González... "He trained with us and he looked sharp. He's an option. "He is a smart player, he has huge potential, and already he brings huge quality to the squad." On Spurs... "We will be facing a top team. It is a difficult change. "We will not change our approach. We are facing a really strong opponent. With our playing style, we can cause any opponents problems." On his start to life at Newcastle... "I was really blessed with the warm welcome they gave me. "I have seen the atmosphere in the stadium already from these two competitive matches - it was really special. "This is a special club. We have a clear idea of how we want to play football. We will not change our approach." On the potential in his young squad... "We want to build on what we are building. "With the young lads we need to expect up and downs. I am really much looking forward to this journey. "The lads are very committed. I am really happy with what I am seeing in training - it will be something special to build on." articles.title: Akinmboni joins Dundee on season-long loan
articles.excerpt: AFC Bournemouth defender Matai Akinmboni has joined Scottish Premiership side Dundee on a season-long loan. The 19-year-old American centre-back moves to Dens Park for the 2026/27 campaign as he continues his development with regular first-team football. Akinmboni joined the Cherries from Major League Soccer outfit DC United in January 2025, signing with the club after making his senior debut for the Washington-based side at just 15 years and 328 days. A United States youth international, Akinmboni progressed through DC United's academy before establishing himself as one of the youngest players to appear in MLS. The move to Dundee will provide Akinmboni with the opportunity to gain further experience of senior football in the Scottish Premiership, with the defender joining a Dundee squad that also includes former Cherries player Owen Bevan. Bevan completed a permanent move to Dundee from Bournemouth this summer. Akinmboni will now link up with his former Cherries team-mate as Dundee continue their 2026/27 Scottish Premiership campaign.

articles.body: EFL Best Bets This Weekend - 29-30 August Seb's EFL Best Bets: Wednesday, Barnet and a Blackpool Shootout Round three of the EFL season and the coupon is starting to tell us things. The Statz acca sheet does the heavy lifting for this column every week - every match result, both-teams-to-score and goals line across the three divisions, priced against the model - and this weekend it likes home favourites with something to prove. Eight bets below, and a Weekend Double that pays around 9/5. Championship Middlesbrough v West Brom (Sat 12:30) Boro put three past Doncaster in the cup in midweek without breaking stride, and their league form line - three wins in five - reads better than a side that was scrapping for the play-offs in spring has any right to expect this early. West Brom have been flat on the road. The model makes the home win a 54% chance, which at the price is the best result bet in the division this week. The bet: Middlesbrough to win at 1.71 full match stats here Watford v West Ham (Sat 3:00pm) West Ham's first Championship August in a generation has gone better than the doom-mongers predicted - three wins in five, and the model rates them at 51% to make it another away day to remember at Vicarage Road. Watford have been generous at the back to everyone who has pressed them. The bet: West Ham to win at 1.79 full match stats here Cardiff v Sheffield United (Sat 3:00pm) The goals game of the division. The model's strongest both-teams-to-score number on the entire Championship coupon lands here at 61%, two sides who have started the season allergic to clean sheets. The bet: Both teams to score at 1.57 full match stats here League One Sheffield Wednesday v Bromley (Sat 3:00pm) Three wins from five for Wednesday, and Hillsborough against newly promoted opposition is exactly the fixture a side with their early-season swagger should be winning. The model has the home win at 59% - the strongest single in League One this weekend - and ranks it highly enough to anchor the Weekend Double below. The bet: Sheffield Wednesday to win at 1.79 full match stats here Blackpool v Peterborough (Sat 12:30) Pick a market, any market: the model makes this the most watchable game in the division, with both teams to score at 63% and the overs number a shade higher still. Posh away days have been chaos for years and Blackpool have won three of five scoring freely. Take the goals over the winner. The bet: Over 2.5 goals at 1.62 full match stats here League Two Barnet v Cheltenham (Sat 12:30) Four wins in five for Barnet, and the model makes Saturday lunchtime at The Hive a 58% home win - the top number on the League Two coupon. Sides that come up with momentum tend to keep swinging until somebody stops them, and Cheltenham on the road do not look like the somebody. The bet: Barnet to win at 1.57 full match stats here York v Exeter (Sat 3:00pm) Another of the promoted sides refusing to read the script. York have lost just once in five and the model puts them at 57% here against an Exeter side finding the fourth tier less forgiving than advertised. The bet: York to win at 1.62 full match stats here Shrewsbury v Salford (Sat 3:00pm) Salford's winless start has come with goals at both ends and Shrewsbury's games have been the same story. The model's top goals number in the division lives here at 61%. The bet: Over 2.5 goals at 1.80 full match stats here The Weekend Double The two strongest numbers on the coupon, one from each of the lower divisions: Sheffield Wednesday to beat Bromley and Barnet to beat Cheltenham . The model makes them 59% and 58% respectively, and the double pays around 9/5 (2.81) with bet365 at the time of writing. One from Hillsborough, one from The Hive, both done by tea-time on Saturday. FAQs How are the EFL best bets picked? Every selection starts on the Statz acca sheet, which prices every match result, both-teams-to-score and goals line across the Championship, League One and League Two against the Statz projections model. The column takes the strongest numbers, checks them against form, and keeps singles in the 1.50 to 2.60 band. What is the Weekend Double? The two strongest model calls across the divisions, combined into one two-leg accumulator with the combined price quoted at the time of writing. It settles like any double: both legs must win. Do you track results? Yes - every column's bets settle publicly the following week, winners and losers alike, and the season's running record is quoted whenever it is claimed. articles.title: The Story So Far: Mohamed-Ali Cho
articles.excerpt: An in-depth look into our 12 th summer signing, Mohamed-Ali Cho… Born on 19 January 2004 in Stains, a commune in the Seine-Saint-Denis department in the northern suburbs of Paris, France, Mohamed-Ali Cho moved to London at one week old and would begin his footballing journey at West Ham United. Briefly returning to France at the age of six to play for Chantilly in 2010, the forward was picked up by Paris Saint-Germain a year later. Spending four years with the Parisian giants, the forward returned to England at the age of 11, joining Everton’s academy. Spending five years with the Toffees, Cho’s next move saw him sign a professional contract with French side Angers on 2 May 2020, becoming the youngest ever player to sign a professional deal in French football. Making his B-team debut in the opening fixture of the Championnat National 2, playing the full fixture in a 2-0 win over Mont-de-Marsan, the forward would make his senior debut eight days later, replacing Sada Thioub in the 81st minute in a 2-0 loss at home to Bordeaux to become the then-youngest ever player to play for the club at just 16-years, seven months and 11 days old. articles.title: Cho Completes Hull City Move
articles.excerpt: Hull City are delighted to announce the signing of French forward Mohamed-Ali Cho from Ligue 1 side OGC Nice for an undisclosed fee. The exciting 22-year-old has penned a five-year deal with the Tigers until the summer of 2031, becoming the club’s 12th summer addition. Comfortable anywhere across the frontline, the pacy attacker made 93 appearances during a two-and-a-half-year spell with Nice, scoring 12 goals and providing 13 assists. The former France Under-21 international helped the Eagles secure fifth- and fourth-placed finishes in 2023/24 and 2024/25 respectively, featuring 13 times in the Europa League over the last two seasons. Cho played four games apiece in both the Champions League and Europa League for previous club Real Sociedad, making 40 appearances for the Spanish side between June 2022 and January 2024. Born in Stains, the former Paris Saint-Germain and Everton prospect became the youngest player to sign a professional contract in France, agreeing terms with Angers at just 16 in January 2020. articles.title: Fulham Vs Chelsea [2-3] Premier League 2026/2027: How Does Xabi Alonso's New Front Three Work? – Tactical Analysis
articles.excerpt: Chelsea’s new front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro starred in Xabi Alonso’s first Premier League win. This tactical analysis examines their complementary roles, pressing and attacking threat against Fulham.
articles.source_type: Manager tactics breakdowns, team shape, pressing and build-up analysis
articles.body: Fulham Vs Chelsea [2-3] Premier League 2026/2027 - Analysis The final match of the opening gameweek of the 2026/2027 Premier League season saw ex-teammates at Liverpool Real Madrid and Spain face off in the dugouts of Craven Cottage , as new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso began his tenure as Blues boss against a familiar face in new Fulham chief Álvaro Arbeloa The contest produced end-to-end action that resulted in a five-goal thriller that fell Chelsea’s way. Both teams leave with some serious defensive issues to address. However, the majority of Chelsea fans and neutrals will have left Monday’s match with the stellar performance of Alonso’s new front three firmly in the front of their minds. The contrasting and complementary profiles, all of whom displayed exactly the type of positivity, confidence and intent to solve problems that you want to see from your attackers, posed a constant threat to the Fulham backline from the first whistle (literally, with Chelsea’s opener coming in the very first minute). This Fulham versus Chelsea tactical analysis details how Alonso’s front three functioned in and out of possession in gameweek one. Fulham Vs Chelsea Lineups & Formations Figure 1 Fulham Lineup Vs Chelsea The hosts lined up in a 4-2-3-1 shape with Bernd Leno in goal behind a back four of Timothy Castagne Calvin Bassey Jorge Cuenca and Antonee Robinson , from right to left. Sander Berge and Alex Iwobi started in midfield, behind a creative attacking trio of Oscar Bobb Josh King and César Palacios , with Gonzalo García leading the line. Arbeloa made four changes to his starting XI during the match, the first of which saw Shea Charles replace Bobb in the 67th minute. A double change followed six minutes later, when Kevin and Ryan Sessegnon replaced Palacios and Berge. Then, in the 82nd minute, another forward, Rodrigo Muniz , was introduced for left-back Robinson. Chelsea Lineup Vs Fulham Meanwhile, the visitors set up in a 3-4-2-1 shape with Robert Sánchez in goal behind a back three of Josh Acheampong Maxence Lacroix and Levi Colwill Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato started as the wing-backs, while Reece James and Roméo Lavia played in central midfield. Chelsea’s attacking trio was Cole Palmer Morgan Rogers and João Pedro Alonso made five changes to his starting XI over the course of the match. In the 65th minute, he introduced Enzo Fernández and Pep Chavarría for Lavia and Hato. Then, 11 minutes later, Pedro Neto was introduced for Malo Gusto. Lastly, in the 82nd minute, Geovany Quenda and Estêvão came on for Palmer and Rogers. Fulham Vs Chelsea Stats While Fulham finished the game on top in the possession department (averaging 60.5% vs Chelsea’s 39.5%) , Chelsea were ultimately more efficient, which is what allowed them to leave Craven Cottage with all three points. The Blues generated more shots ( to Fulham’s ) and a slightly higher xG ( 2.48 vs Fulham’s 2.01 ), but that was enough given the quality in their forward line to make the most of the opportunities. Fulham favoured longer periods of possession, averaging 6.29 passes per possession to Chelsea’s 4.37 , while the Cottagers also had a far lower PPDA of 9.88 to Chelsea’s 17.46 The home side sought to play out from the back and build through the thirds patiently, while Chelsea set up to get the ball into their front three early and aggressively to let their quality on the ball do the work. There weren’t any players in Chelsea’s starting XI you’d really expect to see setting the world alight on the ball outside of that front three, and that showed in how Chelsea played. They looked to find those difference makers all the time, and thanks to some intelligent movement and good progressive passing, they were able to do so often enough to put three past Fulham, while also exploiting Fulham’s possession-based approach with intelligent pressing from the front on the other side of the ball. Chelsea Pass Map & Average Positions Vs Fulham Figure 2 Chelsea’s compact, vertically oriented structure in Figure 2 highlights how their progression had a strong bias towards the right-hand side, particularly running through Reece James (24) in central midfield and Palmer (10), who acted as the key connection into the final third. Though Palmer and Rogers (17) almost mirrored one another on paper, their roles contrasted heavily in practice. From his right-sided position, Palmer assumed the responsibilities associated with a traditional No. 10 far more effectively, acting as the central hub around which Chelsea’s attacks revolved. Rogers was less involved in circulation and played a more dynamic role. An excellent complement to Palmer, Rogers played higher rather than constantly looking to receive and dictate the play like Palmer. He drifted into the half-space and threatened with runs in behind the Fulham backline, resembling more of a second-striker than a traditional No. 10. Chelsea’s Front Three Out Of Possession Chelsea’s out-of-possession strategy required intensity and positional intelligence from their front three, in particular, during all defensive phases, especially the high press. From the first kick of the ball on Monday evening, Chelsea’s front three had clear instructions during the high press: 1. Protect the passing lanes into midfield via their cover shadows. 2. Apply pressure on Fulham’s goalkeeper and centre-backs when receiving on the back foot or in limited space. Figure 3 Figures 3-4 show these pressing tactics in action. Figure 4 The ball makes its way from Leno to Cuenca, with the centre-back positioned very wide. This opens the door for Palmer to close the receiver down and contain him out wide by pressing, with the route to midfield kept in his cover shadow. Chelsea’s midfield and wing-backs, crucially, push up in support of Palmer to prevent Cuenca from escaping via short passing options, which forces the Fulham defender into the long ball, which Chelsea are well placed to deal with thanks to having three centre-backs on the pitch. The resulting recovery led to the opening goal of the game inside the first minute, as Palmer received the ball in space behind Fulham’s midfield line, which had been looking to advance and apply pressure on the second ball following Cuenca’s long pass. Palmer took advantage of this space to receive and turn, while taking advantage of the massive gap that still existed between Fulham’s centre-backs to play João Pedro through to score. This shows how Chelsea’s pressing helped them to take advantage of Fulham’s in-possession tactics throughout the match. Fulham were not set up to go long, quite the opposite, but Chelsea’s coordinated pressing forced them into long balls at times, which created turnovers and opportunities for Alonso’s side to quickly find their front three in transition. This was a recurring sequence throughout the match, with the exact same passage of play that led to the goal recurring just a couple of minutes later, as shown in Figures 5-6. Figure 5 Initially, Chelsea’s front three guard the passing lanes into the centre. Figure 6 When the ball goes back to Leno, João Pedro pounces while keeping the midfielder behind him in his cover shadow. This forces Leno to Cuenca again; Palmer presses while keeping the midfielder behind him in his cover shadow too, leading to the centre-back sending the ball long. Just like the start of the first half, the sequence repeated at the beginning of the second half. articles.title: How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round: Rotation, Goals and Team News
articles.excerpt: Tonight's strongest Carabao Cup selection projects higher than anything in the English leagues next Saturday. The card is not the problem - the team sheets are. How to use the projections, which markets are rotation-proof, and the lineup check that decides it.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round How to Bet the Carabao Cup Second Round: Rotation, Goals and Team News The Carabao Cup second round gets written off as a lottery. On our projections it is not, or at least not for the reason people think. The strongest selection on tonight's seventeen-tie card is Watford at home to Peterborough, projected at 63.4% . The strongest selection anywhere in the four English leagues next Saturday is Wolves at home to Stoke, at 60.2% . The cup card is, if anything, marginally less even than a normal league weekend, because the round pairs teams from different divisions. So the fixtures are not the problem. The team sheets are. Everything below is about that gap. The rotation problem, and why the model cannot solve it Nobody knows who is rotating until the lineups drop. Some managers will field youngsters and a pure second string; others will want to protect league momentum and make one or two changes at most. Two clubs in identical league positions will treat this round completely differently, and neither will tell you in advance. Our projections are honest about their own blind spot here. They are built on league form , and tonight's set was generated on Friday. They do not know who is being rested. When the model says Ipswich are 61.7% to beat Leicester, it means Ipswich's league-standard side against Leicester's league-standard side. That is not a flaw to route around, it is the thing to plan for. It means every number on this page is a starting position , and the last hour before kick-off is where you finish the job. The team news routine Check about an hour before kick-off , when lineups are confirmed. Ours land on the fixture pages as they are announced. Look at the shape of the change, not the count. Six changes with the spine intact is a different proposition to four changes that remove the entire midfield. If you see a teenage midfield, leave it alone. A projection built on league form has nothing useful to say about a side with three academy players in it. Check both teams. A rotated favourite against a rotated underdog is closer to the original number than a rotated favourite against a full-strength one. Where the numbers still help Goals markets sidestep the question This is the most useful thing on the page. A goals market does not care which eleven turns up, and if both managers change things the defending usually suffers before the attacking does. The model's highest both-teams-to-score ties tonight: Tie BTTS 2+ goals Southampton v West Ham 62.4% 81.8% Cardiff v Norwich 61.8% 81.4% Plymouth v Coventry 58.9% 81.3% Watford v Peterborough 57.5% 83.5% Ipswich v Leicester 56.8% 82.3% Blackpool v Lincoln 56.3% 77.2% Walsall v Leyton Orient 55.7% 76.0% Birmingham v Brentford 54.5% 79.5% The ten highest-projected ties on the card all reach 76% or better for two or more goals. That is the shape of a round where nobody is quite settled. Clean sheets are the market to avoid The highest clean-sheet probability on the entire seventeen-tie card is 39.5% , for Wolves away at Sheffield Wednesday. After that it is Fleetwood at 38.9% and Middlesbrough at 38.5%. Not one team on the card is even a 40% chance to keep it out. Backing a clean sheet, a correct score or a to-nil in this round is asking for precision the evening will not give you. If you are backing a winner, back a mismatch Selection Win % Projected goals Watford v Peterborough 63.4% 2.21 Ipswich v Leicester 61.7% 2.12 Middlesbrough at Doncaster 61.1% 2.00 Brentford at Birmingham 58.8% 1.95 Barnsley v Crewe 55.9% 1.80 Wolves at Sheffield Wednesday 54.9% 1.70 Coventry at Plymouth 54.1% 1.91 Note how quickly it flattens. By the seventh name you are at 54%, and below that the card is a coin toss - Fleetwood 45.6%, Lincoln 45.1%, Millwall 44.5%. There is no value in reaching down that list for a favourite; if the model will not commit past the halfway mark, neither should you. How we are playing it Two trebles on today's Daily Acca , deliberately built as opposites. The first takes the three strongest projected winners - Middlesbrough, Watford and Ipswich - and accepts the rotation risk in exchange for a price. The second takes the three highest both-teams-to-score ties and avoids the question entirely: it does not matter who is rested if both ends of the pitch are leaky. Both are staked at a point, both are priced around 4.0, and both are published before team news, which is precisely why the routine above matters. Our record on every acca is public in the column's own ledger , winners and losers alike. Five things to remember The card is not a lottery, the team sheets are. The projections rate tonight's favourites slightly higher than next weekend's league card. Goals markets are rotation-proof. The ten best ties on the card all reach 76% for 2+ goals. Leave clean sheets and correct scores alone. Nothing on the card reaches 40%. Do not chase a favourite below about 55%. The list flattens into coin tosses fast. Check the lineups an hour before. It is the single highest-value thing you can do in this round, and it costs nothing. The small print All projections were generated before team news and are built on league form. They do not model rotation, and we are not claiming they do. Prices quoted are bet365 at the time of writing and will move. A projection is a probability, not a forecast of one evening. A 63.4% favourite loses more than a third of the time. 18+. articles.title: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Highlights, man of the match, stats as Pedro, Palmer, Rogers light up Craven Cottage
articles.excerpt: Chelsea claim West London derby bragging rights with a thrilling 3-2 win against Fulham on Monday.
articles.source_type: Match previews with team news and predicted XIs for every fixture
articles.body: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Highlights, man of the match, stats as Pedro, Palmer, Rogers light up Craven Cottage - Sports Mole Menu Loading... Premier League Gameweek 1 Fulham Aug 24, 2026 8.00pm HT : Craven Cottage Chelsea Josh King 23' Gonzalo GarcÃ­a 54' Calvin Bassey 76' Timothy Castagne 88' JoÃ£o Pedro 1' Levi Colwill 5' RomÃ©o Lavia 12' Morgan Rogers 41' Cole Palmer 49' Reece JamesÂ 75' Fulham 2-3 Chelsea: Highlights, man of the match, stats as Pedro, Palmer, Rogers light up Craven Cottage Ellis Stevens 24 Aug 2026 21:55 Â© Iconsport / Sportimage Ltd/Alamy Live News Chelsea secured the West London derby bragging rights with a thrilling 3-2 victory over Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday night. Chelsea raced into the lead after just 31 seconds thanks to Joao Pedro 's delightful dink, and that early goal set the tempo for the half, with the two attack-minded sides trading chances in an energetic, back-and-forth clash. Josh King eventually equalised for Fulham after a spell of pressure, with Robert Sanchez making a costly error, but Chelsea restored their lead just before the break through a debut goal from Morgan Rogers The goals continued to flow in the second half, as Cole Palmer extended Chelsea's lead just five minutes after the restart, only for Gonzalo Garcia to pull one back on his Premier League debut six minutes later. Fulham pushed for an equaliser as the game edged towards full-time, but Chelsea came closest to scoring when Pedro was denied a second for offside, with the Blues ultimately holding on to secure all three points at Craven Cottage. SPORTS MOLE'S VERDICT Regardless of the result, both teams will take plenty of encouragement from their attacking performances, but there may be some concerns over their defensive displays. Chelsea and Fulham both looked dangerous from minute one until minute 90, including their respective summer signings demonstrating their ability and contributing in the final third. Chelsea's trio of Pedro, Palmer and Rogers looked particularly threatening, pressing high and constantly combining in attacking areas - something Chelsea supporters will be hoping to see even more of as the season progresses. However, the Blues did look defensively vulnerable, particularly goalkeeper Sanchez, who made errors in each of Fulham's two goals, while the Cottagers were caught in possession numerous times high up the pitch. Ultimately, Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa will be largely pleased with their performances and will be looking to build on the positive aspects in the coming weeks. FULHAM VS. CHELSEA HIGHLIGHTS Joao Pedro goal vs. Fulham (1st min, Fulham 0-1 Chelsea) "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds ? pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Unbelievable start for Chelsea! Pedro scores after 31 seconds! Jorge Cuenca's long ball forward is headed back into Fulham's half to Cole Palmer, who immediately slides a pass through to Pedro. Pedro drives into the box and expertly lobs the onrushing Bernd Leno, finding the bottom-left corner. Josh King goal vs. Chelsea (23rd min, Fulham 1-1 Chelsea) Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike ? pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 King equalises for Fulham! Robert Sanchez will not want to watch that back! King picks up the ball on the right side and plays a give-and-go with Timothy Castagne, receiving the ball back and driving into the Chelsea penalty area. The midfielder quickly unleashes a strike towards the front post, catching Sanchez off guard with the keeper guarding the far corner, and the ball flies through the Spaniard's hands into the back of the net. Morgan Rogers goal vs. Fulham (40th min, Fulham 1-2 Chelsea) A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! ? pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Rogers restores Chelsea's lead! Palmer skilfully spins away from Sander Berge and plays through Maxence Lacroix, who brilliantly races towards the byline and pulls a pass back to Rogers inside the box. Rogers calmly side-foots his effort into the middle of the gaping goal, beating two Fulham defenders on the line and finding the back of the net. Cole Palmer goal vs. Fulham (49th min, Fulham 1-3 Chelsea) "Cole Palmer back to his best!" Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! ? pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Palmer makes it three! Sanchez's long ball is flicked forward by Rogers to Pedro, who races into the Fulham penalty area and squares up his marker. Palmer surges around the outside of Pedro, who waits for the run and plays a perfectly weighted pass to Chelsea's number 10, who clinically finishes through Leno's legs. Gonzalo Garcia goal vs. Chelsea (54th min, Fulham 2-3 Chelsea) Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot ? pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 24, 2026 Garcia pulls one back for Fulham! Game on! Cuenca's long ball into the Chelsea box evades Levi Colwill and finds Castagne, who strikes a first-time effort towards goal with his left foot. Sanchez parries the ball back into the danger area, and Garcia is there to nod home on his Premier League debut. MAN OF THE MATCH - COLE PALMER © Iconsport / David Klein / Sportimage Both sets of attackers produced impressive performances, but Palmer was certainly the pick of the bunch. Chelsea's number 10 looked at his very best today, consistently beating defenders, taking shots and creating chances, while also putting in a defensive shift. Palmer ended the game with the most completed dribbles (five), most shots (five) and three chances created, as well as registering a goal and assist. FULHAM VS. CHELSEA MATCH STATS Possession: Fulham 61%-39% Chelsea Shots: Fulham 14-18 Chelsea Shots on target: Fulham 6-6 Chelsea Corners: Fulham 6-4 Chelsea Fouls: Fulham 12-7 Chelsea BEST STATS 31 - Timed at 31 seconds, João Pedro has scored the quickest ever goal on MD1 in a Premier League season. Impression. pic.twitter.com/moYzfCa9q4 — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) August 24, 2026 5 - Morgan Rogers has now also become the first Chelsea player to create five chances on his Premier League debut for the club on record since 2003-04. Inventive. https://t.co/GQpzBzntvC — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) August 24, 2026 WHAT NEXT? Fulham's attention turns to the EFL Cup with a midweek match against AFC Wimbledon, before returning to Premier League action against Sunderland on Sunday. Chelsea will also appear in midweek against Luton Town in the EFL Cup second round, followed by a clash with Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday. Arsenal transfer news: Al-Hilal 'getting closer' to finalising Gabriel Martinelli fee, Brazilian left with decision Darren Plant 24 Aug 2026 17:30 Â© Iconsport / ALLSTAR PICTURE LIBRARY, Allstar Picture Library Ltd / Alamy Arsenal and Al-Hilal are allegedly edging nearer to agreeing a deal for Gabriel Martinelli Amid speculation about his future, the long-serving Gunners player has been left out of the club's opening two squads of the season. The Premier League champions are seemingly open to cashing in on the Brazil international, rather than activating an option which would extend his contract until 2028. As well as Galatasaray, Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal have been heavily linked with a move for the 25-year-old. According to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano , whether Martinelli moves to the Middle East could be a decision left down to him. © Imago / Sportsphoto What fee could Al-Hilal pay for Martinelli? The report alleges that a fee between £50m and £55m has been mentioned during discussions involving the two teams. Club-to-club talks are said to be in their final stages, with Arsenal ready to accept that sum of money for Martinelli. With terms between the clubs likely to be agreed, Martinelli will be left to decide whether he wants to take the opportunity to move to Saudi Arabia. Fellow winger Malcom is the only other Brazilian player in the Al-Hilal squad. A total of 62 goals and 36 assists have been contributed from 278 appearances for Arsenal in all competitions. © Iconsport / PA Images Are Arsenal right to cash in on Martinelli? Christos Tzolis has made a strong start on the left flank since his arrival from Club Brugge, something that has perhaps encouraged Arsenal to part ways with Martinelli. However, with Leandro Trossard having already left the Emirates Stadium and Martinelli having made at least 50 outings in the last two seasons, it feels like Mikel Arteta is taking a risk. Should Arsenal, as expected, choose to reinvest the money in a left-winger who they deem to be an upgrade, they will hope that he can show similar levels of availability to Martinelli over the course of a long season. articles.title: xG Report: The Weekend's Biggest Chance Creators in All Four English Divisions
articles.excerpt: Brentford created the most in England. West Ham created 3.23 expected goals at home and lost to a Charlton side who managed 0.70. The top five chance creators in every English division, plus the early Championship, League One and League Two xG tables.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Weekend xG Report: Championship, League One, League Two xG Report: The Weekend's Biggest Chance Creators in All Four English Divisions Brentford created the most in England this weekend: 3.87 expected goals against Tottenham, from a home side that scored three and could have had more. That is the headline number. The more interesting one is 3.23, which is what West Ham generated at home to Charlton in the Championship. They lost 2-1. Charlton had 0.70 xG and took all three points. That is the weekend in one fixture, and the reason this column exists. Below are the top five chance creators in each of the four English divisions, the biggest gaps between what teams deserved and what they got, and the early xG tables for the Championship, League One and League Two. The top five xG teams in every English division All figures are total expected goals from the weekend's fixtures, with the opponent's xG alongside for context. Premier League Team Scored Match Brentford 3.87 Brentford 3-0 Tottenham (0.59) Liverpool 3.64 Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool (1.27) Brighton 3.19 Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa (0.33) Manchester United 2.19 Hull City 2-0 Man Utd (0.99) Manchester City 2.13 Man City 2-1 Bournemouth (0.57) Liverpool drawing 2-2 at Newcastle having created 3.64 to their hosts' 1.27 is the sort of result that looks like a title-race wobble and reads, in the numbers, like an away performance that deserved more. United's 2.19 without a goal at Hull is the opposite problem, and one we flagged in our Gameweek 1 review Championship Team Scored Match West Ham United 3.23 West Ham 1-2 Charlton (0.70) Millwall 2.93 Millwall 3-0 Norwich (0.96) Cardiff City 2.81 Derby 2-2 Cardiff (1.88) Lincoln City 2.44 Lincoln 1-3 Portsmouth (1.39) Southampton 2.43 Southampton 3-1 Stoke (1.13) Three of those five failed to win. Lincoln lost 3-1 at home having created a full expected goal more than Portsmouth, and just outside the five, QPR drew 0-0 with Bolton having generated 2.09 xG to Bolton's 0.16 - the most lopsided chance count of the weekend anywhere in England. League One Team Scored Match Stockport County 3.01 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool (1.85) Wycombe Wanderers 2.26 Wycombe 1-1 Plymouth (0.93) Luton Town 2.19 Luton 2-2 Notts County (0.55) Huddersfield Town 2.06 MK Dons 1-1 Huddersfield (1.38) Blackpool 1.85 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool (3.01) Stockport against Blackpool was the weekend's clearest case of a game not going the way the chances did. Stockport created more than 3.0 xG at home, Blackpool created 1.85, and Blackpool won. Luton, meanwhile, drew a game in which they had four times their opponents' expected goals. League Two Team Scored Match Bristol Rovers 3.42 Bristol Rovers 5-3 Newport (0.64) Colchester United 2.48 Colchester 2-1 Oldham (0.42) York City 2.19 Rotherham 1-1 York (0.83) Exeter City 2.15 Exeter 2-0 Accrington (0.85) Crawley Town 2.10 Rochdale 1-2 Crawley (0.88) Bristol Rovers had the highest xG in the EFL and the highest score in the country, and the match still produced one of the strangest lines of the weekend: Newport scored three goals from 0.64 expected . Eight goals from a combined 4.06 xG is not a normal afternoon. The biggest gaps between chances and goals Two lists, both from this weekend, across all four divisions. Scored far more than they created Team Goals Match Newport County 0.64 Bristol Rovers 5-3 Newport Barnet 1.38 Shrewsbury 1-3 Barnet Portsmouth 1.39 Lincoln 1-3 Portsmouth Notts County 0.55 Luton 2-2 Notts County Charlton Athletic 0.70 West Ham 1-2 Charlton Created far more than they scored Team Goals Match West Ham United 3.23 West Ham 1-2 Charlton Manchester United 2.19 Hull City 2-0 Man Utd Queens Park Rangers 2.09 QPR 0-0 Bolton Walsall 2.03 Walsall 0-0 Grimsby Stockport County 3.01 Stockport 1-2 Blackpool None of this means the results were wrong. Finishing is a skill, goalkeepers have good days, and a 0.64 xG afternoon that yields three goals is a real three goals. What the gap tells you is how repeatable the performance was - and over a season, teams in the second list usually start scoring more. The early EFL xG tables Two games in. Everything below is a very small sample and should be read as a description of what has happened, not a projection of what will. Full, updating versions live at Championship xG League One xG and League Two xG The tables are ordered by expected points - what a team's chances, and the chances they gave up, were worth on average rather than what the scoreline delivered. Championship Team xGA xPts Actual pts Millwall 6.3 1.4 5.2 Middlesbrough 4.1 1.8 4.2 Wrexham 3.6 1.6 4.1 Wolves 3.6 1.6 4.1 QPR 4.1 2.4 3.9 Southampton 4.0 2.4 3.8 West Ham United 4.8 3.4 3.4 West Bromwich Albion 4.2 3.7 3.2 Millwall are the only side in the division top of both tables: most expected points, and six actual points from two games. At the other end of the same list, Charlton have six points from 1.6 expected - the largest gap in the EFL - and West Ham have one point from 3.4. League One Team xGA xPts Actual pts Sheffield Wednesday 4.5 1.4 4.6 Luton Town 3.9 2.3 3.8 Huddersfield Town 3.1 1.8 3.6 Wigan Athletic 3.7 2.9 3.4 Reading 2.8 2.2 3.2 Stockport County 4.4 3.6 3.1 Wigan are the story here: fourth on expected points and pointless. Bradford , meanwhile, sit 18th on expected points with a maximum six. League Two Team xGA xPts Actual pts Walsall 4.9 2.5 4.2 Chesterfield 4.4 2.1 4.2 Bristol Rovers 5.4 2.7 4.1 York City 4.2 2.8 3.6 Northampton Town 2.0 1.0 3.6 Crewe Alexandra 3.2 2.0 3.4 League Two is the tightest of the three. Bristol Rovers have the division's best raw xG at 5.4 but only three points; Barnet and Crewe have maximum returns from mid-table expected-points figures. How to read this, and what we are not claiming Two matches is not a sample. Our own xG pages hide their over- and under-performance callouts until every team has played six, for exactly this reason. Nothing above is a prediction. xG measures chance quality, not merit. A side that scores three from 0.64 has not got lucky in any moral sense. They have finished well, or been finished against badly. Expected points come from the chances, both ways. A team can top the xG column and sit lower on expected points because of what they conceded at the other end. The data is SportMonks team xG , imported after each round. It lands hours after full time rather than at the whistle, which is why this column runs at the start of the week rather than on Saturday night. If you want the numbers that update themselves rather than a weekend snapshot, the Championship League One and League Two xG tables refresh as each round imports, and our EFL Best Bets column uses the same underlying model. articles.title: Super Sub Report: What Every Premier League Substitution Produced in Gameweek 1
articles.excerpt: Under Super Sub a player prop continues on the replacement, so the number that counts is the pair's combined total. Here is what all 90 Gameweek 1 substitutions produced - fouls, shots, on target and tackles, player by player.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Super Sub Report: Gameweek 1 Substitution Stats Super Sub Report: What Every Premier League Substitution Produced in Gameweek 1 Martin Ødegaard came off on 76 minutes against Coventry having had three shots, one of them on target, and made three tackles. Mikel Merino replaced him and had two more shots, one on target, in fourteen minutes. Between them: five shots, two on target, three tackles That pairing matters because of how Super Sub works. bet365 call it Sub On Play On, Sky Bet and Paddy Power call it Super Sub, Betfair call it Safe Sub, and on the markets it covers the principle is the same - when the player is substituted, his replacement's tally continues the line. So the figure that counts is the pair's combined total, not the starter's own. We have a full explainer on the rule and which books offer it This is the first edition of a weekly column. Every Premier League round, we take every substitution and publish what the two players produced between them. Gameweek 1 is now complete: ten matches, 90 substitutions Gameweek 1: the pairs Each cell shows what the player who came off produced, plus what his replacement produced, and the player total for the pair. These are twelve of the round's most productive pairings. Match Came off Came on Fouls Shots On target Tackles Arsenal 3-0 Coventry Martin Ødegaard (76') Mikel Merino (14m) 0 + 1 = 3 + 2 = 1 + 1 = 3 + 0 = Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Mathias Jensen (67') Yegor Yarmolyuk (23m) 3 + 1 = 2 + 1 = 1 + 0 = 2 + 2 = Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa Jack Hinshelwood (64') C. Kostoulas (26m) 0 + 0 = 3 + 2 = 2 + 0 = 2 + 1 = Everton 2-0 Crystal Palace JP. Mateta (63') J. Strand Larsen (27m) 2 + 2 = 2 + 1 = 0 + 1 = 2 + 0 = Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland Julio Enciso (71') Jack Clarke (19m) 1 + 0 = 3 + 2 = 0 + 1 = 1 + 1 = Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland Issahaku Fatawu (66') Kasey McAteer (24m) 1 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 4 + 1 = Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool Florian Wirtz (63') A. Mac Allister (27m) 0 + 0 = 3 + 0 = 1 + 0 = 1 + 2 = Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Dango Ouattara (67') Jaidon Anthony (23m) 3 + 1 = 2 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 2 = Brighton 4-0 Aston Villa Yasin Ayari (64') Costinha (26m) 2 + 0 = 2 + 2 = 0 + 1 = 0 + 1 = Nott'm Forest 0-1 Leeds Harry Wilson (66') Noah Okafor (24m) 1 + 1 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 2 + 2 = Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Oscar Bobb (67') Shea Charles (23m) 1 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 0 + 0 = 3 + 2 = Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Cole Palmer (83') Estêvão (7m) 0 + 0 = 5 + 0 = 2 + 0 = 2 + 0 = The Fatawu and Wilson rows are the ones to sit with. Neither pair troubled the goalkeeper at all, and both produced a healthy tackle count - a reminder that the volume in these markets is defensive far more often than it is attacking. The last row is the counter-example, and it is just as important. Cole Palmer had five shots and two on target before being taken off on 83 minutes at Craven Cottage. Estêvão came on for the closing seven minutes and added nothing to any of the four columns. A replacement is only worth what his minutes allow, and seven of them are worth very little. How often the pair got somewhere the starter did not A second way of reading the same 90 substitutions. For each standard line, how many times did the player who came off finish below it, and how many times did the pair's combined total reach it anyway? Line Starter finished below it Pair total reached it 2+ tackles 3+ tackles 2+ fouls 1+ foul 3+ shots 1+ shot 1+ shot on target 1+ tackle 2+ shots 2+ shots on target That is 100 times across the round, at the time of writing, that a pair's combined figure landed on the right side of a standard line when the starter's own did not. Read the narrow version and it sharpens. Take only the players who came off exactly one short: on 2+ tackles that happened 37 times and the replacement supplied the missing tackle in 14 of them, and on 3+ shots it happened 18 times and the replacement supplied the shot in 8. The market that behaves differently is shots on target. Fifty-nine players came off without one; nine had a replacement who managed one. And on the harder 2+ line, 83 starters finished below it and the replacement got the pair there just twice. It is simply a rarer event to ask of somebody with 25 minutes, which is worth knowing before you decide the rule is worth more than it is. The busiest cameos Substitutes who put up numbers without any help from the man they replaced: Joe Willock (34 mins, Newcastle) - a shot, one on target, two tackles and two fouls. The most complete cameo of the round. Yéremy Pino (35 mins, Crystal Palace) - two shots, two tackles, a foul. Evann Guessand (27 mins, Crystal Palace) - a shot on target, a tackle, two fouls. Anan Khalaili (35 mins, Crystal Palace) - four tackles , more than most starters managed. Mikel Merino (14 mins, Arsenal) - two shots, one on target, in a quarter of an hour. Crystal Palace appear three times. Two down at Goodison, they changed things early and their substitutes chased the game - which is the game-state effect in miniature, and a reminder that what a replacement does is shaped by the scoreline he walks into. What to watch in Gameweek 2 Volume markets carry the effect. Tackles and fouls account for 64 of the 100 threshold crossings above. Shots on target account for eleven. Time on the pitch is the lever. The replacements who put up numbers here mostly had 20 minutes or more. A change on 85 minutes rarely moves anything. The bench decides it. A holding midfielder replaced by another holding midfielder keeps a tackle count ticking. Replaced by a striker because the team is chasing, it stops - and the shot count starts instead. It can go the other way. If the player is his side's best tackler, nobody replacing him matches that rate, and the pair's total grows more slowly than his own would have. The explainer works through that case. Our player projections and the Bet Builder tool model a player's own expected output, which is the right thing to model for an ordinary market and an incomplete picture on one where a replacement's numbers are added to his. What this column does and does not tell you These are match statistics, not bet settlements. Everything above is what players did on a pitch. We do not know which lines a bookmaker offered, whether anybody backed them, whether Super Sub applied to that market, or how any individual bet was settled. Nothing here should be read as a bet won or lost. Market coverage belongs to the bookmaker. Which markets and competitions carry the rule varies by operator and can change. Check the operator's own terms. The numbers move after the match. Provider stat corrections land for days, and they move in both directions. Between two runs of the same query a tackle was added to the Brighton game, and a shot on target came off another, taking the 2+ shots on target count down from three to two. Treat every total here as a snapshot. Updated for the full round. This edition first published with nine matches, before Fulham v Chelsea had been played, and now covers all ten. From Gameweek 2 the column runs on the Tuesday, once the round is complete. Lines overlap. A pair reaching 1+ tackles may also reach 2+. The 100 counts thresholds, not bets. 18+. articles.title: Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant
articles.excerpt: All three are owned by fewer than three percent of managers. All three cost £6.0m or less. All three scored on the opening weekend, and one of them we flagged before a ball was kicked.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant Three Players Who Just Became Very FPL Relevant The opening weekend of an FPL season is where template squads meet reality. Erling Haaland, in seven out of ten teams, did not score. Three players owned by barely anyone did. Here are the three whose weekend actually changes something, with what they cost and how many managers already have them. Ownership and prices are from the Statz FPL data at the time of writing. Anton Stach, Leeds, £6.0m, 1.2% owned Stach scored the only goal at the City Ground, winning Leeds the round's sole away victory against a Forest side the model made 44.8% favourites. We flagged him before the season started: in our FPL coverage he was the deep cut, a top-12 projected player in the entire game at £6.0m with ownership that rounded to nobody. That case has not weakened. A midfielder at that price who takes set pieces and arrives in the box is the definition of an FPL differential, and 1.2% ownership means his goals move your rank rather than keeping you level. Jack Hinshelwood, Brighton, £6.0m, 0.9% owned Two goals in a 4-0 win, in a Brighton side missing Baleba, Mitoma and Ferguson. That last part is the important part: Hinshelwood's route into the team came from an injury list, and the question every FPL manager now has to answer is what happens when those three are fit. At £6.0m and under 1% ownership he is the sort of pick that wins you a gameweek. Whether he holds the shirt into September is a different question, and the predicted line-ups will answer it before the deadline rather than after. Maxim De Cuyper, Brighton, £4.5m, 2.7% owned The one that matters most, because of the price. A £4.5m defender who scored and kept a clean sheet in the same afternoon is exactly the profile our budget enablers guide was written about: the cheap slot that quietly funds a premium elsewhere while contributing points of its own. The honest caveat One gameweek is one gameweek. Two of these three owe their minutes at least partly to somebody else's injury, and a single haul is not a projection. The way to judge them is the same as it was in July: look at the expected minutes first and the points second. The Statz Season Rankings model both across all 38 gameweeks, and the Team Planner will tell you what any of them is projected to add to your specific squad rather than to a hypothetical one. articles.excerpt: FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways – Don’t Overreact The FPL General picked the wrong season to go without the two-mium. If he had started without Haaland and Bruno Fernandes this season he would be laughing. And that kind of summarises gameweek 1. Outside of the Arsenal picks, and Szoboszlai nobody owned by more than […] The post FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways – Don’t Overreact appeared first on Full90 FPL .
articles.source_type: Gameweek previews, transfer tips, captaincy corner, fixture focus
articles.body: FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways - Don’t Overreact - Full90 FPL Skip to content FPL Gameweek 1 Review and Takeaways - Don’t Overreact The FPL General picked the wrong season to go without the two-mium. If he had started without Haaland and Bruno Fernandes this season he would be laughing. And that kind of summarises gameweek 1. Outside of the Arsenal picks, and Szoboszlai nobody owned by more than 25% of managers returned. If Pedro doesn’t return tomorrow this will have been one of those good weeks to have a bad week. So, I can’t be too upset to be on 46 points all out. Though obviously I am frustrated, I am trying not to overreact to anything. Just look how crazy some of the opening day results are based on our pre-season expectations. We know almost nothing. If you had a plan coming into this season, stick to it. As most of the PL teams now know, stability matters… Don’t Overreact The clear caveat is that this is still only one week’s worth of information I am going to do some conjecture with it. We will likely see in a couple of weeks what is the “truth.” I’m writing this at the top so that I don’t have to say “we will see” after every statement. Just remember, Reijnders looked like the next De Bruyne after gw1 last season… Did Bench Boost 1 Work? Well, it wasn’t great for me but it was fine and I am happy it’s done. I got 9 points which is about the minimum you expect. Joe smashed it with 18 points though – good for him, the little bastard. Match-By-Match Reviews I watched 4 games this weekend and the highlights for the rest. I’ve also reviewed all the stats so we can see who was lucky and who wasn’t. Arsenal 3-0 Coventry xG 1.88-0.20 Arsenal Smash Coventry The first game of the season was a bloodbath. It was hard to tell whether Arsenal were just elite or Coventry were just dreadful. I suspect a bit of both. On xG, it was only 1.88-0.20 so maybe we shouldn’t read too much into this. But it’s hard not to when you add this performance to the Community Shield performance – Arsenal’s attack was just way better than I remember it being last season. Partly that is down to newboy Tzolis who had 4 shots for 0.19 xG and 3 key passes for 0.14 xA – if you watched the game you’ll be shocked about how low that is because he looked electric. He was even stepping into a sort of second striker role when Arsenal worked the ball down the right, which they frequently do when Saka is playing. He didn’t make a full 90, getting hooked at 76 mins for Eze which is a bit of a concern. My conclusion on him is this then, if you picked him then it was a good one but I am not desperate to get him in right now. That’s pretty much how I feel about Odegaard too who also put up 3 key passes for 0.1 xA and 3 shots for 0.21 xG. The thing about Ode is that he is so involved in everything that he takes the bonus points too. But he also went off at 76 mins for Merino As expected, neither Saka nor Rice made it much past 65 mins. Until they play a 90, I just don’t think we can go there. In defence, they looked solid of course. None of them got DefCons but Coventry were really bad so I’m not surprised. Of course Cala got the goal and was a good pick but it didn’t help my nerves about rotation when he went off before 90. Are Coventry Fucked? As for Coventry, I think they were really, really shit. I know that Arsenal were the winners of the Premier league last year but that was some weak, pathetic shit we saw from Coventry. It’s probably not an original thought to say I don’t think that Lampard is a great coach but this terrible performance reminded me. Thomas got defcons at least. Hull City 2-0 Man United xG 1.01-1.83 Disastrous Start for Man United In complete contrast to Coventry, Hull looked properly up for this game. If you watched the highlights you’d be forgiven for thinking that Hull dominated but United were better on xG and put up 21 shots to Hulls 8 shots. But still. Cunha started up top and had 3 shots for 0.24 xG and 2 key passes for 0.21 xA. He was hooked after 80 mins. Mbeumo put up 4 shots for 0.5xG and 0.23 xA and lasted the full 90 mins. Dorgu started left wing and put up 0.47 xG from three shots in a single half before being replaced with Rashford who didn’t get a single shot off. Sesko played 23 mins and only got 1 shot off for 0.04 xG. Bruno Fernandes put up 3 shots for 0.08 xG – all from miles outside the box – and 3 key passes for 0.26 xA. A lot of these guys then outperformed the Arsenal boys on underlyings but just failed to actually put the ball in the net. They lacked a lot of energy and just seemed to be so slow – letting Hull grab the ball far too often. I don’t think we should worry too much about Mbeumo and Bruno – they both played 90 and put up reasonable numbers. But, I am a little worried about how much depth Man United have because that means that any of these guys, besides maybe Bruno, could get hooked before 90 and we really want 90 mins. None of the back line got close to defensive contribution points and they were obviously not that great either. Perfect Premier League Start for Hull Realistically, I can’t see us going for any Hull assets regularly but I want to call out two interesting players. Firstly, Slater took corners and set pieces for only 4.5 – he could be a great pick for that 8th attacker slot that just sits on your bench. Obviously he also got an assist. Secondly, McBurnie had two shots in the first 20 mins, and was pretty unfortunate not to get a goal in my opinion. Again, he’s a rotation option (or Draft option). Egan got 21 defensive contributions and Mendy got 13. Now open for 2026/27 Every premium tool, £25 for the season. £25 season pass or £5 a month Join Full 90 FPL 14 day refund, no questions asked. The season pass does not auto-renew. Rotation Planner The cheap pairs whose fixtures cover each other Transfer Planner Whose fixtures are about to turn, and who replaces them Captaincy Picker and Matrix The armband this week, and the one coming in three Top 150 Draft Rankings £5 on its own. Included here, plus the mid-season refresh The Midweek Fixture No ads Across the whole site and every tool, while you are a member Still free for everyone: the fixture ticker Ipswich 2-1 Sunderland xG 1.80-0.66 Ipswich Catch the Black Cats Napping Literally. The first goal was a fantastic counter-attack that saw Enciso drive forward and assist Emersonn who put up 0.82 xG from 3 shots in just 66 mins. Enciso went off injured and Jack Clarke came on and scored the second. O’Shea got 18 defensive contributions from right back and Nunez got 12 defcons in 80 mins. Sunderland confirm fears? I said multiple times coming into the season that I was worried about these guys – they’re underlying numbers suggest they were pretty poor last season, potentially this result confirms those fears. However, they did most of their good work at home so maybe not. Angulo took the free-kick for the goal and it was brilliant. But that was about all he did and he only lasted 59 mins. Brobbey had 2 shots for 0.3 xG but was taken off after 67 mins. Le Fee did basically nothing and got subbed at 80 mins. My hero Granit Xhaka got defcon points and an assist after being fouled for the free kick. Ballard narrowly missed out on defcon points and O’Nien was replaced on 67 mins. Brentford 3-0 Spurs xG 3.87-0.57 Spurs Still Suck We’ve just reviewed all the promoted teams and NONE of them conceded this much in terms of xG. They conceded 26 shots. 26! It was an almost completely new backline of Robertson, Senesi, van Hecke and Gray – Robbo and Senesi got defcon points and van Hecke was only 1 away from getting the points. But obviously, they conceded 3 times… And, as you can tell from the expected numbers, they were woeful going forward. Their attack is a hard avoid at the moment. Brentford’s Stability Prevails 10 of Brentford’s players were regulars from last season. Schade smashed Dango out of the water in terms of underlying numbers – 0.52 xG from 5 shots v.s. 0.05 xG from 2 shots. The latter was subbed off after 67 mins for Anthony top cap off basically every Dango owner’s fear come true. In a rare turn of events, Thiago hit the post with a pen to finish with no returns from an xG of 1.0. There was only one newbie to Brentford’s team and he absolutely smashed his debut. Sangare got defcons, one real assist and one FPL one. He was great but it is worth noting his xA was only 0.33. At the back, Ajer got DefCons but might not keep his spot when van den Berg is back. Kayode had 4 shots for 0.5 xG and walked away with a goal. Lewis-Potter played left-back and scored from his 2 shots and 0.77xG. Everton 2-0 Palace xG: 1.12-1.96 Everton Ride Their Luck A bit like last season then. They somehow give up a tonne of xG but walk away with a clean sheet. Nobody got defensive contribution points but Tarkowski was only one off and Branthwaite was only two off. Ndiaye was the best 6.0 going into this week because he got a full 90 and an assist. Dewsbury-Hall scored off 0.12 xG and Barry scored off two shots and 0.45 xG. Palace Falter The big news is that Ismalia Sarr didn’t even make the starting lineup after Galatassaray made a bid for him. Munoz was still in the team (despite the transfer rumours around him). He had a couple of shots in the first half but was subbed at 55 mins. Richards, Wharton, and Kamada all walked away with DefCon Points. As expected, Mateta didn’t play 90 and was subbed at 63 mins for Strand Larsen after two shots for 0.70 xG. Man City 2 – 1 Bournemouth xG: 2.36-0.63 Maresca’s Fifa Career Enzo Maresca is playing Fifa. Either that, or he’s taking tips from Thomas Tuchel. By my count, he started six defenders – with Guehi playing DM and O’Reilly playing in the 10. Foden was playing on the right-wing which I think was also weird. The goal they conceded didn’t do anything to convince me that the defensive frailties witnessed in the Community Shield were a one-off. As if they wanted to make City feel better for being bad in defence, Bournemouth left Guehi open whilst two of them wrestled Ruben Semenyo was the only midfielder to make 90 mins and he switched from the left to the right when Grealish came on for Foden on the 82nd minute. Cherki got the assist after coming on got O’Reilly in the 63rd minute. He found Gvardiol in the box basically playing second striker which is REALLY interesting if he can lock down a starting spot. Of course, Haaland blanked which basically meant that nobody got a return from their captain in gameweek 1 Bournemouth Brilliant? Well. No. Not really. They looked competent and good, like they normally do. But they didn’t create that much and relied on counter-attacking. Evanilson got the assist to the goal but didn’t get a shot off. Tavernier was the one who scored and the only one of the front four to make it to 90 mins. Silva got defensive contributions. Brighton 4 – 0 Villa xG: 3.67-0.31 Villa Are In Trouble The xG numbers show that the final scoreline doesn’t lie. Villa were shit. It’s probably not escaped your attention that they have been gutted by transfers out but I expected that Emery would just pull something out of the bag and put on a decent performance, even if they lost. Well that was wrong. Watkins must be on his way out because I don’t see any good reason not to start him. That hopefully will make Jackson a good pick if he goes over there. Brighton Actually Brilliant 21 shots, 6 big chances, 3.67 xG and a 4-0 win against an Emery team. Hats off to them. None of them got close to defcon points but that’s probably not a shock given how bad Villa were. Rutter started at striker but I’d still be nervous about going there until the transfer window closes. Hinshelwood got two goals from 3 shots for 1.41 xG. He was quite overlooked before the season began, including from me, despite how high many of us were on him at the end of last season. De Cuyper played on the wing which is interesting if that carries on. Gross did nothing which made me happy and most man

articles.body: Elche vs Barcelona Predictions & Betting Tips Elche vs Barcelona Predictions and Betting Tips - La Liga Barcelona start the season as the model's champions: 53.8% in our La Liga projection , the best attack in the division, and a first assignment at Elche, who the same model expects to spend the year in a six-club scrap to stay up. You know how this is supposed to go. So does the market, which is the problem with betting on it. Kickoff is 8:30pm UK on Sunday. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News As with all La Liga fixtures, Statz does not publish a predicted XI the way it does for the Premier League, so the names below are the players our props board expects to be involved rather than a confirmed team sheet. Barcelona 's expected group includes Joan García in goal, Koundé, Eric García and Balde across the back, Marc Bernal and Fermín López in midfield, with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha providing the width. Elche are expected to feature Dituro, Affengruber, Chust, Sangaré and Valera. No confirmed absences have been published for either side at the time of writing. Recent Form Barcelona's closing five read WWLWL, Elche's DLWDD. The projections are emphatic: 2.21 goals to 1.00, with Elche given a 10.9% chance of a clean sheet , one of the lowest numbers on the weekend's board anywhere in Europe. Barcelona win this in 64.3% of simulations. Elche take it in 15.2%, which is a bigger number than a 9.00 price suggests. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats Marc Bernal to be carded at 3.75 is the standout, and it is not close: a 32.3% projection is the highest on either side's board. A young midfielder holding the middle of the pitch while his side chases the ball for long spells is a booking waiting to happen, and Elche will be running at him. Eric García at 5.50 is the same argument at a bigger price. Beyond that the board leans on fouls markets from our commentary-parsed data, which are noisier than the cards and shots lines and are worth treating as softer evidence. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Barcelona at 1.30 implies a 77% chance. The model says 64.3%. Over 2.5 at 1.44 implies 69% against a 62.3% projection. Both teams to score at 1.75 is the closest thing to a fair price in the game, and even that is a shade the wrong side of the line. Our La Liga preview has them winning the title in 39.3% of simulations against Barcelona's 53.8%, a gap of less than two projected points across 38 games. In a race that tight, a Saturday night in Cornella is not a warm-up. It is one of the 38 games that decides it. Espanyol are the sort of opponent that has quietly ruined title bids before: awkward, at home, with nothing expected of them. The model gives them 18.1%, which is more than you might think. On that basis Real Madrid 's expected group is built around Courtois in goal, a back line featuring Alexander-Arnold, Huijsen, Konaté and Cucurella, with Valverde and Güler in midfield and Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior ahead of them. Espanyol 's side is expected to include Riedel, Expósito, Núñez and Álvaro Calatrava. No confirmed absences have been published for either side at the time of writing. Recent Form Madrid closed last season WLWWW, Espanyol LWWDW at home. The projections split them clearly: 1.86 goals to 0.95, with Madrid given a 38.8% clean sheet against Espanyol's 15.6%. That is a comfortable enough read, and it is worth holding onto the gap between it and the price. A 57.9% chance is not the same thing as a formality. Álvaro Calatrava 1+ shot on target at 2.10 carries a 50.8% projection and a last-five line of two, three, zero, two and four. Espanyol will not see much of the ball, but he is the man they aim at when they get it, and a shade over evens for a player who has hit the target in four of his last five is the most sensible number in this match. The braver version is his 2+ at 7.00. For Madrid, Trent Alexander-Arnold to be carded at 5.50 (21.3%) is the one the model rates, and Dean Huijsen at 4.50 carries the higher projection at 25.9% - centre-backs against a side that will be countering all night. The model says 57.9%. That is not a small disagreement, and it is the wrong way round for anyone wanting to back the favourite. The goals markets are no kinder. Over 2.5 at 1.62 implies nearly 62% against a projection of 53.2%. The only two prices on the board that the model actually rates are under 2.5 goals at 2.30 (46.8% against an implied 43.5%) and Espanyol at 7.00, where an 18.1% chance is priced as a 14.3% one. Summary The bet: Under 2.5 goals at 2.30. Madrid should win. They will probably win without ever going through the gears, which is precisely the shape of game that finishes 2-0 rather than 4-1, and the under is the one price here that the model prefers to the market's version of it.
