articles.title: The FPL Team Planner That Does Your Homework For You: Import, Project, Optimise
articles.excerpt: Every FPL manager runs the same loop: check fixtures, second-guess transfers, wonder if the armband is right. The Statz Team Planner runs that loop for you - import your real squad in seconds, see projected points on every player for the next six gameweeks, and let the optimiser propose transfer plans with the reasoning attached. Here's everything it does.
articles.source_type: Head-to-head player comparison, goalkeeper and position value analysis
articles.body: FPL Team Planner - Import Your Squad & Optimise Transfers The FPL Team Planner That Does Your Homework For You: Import, Project, Optimise Every FPL manager runs the same weekly loop. Check the fixtures. Second-guess two transfers. Wonder whether the captaincy is right. Do it all in your head, on a bus, four minutes before the deadline. The Statz FPL Team Planner exists to run that loop properly: your actual squad, projected points on every player, fixtures for the run ahead, and an optimiser that proposes your next moves - with its reasoning shown. It's the piece of the Statz FPL toolkit that ties everything else together, and this is the full tour: what it does, how the optimiser thinks, and why the managers using it are making decisions with numbers the official app simply doesn't have. Get your squad in, in seconds Three ways in, no typing your team out player by player. Enter your FPL Team ID and the planner pulls your real squad, bank and chips. Start from scratch if you're planning a draft. Or - the party trick - upload a screenshot of your team from the official app, and the planner reads the players off the image and rebuilds your squad automatically. Once you're in, your squad, transfers and plans save to your account, so the plan you sketch on your laptop is waiting on your phone at the deadline. The pitch view: your team, with the numbers switched on The planner's home screen looks like your team - a proper pitch, shirts, bench - but every player carries the number the official app never shows: projected points for the gameweek , from the same Statz model behind the Season Rankings . The header runs the totals for you: your bank, free transfers, a Team Rating out of 100 , and your squad's total projected points for the gameweek. The pitch view: projected points on every shirt, captaincy marked, and your gameweek total in the header. Step forward through the gameweeks with the arrows and the whole squad re-projects against each week's fixtures - so "should I hold this transfer?" becomes a question you can answer by looking. Chips live in the header too, so a Wildcard or Bench Boost can be planned into a specific week rather than panic-played. And the camera button exports your squad as a shareable image for the group chat. The transfer market, sorted by what actually matters The Players panel is a transfer shortlist with projections built in: search anyone, filter by position, club or price, and sort by projected points over the next six gameweeks rather than last season's totals. One column tells you what a player is likely to do for the week ahead; the six-gameweek column tells you what he's worth across the run - which is the number transfers should actually be bought on. The player market, sorted by six-gameweek projected points - the number a transfer should be judged on. Fixtures as a heatmap, three ways The Fixtures tab turns the run-in into a heatmap you can read at a glance, with a gameweek range slider and three modes: projected goals per fixture, clean sheet percentage , and classic FPL FDR if you want the official difficulty view. Totals rank every club across your chosen window, so "whose fixtures turn?" stops being folklore and becomes a sorted column. The fixtures heatmap in projected-goals mode: every club's run, quantified and ranked over your chosen gameweeks. Optimise: the feature that earns the bookmark Then there's the button that separates this from every fixture ticker and rate-my-team thread: Optimise . It works in two modes. Starting fresh - or holding a wildcard - it builds the best £100m squad for the next six gameweeks outright, with its projected total attached, and loads it straight onto your pitch to tweak. With your real squad in, it proposes a concrete transfer plan instead: which players out, which in, in which gameweek, whether a points hit is worth taking, and what the whole package is projected to gain. Draft mode: the optimiser's best £100m squad for the opening six gameweeks, projected total attached, one tap to load. Two things make it trustworthy rather than a black box. First, every move shows its working : the incoming and outgoing player's projected points for each of the next six fixtures, side by side, with captaincy-ceiling weeks flagged. Second, the "Why these moves?" panel says it in plain English - a fixture swing, a captaincy upgrade, value released from the bank - and the arithmetic is printed at the bottom: points in, points out, minus any hit, equals the net gain. Agree with it and one tap applies the plan; disagree and you've still learned exactly where the model thinks your squad is leaking points. Plans, leagues and the weekly routine Everything you sketch saves as a Plan - so you can keep a safe route and an aggressive route side by side and decide on deadline day, with an undo button for every experiment along the way. The Leagues tab brings your mini-league into the planner, because half of FPL is knowing what the manager above you is likely to do next. Under the hood it's the same engine as the rest of the toolkit: projections built on expected minutes first (the Season Rankings model), refreshed as new data lands, sharpened by the predicted line-ups behind Team News . The planner is where those numbers stop being a leaderboard and start being your decisions: fifteen minutes a week, squad in front of you, projections on every option. The planner is free to try with your own squad at statz.ai/fpl/my-team - full projections and the optimiser are part of FPL Pro FAQs What is the Statz FPL Team Planner? A squad-planning tool at statz.ai/fpl/my-team that loads your real FPL team and adds what the official app doesn't have: projected points on every player, multi-gameweek fixture heatmaps, chip planning, saved transfer plans and an optimiser that proposes your next moves with the reasoning shown. How do I import my FPL team into the planner? Three ways: enter your FPL Team ID and it pulls your squad automatically, build a squad from scratch, or upload a screenshot of your team from the official app and the planner reads your players off the image. What does the FPL optimiser do? It analyses your squad, bank, free transfers and the projections for the coming gameweeks, then proposes specific transfers - including when a points hit is worth it - showing the six-gameweek projection for every player in and out, plus a plain-English explanation and the net expected points gain. Is the FPL Team Planner free? Importing and building your squad is free with a Statz account. Full player projections and the optimiser are part of FPL Pro. articles.body: Newcastle vs Liverpool Predictions & Betting Tips - PL Gameweek 1 Newcastle vs Liverpool Predictions and Betting Tips - Premier League Football rarely writes a script this neatly. Alexander Isak, the striker Newcastle turned into one of the most valuable players in Europe, walks back into St James' Park on Sunday afternoon wearing a Liverpool shirt. Whatever the reception is, it will not be muted. Underneath the noise is the best fixture of the weekend and the model's strongest goals call of the round. Liverpool are favourites, but only just, and both defences look considerably less trustworthy than either club would like. Kickoff is 4:30pm UK, live on Sky. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News Liverpool's front four is frightening and their treatment room is fuller: seven players are out , including Ekitiké, Bradley, Gomez, Leoni and Bajcetic. Wirtz, Szoboszlai and Gakpo line up behind Isak, with Van Dijk marshalling a back line that has Frimpong and Kerkez as its full-backs. Newcastle's rebuilt side tells the story of their summer. Our season preview has them projected twelfth after sales reported beyond £240m, and the XI hands starts to Bamba, Ramsey and William Osula. Livramento is a doubt, Miley is out. Newcastle predicted XI (4-3-3): Horníček; Burn, Botman, Thiaw, Hall; Bamba, J.Ramsey, Joelinton; Barnes, Elanga, Osula. Liverpool predicted XI (4-2-3-1): A.Becker; Kerkez, Virgil, Araujo, Frimpong; Mac Allister, Gravenberch; Gakpo, Wirtz, Szoboszlai; Isak. Recent Form Neither side arrives in form: Liverpool WLDLD, Newcastle LWDWL. The projections are close, 1.55 goals to 1.35 in Liverpool's favour, and the clean-sheet numbers are the interesting part - 25.9% and 21.2% , both weak, in a game that will be played at a hundred miles an hour. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The pick of the board is Dominik Szoboszlai to be carded at 4.75 , a 25.9% chance in a fixture with this temperature. articles.body: Man City vs B'mouth Predictions & Betting Tips - PL Gameweek 1 Man City vs Bournemouth Predictions and Betting Tips - Premier League Spare a thought for Bournemouth. Of all twenty clubs, the fixture computer handed them the hardest opening run in the league - City away, Everton, then Newcastle - and this is the worst of the three. The model's loudest single number of the entire opening round lives in this game: over 2.5 goals at 64% . City are projected for 2.29 goals, Bournemouth for a clean sheet chance of 10.2%, the lowest of any side this weekend. Erling Haaland starts a season against opponents the model expects to concede more than two. Kickoff is 2:00pm UK on Sunday, live on Sky. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News City's summer rebuild is on display: Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal for his home debut, Marc Guéhi alongside Rúben Dias, and Antoine Semenyo joining Doku and Foden behind Haaland. Rodrigo is out and Grealish is a doubt. Bournemouth are missing three squad players plus the suspended Christie, which is not what you want before a trip to the Etihad. Justin Kluivert and Evanilson carry the counter-attack. Man City predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Gvardiol, Guéhi, Rúben, Matheus N.; Anderson, O'Reilly; Doku, Foden, Semenyo; Haaland. Bournemouth predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Petrović; Truffert, Hill, Silva, Sanchez; Cook, Scott; Tavernier, Kluivert, Rayan; Evanilson. Recent Form City closed WWWDL, Bournemouth DWWDD, which is a perfectly respectable line that will count for very little here. The projections are brutal: 2.29 goals to 1.01, clean sheets 36.4% against 10.2%. Among the starters, Elliot Anderson 2+ shots at 2.10 is the one worth a look on a 49.4% projection - a summer signing the model rates as a top-ten player in the whole game, in a match City will spend camped in the opposition half. Phil Foden to be carded at 10.00 appears on the value list but has not been booked in any of his last five, which tells you what the model thinks of it. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles City at 1.48 for a 64.9% chance is fair rather than generous, and short prices about teams with Community Shield rust and a World Cup summer behind them are not where I want to be. The goals number is the bet. Over 2.5 at 64% (1.44 at the time of writing) is the model's strongest call anywhere on the round, and the logic is not complicated: City will score, Bournemouth's shot map says they will have their moments on the break, and neither of those things stops after the opening goal. Summary The bet: Over 2.5 goals at 1.44. City by two is the likeliest outcome and the market knows it. The value is in the total, not the result. articles.body: Brentford vs Spurs Predictions & Betting Tips - PL Gameweek 1 Brentford vs Tottenham Predictions and Betting Tips - Premier League New managers get honeymoons. They rarely get them at Brentford. Roberto De Zerbi takes charge of his first Premier League game for Tottenham on Saturday teatime, at a ground where visiting sides with grand plans have been getting bullied for years. Spurs closed last season in their best form of the campaign and the market has priced in a good chunk of optimism about the new era. The model has not: it still leans Brentford, at 41.3% against 30.2%. Kickoff is 5:30pm UK, live on Sky. Numbers from the live Statz match centre Lineups and Player News Brentford are close to full strength, with only Milambo doubtful, and line up as you would expect: Kelleher behind a settled back four, Thiago leading the line, Damsgaard pulling the strings. Spurs are the unknown. Kulusevski, Xavi Simons and Odobert are all out , with Kudus a doubt, and our team news desk expects De Zerbi to go with three at the back given the centre-back depth available to him, with Tonali and Fernandes in the engine room and one of Tel or Maddison supporting Solanke. That is a lot of new information to process in one afternoon. Brentford predicted XI (4-2-3-1): Kelleher; Hickey, Collins, Ajer, Kayode; Sangaré, Jensen; Anthony, Damsgaard, O.Dango; Thiago. Spurs predicted XI (3-5-2): Kinsky; Van de Ven, Senesi, Van Hecke; Udogie, Gallagher, Fernandes, Tonali, Pedro Porro; Solanke, Maddison. Recent Form Spurs' closing WWDLW is the better recent line, but the model still favours Brentford at home: 1.49 projected goals to 1.25, and a 28.8% clean sheet to 22.6%. A brand new system cuts both ways, and Brentford's team-strength numbers have always held up in this fixture. Statz Team Projections See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Interesting Player Stats The props board here is thin, which is itself worth knowing. Among the starters, Aaron Hickey 1+ shot at 2.00 is the one the model likes, on a 55.5% projection, with Brentford's wing-backs getting forward relentlessly against a Spurs shape nobody has seen yet. Michael Oliver takes charge, and his games run hot: 27.5 fouls and 4.25 cards a game . Mika Kayode's fouls-drawn line at 2.75 reflects that, though fouls come from our commentary data and are noisier than shots. Statz Bet Builder See the live Statz numbers for this fixture Betting Angles Brentford at 2.40 sits a shade under the model's 41.3%, so there is a small edge on the home win if you want it. I understand the temptation to oppose a brand new system on day one. The firmer call is both teams to score at 55.2% (1.57 at the time of writing), the second-strongest BTTS number of the round. Two attacking sides, a referee who lets the game breathe, and a Spurs back three still learning each other's habits. Summary The bet: Both teams to score at 1.57. De Zerbi's Spurs will be worth watching by October. Whether they are worth backing in their first away game, in a tight ground, against a side built to punish exactly this kind of afternoon, is another question entirely. Brentford at 2.40 is defensible. Goals at both ends is the bet I actually want. articles.title: Wilfried gnonto joins acf fiorentina on loan
articles.source_type: Manager fitness updates, injury detail and expected return timelines
articles.body: Wilfried Gnonto joins ACF Fiorentina on loan - Leeds United Previous Mens Wilfried Gnonto joins ACF Fiorentina on loan 01 Sep 26 Forward heads to the Serie A. Share Leeds United can confirm Wilfried Gnonto has joined ACF Fiorentina on loan until the end of the 2026/27 season. The forward links up with the Serie A side on a temporary basis and in doing so returns to his home nation of Italy, having left in 2020. Gnonto joined the Whites in August 2022 and has been a regular member of the squad since arriving, amassing just short of 150 appearances for the club. A hugely popular member of the team, Willy played a key role in helping the club to achieve promotion back to the Premier League in the 2024/25 campaign, scoring nine goals and grabbing six assists as the Whites lifted the Sky Bet Championship trophy. Last term, the Italy international made 29 appearances across all competitions, helping United retain their Premier League status and reach the semi-finals of the Emirates FA Cup. Gnonto heads to a Fiorentina side who will be looking to improve on last season’s 15th-place finish in Serie A under the newly appointed Fabio Grosso. In the previous campaign, the Viola also reached the semi-finals of the UEFA Conference League. Willy now heads out on loan with the best wishes of everyone at Elland Road during his time in Florence and we look forward to seeing his progress while away from the club. articles.source_type: Manager fitness updates, injury detail and expected return timelines
articles.body: Largie Ramazani joins Burnley on loan - Leeds United Previous Next Mens Largie Ramazani joins Burnley on loan 01 Sep 26 Forward makes Championship switch. Share Leeds United can confirm Largie Ramazani joined Burnley on a season-long loan, which will become a permanent transfer next summer, based on the winger making an achievable number of appearances for the Sky Bet Championship side. The forward arrived at Elland Road ahead of the 2024/25 title-winning season, signing for an undisclosed fee from UD Almería. The Belgian made his debut for the Whites in a victory over Yorkshire rivals Hull City on home soil before opening his account for the club with a goal in the away win at Cardiff City. Ramazani featured 29 times in the second tier and scored six times in a memorable year which saw United crowned champions and return to the Premier League. With his game time in West Yorkshire limited last term, the 25-year-old enjoyed time on loan at La Liga side Valencia CF. Whilst at the Mestalla club, Ramazani netted six goals in 31 appearances across all competitions. A hugely popular figure behind the scenes at Thorp Arch and Elland Road, Largie departs the club with the best wishes of everybody. We wish him well during his time in Lancashire and beyond. articles.source_type: Manager fitness updates, injury detail and expected return timelines
articles.body: EFL Cup Ticket Information: Chelsea (A) - Leeds United Previous Ticketing EFL Cup Ticket Information: Chelsea (A) 02 Sep 26 Details for Stamford Bridge clash. Share We can now confirm ticket and ballot information for our Carabao Cup Round Three away fixture against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday 9th September, KO 8pm. IMPORTANT INFORMATION: Our ticket allocation for this fixture will be digital tickets. A digital ticket will be emailed to each ticket holder. Digital tickets will be sent out by close of business on Monday 7th September . Digital tickets can only be downloaded once. Please note, screenshots of digital tickets will not work. All supporters are encouraged to arrive early for this game and ensure that they have downloaded their digital ticket to their Apple /Google wallet on their smartphone before arriving at Stamford Bridge. Any supporters who require assistance with their digital tickets on matchday, must ensure that they travel with their photo identification as this will be required by the Chelsea Box Office team to verify that they are the ticket owner. AWAY SEASON TICKET HOLDERS: Any Away Season Ticket Holders who are enrolled on the Away Auto Cup Scheme will automatically have their payment card charged and their ticket dispatched. Away Season Ticket Holders not enrolled on the Away Auto Cup Scheme are guaranteed a ticket, but must purchase their reserved away ticket online between 10am on Thursday 3rd September and 9am on Saturday 5th September. How to purchase a reserved away ticket: 1. Login to your online ticketing account – 2. Hover over your name (top right) and click ‘My Account’ 3. Click ‘Reservations’ 4. Select the Chelsea ticket and click the ‘Confirm Reservation’ button 5. Proceed and pay for your ticket. BALLOT APPLICATION DATES: Due to the limited timescales, the usual sales window is shorter for this fixture. Online ballot application dates: Thursday 3rd September - Tracker Ballot Ballot opens at 10am and closes at midnight Supporters who attended 6 or more away games in the 2025/26 season can apply 50% chance of success Friday 4th September - Tracker Ballot Run Tracker ballot will be run and successful applicants notified by midday. Friday 4th September - Season Ticket Holders / Members Ballots Separate ballots will open at 1pm; one for Season Ticket Holders and one for My Leeds Members. These ballots will close for applications at midnight. Season Ticket Holders and Members who are unsuccessful with their Tracker Ballot application can submit a further application during this window. Saturday 5th September - Season Ticket Holders / Members Ballots Run The Season Ticket Holders and Members ballots will be run and successful applicants notified by midday. Please note, we can only guarantee that we can allocate adjoining seats for those supporters who apply within the same ballot application. TICKET ALLOCATION: 4046 MATCH TICKET PRICING: £35 Adult £27 Senior 66+ £27 Under 23 years £17 Junior under 20 years Please note that all supporters under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an adult over the age of 18. Any supporter under the age of 16 unaccompanied by an 18 year will not be allowed entry to the stadium. All supporters regardless of age will need a valid ticket. ACCESSIBILITY: Accessible Tickets There are 30 wheelchair spaces, these are priced at the above relevant age category with a free personal assistant where required. Ambulant seating is available. Accessible Parking 9 accessible car parking spaces are available, (6 Stamford bridge underground, and 3 Fulham Broadway) they can be pre-booked on a first come first basis via Chelsea FC online form found here and is available to both home and away supporters. Supporters can apply until 3 days prior to the fixture. IMPORTANT INFORMATION: Refunds The deadline for any match ticket refunds for this fixture is midday on Monday 7th September. Coaches There is a limited area for supporter coaches in Chelsea FC coach park area (Imperial Road). Imperial Road is now part of the South Fulham Traffic Congestion and Pollution Reduction Zone, so access is usually restricted to borough residents and other specially authorised vehicles. To ensure a coach parking space is allocated and avoid the risk of incurring a Penalty Charge Notices (PCNs) please following this link Book Coach Parking – Chelsea FC - Coach Parking – Imperial Road (gotocsp.com). Please note Chelsea FC cannot accommodate more than 20 away supporter coaches. All coach and minibuses must be booked onto the system no later than 12 noon, three days prior the fixture date. Coach drivers are required to remain with their vehicle throughout the match in case they need to move it. Bag Policy Supporters are reminded that no bags larger than A4 will be permitted into the stadium. This equates to 30cm x 20cm x 10cm, about the size of a standard handbag. Please note there is no baggage deposit facilities available for any larger baggage items. Away Section The entire away section is designated a safe standing area, and supporters will have an allocated position that they must occupy. Supporters in safe standing area are required to comply with our Supporter Code of Conduct, a copy of which is available at www.chelseafc.com/tickets/conditionsofissue. Visiting Supporters Guide The visiting supporters guide can be found below should you require more information for your supporters: https://www.chelseafc.com/en/tickets-guides-policies-and-forms. OFFICIAL COACH TRAVEL: Coach ticket prices - £57 adults, £46 concessions Departs from outside the East Stand at 1.30pm Related Content A reminder to all supporters regarding ticket touting Ticketing A reminder to all supporters regarding ticket touting 28 Aug 26 Ticket Information: Newcastle United (H) Ticketing Ticket Information: Newcastle United (H) 27 Aug 26 Ticket Information: Brighton & Hove Albion (A) Ticketing Ticket Information: Brighton & Hove Albion (A) 18 Aug 26 Latest News

articles.body: FPL Price Change Predictor 2026/27: Live Guide The official FPL Price Change Predictor is now live for 2026/27. Log in to Fantasy Premier League and select Price Changes to see which players are moving towards a price rise or fall. The predictor uses official FPL transfer activity and updates every 15 minutes. It is a timing guide rather than a guarantee, so use it alongside minutes, fixtures and team news before making a transfer. The feature was launched by the Premier League after the Gameweek 1 deadline . For other squad-building data, visit our free FPL tools , including the FPL DEFCON comparison tool What is the official FPL Price Change Predictor? The predictor is an official Fantasy Premier League page that tracks every player's progress towards the next price rise or drop. It shows current progress as a percentage calculated from official transfer activity. After a calibration period of at least one Gameweek, FPL says it will also show a predicted progress percentage. Labels such as “Very Likely to Rise” and “Likely to Drop” translate the data into a quicker status. This is the first official FPL tool dedicated to predicting price changes. Third-party services have estimated changes for years, but they have had to infer the unpublished thresholds from player ownership and observed changes. Is the FPL Price Change Predictor live? Yes. The predictor became available after the Gameweek 1 deadline on 21 August 2026. To find it: log in on the Fantasy Premier League website select Price Changes in the main navigation; and filter the table by your team, your watchlist or all players. Player prices were locked before the Gameweek 1 deadline. They can now rise or fall at the daily price-change update. What does the predictor show? The main table lists every player and can be filtered to show: players in your team; players on your watchlist; or the full player pool. Price-change status also appears on individual player profiles. FPL says the Pick Team and Transfers screens will include a price-change view, letting managers check their own squad as part of the normal transfer workflow. What does a percentage over 100 mean? According to the Premier League, anything above 100 per cent indicates that the player is expected to pass the rise or fall threshold at the next 00:00 UK update. It still does not guarantee a change. For example, a player could display 105 per cent shortly before midnight, then receive enough late transfers in the opposite direction to move back below the estimated threshold. FPL explicitly describes the predictor as a guide. Treat the status as evidence for timing a move, not a promise that the price will change. How often is the FPL predictor updated? The predictor page updates every 15 minutes. Player price changes happen once per day at 00:00 UK time The percentage can move in either direction as managers continue buying and selling players. A stale screenshot or an update from earlier in the day may no longer represent the current position. The most important limitation remains the same: predicted progress is not the only factor in a good transfer. Should you make an early transfer to avoid a price rise? Sometimes, but price protection has a cost. An early transfer can secure a player before a rise and preserve team value. It also exposes your squad to injuries, rotation news and other information that arrives before the next deadline. Before moving early, consider: whether the player is likely to start; whether either club has another match before the FPL deadline; how much the possible price change affects your planned move; whether you would still want the player at the higher price; and whether you have a free transfer or would take a points hit. A predicted rise can make the timing urgent, but it does not make the underlying transfer good. Decide on the player first, then use the predictor to decide whether waiting is worth the risk. Official predictor versus third-party price-change sites The official tool has one major advantage: it is built from official FPL transfer data and integrated into the game. That does not necessarily make every independent tool redundant. Third-party services can still differentiate through: notifications before a likely change; historical prediction accuracy; daily price-change histories; combined transfer, fixture and expected-points analysis; and alternative views for planning several moves. FPL has also said its own prediction remains a guide. The value of any predictor should be judged by how clearly it communicates uncertainty and how accurately it performs after calibration. When do FPL prices change? FPL price changes happen at 00:00 UK time Official FPL price-change rules say a player can rise or fall by £0.1m in one daily update and by up to £0.3m in a Gameweek. The predictor's percentage is designed to show who is approaching the next change. Check it close enough to the update to use current information, but do not let a possible £0.1m move override a better transfer decision. Our FPL defensive contribution guide explains another new-season factor to consider when comparing players. If your group would rather draft unique squads and trade players during the season, Draft Fantasy for the Premier League supports auction and snake drafts, waivers, trades and custom scoring. Read the 2026/27 launch guide for the full setup. Create a 2026/27 Premier League Draft Fantasy league FPL Price Change Predictor: quick answers Where is the FPL Price Change Predictor? Log in to the Fantasy Premier League website and select Price Changes in the main navigation. Does 100 per cent guarantee a price change? No. It indicates that a player is expected to pass the threshold, but transfers can move the percentage before the midnight update. How frequently does the predictor update? The predictor page updates every 15 minutes. Player prices change at 00:00 UK time. How much can an FPL player's price change? A player can rise or fall by £0.1m per day and by up to £0.3m in one Gameweek. Want a fantasy game where players move between managers through waivers and trades instead? articles.body: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Gameweek 3 Pickups Anthony Elanga is the best Gameweek 3 waiver claim. Lewis Hall is the priority defender, while Eddie Nketiah is the forward to add before his points catch up with his chances. Pascal Groß offers a safer midfield role; Dan Ndoye and Amar Dedić are deeper-league alternatives. This is advice for draft leagues , where each player has one owner. The roster rate measures how often a player is already owned across completed private Draft Fantasy leagues, so first check who is actually free in your Draft Fantasy Premier League transfer market. Scoring note: the order uses Draft Fantasy regular scoring, which matches official FPL scoring. Custom-scoring leagues calculate points from the commissioner's values, so extra rewards for shots, chances created or defensive actions can change the order. The Gameweek 3 claim order Best fantasy football waiver claims for Gameweek 3 Priority Player Pos Rostered GW1–2 GW3–5 Anthony Elanga NEW Midfielder 39.1% 17 pts · 156 min BOU LEE HUL Lewis Hall NEW Defender 47.2% 14 pts · 180 min BOU LEE HUL Pascal Groß BHA Midfielder 32.4% 15 pts · 180 min LEE COV ARS Eddie Nketiah CRY Forward 7.7% 3 pts · 122 min FUL IPS LEE Dan Ndoye NFO Midfielder 4.7% 12 pts · 126 min TOT AVL COV Amar Dedić NEW Defender 8.7% 12 pts · 180 min BOU LEE HUL Draft Fantasy regular-scoring totals and private-league roster rates, 1 September 2026; fixture difficulty runs from 1 (easiest) to 5 (hardest). All ten Gameweek 2 matches had finished on the pitch when this snapshot was taken, but the official post-Gameweek review had not locked the round. Small scoring corrections remain possible. The ranking is built on roles, underlying involvement, roster availability and three fixtures rather than one provisional bonus point. Create a Premier League draft league to play with unique squads, configurable waivers and a live transfer market. Why Elanga leads the order Elanga has started both matches, scored in both and played 156 minutes. The two goals came from 0.42 expected goals, so the finishing rate will not continue unchanged. His role is still more useful than the headline: he registered three shots on target and Newcastle's run improves from Bournemouth at home to Leeds away and Hull at home. A 39.1% roster rate makes him available often enough to justify an aggressive claim. Use 8–14% of remaining FAAB as an editorial starting range when he would enter your lineup. Spend less when he would only replace bench depth; these are bid guides, not fixed player prices. Hall is the defender to claim; Dedić is the fallback Hall has completed 180 minutes and followed an 11-action defensive game in Gameweek 1 with 13 defensive contributions, a clean sheet and maximum bonus in Gameweek 2. His 0.66 expected assists across two matches also gives him an attacking route that does not depend on another clean sheet. The concern is availability rather than evidence: Hall is already rostered in 47.2% of completed private leagues. Start around 7–12% of remaining FAAB if he is free and upgrades a weekly starter. Dedić is the practical second request. He has also played every minute, then added an assist and two key passes in Gameweek 2. His 8.7% roster rate makes him far likelier to survive to a fallback claim. Bid 1–4% , because Hall owns the stronger creative numbers even though both receive the same fixture run. Groß supplies the safer midfield role Groß has two full matches, six key passes and 0.38 expected assists. A goal and an assist at Chelsea produced the Gameweek 2 return, but the 90-minute role and chance creation are the reasons to buy. Leeds at home and Coventry away are rated two and one before a much harder Arsenal fixture. Rank him above a volatile scorer when you need a midfielder to start immediately. An editorial range of 6–10% of remaining FAAB is reasonable; custom leagues that reward key passes can move him closer to Elanga. Brighton teammate Diego Gómez is the lower-cost alternative. He has two assists, 0.56 expected goals and 0.65 expected assists in 175 minutes, but using both midfielders as separate high bids would overcommit to the same fixtures. Put Gómez behind Groß in the same request chain instead. Nketiah is the forward whose process beats his points Nketiah has only three points, which is why he remains rostered in 7.7% of leagues. The underlying case is much better: two starts produced 0.96 expected goals, 0.58 expected assists and three key passes in 122 minutes. He now faces three opponents rated two, one and two. This is not a guarantee that the finishing changes in Gameweek 3. It is a chance to buy a scarce starting forward before a return makes him obvious. Use 4–8% of remaining FAAB when he replaces a forward without secure minutes. Managers with three dependable forwards should preserve their budget. Ndoye is the deeper-league upside claim Ndoye has started twice but played only 126 minutes, so his role is less secure than those above him. Gameweek 2 supplied the upside: a goal, two key passes, 0.35 expected goals and 0.63 expected assists in 65 minutes. Nottingham Forest also receive difficulty ratings of one, three and one over the next three. Treat him as a fifth-midfielder claim, not proof that a six-point average will last. A 1–4% bid is enough in most FAAB leagues. If you need a steadier 90-minute floor, Groß should remain higher in the queue. Hold last week's hits, but step back from Emersonn The strongest Gameweek 2 waiver recommendations mostly reinforced their roles. Mamadou Sangaré, Anton Stach and Keane Lewis-Potter each played at least 87 minutes; Sangaré and Stach again reached double figures for defensive contributions, while Lewis-Potter added an assist. Do not drop them merely because their second score was lower than the opening return. Maxim De Cuyper also played 90 minutes and now reaches the favourable Leeds and Coventry fixtures. Thierno Barry failed to score but generated 1.48 expected goals in 69 minutes, then moves into two difficulty-one fixtures after Manchester United. Both remain holds. Emersonn is the exception. He fell from 65 minutes to 45, produced no shot and is now flagged with a knee problem in the official player data. Do not add him before his availability and role are clearer. That is new evidence, not a verdict on the opening goal. Build a claim queue around the player you will drop Fix a weak starter before adding depth. Elanga, Hall or Groß should lead when one immediately improves your lineup. Pair alternatives in one position. Use Hall then Dedić at defender, or Groß then Gómez at midfield, rather than six unrelated requests. Pay for role and opportunity. Nketiah's three points can be more actionable than a bench player's isolated goal. Protect scarce FAAB and priority. The fantasy football waiver rules guide explains how bidding, rolling priority and weekly reset change the cost of each claim. Check the full run. The free fixture difficulty tool shows why a neutral Gameweek 3 matchup can still lead into two strong starts. The verified Gameweek 3 deadline is Friday 4 September at 17:30 UTC . Waivers follow the processing schedule shown inside your own league, so submit the queue before that process rather than waiting for the match deadline. articles.title: Romeo lavia on how xabi alonso is trying to find that extra one per cent
articles.source_type: Head coach team news ahead of each fixture, injury updates, official previews
articles.body: Romeo Lavia on how Xabi Alonso is trying to find that extra one per cent | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club Romeo Lavia is feeling great. But best of all for Blues fans, the midfielder believes he is going to get even better with the support of his team-mates and new manager. The 22-year-old has now started both Premier League games under manager Xabi Alonso and is enjoying making an impact on the pitch, something he did from the off last Sunday when he tapped home his first Chelsea goal to open the scoring against Brighton as the Blues won 4-3 at the Bridge. Having made it two wins in two in the league, Lavia highlighted the Blues’ developing mentality, which he believes is making the difference. ‘Our mentality has been great so far, starting from pre-season,’ Romeo opened. ‘And the manager has really been big on that to help us get that extra per cent to help us get the three points on the weekend. So far, it's been great. ‘It's all about building confidence. Obviously, my team-mates are giving me a lot of it, and the manager as well. It's just about building game by game, and I feel great, so hopefully it can continue forever.’ Even the cool, calm and collected Lavia couldn’t hide his joy after scoring his first for Chelsea, admitting he might have the video on loop! He continued: ‘It means a lot to score my first – a lot. I’m very happy – to score at the Bridge as well. For a first one, it can't get any better. I think I'm going to rewatch the goal a few more times. It's not the best-looking goal, but I'll take it every day. ‘It was a fantastic reaction from the fans, and from my team-mates as well. I really felt the love, so it was an amazing feeling.’ In a game that saw the visitors peg the Blues back, Lavia recognises the group will only get better in time, with all eyes on our trip to the Emirates this weekend, where we’ll go head-to-head with London rivals Arsenal. ‘We know our colleagues, and when we know that our colleagues can take over, we just need to make sure the rest goes with it,’ he added. ‘We realise that it's automatic – that we just push each other. We know our colleagues will take over in the end. It's honestly a great group to be in, and the demands in training every single day make it easier to then perform on the weekend. ‘There's a lot of work that goes behind the scenes, and it was just about putting that into practice. And we're happy that they came off well [against Brighton], so I’m very happy.’

articles.body: Premier League ticket news: Brentford away - loyalty point update for season ticket holders | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club Details have been announced on the loyalty points required by season ticket holders wishing to access ticket sales for this month's west London derby. Chelsea travel to Brentford’s Gtech Community Stadium for a league encounter on Friday 18 September. The match kicks off and 8pm and ticket sales will be as follows: As tickets for this match are being sold on a loyalty-point basis and the match takes place in the first month of the season, loyalty points accrued during the previous season will be taken into account. Wednesday 2 September from 10am until 11:30am: Tickets will be sold to season ticket holders with 165 loyalty points or more who can purchase one ticket per person. Wednesday 2 September from 12pm until 1:30pm: Tickets will be sold to season ticket holders with 160 loyalty points or more who can purchase one ticket per person. Wednesday 2 September from 2pm until 3.30pm: Tickets will be sold to season ticket holders with 155 loyalty points or more who can purchase one ticket per person. Wednesday 2 September from 4pm: All remaining season ticket holders who have yet to purchase can purchase one ticket per person. Thursday 3 September from 10am until 11:30am: Tickets will be sold to members on a loyalty-point basis, one ticket per person. The number of loyalty points required will be announced on this website no later than 9:30am on Thursday 3 September. Thursday 3 September from 12pm until 1:30pm: Tickets will be sold to members on a loyalty-point basis, one ticket per person. The number of loyalty points required will be announced on this website no later than 9:30am on Thursday 3 September. Thursday 3 September from 2pm until 3.30pm: Tickets will be sold to members on a loyalty-point basis, one ticket per person. The number of loyalty points required will be announced on this website no later than 9:30am on Thursday 3 September. Thursday 3 September from 4pm: All remaining members who have yet to purchase can purchase one ticket per person. Tickets will be sold online only. Application process for supporters with access needs Supporters who require accessible tickets can submit an application form found here during the selling period. Alternatively, supporters if they are able to do so, can call our Access Team on 0371 811 2012 0044 207 915 1950 (international callers) to reserve tickets and request further information. Personal assistant tickets can only be allocated using this process. Allocation We have received an allocation of 1,725 tickets which includes an allocation of 14 non-ambulant and 14 personal assistant tickets. Ambulant tickets will be taken from the main allocation. Dispatching of tickets The entire allocation for this fixture will be in sent in the post, via first class delivery. Tickets will be sent from the week commencing Monday 7 September. Duplicate tickets Supporters who do not receive their tickets should email the ticket office on Friday 18 September no later than 12pm. Please note that away duplicate tickets can only be collected by supporters in the booking. Loyalty points Loyalty points will continue to be awarded for purchasing away tickets. If using away ticket transfer, points will remain with the original ticket purchaser. Supporters will receive three loyalty points for this match. articles.title: Pga south league report chelsea womens under 18s 6 1 crystal palace u21s
articles.source_type: Head coach team news ahead of each fixture, injury updates, official previews
articles.body: PGA South League report: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s 6-1 Crystal Palace Under-21s | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club Chelsea Women’s Under-18s made it three wins from three so far this season with a 6-1 victory over Crystal Palace Under-21s. Chelsea Women's Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, took the lead through captain Keira Johnson before an own goal doubled our advantage. Palace pulled one back, but Gabi Storey struck just before half-time to send the Blues into the break 3-1 ahead. Carla Gardiner, Aysia Matabaro and substitute Annie Boichat added further goals after the interval. Leanne Champ’s side created plenty of chances and worked hard defensively when required to continue our positive start to the campaign. Blues ahead Chelsea’s patience in possession was rewarded after 19 minutes. The ball was worked around the back line to Sophie Leach, whose pass through the Palace shape found Storey. The midfielder turned and lifted the ball over the defence for Matabaro, who beat her marker to reach the byline and pulled a cross back for the arriving Johnson to power home first time. Sadie Gregory replaced Emelia Addison a minute later and Chelsea doubled the lead on 34 minutes after another well-worked move. Quick passing moved the visitors out of position, allowing Leach to find Johnson between the lines. They combined to release Maisie Brickell on the right, and she took a positive first touch towards goal before skipping past two defenders. Her cross took a deflection off a Palace defender and reached the goalkeeper, who spilled the ball over the line for an own goal. Palace reduced the deficit five minutes later, capitalising on a transition in Chelsea’s defensive half, but the Blues restored our two-goal cushion before the interval. Two-goal advantage restored Brickell and Matabaro combined down the right in the 44th minute and, although the visitors defended Matabaro’s shot well, Chelsea’s midfield reacted quickly to regain possession. Storey collected the ball on the edge of the box, shifted it out of her feet and struck from 20 yards, sending her effort across goal and into the bottom corner. Champ made three changes at half-time, with Zoe Ciccardini, Tess Finn and Jahyma Putman replacing Elise Christian, Storey and Chelsea N’Drin. Ciccardini was involved as Chelsea added a fourth eight minutes after the restart. She won the first contact from a Palace throw-in, and Johnson gathered the loose ball centrally before spotting Gardiner’s run between the two centre-backs. Johnson’s pass released the forward, who showed composure as the goalkeeper rushed off her line and dived at her feet. Gardiner took the ball around her and passed into the empty net. Matabaro and Boichat on target Matabaro added our fifth on 67 minutes at the end of another flowing move. Ciccardini took a quick throw-in down the left to Matabaro, who turned as Chelsea worked the ball back around to Finn. Finn played forward to Rebekah Pierce on the edge of the box, and she combined with Johnson to find Brickell out wide. Another dangerous delivery across the box picked out Matabaro, who finished first time. Boichat replaced Gardiner in the same minute and needed just eight minutes to add her name to the scoresheet. Chelsea were awarded a free-kick down the side of the penalty area, and Brickell floated her delivery over the wall towards the players waiting at the far post. Boichat met it with a header that struck the crossbar and went in to complete the scoring. What it means The result continues Chelsea’s winning start to the Professional Game Academy South League season. After two matches, the Blues have six points, with 14 goals scored and just one conceded. What’s next? Chelsea travel to Southampton for our next Professional Game Academy South League fixture on Wednesday 2 September. We then head to Swindon Town in the Women’s National League Cup on Sunday 6 September. Team Women’s Under-18s (4-3-3): Bella Bartlett; Elise Christian (Zoe Ciccardini 45), Sophie Leach, Emelia Addison (Sadie Gregory 20), Maisie Brickell; Gabi Storey (Tess Finn 45), Chelsea N’Drin (Jahyma Putman 45), Keira Johnson (c); Rebekah Pierce, Carla Gardiner (Annie Boichat 67), Aysia Matabaro Scorers: Johnson 19, own goal 34, Storey 44, Gardiner 53, Matabaro 67, Boichat 75 Booked: Gregory 84 Manager: Leanne Champ

articles.body: Carabao Cup ticket news: Leeds at home | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club Ticket selling details have been announced for our third-round tie next week... Chelsea take on Leeds United in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday 9 September with kick-off at 8pm at Stamford Bridge. Ticket sales for this match will be as follows: Leeds have taken an increased allocation in the Shed End for this fixture meaning we have to displace all season ticket holders in the Shed upper and Shed lower tiers. Therefore, displaced season ticket holders can purchase any of the available seats not taken by a season ticket holder during the reservation period. There will be a specific on-sale period providing displaced season ticket holders with the priority opportunity to purchase elsewhere in the stadium. Tuesday 1 September from 7pm Season tickets holders who are part of the cup scheme will have payment for their own seat taken through an automated process. Any failed transactions will result in your season ticket seat being in a reservation status meaning that it can be purchased by Monday 7 September 10am. Wednesday 2 September from 12pm until Thursday 3 September 9am: Season tickets holders who are not part of the cup scheme can purchase their own seat. Thursday 3 September from 10am until 2pm: Displaced supporters in the Shed End lower and upper tiers have priority to buy another available seat in other areas of the stadium and any remaining season ticket holders who have not purchased a ticket can also purchase. Due to the reduced timelines to sell this fixture, sales to members will be online (there will be no ticket application window for this fixture). This fixture will be sold on loyalty points accrued during the previous season. More information will be released prior to the sale. Thursday 3 September from 2:30pm: Tickets will be sold to True Blue+, True Blue or Junior Blue members with the required loyalty points or more who can purchase one ticket per person. Season ticket holders who are yet to purchase will also be able to purchase one ticket per person. Friday 4 September from 2:30pm: Tickets will be sold to CFC Blue members with the required loyalty points or more who can purchase one ticket per person. True Blue+, True Blue or Junior Blue members and season ticket holders who have not already purchased can also purchase during this period. Season ticket holders who are yet to purchase will also be able to purchase one ticket per person. Tickets for this match are priced at Category F Tickets will appear on the Chelsea Official App prior to the event. Tickets sold online are for Chelsea supporters only. All persons under the age of 16 will be required to attend with and sit next to, a person aged 18 years of age or over. Club Chelsea Westview Members and season ticket holders can purchase Westview tickets for Carabao Cup home games via the Chelsea FC Official Ticketing Portal. A maximum of four tickets can be bought per person, and only the ticket purchaser is required to be a member or season ticket holder. You are not required to be a member or season ticket holder to purchase non-Westview Club Chelsea packages. Club Chelsea tickets are non-refundable unless the match is cancelled, postponed, or moved more than 48 hours either side of the scheduled fixture date. All Club Chelsea ticket purchases are subject to Club Chelsea terms and conditions. For any further Westview enquiries, please email clubchelsea@chelseafc.com Loyalty points Loyalty points will now only be awarded for attendance at men’s first-team home matches and no longer accrued for purchasing tickets. Points will be added to eligible accounts following each game, provided the ticket has been scanned at the turnstile. This means that supporters purchasing tickets on the ticket exchange, or receiving tickets via ticket forwarding, will now receive loyalty points for attending matches. Please note those with Ticket Forwarding Memberships will not accrue loyalty points for attendance. Supporters will receive five loyalty points for attending this match. Points will be applied after the fixture has been played. Application process for supporters with access needs Due to the reduced timelines to sell this fixture there will be no ticket application window for this game. Supporters who require accessible tickets can submit an application form found here during the selling period. Alternatively, Supporters if they are able to do so, can call our Access Team on 0371 811 2012 0044 207 915 1950 (international callers) to reserve tickets and request further information. Personal assistant tickets can only be allocated using this process. Accessible car parking Supporters can apply for car parking by clicking here from Thursday 3 September You are required to display your Blue Badge while parked at Stamford Bridge. Ticket exchange Those who have enrolled on the cup scheme will be able to list on the ticket exchange for this cup fixture. The sales information on the Buy Tickets page will be updated once the ticket exchange is open. The ticket exchange will close three hours before kick-off, unless stated otherwise. Ticket forwarding Once open, season ticket holders and members can send and receive tickets up until three hours before kick-off. Please note that those who have forwarded their ticket will not be able to list their ticket on the ticket exchange. Click for ticket forwarding FAQs Match and ticket on-sale dates are subject to change. All ticket sales are subject to availability. Please check the website for the latest information.

articles.title: Usmnt star folarin baloguns potential move to everton snag deadline day
articles.source_type: News, scores, standings and fantasy projections
articles.body: USMNT star Balogun's move to Everton appears to hit medical snag on deadline day - CBS Sports site: media | arena: soccer | pageType: stories | section: | slug: usmnt-star-folarin-baloguns-potential-move-to-everton-snag-deadline-day | sport: soccer | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/soccer/reg/free/stories CBS Sports Golazo Network UEFA Champions League EFL Championship 2027 Women's World Cup USMNT star Folarin Balogun's potential move to Everton appears to hit medical snag on deadline day Chuck Booth Sep 1, 2026 at 8:38 pm ET 2 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Now Playing Share Video Link copied! Another transfer window has seen a move for a United States men's national team forward collapse, as Folarin Balogun is now set to stay at Monaco after there was a €45 million agreement to send him to Everton for a new challenge. Last transfer window, it was Ricardo Pepi who saw a move to Fulham not happen, and now it's Balogun, as the American failed his medical , according to reports. It seemed as if the deal might end up being completed as Everton submitted a deal sheet to iron out the final details with Monaco, but it still didn't end with the American moving, according to the Times The Athletic also adds that it was Baogun himself who called the move off, leaving the Everton training ground without signing on deadline day Tuesday. This is after Monaco called off the sale of Lamine Camara to Chelsea because it seemed like they would get Balogun's deal over the line. Neither of these happening leaves the club in financial limbo while also leaving Balogun to figure out what's next for himself. Balogun hasn't appeared for Monaco since the World Cup, where he scored three goals for the United States in a strong performance. It seemed like all was set for him to head back to England , where his journey started in the Arsenal academy, only to stay in France with Monaco. While he may not be getting his big move yet, this isn't the worst outcome for Balogun, as when healthy, he's a starter for the, club and he will also still be able to take part in European soccer in the Europa Conference League. While it is a blow to see a transfer fall apart like this, it's also no guarantee that he'd become a starter for the Toffees as well. Everton striker Thierno Barry has been experiencing a breakout of his own, and it's not so straightforward that the American could beat him out for a spot. Balogun's movement and ability to create his own shot are strong, but Barry is a bigger body for tangling with Premier League defenders as well. The grass isn't always greener when it comes to transfers, and this is one where, if it doesn't work out, the USMNT would struggle to determine who would lead the line. CBS Sports Balogun has come into his own to become the unquestioned starter for the national team, and if he ended up at a club where he isn't a regular, Mauricio Pochettino would have a tough decision to make. For Everton, this puts the club into a tough position. Beto has already moved to Fiorentina , and they also tried to move for Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee as a fallback option, but there wasn't time to sort that out, leaving Moyes with only Barry as a senior striker. Monaco needed to sell to balance their own finances, so this does put them in a tricky situation, as only leagues like Turkiye and Major League Soccer have transfer windows that are still open after Tuesday. Time is limited for clubs to get things done, and when issues like this come up, it gets down to one club saying one thing and another saying the opposite. It's hard to prove which is correct since Balogun hasn't played this season for Monaco, but there's still plenty of time to make the best of his situation as moves could still be available in January or next summer for the 25-year-old. articles.title: Mls returns to u s open cup in 2027 all 27 teams set to participate for first time since 2024
articles.source_type: News, scores, standings and fantasy projections
articles.body: MLS returns to U.S. Open Cup in 2027: All 27 teams set to participate for first time since 2024 - CBS Sports site: media | arena: soccer | pageType: stories | section: | slug: mls-returns-to-u-s-open-cup-in-2027-all-27-teams-set-to-participate-for-first-time-since-2024 | sport: soccer | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/soccer/reg/free/stories CBS Sports Golazo Network UEFA Champions League EFL Championship 2027 Women's World Cup MLS returns to U.S. Open Cup in 2027: All 27 teams set to participate for first time since 2024 Chuck Booth Sep 2, 2026 at 8:01 am ET 2 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Now Playing Share Video Link copied! All 27 United States-based MLS teams will make their return to the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup in 2027. The oldest running soccer competition in the country, the Open Cup has been going since 1913, and any club sanctioned by the United States Soccer Federation can take part in it. It is also the third-longest continuously running cup competition in the world. But in 2024, due to match congestion, MLS teams that were involved in Concacaf Champions Cup play were no longer in the Open Cup, making this historic competition not feature all of the MLS sides for the past few seasons. During that time, prize money has risen in the Open Cup, and resources have also been devoted to covering travel costs, and MLS will return as the tournament's later rounds now shift to September in order to accommodate the calendar shift, with a one-million-dollar prize for the winner and a spot in the Concacaf Champions Cup on the line for the champion. The competition has been won by an MLS team every year since 2000, with the Rochester Rhinos of USL being the last non-MLS side to win the tournament, but it can offer an entry into the Champions Cup for any team in American soccer. "The Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup is one of the most powerful platforms we have to showcase what makes American soccer special," said Dan Helfrich, U.S. Soccer Chief Operating Officer. "When you bring various levels of the soccer community together, you create a connected, competitive environment that moves the sport forward and gives fans the drama of knockout soccer. Along with MLS, USL, and all of the Member Organizations represented in the Open Division, the U.S. Open Cup reflects our shared commitment to strengthen the future of the game in this country." Format In the future, the Open Cup will be a 96-team field, including all MLS teams, and the first-round matchups will be announced in early 2027, with teams still being matched based on geography. Gameday rosters will also expand from 18 to 20 players. The first round will consist of 32 teams from MLS Next Pro independent clubs, amateur clubs, and teams from USL League One and the USL Championship. Five seeded teams from the USL will enter in the round of 64. This is also the round where MLS sides will enter. articles.title: Grading usmnt summer transfers as folarin balogun deal collapses gio reyna
articles.source_type: News, scores, standings and fantasy projections
articles.body: Grading USMNT summer transfers as Balogun deal collapses, Gio Reyna joins Strasbourg - CBS Sports site: media | arena: soccer | pageType: stories | section: | slug: grading-usmnt-summer-transfers-as-folarin-balogun-deal-collapses-gio-reyna | sport: soccer | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/soccer/reg/free/stories CBS Sports Golazo Network UEFA Champions League EFL Championship 2027 Women's World Cup Grading USMNT summer transfers as Folarin Balogun deal collapses and Gio Reyna joins Strasbourg Chuck Booth Sep 1, 2026 at 8:50 pm ET 4 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Now Playing Share Video Link copied! What started as a quiet transfer window for American players ended with a bang of the unfortunate variety as Folarin Balogun's move to Everton eventually fell through , leaving the Monaco man in limbo. There were issues during his medical, according to reports, and while the deal was renegotiated, it unfortunately led to it not being completed, leaving Everton without an adequate number of strikers following Beto's move to Fiorentina , and also sending Balogun back to Monaco after his wild summer. From the highs of scoring at the World Cup to the red card being rescinded, that is one of the lasting stories from the tournament, Balogun's summer has been a strange one, and that will only continue after he got so close to a return to the Premier League. But while he didn't get his move, there were plenty of Americans who went to new clubs in Europe during the summer, from Gio Reyna leaving the Bundesliga to Americans flocking to the English Championship. Let's take a look at those moves and what they could mean for Mauricio Pochettino's national team moving forward. Gio Reyna gets a fresh start Transfer: Borussia Mönchengladbach Strasbourg The past few seasons have been lost ones for Gio Reyna between Nottingham Forest Borussia Dortmund , and Borussia Mönchengladbach, but now he's made a move to France to join Strasbourg. It's a new environment for Reyna, but in getting his first start for the club, the American has gotten off to a strong start. Still only 23, if Reyna can make the most of this move to France, there's no reason why he can't get back to being a USMNT regular. A surprise addition to the World Cup squad, it's clear that Mauricio Pochettino rates Reyna, and there's the additional benefit of being in the Chelsea system, so if he really breaks out, either there's a route back to the Premier League or to other clubs in the world. Grade: B Could Cole Campbell break out Transfer: Borussia Dortmund to SV Elversberg Another former Dortmund man getting a fresh start, Cole Campbell has become a record signing for SV Elversberg and has already gotten off to a good start, scoring his first goal for the German club. With the high expectations that they have for the 20-year-old, this is a great chance to show what he can do in a league that he's familiar with. Get that done, and there could be national team call-ups and a place at the Olympics in his future. Grade: A Zavier Gozo makes it two Americans at Crystal Palace Transfer: Real Salt Lake to Crystal Palace It has been quite the year for teenagers in the USMNT pipeline as Real Salt Lake winger Zavier Gozo has moved to Crystal Palace, where he'll join Chris Richards. While his debut against Manchester City was tough sledding, that's one of the hardest Premier League games that the 19-year-old will be involved in. Strong on the ball and also having the speed to keep up in the Premier League, this is a great move for him to develop at a higher level as the USMNT winger depth is improving rapidly. It's always good to see when a club values a player like him, coming in by using them in their plans early, so it'll be a move worth watching. Grade: A The American pipeline to the Championship has never been stronger There are more Americans in England 's second division by the day, so here's a round-up of all the new additions to clubs. Sebastian Berhalter ( Vancouver Whitecaps to Middlesbrough): Moving to Middlesbrough and immediately slotting into the starting lineup, there's so much to enjoy about Berhalter taking a step up from the Vancouver Whitecaps; he's in a place where there are many familiar faces as an American quartet pushes for the Premier League together. Grade: A Max Arfsten Columbus Crew to Middlesbrough): Alongside Berhalter, the wing back is a new arrival at Boro , joining from the Columbus Crew. With so many American defenders already in Europe, Arfsten is the latest to follow their path. Grade: A Rokas Pukstas ( Hajduk Split to Middlesbrough): After growing as a player in Croatia , Pukstas is ready for his next challenge, joining the group of Americans pushing for the Premier League. Able to operate as a 10 or deeper in midfield, he'll bring much-needed versatility to the squad. Grade: B Caleb Wiley (Chelsea to Preston North End on loan): Constantly on loan from Chelsea, Wiley has made his latest move after spending last season at Watford. He scored on his Preston North End debut, which could be something that helps lead to a permanent move. Grade: B Luca Bombino San Diego FC Stoke City Another American to debut immediately upon joining their new club, the left back will be able to have a chance to make an impact. He's only 20 years old and can also get up the pitch; this could be the start of something special. Grade: A Jack McGlynn Houston Dynamo to Stoke City): Wielding one of the best deliveries of any member of the USMNT, it will be an adjustment to such a physical league with his defensive liabilities, but if Stoke can use McGlynn correctly, it could be a serious boost to the club . Grade: B Add CBS Sports on Google Around the Web Promoted by Taboola

Evangelista was traded to the Devils from the Predators on Tuesday in exchange for a conditional first-round pick and a second-round pick, both in the 2028 NHL Entry Draft. It's a bit of a surprise that the Predators are parting with Evangelista, who put up a career-high 56 points (12 goals, 44 assists) in 81 regular-season games in 2025-26. The 24-year-old winger held out of camp last fall before signing a two-year contract, so he'll be playing for a new deal with the Devils throughout 2026-27. Expect Evangelista to slot into a middle-six role, and the playmaker should also be an option to see power-play minutes. His fantasy value gets a slight bump by moving to a stronger offense, but since his offense heavily relies on assists, he'll need to click with his new teammates quickly to make good on that upgrade in surroundings. articles.body: Dodgers' Eric Lauer: Torched for seven runs - CBS Sports site: fantasynews | arena: mlb | pageType: stories | section: | slug: dodgers-eric-lauer-torched-for-seven-runs | sport: baseball | route: article_single_fantasy | 6-keys: media/fantasynews/mlb/reg/free/stories Power Rankings Expert Picks Fantasy Baseball Dodgers' Eric Lauer: Torched for seven runs RotoWire Staff Sep 2, 2026 at 2:37 am ET 1 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Now Playing Share Video Link copied! Lauer (8-7) allowed seven runs on eight hits, one walk and one hit batsman while striking out two over three innings to take the loss versus the Cardinals on Tuesday. Lauer was tagged for a pair of home runs in the second inning, but it was a parade of hits in the third inning that brought his start to an early end. With 20 runs allowed (19 earned) over his last 20.1 innings, Lauer is stumbling to the finish line this year. However, the Dodgers need him in the rotation while Roki Sasaki (finger) is out, as Justin Wrobleski has moved to the bullpen. Lauer has put up a 5.23 ERA, 1.31 WHIP and 72:35 K:BB through 108.1 innings over 22 games (18 starts) this season. His next start is tentatively projected to be at home versus the Nationals over the weekend. The Dodgers' pitching plans for the next turn through the rotation likely hinge on Shohei Ohtani's availability to take the mound after he was scratched from a start Sunday versus Detroit due to ongoing knee and biceps concerns. articles.source_type: Team news, debutants, rotation plans, match reports
articles.body: ‘We’re in a strong place’: Director of football Phil Giles reflects on Brentford’s summer transfer window | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Director of football Phil Giles believes Brentford have emerged from the summer transfer window with a stronger squad after retaining the core of Keith Andrews’ group and adding five new first-team signings. Jannik Schuster, Jaidon Anthony, Callum Wilson, Mamadou Sangaré and El Hadji Malick Diouf arrived during the window, with all but Diouf joining before the start of the Premier League season. Following a summer of significant change in 2025 , continuity and targeted additions were central to the club’s approach this time around. “Last summer, we sold more than we bought,” Giles explained. “The aim this year was to keep the squad together, build on Keith’s first season and add some extra quality. I think we did that. “Every summer, you need to add some freshness. It makes us less predictable for the opposition and creates competition for places.” Combined with the relationships already established within the squad, Giles thinks that has helped the Bees make a positive start. “I’m very pleased,” he continued. “They’re all coming in to compete for a first-team place. “There’s always a balance between players who are ready now and development projects. These players were more or less ready to go from day one, which is great. “By keeping what we had together and adding them, I think the squad looks really strong. “The players who were here last year know each other, know the coaching staff and understand the style of play. “They’ve already built relationships on the pitch, so we weren’t starting from scratch with a lot of new players. “We’ve dropped a few additions into a group who already knew what they were doing. “In theory, that should allow you to make a good start in the league, and I think we’ve done that. We’ve played really well during the first couple of games, so it’s been positive so far.” Giles admitted that the level of spending across the wider transfer market exceeded his expectations. “At the start of the summer, after a lot of spending last year, I thought it might be quieter and perhaps there wouldn’t be as much money floating around – but I was completely wrong!” he said. “It’s been interesting. There’s been a lot of money spent. “We’ve invested a significant amount by our standards, but when you compare that with clubs spending £70 million, £80 million or even £120 million, we’re obviously not in that ballpark. “To be able to compete with those clubs without spending that sort of money is testament to our scouts and recruitment team, who continue to find players capable of helping us. “I want to give all the staff credit – not only for identifying and signing players, but for integrating and developing them. “We’ve got a really good squad and, in today’s market, a valuable one. We’re in a strong place as a football club.” Having finished in the Premier League’s top half in three of the last four seasons, Giles wants Brentford to continue progressing without placing limits on what the team can achieve. “The target in any season is to keep improving – that’s always the baseline,” he concluded. “We’ve finished in the top half of the Premier League in three of the last four seasons. “Getting better would mean finishing in the top half again, and you’d hope that one day that will lead to European qualification. “The trick is to keep getting better and not worry too much about where that might take you. “We don’t yet know how good the other teams are. If they’re all brilliant, it becomes harder for us! We’ll let everything settle down and see. “Let’s keep being us, let’s keep trying to improve, and we’ll see where we land.”

articles.body: Things to know if travelling to Elland Road | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford take on Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday 30 August (2pm kick-off BST). The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. If you are heading to Elland Road, here is everything you need to know to ensure you are ready for your visit. Digital tickets are in use for this matchday and you will receive an email with instructions on how to download yours. Travel – rail replacement services on parts of your journey Travel to Leeds on matchday is disrupted by maintenance works on LNER lines. Rail replacement bus services will take you part of the way on your journey. From London St Pancras, journeys to Leeds could take between four hours and five hours and 30 minutes, with multiple changes. You will have to board a train as early as 6.30am to make it to Leeds in good time. We strongly recommend that you plan your journey to the match and home again ahead of time and book tickets early as many routes have already sold out. Local travel to the ground Leeds train station is approximately 40 minutes’ walk from Elland Road. Bus services from the city centre will take you to Elland Road, including: 9A, 24, 51, 52, 55, 55C, 65, 75. You can also take the matchday shuttle service (R2) to the ground. Bus stops directly outside the ground are suspended for one hour before and one hour after the match. You may have to walk a short distance if you arrive close to kick-off. We recommend using the Citymapper app to help navigate public transport in the city. Driving and parking Driving from London to Leeds will take around four hours and possibly longer if driving in poor weather. Paid car parking operated by the home club or its partners is available at Elland Road or near to the ground. The main car park for away fans is the park & ride drop-off point off Bobby Collins Way, which is near the away coaches. For more information, see the car parks section on Leeds’ website A park & ride matchday shuttle is also available, with shuttles running from two and a half hours before kick-off until 25 minutes after full-time. This must be paid for in advance. More information is available here Ticketing information – digital tickets are in use for this fixture Tickets for this fixture will be distributed digitally. You will receive your ticket(s) by email ahead of the match. Please follow the instructions on the email to get your ticket ready on your phone. For those that have requested a physical ticket or have sent a duplicate ticket request, the away ticket office is located in the west stand car park opposite the away supporter entrance. Any duplicate ticket requests must be sent to Leeds United by the Brentford box office. Please contact Brentford's box office with any enquiries ahead of matchday. If you’re collecting your ticket at Elland Road, please remember to bring ID. Please also observe and respect the family friendly seating. Anyone who holds a ticket in this area is reminded that they should be seated for the duration of the match. Accessibility Accessible parking is available for blue badge holders only in Fullerton, off of Elland Road. You cannot pre-book this area but it is free for blue badge holders. Visiting disabled supporters who have purchased accessible seats enter the stadium by Exit W1 gate. Elland Road has elevated wheelchair platforms for visiting fans. Accessible toilets are in the away end and unlockable with a RADAR key. If you need access, speak to a wellbeing officer identified by their blue vests. Changing places facilities are also available, but please contact [email protected] prior to your visit. Your matchday at Elland Road Leeds operates an away fanzone in the west stand car park. Food and drink including alcohol will be served from two hours before kick-off. There are no away pubs in the vicinity of Elland Road. Some pubs in the city centre will accept Brentford fans but entry is at the discretion of the venue. Visiting supporters enter the ground at entrances 1 and 2 of the west stand. Turnstiles open 90 minutes before kick-off. Bags larger than A4 in size will not be permitted inside. There is no luggage storage facility at Elland Road. Have a safe trip and enjoy the match!
