articles.body: Leeds United 1 Brentford 1: Kevin Schade scores in Elland Road draw | Brentford FC Kevin Schade's first goal of the season was cancelled out by Dominic Calvert-Lewin as Brentford were held to a 1-1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road. Schade's first-half effort looked to be enough for the three points, but Calvert-Lewin struck with 11 minutes remaining and it ended honours even in West Yorkshire. Keith Andrews made two changes to the side who beat Tottenham Hotspur 3-0 on the opening weekend of the Premier League season. Jaidon Anthony , playing against the side he spent the 2023/24 season on loan with, made his first league start for the Bees while Mikkel Damsgaard also came into the starting XI. El Hadji Malick Diouf was named on the bench. Brentford, wearing the Kingsman- inspired away kit for the first time, had the first effort on goal inside the opening eight minutes, but Igor Thiago 's back-post volley from a tight angle was straight at James Trafford. The England international goalkeeper was then well-positioned to collect a Nathan Collins header moments later. Damsgaard tested Trafford with a curling shot and Ethan Ampadu sent a speculative effort comfortably wide of Caoimhín Kelleher 's goal at the other end as the Bees continued to control the contest against a well-organised Leeds defence. Five minutes before the break, the west Londoners got their reward for a dominant first-half display. Mamadou Sangaré swept the ball to his right for Anthony, whose cross was headed back into a central position. Sangaré picked it up again and his blocked shot fell to Keane Lewis-Potter on the left side of the box. His near-post delivery was turned into the far corner of Trafford's goal by a sublime Schade flick. Leeds made two changes at the interval but it didn't take long for the Bees, orchestrated by Sangaré, to dictate the game again. Their first set-piece of the second half created the first opportunity. Collins beat Ampadu to Vitaly Janelt 's deep corner to loop it back towards the penalty spot before Damsgaard got a bit too much on his header and it went over the frame. Kelleher, largely a spectator for the previous hour, was called into action for the first time and made a smart stop to deny James Justin after the left-back had cut inside and pulled the trigger from 25 yards. Brentford thought they should have had a penalty at the other end shortly afterwards. Dango Ouattara , five minutes after his introduction from the bench, led a lightning counter attack down the right flank. Eventually, he cut inside and switched the ball to Schade, who took a touch before going down after Jayden Bogle appeared to step on his foot. Referee Tony Harrington waved the appeals away. Some superb recovery defending from Lewis-Potter prevented the hosts from equalising following a breakaway of their own at the other end. After clearing the ball from a Bees corner, Lukas Nmecha poked the ball forward to put Dan James, positioned just inside his own half, through on goal. Under pressure from Lewis-Potter, the Welsh winger sent a wild shot high and wide of the target. Leeds were level, however, with just over 10 minutes remaining. Ampadu played the ball from the right wing into Nmecha inside the box. He took a touch and fired the ball across the six-yard box where Calvert-Lewin tapped into an empty net. Thiago nearly restored the lead instantly. The Brazilian's header from an Ouattara cross was parried by Trafford and, at full stretch, he could only turn the rebound into the side netting. Anton Stach sent a stoppage-time free-kick wide of the mark as both teams made it four points from their opening two league fixtures. Leeds (3-4-3): Trafford; Muharemović, Bijol (Tanaka HT), Rodon (Elvedi 34); Bogle (James 68), Ampadu, Stach, Justin; Aaronson (Wilson HT), Calvert-Lewin, Okafor (Nmecha 69) Subs not used: Cairns, Gudmundsson, Longstaff, Gnonto Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher; Kayode (Wilson 89), Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter (Henry 89); Sangaré, Janelt, Damsgaard (Yarmoliuk 69), Anthony (Ouattara 61), Thiago, Schade (Hickey 89) Subs not used : Valdimarsson, Schuster, Carvalho, Diouf Attendance: 35,974 Andrews: A solid away point Keith Andrews reflected on Brentford's away fixture against Leeds United. "I’m really proud of what we produced. In the first half, we played some pretty impressive football," said Andrews. "We were in a good place and controlled pretty much the whole half, which isn’t easy to do when you come here. "In the second half, it was a different game. They made attacking subs and changed their system. "Overall, it’s a solid away point." Schade on Leeds stalemate Kevin Schade shared his thoughts after Brentford's 1-1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road. "We need to keep working on the good things. We dominated the first half and probably needed to score more goals and put in more crosses in the final third," said the German forward. "In the second half, they changed a few things and we couldn’t adapt enough." On scoring his first goal of 2026/27 and his ambitions for this year, he added: "I want to achieve more than the other seasons, but I’ll take it game by game, work on things and then the goals will come."

articles.body: Jayden Meghoma joins Portsmouth on loan | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford defender Jayden Meghoma has joined Sky Bet Championship side Portsmouth on a season-long loan. The 20-year-old left-back will spend the duration of 2026/27 at Pompey alongside fellow Bees loanee Benjamin Arthur. Meghoma , who has represented England at every level from under-16s to U20s, came through the youth ranks at Tottenham Hotspur before joining Southampton aged 16. He signed his first professional contract in July 2023 and made his first-team debut the following month in a Carabao Cup tie against Gillingham. Three more appearances – all in the FA Cup – followed that season before he sealed a move to Brentford on Deadline Day of the 2024 summer transfer window. Meghoma featured in three Carabao Cup ties and made his Premier League debut against Chelsea during the first half of 2024/25, before joining Preston North End on loan in January of that campaign. He spent the duration of last term with Glasgow giants Rangers and made 44 appearances across the Scottish Premiership, Champions League qualifying, Europa League, SFA Cup and League Cup. During his time in Scotland, he also scored his first goal in senior football, a superb long-range effort against Dundee United.

articles.body: Brentford encourages community to talk more about mental health with Talking is the Best Tactic | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford Football Club and Brentford FC Community Sports Trust will continue to use the power of football to encourage conversations around mental health this season through Talking is the Best Tactic , the campaign delivered as part of the Premier League's Together Against Suicide initiative. This Saturday’s fixture against Sunderland will be dedicated to the campaign, building on last season's launch. Brentford is encouraging supporters to take simple actions that could make a meaningful difference to supporting someone’s mental health. This week, the club and Trust installed a bench in Gunnersbury Park, the sixth to be added in the local area to encourage the community to pause, connect and talk. Last season, some of our players took to the benches to share their own experiences of mental health, including Fábio Carvalho and former Bees player Jordan Henderson. The installation of benches was inspired by Brentford's longstanding commitment to supporting mental wellbeing and the work of consultant psychologist Michael Caulfield, whose bench at the Robert Rowan Performance Centre (RRPC) provides a safe, confidential space for players, coaches and staff to speak. On Saturday, ahead of our game against Sunderland, from 12.30pm the RRPC bench will be located outside Entrance B at Gtech Community Stadium so fans can make a personal commitment linked to mental wellbeing and supporting others. Trained representatives from Brentford FC Community Sports Trust and the Samaritans will be on hand to speak with supporters and provide information about health and wellbeing programmes available in the local community. Support a loved one This season, Talking is the Best Tactic is encouraging supporters to take small actions towards better mental health through simple conversations or small acts of support. The Sunderland fixture is our dedicated Friends and Family fixture, where Brentford members (excluding overseas and junior members) can purchase an additional ticket and invite a friend, family member or someone they haven't seen for a while to the game. The fixture provides the perfect opportunity to reconnect with someone, spend time together and start a conversation. Supporting someone through conversation doesn't require the perfect words. Whether it's checking in with a friend, taking time to listen or helping someone access support when they need it, small actions can make a big difference. Purchase your ticket now Help is available For those experiencing poor mental health, support is available and no one has to face challenges alone. Brentford FC Community Sports Trust continues to provide free opportunities for people to connect and talk through initiatives including: Singing for Thought: A welcoming seven-week programme designed to boost mood, build confidence and bring people together through music. Led by an experienced choir leader, sessions are relaxed, fun and open to everyone. No previous singing experience needed - just bring your voice! Sign up here Walking for Wellbeing : A friendly community walking group designed to help people get outside, connect with others and improve their wellbeing. The group is a supportive space for anyone who wants to meet new people, build confidence or increase their daily step count weekly, every Friday. Sign up here Resources for urgent and local help can be found on our Talking is The Best Tactic webpage Anyone in need of urgent mental support should always call 999 in an emergency or contact NHS urgent mental health support via 111 and select option 2. You can also call Samaritans on 116 123 – free, available 24/7. Across local west London pubs, One Over the Ait, Kew Bridge, The George IV, The Bell & Crown and The Pilot in Chiswick, our special free Talking is The Best Tactic coasters will be available on Saturday morning. The coasters include details of urgent and local support for poor mental health. Everyone has a role Suicide affects people of all ages and backgrounds and affects men disproportionately. Sadly, men account for nearly three-quarters of suicides in the UK, yet too often feel unable to talk about what they're experiencing. Talking is the Best Tactic encourages all of us to play our part by checking in with those around us, asking simple questions and taking the time to listen. Throughout the 2026/27 season, Brentford will continue to encourage supporters, staff and the wider west London community to help create a culture where people feel able to talk.

articles.body: Brentford Women 8 Aylesford 2: Kiszkis scores hat-trick in dominant victory | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Brentford Women were in fine form as they beat Aylesford Women 8-2 at Honeycroft to make it three wins from three to start the London South East Premier Division campaign. The Bees came from behind with an emphatic victory; Wiktoria Kiszkis bagged a hat-trick, with Ashley Cheatley, Maddie Phillips, Becca Teale and Ilana Harris-Walters all getting on the scoresheet. It was a nightmare start for Brentford, who found themselves behind within 50 seconds. Williams' side failed to clear their lines on three occasions inside the box before the ball fell to Leigha Bradding-Butler, who fired through the bodies to put Aylesford 1-0 up. The west Londoners found themselves behind for the first time this season, but showed excellent character to respond instantly. Maï Louvrier's lofted through ball was met by Kiszkis , who nodded the ball into her own path before firing a left-footed half volley in to level the score on six minutes. Kiszkis almost had her second on 15 minutes when she again found space in between the Aylesford backline and keeper. She got to the ball first and poked her effort round Sade Rider but wide of the post. Two minutes later, Brentford found the lead through an own goal; Phillips capitalised with a short corner as Aylesford slept and flashed a ball across the six-yard box. Cheatley got the last touch in a red and white shirt as the ball ricocheted around the goalmouth before crossing the line as the Bees went 2-1 up. Teale fired just over from outside the box seconds after the restart and Cheatley's improvised flick went just wide as the west Londoners began to assert themselves on the game. On 24 minutes, Millie Constantine drove down the left and put a superb cross in to the back post which Kiszkis just couldn't connect with on the stretch. Lucy Potter then lifted an inch-perfect pass into Cheatley, who mishit her half-volley and missed the target. Williams' side were really applying the pressure and it paid off on 31 minutes when Abbi Smith turned in the box and was brought down. Phillips stood up and calmly tucked her penalty into the bottom-left corner to make it 3-1. Potter had a strike from range well saved from Rider after a clever free-kick found her in space. The Aylesford keeper injured herself in making the save and outfielder Juliette Blyghton had to go between the sticks as the Bees went into the break with a two-goal advantage. Mya Francis-Pownall was called into action a minute into the second half, intercepting at the feet of Bradding-Butler in the nick of time to protect the lead. The Bees stepped it up a gear and Cheatley made it four for Brentford on 49 minutes after running onto a perfectly weighted, slotted pass from Kiszkis and tucking the ball home. Two minutes later and Kiszkis doubled her tally for the day and added Brentford's fifth. Makeba Black's excellent diagonal ball was met by Teale who played the ball into the box for Kiszkis. The west Londoners' no.9 took her time, rode a challenge and then smashed home from close range to make it 5-1. Williams' side went close again as Cheatley almost scored a spectacular left-footed volley, but sent it too high, and Teale arrived at the back post from a Smith corner but fired wide. The floodgates had opened and Harris-Walters added a sixth shortly after coming off the bench, improvising a half-volleyed finish after controlling the ball with her chest to score her first of the season. Then, on 68 minutes, Teale capped her brilliant performance off with a goal, opening her account for the 2026/27 campaign. After breaking into the box, she chopped past her defender and struck a fierce effort into the bottom corner as the Bees went 7-1 up. Aylesford did pull one back with 20 minutes to play, when Rebecca Keyte headed home from a free-kick. Kiszkis went desperately close to scoring her third, bending an effort that bounced inches past the post, before Freya Worsley fired a strike narrowly wide. With just over five minutes left on the clock, Kiszkis did get her hat-trick, striding into the box and striking across the keeper with her left foot to make it 8-2. It was an excellent display after going behind and in the end a comfortable victory with a rotated squad. Williams' side have started the season with a bang, winning their opening three league games as they now prepare for a tough away day at Hammersmith FC. Brentford: Francis-Pownall, Phillips, Teale, Potter, Kiszkis, Smith (Worsley 69), Cheatley, Louvrier, Gilligan (McCrea 59), Black (Berry 69), Constantine (Harris-Walters 59) Aylesford: Rider, B. articles.body: Match Preview: Brentford U21s v Sunderland U21s | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Sam Saunders’ Brentford Under-21s return to Premier League 2 action at Wheatsheaf Park on Monday when they host Sunderland Under-21s (1pm kick-off BST). After a busy opening to the season across the Premier League Cup and PL2, the young Bees will be hoping to make it two league wins from as many games. The west Londoners have started positively at both ends of the pitch this season, keeping a clean sheet in a 2-0 Premier League Cup win over Wycombe Wanderers and scoring three goals to beat Stoke City U21s in PL2 Saunders' side have enjoyed a spread of goalscorers, with Josh Dasilva Michel Boni Kaye Furo and Theo Mawene each netting so far this campaign. Last time out Brentford impressed on their way to a 3-2 win away at Stoke. Furo got the Bees off to a flying start with an early goal, with Mawene following suit later on in the first half with a brilliant individual effort. Theo opening his account 🤩 pic.twitter.com/Zj0R8GK23s — Brentford Academy (@BrentfordFCPDP) August 21, 2026 The hosts pulled one back before the break, but Saunders’ side reacted positively out of half-time to piece together a superb early move before Jayden Meghoma ’s cross was turned into the Potters’ net by a defender. While Stoke scored a second goal to make the latter stages of the second half tense, the Bees held on to take home all three points. About Sunderland U21s Sunderland sit second in the PL2 table following a dominant 5-1 win over Nottingham Forest in their season opener. Trey Ogunsuyi starred for the young Black Cats with a hat-trick, while Jack Whittaker and Timur Tutierov also got on the scoresheet in the impressive victory. Sunderland also got their Premier League International Cup campaign under way with a 1-1 draw against PSV U21s. Led by head coach Matt Craddock, Sunderland will return home for their next two PL2 fixtures, which are against Ipswich Town and Norwich City. articles.body: Brentford U21s 5 Sunderland U21s 1: Kaye Furo hat-trick and Fábio Carvalho on scoresheet as Bees win on PL2 home debut | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Kaye Furo was in scintillating form, bagging a hat-trick as Brentford Under-21s maintained their impressive start to the 2026/27 season with a 5-1 victory over Sunderland Under-21s in their first Premier League 2 home fixture at Wheatsheaf Park. Furo also provided the assist for Fábio Carvalho’s goal, with Riley Owen scoring the fifth, in a game which saw first-team players Benjamin Fredrick, Ji-soo Kim, Gustavo Nunes and Josh Dasilva feature for Sam Saunders’ side. It was a blistering start from the home side as Owen picked up possession and, inside the first minute, slid the ball through to Furo . The striker showed composure to take the ball around the goalkeeper before slotting into the empty net to give his side the lead. Nunes was next to go close as he attempted a delightful chip which beat the goalkeeper but clipped the top of the crossbar. Sunderland had chances of their own, with Trey Ogunsuyi firing a volley from inside the box which Reggie Rose stretched low to his corner to tip around the post. Minutes later, a fine move from the visitors on the edge of the box saw Jack Whittaker break into the area with the ball, but with only the goalkeeper to beat, he dragged his shot wide. On 33 minutes, Furo could have had his second of the game as he was found by Owen once again, but this time his effort flew over the bar. Ogunsuyi tested Rose again as he swivelled inside the box and struck a shot on target, but the goalkeeper got down well to hold onto the ball. Just before the half-time whistle, Furo powered through on goal in similar fashion to his first goal after being played through by Rose, but on this occasion he skewed his left-footed effort wide. Sam Saunders' side began the second period with an increased tempo, as Nunes and Owen had chances to score but they sent their efforts wide from close range. The deserved second came on 52 minutes as Furo picked up a loose ball before calmly playing Carvalho through, with the midfielder slotting the ball past Joe Cowan. The young Black Cats halved the deficit when Charlie Dinsdale sent a cross into the area which deflected off Rose and into the net, with the goalkeeper unable to keep the ball out. Despite the setback, the home side restored their two-goal advantage, with Furo grabbing his second as he found himself well placed to volley Nunes' corner into the net. Second-half substitute James Barker almost made an immediate impact for Sunderland as his first effort after coming on struck the post with Rose beaten. Furo completed his hat-trick firing low and hard past Cowan from just inside the area with a fantastic finish. There was still time for a fifth as Owen, who had been energetic throughout the game, broke clear and found the finish to match his powerful run into the box, leaving the goalkeeper with no chance. Brentford would take home the three points as the Bees march on in the PL2. Brentford now turn their attention to their second Premier League Cup game where they travel away to take on Hull City on Tuesday 8 September. Brentford U21s: Rose, Fredrick (Shield 46), Picotto (Wheeler-Henry 46), O'Connor (Klimas 78), Ji-soo, Grey, Nunes, Owen, Furo, Dasilva (Holland 26), Carvalho (Wilson 78) Subs not used: Wolfheimer, Boni Booked: Nunes 45, Rose 90+2 Sunderland U21s: Cowan, Jones (Holcroft 61), Lightfoot, Whittaker, Neild (Bell 61), Kindon, Dinsdale (Barker 81), Munyakazi (Hester 61), Ogunsuyi, Proctor, Jones (Scorer 81) Subs not used: Metcalf, Scott Booked: Jones 63, Bell 90+4 Saunders: Attitude and work ethic were spot on Brentford Under-21s head coach Sam Saunders reflected on the attitude, discipline and attacking threat shown by his side in their 5-1 victory over Sunderland Under-21s in Premier League 2. "The attitude, the desire and the work ethic from the players were top," he said. "We knew we had to find solutions to their aggressive press, and I thought Kaye was outstanding. The players who played around him managed the game really well, and the longer the game went on, the more open it became for our attacking players. "Yes, we could have taken more of our chances, but we did switch off in some small moments. Even though we were in control, we could have been more decisive in those key moments. We have to remain committed and focused for the full duration of the game, because the more they tired, the more opportunities we had to score. "The minimum we ask is that the players work hard and are good people, and the players who came off the bench and did well are a testament to that, as are the players who didn't make the squad. It shows the strength we have within the group and the collectiveness of the team. There was no sulking; they just got their heads down and worked hard."

articles.body: Analysis: Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangaré partnership excels in Brentford v Leeds United draw | Brentford FC Brentford's attacking trios have rightly earned plaudits over recent Premier League seasons - but the early indications are that their midfield will jostle for top billing this term. The Bees had to share the spoils at Elland Road against Leeds United on Sunday, but head coach Keith Andrews declared he was "very proud" of his side's performance in an entertaining 1-1 draw in West Yorkshire. Dominic Calvert-Lewin tapped home from close range late on to cancel out Kevin Schade 's 41st-minute opener and earn the hosts a point - their manager Daniel Farke afterwards describing Brentford's form as "red-hot". Brentford were, indeed, excellent for large swathes of the contest and their midfield pivot of Mamadou Sangaré and Vitaly Janelt was central to an impressive performance. Sangaré delivered another outstanding display to fuel his growing reputation as one of the star signings of the summer transfer window, and the Mali international has quickly forged an impressive partnership with Janelt. Alongside Mathias Jensen , who was ruled out by injury against Leeds, Sangaré and Janelt bossed proceedings in the 3-0 opening-weekend win over Tottenham Hotspur and again stole the show for long periods at Elland Road. "That is UNBELIEVABLE!" 😱 Kevin Schade with a stunning finish to give Brentford a deserved lead against Leeds pic.twitter.com/IwmWd8sOUu — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) August 30, 2026 Snapping into tackles and linking play superbly, the midfield duo set the tempo in a commanding first-half performance that saw the visitors deservedly lead at the break after Schade conjured up a delightful flick from Keane Lewis-Potter 's low cross from the left. So far this season, Brentford's destructive tendencies without the ball have been balanced with control in possession in the middle of the park, and Sangaré and Janelt's statistics told a story on Sunday. They combined to win seven tackles and eight interceptions over the course of the encounter, and also won three aerial duels between them. On the ball, Sangaré (56) completed more accurate passes than any Brentford player, while Janelt's tidy distribution was evidenced by an assured 85 per cent pass completion rate. Brentford fired in 22 shots to Leeds' 12 and the way in which they penned back their hosts, particularly prior to the interval, bodes well for the rest of the season. Goalscorer Schade won a penalty during a typically high-energy performance against Spurs on the opening weekend, and the German's sublime finish against Leeds opened his account for the 2026/27 campaign. The 24-year-old has scored 22 Premier League goals for the Bees since moving to west London at the start of 2023, and Schade now sits eighth on the division's all-time list of prolific German players after overtaking Leicester City cult hero Robert Huth (21 goals). The draw also preserved Schade's status as something of a lucky charm: Brentford are still yet to lose a game in which he has found the back of the net.

articles.body: West Ham U18s 5 Brentford U18s 4: Jai Nwosu hat-trick not enough as Bees defeated in nine-goal thriller | Brentford FC | Brentford FC Jai Nwosu scored a hat-trick but Brentford were narrowly beaten 5-4 by West Ham United in an entertaining U18s Premier League contest on Saturday morning. The young Bees twice held the lead at Little Heath Sports Ground but were ultimately edged in an exciting end-to-end game, with Nwosu’s treble unable to prevent the hosts from claiming all three points. The young Bees took the lead on five minutes with their first chance of the game as Jovan Kasujja delivered a perfect cross for Nwosu , who acrobatically steered the ball into the net. Despite the goalkeeper getting a strong palm to the effort, he could not keep it out. The young Hammers were not behind for long, though, as Bailey Pammenter pounced on a fantastic through ball before striking a firm effort which squirmed underneath Layton Nicholls On 29 minutes, Brentford went back in front as Jai Bansoodeb capitalised on a mistake from Tommy Goodger, with the goalkeeper heading the ball straight into the midfielder’s path. Bansoodeb calmly slotted the ball into the net. Nwosu could have added a third before the break as he rose highest to meet a Nathaniel Ogungbemi cross, but his firm header whistled just wide of the post. The striker had another opportunity to extend Brentford’s lead after doing well to fend off his opponent and break through on goal, but with only the goalkeeper to beat, he skewed his effort wide. Gary McDermott’s side began the second period on the front foot, but West Ham were awarded a penalty after Charles Gadsdon was brought down following a powerful run into the box. Joel Kerr stepped up and calmly converted from the spot. Pammenter then grabbed his second of the game, reacting quickest after Nicholls had parried an initial effort from Gadsdon on the edge of the box to put the home side ahead. Second-half substitute Christlife Mandungu went close to extending West Ham’s advantage when he smashed an effort from outside the box against the crossbar. The home side had turned the tide and were creating a number of opportunities, with Dylan Danso and Josh Oladapo-Gamu making important interventions on several occasions. Nwosu was then played through on goal and produced a delightful finish, chipping the goalkeeper to bring Brentford level. The striker completed his hat-trick in spectacular fashion, scoring another chip, this time from outside the box, to put the young Bees back in front. Mandungu then curled an effort into the net to level the scores once again. Frankie Day ultimately had the final say, pouncing on a Brentford loss of possession before getting beyond Micaiah Fanoiki and rounding Nicholls to score the winner. It was a tough defeat for the young Bees in an entertaining match. McDermott's side are next in action on Saturday 5 September when they host Aston Villa. West Ham: Goodger, Montague (Day 60), Kerr, Omotoye, MacAj, Agyemang, Lila (Madungu 60), Gadsdon (Ugate 56), Pammenter (Longman 60), Peychev (Noble 82), Magowan Subs not used: Tomlin, Smith. Booked: Day 68 Brentford: Nicholls, Fanoiki, Danso (Biggs 85), Oladapo-Gamu, Ogungbemi (Zetter-Plummer 46), Cohalan, Noni (Roca 60), Bansoodeb (Trialist A 82), Kasujja, Nwosu, Madden Subs not used: Lyon, Mason, Serme Booked: Roca 90+3

articles.body: Why Am I Missing a Free Transfer in FPL? | OneFPL Loading OneFPL page In this article sections The short answer If you think FPL has not given you a free transfer, the most common reason is that you used a Wildcard or Free Hit in the previous Gameweek. The free transfer received for the chip Gameweek is used as part of activating that chip. Previously banked transfers are not lost. Example You enter GW5 with: two saved free transfers; plus the normal new Gameweek transfer. You play Free Hit. The new GW5 transfer is used by the chip. Your two previously saved transfers remain available in GW6. What about Triple Captain or Bench Boost? Those chips do not use your weekly transfer. If you played Triple Captain or Bench Boost and made no transfer, the normal free-transfer rules continue. Other reasons the number may look wrong Check whether: you already used a free transfer; you were already at the maximum bank of five; you activated Wildcard or Free Hit; you are looking before the next Gameweek transfer has been awarded. Maximum bank You can store up to five free transfers If you already have five, leaving another transfer unused will not create a sixth. Read How many free transfers can you bank in FPL? OneFPL verdict Before assuming there is an account problem, check your previous Gameweek's chip and transfer history. The official FPL Transfers page shows your full history. articles.body: What Happens If Your FPL Captain Does Not Play? | OneFPL Loading OneFPL page In this article sections The short answer If your FPL captain records zero minutes , the captain multiplier moves to your selected vice-captain. If the captain makes any official appearance, even a short cameo, the multiplier stays with the captain. Captain and vice-captain outcomes Captain Vice-captain Result Plays Any outcome Captain scores x2 0 minutes Plays Vice-captain scores x2 0 minutes 0 minutes Nobody receives x2 Late cameo Plays Captain keeps x2 What happens with Triple Captain? The same promotion rule applies, but the multiplier is Triple Captain Vice-captain Result Plays Any Captain scores x3 0 minutes Plays Vice-captain scores x3 0 minutes 0 minutes Triple bonus is lost The chip is not returned if neither player plays. Does a one-minute cameo keep the captaincy? Yes. An official appearance means the captain keeps the multiplier. That is why expected minutes matter when choosing a captain or Triple Captain. Are automatic substitutions different? Yes. Auto-subs decide which bench player replaces a zero-minute starter. The captain multiplier moves only to the selected vice-captain — not to the substitute entering the XI. Can Triple Captain be cancelled before the deadline? Yes. Triple Captain can be cancelled before the Gameweek deadline. Read FPL Triple Captain explained OneFPL tools Use OneFPL Team News before the deadline and the Live Table during the Gameweek. articles.body: How Many Free Transfers Can You Bank in FPL? 2026/27 | OneFPL Loading OneFPL page In this article sections The short answer You can bank a maximum of five free transfers in FPL. You receive one free transfer after each Gameweek deadline. If you do not use it, it rolls forward until your total reaches five. Important chip rule: Triple Captain and Bench Boost do not use your weekly transfer. Wildcard and Free Hit do. How free transfers build Start of Gameweek Transfers used Free transfers next Gameweek Five is the maximum. You cannot bank six. What happens to your free transfer when you use a chip? FPL chip What happens to your weekly transfer? Banked transfers Triple Captain ✅ Normal rules apply ✅ Kept Bench Boost ✅ Normal rules apply ✅ Kept Wildcard Current week's FT is used by chip ✅ Earlier saved FTs kept Free Hit Current week's FT is used by chip ✅ Earlier saved FTs kept If I use Triple Captain, do I still get my weekly free transfer? Yes. Triple Captain only changes your captain's points multiplier. You can still make your normal free transfer, or leave it unused and bank it for the next Gameweek. Read the full answer: Does Triple Captain use your free transfer? What does an extra transfer cost? Each confirmed transfer beyond your free allowance normally costs four FPL points Example: two free transfers available; three transfers confirmed; one extra transfer; -4 points What happens with a Wildcard? Previously saved free transfers are maintained. The current Gameweek's newly received transfer is used as part of the chip. A Wildcard gives unlimited permanent transfers for that Gameweek. What happens with a Free Hit? Previously saved free transfers are also maintained. The Free Hit squad is temporary and your old squad returns at the following deadline. Best reasons to bank transfers Bank when: your team has no urgent problem; a future fixture swing is more important; you want to make linked moves later; transfer or injury news is still uncertain. articles.body: FPL Bench Boost Explained: Rules, Transfers & FAQs | OneFPL Loading OneFPL page In this article sections What does Bench Boost do? Bench Boost adds the points scored by all four of your substitutes to your Gameweek total. Normally only your starting XI score unless automatic substitutions are required. Does Bench Boost use your free transfer? No. Normal transfer rules continue when you play Bench Boost. You can use your weekly free transfer, bank it, or make extra transfers for the normal points cost. Does bench order matter on Bench Boost? For points, all four bench players count , so the normal first-sub/second-sub priority does not determine which bench scores are included. You should still save a valid team and captain before the deadline. Do automatic substitutions matter? Bench Boost already includes the points from all substitutes. The chip's purpose is to score from the full 15-player squad rather than only relying on auto-subs. What if a benched player does not play? They simply score zero unless FPL later credits an appearance. Bench Boost does not guarantee points — it only counts whatever the bench actually scores. Can Bench Boost be cancelled? Yes. Bench Boost can be cancelled before the Gameweek deadline. Can you use Wildcard and Bench Boost together? No. Only one chip can be active in a Gameweek. A common strategy is Wildcard first and Bench Boost in a later Gameweek. How many Bench Boosts do you get? Two in 2026/27 — one in each half of the season. articles.body: How to Rank Your FPL Mini-League and Win the Bragging Rights — FPL Ranker Blog ← Back Blog STRATEGY How to Rank Your FPL Mini-League and Win the Bragging Rights FPL Ranker July 20, 2026 To rank your FPL mini-league on FPL Ranker, enter any manager’s team ID to load live standings, gameweek points and rank movement. You get ESPN-style headlines, effective ownership, captaincy and chip tracking, plus a Rank My Team verdict — everything you need to see who is really winning your mini-league and why, updated with official Fantasy data every gameweek. What you need to rank your mini-league All you need is a Fantasy Premier League team ID — the number in your team URL at fantasy.premierleague.com/entry/1234567. Enter it once and FPL Ranker pulls your live squad, your gameweek points and every classic mini-league you belong to. There is no login and nothing to install. The tools are free forever; a small commission from official kit links keeps them that way. Reading the standings like an analyst The standings table goes beyond rank and total points. Rank movement shows who climbed and who fell this gameweek, effective ownership reveals which popular picks actually moved the table, and captaincy tracking shows where the big hauls came from. ESPN-style headlines turn the raw numbers into a story — the manager who nailed the captain, the bench disaster, the differential that swung the week. Using the Rank My Team verdict The Rank My Team verdict grades your XI on the season using points-per-game, form and minutes, then projects upcoming gameweeks from form, fixture difficulty and minutes certainty. Use it to decide who to bench, who to captain and when to spend a transfer. FAQ How do I find my FPL team ID? It appears in the URL of any manager's team page: fantasy.premierleague.com/entry/1234567/event/1 — the 1234567 is the team ID. The ID is public. It is how the official Fantasy site links to a squad, and it is what third-party tools ask for when they load someone's team. It is not a password and it grants nobody access to your account — knowing your ID lets someone view the same public squad page that the official league table already links to. The manual method: one ID at a time Open your mini-league on the official Fantasy Premier League site, go to the Standings tab, and click a manager's team name. That opens their squad page, and the number in the URL after /entry/ is their team ID. Copy it, go back, and repeat for the next manager. This works, but the official standings page never shows the IDs as a list — so a 20-manager league means 20 round trips through the URL bar, and there is no export. That is the whole reason this question gets asked. The fast method: the Ambassador tab Each ID links straight to that manager's official Fantasy squad page, and Export CSV downloads the whole roster — rank, team, manager, team ID, total points, gameweek points, the official FPL link and an FPL Ranker link for each manager. Copy list puts the same roster on your clipboard for a group chat. It is sign-in gated on purpose. A roster of manager names and IDs should not be bulk-scrapeable by anyone who happens to know a league code, so exporting is tied to a real account. 1. Open the Ambassador tab on your league. 2. Export CSV pulls every team ID into one file. (IDs are blurred in this screenshot; yours show in full.) What to do with the list The common use is comparison. With every ID in one place you can pull up any rival's squad, see their captain, and check their transfers without hunting through the official table each week. The export opens straight in Google Sheets, Excel or Numbers. Every row is one manager — rank, team name, manager name, FPL team ID, total points, gameweek points, a link to their official Fantasy squad and a link to their FPL Ranker page — so you can sort it, filter it, or paste a single column into whatever tool you use next. The other use is the one the tab is named after. Share the CSV in your league chat so everyone can paste their own ID into a tool and see their season — rank movement, gameweek headlines, and where they actually gained and lost ground. A mini-league is more fun when everyone can see the story, not just the table. The same export opened in Google Sheets — one row per manager, ready to sort, filter or share. Fetching the latest information from Fantasy Premier League Blog ← Back Blog tips · cover TIPS FPL Gameweek 2 Captain Picks and Transfer Targets 2026/27 FPL Ranker August 27, 2026 For FPL Gameweek 2, Haaland remains the safest armband despite his opening blank, with João Pedro and Cole Palmer the strongest alternatives at home to a depleted Brighton. Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo face Ipswich at Old Trafford. The most-bought players are De Cuyper, Sangaré and João Pedro; the most-sold is Pedro Porro. The deadline is Friday 28 August at 18:30 BST. Gameweek 2 deadline and fixtures The Gameweek 2 deadline is Friday 28 August 2026 at 18:30 BST, 90 minutes before Crystal Palace host Manchester City to open the round. The gameweek then runs across four days and closes with Aston Villa v Arsenal on the Monday night. On the official Fixture Difficulty Ratings, the softest assignments belong to the home sides in Chelsea v Brighton (2), Man Utd v Ipswich (2), Tottenham v Newcastle (2), Sunderland v Fulham (2) and Coventry v Hull (2). The hardest single fixture on the slate is Aston Villa v Arsenal, rated 4 for both teams. The full round: Crystal Palace v Man City (Friday), Liverpool v Nottingham Forest, Bournemouth v Everton, Coventry v Hull, Tottenham v Newcastle (Saturday), Chelsea v Brighton, Leeds v Brentford, Sunderland v Fulham, Man Utd v Ipswich (Sunday), Aston Villa v Arsenal (Monday). Gameweek 2 captain picks Haaland (£15.5m) is still the default. One blank against Bournemouth does not undo the profile — he took five shots in that match, and he is captained by more managers than anyone else in the game for a reason. Crystal Palace away is rated 3 rather than 2, which is the only real argument against him, and it is a thin one. If you are happy taking the field-average outcome, this is the pick. João Pedro (£7.6m) is the aggressive alternative. Chelsea are at home to a Brighton side missing Yankuba Minteh for at least a fortnight, with Carlos Baleba, Kaoru Mitoma and Stefanos Tzimas all doubts, and the fixture is rated 2. João Pedro scored and assisted in the 3-2 win at Fulham and is now owned by 67.6% of managers, so this is a low-risk pivot rather than a punt. Cole Palmer (£9.5m) is the higher-variance version of the same fixture. He is on penalties and set pieces, he recorded the highest BPS total of Gameweek 1 (60), and he is owned by only 15.2% — captaining him is a genuine differential inside a soft home fixture. Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) and Bryan Mbeumo (£8.0m) are the contrarian route: Ipswich at Old Trafford is a 2, and both are coming off a two-point return that has driven roughly 188,000 and 175,000 managers to sell them. The uncomfortable read is that Haaland, João Pedro and Fernandes are all owned by a third or more of the game, so none of them is a rank-mover in a big mini-league. Palmer at 15.2% is. Which of those matters depends on whether you are protecting a lead or chasing one — the mini-league standings on FPL Ranker will tell you which of the two you actually are before you set the armband. The Scout GW2 squad The Scout squad for Gameweek 2 lines up 3-5-2 and lands at just under the £100m budget, built around a triple Arsenal spine at the back and the two Manchester United attackers at home to Ipswich. Haaland takes the armband. The bench is deliberately cheap — Dúbravka in goal, Drameh and Slater from Hull, and Walle Egeli from Ipswich — which is the standard early-season shape: spend the money on eleven starters and accept that the bench is there for autosubs rather than for Bench Boost value. The official Premier League version of the Scout selection is published separately as a Wildcard-and-new-starter template and is worth reading alongside it. Transfer targets: who the market is buying Maxim De Cuyper (Brighton, £4.6m) is the most-bought player in the game with roughly 421,000 moves in after his 17-point opener. He has already risen £0.1m. The caveat is the fixture: Brighton travel to Chelsea in Gameweek 2, which is the hardest assignment on their card for weeks, and Brighton are missing several attackers. He is a good buy on role and price; Gameweek 2 is not his best entry point. Mamadou Sangaré (Brentford, £5.6m) is second with roughly 359,000 moves in, and he is the more fixture-proof of the two. Two assists plus 13 defensive contributions in Gameweek 1 is exactly the dual-route profile that defensive contribution scoring rewards — his floor does not depend on Brentford keeping a clean sheet. Leeds away is rated 3. Behind them, João Pedro (roughly 326,000 in), Palmer (292,000), Riccardo Calafiori (276,000), Michael Kayode (270,000) and Martin Ødegaard (253,000) are all being bought. Calafiori, Kayode, Ødegaard, De Cuyper, Sangaré and João Pedro all rose in price on 27 August — the first price changes of the season. If you are choosing between them on fixtures rather than form, Liverpool have the best run in the game from Gameweek 2 to Gameweek 5 (average difficulty 2.50), followed by Leeds, Man City, Newcastle and Tottenham on 2.75. Arsenal have the worst of the traditional big six at 3.50, with trips to Aston Villa, Chelsea and Brighton in that window — worth weighing before you buy a third Arsenal defender. Who to sell, and who is flagged Pedro Porro (Tottenham, £5.5m) is the most-sold player in the game at roughly 293,000 moves out after recording zero minutes in Gameweek 1. Ollie Watkins (roughly 212,000 out) and Viktor Gyökeres (193,000) are in the same boat and have both dropped in price. Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest, £8.0m) is second on the sold list with a knee injury and a 75% chance of playing, away at Liverpool. That is a straightforward move if you can make it without a hit. Other flags to check before the deadline: Moisés Caicedo and Marc Palestra (Chelsea), Bruno Guimarães (Arsenal), Jack Hinshelwood (Brighton), Matheus Nunes (Man City), Amad (Man Utd) and James Maddison (Tottenham) are all listed at 75%. Ismaïla Sarr (Crystal Palace) is injured with no return date, Dan Burn (Newcastle) is expected back on 14 September and Jérémy Doku (Man City) on 5 September. Hinshelwood is the one that stings — he scored 16 points in Gameweek 1 and is now doubtful. On hits: with the market this active it is tempting to take a -4, but Gameweek 2 is early enough that most of what looks broken is a squad-shape problem rather than a one-player problem. Fix it on a Wildcard once minutes settle. If you want a read on which of your own players are genuinely underperforming rather than merely unlucky, the Rank My Team verdict on FPL Ranker grades your XI on form, minutes and fixtures. articles.body: Is My FPL Team Good? Rate My FPL Team Score Explained | FPL Copilot Back to blog Rate My Team is FPL Copilot's free squad rater: enter your Team ID and the Copilot Score rates your Fantasy Premier League squad from 0 to 100 on projected points, captaincy, bench, fixtures and budget, then names the single change that helps most. 80 and above is elite, 60 to 79 is strong, and below 60 means your squad has a structural problem. Is your squad actually good, or does it just feel good? Here is what the score measures, what a good number looks like, and how to move it. Rate your team, right here. Enter your Team ID, or drop a screenshot of your squad. Free, no sign-up. Drop a screenshot of your team What Is the Copilot Score? The Copilot Score is a 0-100 rating of your FPL squad setup for the upcoming gameweek. Not just "are your players good" but "is your team set up to score the most points possible this week." I check five things: Starting XI strength. Total xPts for your first team. Simple question: are your best players on the pitch? Captain pick. Are you captaining the highest-xPts player? Most managers aren't. It's the easiest free points in FPL. Bench strength and order. A good bench catches auto-subs when rotation hits. A bad bench costs you. I check both the quality and whether your bench order is right. Fixture outlook. Great players with terrible upcoming fixtures are a ticking time bomb. Budget flexibility. Money in the bank and free transfers give you room to react. Zero flexibility means one injury away from a crisis. What Is a Good Copilot Score? 80 and above is elite. 60 to 79 is strong. Below 60 means something structural is wrong: a weak bench, a suboptimal captain, bad upcoming fixtures, or money locked in the bank. Three markers do most of the work if you want to sanity check it by hand. Projected xPts above 55 for your starting XI is good. Your captain should be the highest-xPts player you own. Your bench should be three or four nailed 4.0m to 5.0m starters, not non-playing fodder. The Copilot Score rolls those three plus fixture outlook and budget into one number in about two seconds. 0-100 Copilot Score Squad rating Factors XI, cap, bench, fix, budget Free trial Pro experience Just your Team ID Get your squad rated right now. Rate My Team → How to Improve Your Score Fix your captain first. This is almost always the biggest quick win. If you're not captaining the highest-xPts player, just switch. That alone can move your score by 10-15 points. Check your bench order. Your highest-xPts bench player should be first sub. Over a season, good bench ordering gains you 5-10 points from auto-subs. Takes 5 seconds. Most managers never bother. Don't hoard money. 0.5m in the bank is flexibility. 2.0m in the bank is a player upgrade sitting on the bench. That money should be on the pitch scoring points, not collecting dust. Rate My Team vs the Solver Rate My Team is the diagnosis. The Solver is the treatment. One tells you what is wrong, the other tells you which transfers fix it. Run the rater for the score, run the solver for the moves. Score below 60? You probably need transfers. Score above 80? You're set. Save the free transfer and roll it. Where Do I Find My FPL Team ID? Log in at fantasy.premierleague.com, go to Pick Team, then click Gameweek History. The number at the end of the URL, straight after /entry/, is your Team ID. It is public information, safe to share, and it is the only thing the rater needs. Here's a tip: rate your team before AND after making transfers. If the score doesn't improve, the transfer probably wasn't worth it. It takes seconds. Save yourself a hit. How strong is your squad? articles.body: What Is FDR in FPL? Fixture Difficulty Explained | FPL Copilot Back to blog FDR (Fixture Difficulty Rating) is FPL's 1-to-5 ranking of how hard each Premier League match is for a team. Green means easy, red means hard, yellow sits in the middle. Managers use FDR to plan transfers and chips around easy fixture runs. The live 2026/27 FDR ticker (sortable, all 20 teams) Easy Hard SUN home, sun away The ticker ranks all 20 Premier League teams by total fixture difficulty over the next 3, 6, 8 or 10 gameweeks, so the team at the top of the list has the easiest run across the window you pick. If it has not loaded, the full FDR ticker is the same data on its own page. Prefer the full-screen version with every sorting option? Open the FDR ticker → FDR on its own is a great starting point. Here is what it actually tells you, where it falls short, and how to pair the live FDR ticker with xPts to fix the gaps. What Is FPL FDR? FDR is the Fixture Difficulty Rating that appears next to every fixture on the official FPL site. It is a number from 1 to 5 assigned to each opponent per gameweek. Lower is easier. FDR 1: the easiest tier on paper. FPL almost never assigns it, so real fixture runs bottom out at 2. FDR 2: easy fixture (green). Good transfer target. FDR 3: neutral (yellow). FDR 4: hard (orange-red). Rotation risk territory. FDR 5: very hard (red). Usually top-4 opponents away from home. Teams are rated based on form, recent results, attacking strength, and defensive strength. The algorithm updates after each gameweek so FDR is not static across the season. 1-5 FDR scale Lower is easier Gameweeks FDR updates weekly 1-6 Planning horizon GWs to check ahead How to Use FDR for FPL Transfers Plan five to six gameweeks ahead, never one. Sum a team's FDR across your window and sort by the lowest total: over three gameweeks the range runs 6 to 15, and in practice anything under 9 is a genuinely soft run while 11 or more is one to swerve. The workflow: Check 5-6 gameweeks ahead. Find teams with three or more green fixtures in a row. Those are your transfer targets. Avoid red fixture runs. If a player you own has four FDR 4-5 fixtures, sell unless their individual xPts is still elite. Stack 3 teams with green runs. Concentrate your 15 players in clubs with the best fixture swing. The 3-per-club limit still applies. Use FDR to time chips. Wildcard before a green swing. Bench Boost in a DGW with easy fixtures. Free Hit in a BGW. See which fixtures your squad faces Check Expected Points → Why FDR Alone Is Not Enough FDR is a rough team-level signal. It cannot tell you what matters most for FPL scoring: Home vs away split. FDR treats Arsenal (H) and Arsenal (A) as the same difficulty. Home teams score 30% more goals on average. Real difficulty is very different. Style matchups. A high-press team vs a long-ball team is easier than vs a possession team. FDR ignores style. Individual matchups. A fast winger vs a slow fullback is a green fixture for that player even if the team FDR is red. Rotation risk. FDR does not know if Pep will rest Haaland or if Arteta will rotate Saka. The easy fixture means nothing if your player sits on the bench. Set-piece duties. Two players in the same team with identical FDR can have very different ceilings based on penalties and free kicks. Using FDR alone is like picking a restaurant by postcode. It narrows the field but does not pick the meal. xPts vs FDR: What Actually Predicts FPL Points Expected points (xPts) is what FDR becomes when you combine it with every other variable that matters. The FPL Copilot xPts model processes 50+ data points per player per gameweek: Fixture difficulty (including FDR) Home vs away split Opponent xG conceded, xG against, and defensive style Individual player xG, xA, shots, key passes Projected minutes and rotation risk Set-piece duties (penalties, free kicks, corners) Clean sheet probability for defenders and keepers Bonus point patterns from BPS history Everything FDR captures plus everything it misses. For captain picks, transfers, and chip timing, xPts is the single number that matters. 50+ Data points Per player per GW 73% Top-5 accuracy Captain picks +20-30 Season gain vs form-based picks Where FDR Still Wins FDR is free, official, and easy to read at a glance. Three use cases where it is still the right tool: Season planning at a high level. Looking 8+ weeks out, FDR gives a reasonable team-level fixture swing picture before individual xPts data stabilises. Quick vibes check. Glancing at next week's FDR before deadline to confirm nothing obvious is wrong. New season pre-draft. Before the first ball is kicked, FDR is often the only signal available because there is no xG or form data yet. Once the season is underway, xPts beats FDR on every gameweek-to-gameweek decision. But FDR as a sanity check never hurts. Common FPL Fixture Planning Mistakes Only checking next week. FPL transfers reward 5-8 GW horizons. Planning one week ahead misses the 2-week holds that win leagues. Ignoring home/away. A home FDR 3 often beats an away FDR 2. Assuming FDR 5 means zero points. Premium attackers (Haaland, Saka, Bruno Fernandes) still return against top defences. Fixture-proof players exist. Reacting to one bad fixture. Selling after one red match when the next three are green is a classic mistake. Forgetting DGW and BGW. FDR does not flag blank or double gameweeks. Check the FPL calendar separately. FDR narrows your shortlist. xPts picks the winner. Use FDR to scan teams with easy runs, then use the xPts table to find the specific player inside those teams with the highest ceiling. That is how every elite manager plans transfers. Which players have the best fixtures? Enter your Team ID and I use fixture data plus 50 other signals to find your best transfer targets across the next 1 to 10 gameweeks. articles.body: FPL Chips 2026/27: Chip Strategy & When to Play | FPL Copilot Back to blog TL;DR Your FPL chip strategy for 2026/27 comes down to timing, not luck. You get two sets of chips, one for each half of the season, and the first set expires at the Gameweek 19 deadline. Do not rush them. Wildcard on a fixture swing, Bench Boost in a double gameweek, Free Hit on a blank, Triple Captain on your best premium in a high-ceiling week. Here is the plan. Copilot verdict WAIT The most common chip mistake is playing them early out of boredom. Hold each one for the moment it is designed for. Patience is the whole strategy. I ran the chip optimizer over 300+ real squads to find out what timing is actually worth. Optimal chip timing gained an average of 49 points against a no-chip baseline, and 69% of those squads gained between 40 and 60 points. That is from timing alone, with no extra transfers. +49 points gained avg from optimal chip timing 69% of squads gained 40-60 points 300+ real squads tested every valid chip combination How FPL Chips Work in 2026/27 You start the season with a full set of chips: one Wildcard, one Free Hit, one Bench Boost, and one Triple Captain. The first set has to be used by the Gameweek 19 deadline. A fresh set unlocks for the second half, and you can only play one chip in any single gameweek. That structure is the strategy. Two Wildcards, two Bench Boosts and two Triple Captains across the year means you rarely need to force one. Wait for the right gameweek and the same chip is worth far more. When to Play Your First Wildcard Not in the opening weeks. Fixture difficulty and form only settle after about six gameweeks, so an early Wildcard spends information you do not have yet. The strongest first-Wildcard window is usually a clear fixture swing once the season has taken shape, often in the run toward the first set of double gameweeks. Use the live FDR ticker to spot the swing: when a cluster of teams flips from red fixtures to green, that is your Wildcard trigger. I test every valid chip combination for thousands of squads. The ones who guess their timing lose 40-plus points to the ones who wait for the data. Chips are patience, not gut feel. When to Play Bench Boost and Triple Captain Bench Boost: a double gameweek where all 15 of your players have two fixtures and a nailed bench. Build toward it with a Wildcard the week before so every bench slot is a starter, not fodder. Triple Captain: your best premium in a double gameweek or a soft home fixture. Haaland with two games is the textbook target. Do not waste it on a single tough fixture. Free Hit: a blank gameweek where half your squad has no fixture. Free Hit is a one-week rescue, so timing beats squad quality here. Remember the one-chip-per-gameweek rule. You cannot Bench Boost and Triple Captain the same week, so a double gameweek forces a choice between them. FPL Chips 26/27: Guides by Gameweek GW1 and GW2 are played and the next deadline is Gameweek 3 on Friday 4 September at 6.30pm. If you are playing a chip this week, these are the live ones, each with the solver-built squad or armband on current projections: Wildcard GW3: best draft and template squad Free Hit GW3: best team for one gameweek Triple Captain GW3: who to captain Further out, or back at how the early chip weeks looked: Triple Captain GW5: who to captain Bench Boost GW2: best squad and bench picks What Are the FPL Chips? FPL chips are one-off boosts you play on a single gameweek. There are four, and each does one thing: Wildcard. Unlimited free transfers for one gameweek, with no points hits. The new squad is permanent, so you draft for the weeks ahead. Free Hit. Unlimited free transfers for one gameweek, but your squad reverts afterwards. You are renting a team for a single week. Bench Boost. Your four bench players score as well as your XI, so all 15 count instead of 11. Triple Captain. Your captain scores triple instead of double for that gameweek. You play one chip per gameweek at most, and each is worth far more in the right week than the wrong one. That gap is what this guide is about. Build a First-Half Plan Now Two gameweeks in, you still do not need to lock exact gameweeks, but you should know the shape: hold through the opening run, Wildcard on the first real fixture swing once form has settled, then chain Bench Boost and Triple Captain through the winter doubles before the Gameweek 19 deadline. Check your own squad against that shape in the chip planner , or sort the expected points table over the next six gameweeks to see where your fixture swing actually lands. What's your optimal chip timing? Enter your Team ID and I test every valid Wildcard, Bench Boost, Triple Captain and Free Hit combination for your exact squad. Plan My Chips Want more depth on one chip? The Bench Boost guide covers what a good Bench Boost score looks like and how to build a bench worth boosting, the Wildcard guide covers rebuild timing, and the Free Hit guide covers blank gameweeks. For the raw numbers behind the timing, the chip optimizer data breaks down what the solver found across hundreds of real squads.

The squad above is the 15 that maximises it on the latest projections, with every bench slot filled by a player who actually starts. Get those four right and the chip pays; leave one non-starter in and you have thrown away a quarter of it. Copilot verdict ALL 15 SCORE Your bench is not filler this week. Check all four for a confirmed start, a fixture you would happily own, and no rotation risk. Any 0 on the bench is a wasted chip slot. Setting Up a Bench Boost Squad for GW2 Bench Boost scores your whole 15 instead of your XI, so the chip is worth exactly what your four bench players deliver. That flips how you pick them. The pitch above is solver-built for this gameweek on live projected points , so it already applies that logic. Compare your own four against it, and get your squad scored with a free Copilot Score Every bench player needs a fixture. One blank or a rested player is a guaranteed zero in a slot you paid a chip for. Minutes beat name value. A nailed £4.5m defender who plays 90 outscores a £5.5m rotation risk every time on this chip. Check the late kickoffs. A player benched for a midweek rotation is the classic Bench Boost leak. Do not chase a differential on the bench. You want the floor here, not the ceiling. Open the FPL Solver What to Expect From It in a Single Gameweek Worth being straight with you: Gameweek 2 is a single gameweek. All 20 teams play once, and so does every side through Gameweek 6. Your bench covers four fixtures rather than eight, so this is the lower half of the chip's range. That is not a reason to abandon a plan you have already made. If you are boosting because your bench is unusually strong right now, or because you want the chip gone before the fixture list gets complicated, the job is simply to squeeze the most out of the four slots. It is a reason to be strict about starts. A single-gameweek Bench Boost is worth roughly 8 to 12 points from the bench against 18 to 25 in a double, which is the whole timing argument: the Bench Boost guide has the mechanics and the 2026/27 chip strategy guide has the placement. articles.body: FPL Bench Boost GW1 2026/27: Best Playing 15 Squad | FPL Copilot Back to blog Gameweek 1 and Gameweek 2 have both been played. This page stays up as the reference for how an all-15-start Bench Boost squad is built. It is not current advice. Playing a chip at the GW3 deadline (Friday 4 September, 6.30pm BST) instead? The live calls are the GW3 Wildcard draft , the GW3 Free Hit XI and the GW3 Triple Captain pick . For Bench Boost specifically, the GW2 Bench Boost squad shows how the 15 is put together, and the 2026/27 chip strategy plan covers season-long timing. TL;DR Bench Boost in Gameweek 1 is almost always the wrong call, and Gameweek 1 of 2026/27 has now been played. The chip only pays when all 15 players start, which means no £4.0m fodder, a nailed backup keeper and a bench of genuine starters. Even then a single-fixture week caps the return at four extra one-game hauls, so the same chip is worth roughly double in a double gameweek. Copilot verdict WAIT An early Bench Boost is a gamble on a single-fixture week, so hold it for a double gameweek. The all-15-start structure below is still the squad shape you want, and it is what makes the chip pay whenever you fire it. The Best FPL Bench Boost GW1 Squad 2026/27 The pitch above is a Bench-Boost-ready 15 built on the latest xPts, so it moves with the projections rather than sitting frozen on Gameweek 1. The whole point of Bench Boost is that your four bench players also score, so a Bench-Boost-ready squad has no passengers: every player is a projected starter, and the green bench is the boost in action. Even both goalkeepers start for their clubs, so the keeper you bench still brings in points. That is the difference between a Bench-Boost-ready squad and a normal one. Why Every Player Has to Start Under Bench Boost, your bench points count. A normal squad benches three £4.0m fodder defenders who never play, so boosting them adds almost nothing. This squad benches genuine 90-minute starters, which you can confirm on the xPts table , and that is where the extra points come from. People chase a "big" Bench Boost squad. The real trick is boring: 15 players who all start. Boost four nailed defenders and you beat the manager who boosted three who did not. Should You Actually Bench Boost in GW1? No, and the Gameweek 1 results did not change that. Gameweek 1 is a single-fixture week, so Bench Boost adds four extra one-game hauls at most. In a double gameweek those same four players each play twice, which is roughly double the return for the same chip. The smart move is the same every season: build the playing 15 above as your regular squad, hold the Bench Boost, and fire it when the first double gameweek arrives. articles.body: FPL 2026/27 Preseason Guide: Best Opening Fixtures & Team | FPL Copilot Back to blog TL;DR Everton, Man Utd, Liverpool and Newcastle have the best opening fixtures in 2026/27, all averaging 2.83 on fixture difficulty across the first six gameweeks. Build around them, not around last season's points table. Gameweek 1 kicked off on Friday 21 August 2026. The opening-fixture logic below still shapes your transfers through the first six gameweeks. Copilot verdict PLAY IT Preseason is won on fixtures and value, not big names. Anchor your draft to the best opening runs and leave room to react after Gameweek 3. Preseason is over and the season has started. For the current gameweek, see GW3 tips When Does FPL 2026/27 Start? The 2026/27 season began on Friday 21 August 2026. The Gameweek 1 deadline has passed, so this guide is now about the opening run rather than the first draft. Transfers now cost 4 points beyond your free one, so changes need to earn their place. The fixture list is settled, which is what makes the opening run plannable. Start with the projected points and the fixture ticker , then get the draft scored with a free Copilot Score Which Teams Have the Best Opening Fixtures? Four teams share the softest opening six gameweeks, all averaging 2.83 on fixture difficulty: Everton, Man Utd, Liverpool and Newcastle at 2.83, each with two green fixtures in the opening six Sunderland and Arsenal just behind at 3.00, with Sunderland holding three green fixtures Bournemouth (3.67), Fulham (3.33) and Hull (3.17) have the hardest starts, so treat their assets as later buys A player from a team with three easy opening fixtures is worth more than a bigger name facing three tough ones in August. The ticker below is live, so sort it by the easiest run over the next 3, 6, 8 or 10 gameweeks and check the numbers yourself before you commit. Loading FDR ticker... How to Build Your Gameweek 1 Draft A strong opening squad follows a simple shape: Two or three premium attackers from teams with good opening fixtures. These are your captain rotation. Value midfielders (6.0m to 8.0m) with nailed minutes. This is where you find the points-per-million that funds your premiums. A solid defence from teams that keep clean sheets , ideally with a set-piece or attacking threat. A real 4th and 5th defender and a playing bench , not just fodder. Early-season rotation risk is high, so nailed minutes matter more than name value. One budget-enabling goalkeeper pairing so you can spend up the pitch. Do not chase last season's top scorers on reputation. Chase minutes, role, and fixtures. New signings, pre-season friendlies, and manager changes shift the picture right up to the deadline. Every preseason, someone builds their whole team around last year's top scorer and forgets he now has three away fixtures to open. Fixtures first. Names second. Should I Use My First Wildcard Early? No. You get two Wildcards across the season, and burning the first one in the opening weeks throws away information. Fixture difficulty and form only settle after about six gameweeks. The strongest first-Wildcard window is usually once that picture is clear, not Gameweek 2 when you are reacting to a single blank. articles.body: Gameweek 1 Review: Brighton Stars Shine as Hull Shock United | FPL Central GW3 deadline 3d 3h Cherki â² 3.4pp Gameweek review Â· 2026/27 Gameweek 1 Review: Brighton Stars Shine as Hull Shock United The 2026/27 Premier League season is underway, and Gameweek 1 delivered drama, upsets, and unexpected FPL heroes. Newly promoted sides made an immediate mark, several premium assets blanked, and Brighton & Hove Albion produced the biggest individual hauls of the weekend. Thirty goals flew in across the ten matches, with six clean sheets recorded. The results Home Score Away Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City Hull City 2-0 Manchester United Everton 2-0 Crystal Palace Ipswich Town 2-1 Sunderland Nottingham Forest 0-1 Leeds United Brentford 3-0 Tottenham Hotspur Brighton & Hove Albion 4-0 Aston Villa Manchester City 2-1 Bournemouth Newcastle United 2-2 Liverpool Fulham 2-3 Chelsea Arsenal cruise, Hull stun United Arsenal opened their title defence with a controlled 3-0 win at the Emirates - Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Ãdegaard on target as the champions eased past Frank Lampard's newly promoted Coventry City. The bigger story came at the MKM Stadium, where Hull City beat Manchester United 2-0. Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy scored as the hosts defended resolutely against a United side that dominated possession but created little of note - an early lesson that reputation alone counts for nothing in Gameweek 1. Brighton's rout, and goals everywhere else Brighton dismantled Aston Villa 4-0: an early own goal was followed by a strike from Maxim De Cuyper and a quickfire brace from Jack Hinshelwood. Brentford were similarly ruthless, beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-0 at home, while Chelsea edged Fulham 3-2 in the Monday night fixture thanks to goals from JoÃ£o Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer. Manchester City needed late goals from Marc GuÃ©hi and Josko Gvardiol to see off Bournemouth 2-1, and Newcastle United shared the points with Liverpool in a 2-2 thriller. Top FPL scorers Defenders and unexpected midfielders dominated the points list - not the household names most squads were built around. Player Team Points Why Maxim De Cuyper Brighton Goal, assist, bonus Jack Hinshelwood Brighton Brace, maximum bonus Nobel Mendy Hull City Goal in the shock win Semi Ajayi Hull City Goal in the shock win Mamadou SangarÃ© Brentford Two assists Michael Kayode Brentford Clean sheet involvement Anton Stach Leeds United Away win at Forest Cole Palmer Chelsea Goal and assist Cody Gakpo Liverpool Benjamin White Arsenal Bukayo Saka Arsenal Riccardo Calafiori Arsenal Premium frustrations Plenty of highly owned players disappointed. Erling Haaland managed only two points despite playing the full 90 against Bournemouth. Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo both blanked in United's defeat at Hull. Igor Thiago of Brentford failed to score despite a high expected-involvement afternoon and a missed penalty. These blanks will have hurt ranks for managers who loaded up on the expensive Manchester options - in contrast, those who backed Arsenal's defenders or Brighton's attackers enjoyed a strong start. Lessons for Gameweek 2 Gameweek 1 rewarded secure roles with favourable fixtures over pure reputation. Brighton's attacking full-backs and midfielders thrived, while Hull's organised defence produced both clean-sheet points and goals. Promoted sides showed they can't be taken lightly - Hull and Leeds both claimed wins, and Ipswich edged Sunderland. Clean sheets for Arsenal, Everton, Hull and Brighton will encourage continued investment in those defences, though fixture swings arrive quickly. Chelsea's attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and JoÃ£o Pedro looked lively at Fulham and could stay attractive. Differential ownership of Brighton and Hull assets will have created early rank gaps, while heavy ownership of Haaland and United's midfield left plenty of managers frustrated after round one. Looking ahead: Gameweek 2 brings fresh tests - Arsenal travel to Aston Villa, Manchester United host Ipswich Town, and Manchester City face Crystal Palace. Brighton's next assignment, and whether De Cuyper and Hinshelwood can back up their Gameweek 1 form, will be watched closely before any knee-jerk transfers. Prioritise minutes and set-piece involvement over one-week fireworks - a secure role at a club that looked solid in Gameweek 1 is a safer bet than chasing an isolated haul.
